# Stava-mala (BS)

## stavamālā

Srila Rupa Gosvami

Compiled by Srila Jiva Gosvami

Commentary by Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana

Translated by HH Bhanu Swami

This book is dedicated to His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Srila Prabhupada

Founder-Acarya: International Society for Krishna Consciousness

who inspired the world to take up the path of bhakti.

**śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya jayati \|**

**I offer respects to Krsna-Caitanya.**

### Text 1

*sanātanaṁ rūpamihopadarśayannānandasindhuṁ paritaḥ pravardhayan \|*  
*antastamaḥstomaharaḥ sa rājatāṁ caitanyarūpo vibhuradbhutodayaḥ*  
*\|\| 1 \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Showing an eternal form on earth, increasing everywhere the ocean of bliss, may the great form of Caitanya, destroying heaps of darkness in the heart, manifesting in an astonishing way, shine.**

### Text 2

*devācāryaṁ yaṁ viduḥ satkavitve pārāśaryaṁ tattvavāde mahāntaḥ \|*  
*śṛṅgārārthavyañjane vyāsasūnuṁ sa śrīrūpaḥ pātu no bhṛtyavargān*  
*\|\| 2 \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Whom the great souls know as the acarya in poetry, as Vyasadeva in discussions on tattva, and as Sukadeva in explaining the meaning of rasa, may that Rupa protect us, the servants.**

### Text 3

*labdhasanātanarūpaṁ jīvaṁ yo bhajati bhaktimāñjīvaḥ*  
*tasya sanātanarūpaḥ sa nandaputro hariḥ sulabhaḥ*  
*\|\| 3 \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, with eternal form, is easy to attain for the jiva having devotion who worships Jiva who has attained an eternal form.**

### Text 4

*śrīrūpadevavacasāṁ dhvanibhedā ye vibhānti bhūyāṁsaḥ \|*  
*kastāñśakto vaktuṁ tasmātsaṁkṣepataḥ prakāśyāste*  
*\|\| 4 \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The variety of suggested meanings in the words of Rupa which are plenty, being difficult to explain, will be revealed briefly.**

### Text 5

*bhāṣye'sminsādhavaḥ prītāḥ stavamālāvibhūṣaṇe \|*  
*kṛṣṇānandakapāsiddhe bhaveyuḥ śramavedinaḥ*  
*\|\| 5 \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the devotees, knowing my labor, be pleased with this commentary which ornaments Stava-mala and which was completed by the blissful mercy of Krsna.**

## mangalacarana

### Text 1

*srimad-isvara-rupena rasamrta-krta krta \|*  
*stava-malanujivena jivena satnagrhyata \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Stava-mala, by Rupa Gosvami, author of Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu has been assembled by Jiva, who followed him with his life.**

**Комментарий:**

Jiva gathered the garland of verses starting with the glorification of Sri Caitanya, written by Rupa, in order to string them into garland. The individual stavas are arranged in a series. Mala means a series, a garland of flowers, etc., according to Medini. Finally, the stotras, becoming flowers are made into a garland. The devotees should lovingly wear the stotras around the necks.

The garland is described. It was written by Rupa, who is my master (isvara) and who possesses wealth (srimat). His remarkable quality is mentioned. He wrote Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu. Jiva is described. He follows Rupa with his life (anujlvena). This means he was his student. The first verse acts as an invocation since it is the svarupa of auspiciousness.

### Text 2

*pūrvaṁ caitanya-devasya kṛṣṇadevasya tat-param \|*  
*śrī-rādhāyās tataḥ kṛṣṇa-rādhayor likhyate stavaḥ \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**First is written a stava on Lord Caitanya, and then on Krsna, then on Radha, and then on Radha and Krsna.**

**Комментарий:**

The order of the stavas is now explained. A stava on Krsna and Radha together is written.

### Text 3

*virudāvalī tato nānā-cchandobhiḥ keli-saṁhatiḥ \|*  
*tataś citra-kavitvāni tato gītāvalī tataḥ \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Then there is a stava in virudavali form concerning Krsna’s pastimes in various meters. Then there are citra-kavitas and then a collection of songs.**

**Комментарий:**

There are nine syllables in the first phrase of the above verse. Since the line here has irregular syllables, the verse is placed in the gatha category. Its details are written in the commentary on the Gltavall. One should consult that. Pastimes from Nanda’s festival up to the killing of Kamsa are described in eighteen different meters. Citra-kavita refers to the syllables of the poem producing a picture such as a cakra-bandha or poems with two letters, etc. Gltavall is a collection of songs describing Nanda’s festival, etc.

### Text 4

*lalitā-yamunā-vṛṣṇi-purī-śrī-hari-bhūbhṛtām \|*  
*vṛndāṭavī-kṛṣṇa-nāmnoḥ krameṇa stava-paddhatiḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Then there are stavas on Lalita, Yamuna, Mathura, Govardhana, Vrndavana, and Krsna’s names.**

**Комментарий:**

Vrsni-puri means Mathura and sri-hari-bhubhrt means Govardhana. There is a series (paddhatih) of stotras about Vrndavana and the names of Krsna, etc. Paddhati means series of verses according to Visvalocana dictionary.

The figures of speech and various meanings which are written in the original are not described for fear of making the commentary too large. They should be contemplated where they occur.

## prathamaṁ caitanyāṣṭakam

First there are the stotras for Lord Caitanya. First, I will explain the three astakas concerning Caitanya. Rupa, situated in Vrndavana realizing directly Caitanya as the Lord through scriptural proof (krsna-varna, etc.) and through mercy, describing this as the truth, desires to see him.

### Text 1

*sadopāsyaḥ śrīmān dhṛta-manuja-kāyaiḥ praṇayitāṁ*  
*vahadbhir gīrvāṇair giriśa-parameṣṭhi-prabhṛtibhiḥ \|*  
*sva-bhaktebhyaḥ śuddhāṁ nija-bhajana-mudrām upadiśan*  
*sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When will beautiful Caitanya, who is always worshipped by Siva, Brahma and other devatas, who assumed human bodies and possessed great devotion, and who taught to his devotees the pure method of worshipping him, be visible to my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

When will Caitanya come again to the ascertainment of my eyes? Padam means situation, deliverance, place, sign, foot and object according to Nanartha-varga. When will he become the object of my eyes? When will that good fortune be mine?

Caitanya is described. He possesses beauty (sriman). He is served constantly by devatas (glrvanaih) like Siva and Brahma. “But they are not perceived in his presence.” When Krsna appeared, they worshipped him directly. Now however they worship him in bodies like Advaita, Haridasa, etc. They have great affection (pranayitam) for him. What did he do? He taught the method of his bhakti to his devotees like Svarupa Damodara. The bhakti was pure, uncovered by karma, yoga, etc. The meaning is this.

*kṛṣṇavaṇaṁ tviṣā kṛṣṇaṁ sāṅgopāṅgāstrapārṣadam \|*  
*yajñaiḥ saṁkīrtanaprāyairyajanti hi sumedhasaḥ \|\|*

**The intelligent people worship the Lord, black in color, but shining with brilliance, who is accompanied by his associates, weapons, major and minor limbs, chiefly through chanting. (SB 11.5.32)**

The fourth yugavatara is described in the Eleventh Canto. He is Krsna-Caitanya, since it was seen that he propagated the extraordinary dharma of yajna predominated by hari-kirtana. The subject of the verse is known by his extraordinary quality. For instance, this is described in the sutra, janmadyasya yatah: what is indicated as the cause of the creation of the world is Brahman. This avatara is served by devatas (girvanaih). The next verse in Bhagavatam describes this:

*dhyeyaṁ sadā paribhava-ghnam abhīṣṭado'haṁ*  
*tīrthāspadaṁ śiva-viriñci-nutaṁ śaraṇyam*

**I offer respects to your lotus feet which are the object of constant meditation, which destroy all injury caused by the senses, which award all desires, which fulfill the results of visiting all holy places, which are worshipped by Siva and Brahma. (SB 11.5.33)**

The sruti hints at this appearance in many places.

*mahān prabhur vai puruṣaḥ sattvasyaiṣa pravartakaḥ*

**The great purusa (maha prabhuh — Caitanya) is capable of awarding liberation since he stimulates sattva in the jlva. (Svetasvatara Upanisad 3.12)**

Though it is confirmed that Caitanya is directly the Lord, if some unintelligent person is still doubtful, the doubt arises because of lack, of mercy.

*tam akratuḥ paśyati vīta-śokaṁ dhātuḥ*  
*prasādān mahimānam īśam*

**When, by the mercy of the Lord, the jiva sees the glory of the Lord, who is devoid of kamya-karmas, he becomes free of lamentation. (Katha Upanisad 1.2.20)**

The smrti also says:

*athāpi te devapadāmbuja-dvaya-prasāda-leśānugṛhīta eva hi \|*  
*jāgāti tattvaṁ bhagavan mahimno na cānya eko'pi ciraṁ vicinvan \|\|*

**My Lord, if one is favored by even a slight trace of the mercy of your lotus feet, he can understand the greatness of your personality. But those who speculate to understand the Supreme Lord are unable to know you, even though they continue to study the Vedas for many years. (SB 10.14.29)**

His mercy is the cause of seeing him as the Lord. This is seen by positive and negative examples. It is clear in the case of Vasudeva, Sarvabhauma and others. The fourth line is repeated in the seven following verses. That is the poetic custom in astakas.

### Text 2

*sureśānāṁ durgaṁ gatir atiśayenopaniṣadāṁ*  
*munīnāṁ sarva-svaṁ praṇata-paṭalīnāṁ madhurimā \|*  
*viniryāsaḥ premṇo nikhila-paśu-pālāmbuja-dṛśāṁ*  
*sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When will beautiful Caitanya, place of fearlessness for Indra and others, the path to the highest tattva of the Upanisads, the knowledge and austerity of sages, the sweetness of all the devotees, the essence of prema for the eyes of all the gopis, be visible to my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

Caitanya is not the fourth yugavatara who is an amsa of Krsna.

*krte suklo dharma murti raktas tretayuge matah \|*  
*dvapare ca kalau capi syamalangah prakirtitah \|\|*

**In Satya-yuga the dharma murti is white, in Treta-yuga he is red. In Dvapara and Kali, he is syama.**

The normal kali-yuga avatara is syama. Hiding his natural color with the complexion of his beloved, Krsna himself appeared. That is expressed in this verse.

Durgam means a place with no fear. He is the path to the highest tattva (garth) mentioned the Upanisads. He is the wealth of knowledge and austerity (sarvasvam) in this life and the next for the sages. He is the sweetness of dasya bhakti (madhurima) for the group (patala) of dasa devotees (pranata). According to Haima, patala is a synonym for vrnda. He is the essence (viniryasah) of prema for Krsna, of all the women of Vraja. When will he be visible to me?

In this verse, hetv-alahkara is seen. Caitanya is described as the cause of various things such as fearlessness.

Kavya-kaustubha says:

*hetoḥ kāryātmanākhyānaṁ heturityabhidhīyate*

**A statement of something acting as a cause is called hetu.**

Here is an example:

*adrīṇāṁ vidrutiḥ sākṣād ākṛṣṭir vraja-subhruvām \|*  
*sthairya srotasvatīnāṁ ca jīyād vaṁśī-dhvanir vibhoḥ \|\|*

**May the sound of the flute of the Lord, which makes mountains flow, which attracts the women of Vraja, which makes the rivers stop flowing, remain victorious.**

In this verse the sound of the flute causes the melting of mountains, etc. In this way the flute is described. That Caitanya is actually Krsna will be described next.

### Text 3

*svarūpaṁ bibhrāṇo jagad-atulam advaita-dayitaḥ*  
*prapanna-śrīvāso janita-paramānanda-garimā*  
*harir dīnoddhārī gaja-pati-kṛpotseka-taralaḥ*  
*sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When will the Lord, Caitanya, who nourished Svariipa, incomparable in the world, with mercy, who was the object of surrender of Srivasa, who was dear to Advaitacarya, who increased the greatness of Paramananda, who was deliverer of the miserable, and was eager to sprinkle Prataparudra with mercy, be visible to my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

Now Caitanya is described as being directly Krsna. He supported and nourished with sweet mercy his associate Svariipa, incomparable in this world. He was dear to Advaitacarya, or to whom Advaitacarya was dear. Srivasa surrendered to him.

He produced greatness in the sannyasi Paramananda, who was the godbrother of Isvara Puri. He destroyed the ignorance of the world (harih). That is further explained. He delivered persons from the three types of suffering. He was quick (taralah) to sprinkle mercy on Prataparudra, king of Orissa.

As a pun, harih also means a lion. As a lion he gave mercy to the king (gajapatih), leader of elephants. (Usually the lion is the enemy of the elephant.) This is viruddhabhasa-alaiikara. This indicates that Caitanya was an astonishing lion.

Caitanya maintained or manifested an incomparable svariipa in this world, since he is Krsna.

*na tasya pratimāsti*

**There is no one in this world like him. (Yajur Veda)**

He was fond of Advaita who is non-different, though he had various fonns.

*eko'pi sanbahudhā yo'vabhāti*

**Though one he has many forms. (Gopala Tapani Upanisad)**

*ekaṁ santaṁ bahudhā dṛśyamānam*

**The one form is seen as many. (Brhad-aranyaka Upanisad 4.4.19)**

Not giving up oneness, he has various forms. He is the shelter of Laksmi, who serves his feet (prapanna-sri-nivdsah). By his birth (janita), great amounts of bliss (paramananda-garimd) manifested. He gave mercy to Gajendra (gajapatih). The rest of the meaning is clear. There is an arrangement for double meaning of the words.

### Text 4

*rasoddāmā kāmārbuda-madhura-dhāmojjvala-tanur*  
*yatīnām uttaṁsas taraṇi-kara-vidyoti-vasanaḥ*  
*hiraṇyānāṁ lakṣmī-bharam abhibhavann āṅgika-rucā*  
*sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When will Caitanya, ornament of the sannyasis, impassioned by the taste of bhakti’s joy, whose body shines from the sweet influence of a million Cupids, whose cloth shines like the morning sun, whose bodily complexion derides the intense beauty of gold, appear before my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

Caitanya was impassioned (uddama) by the tastes of happiness from bhakti (rasair). Rasa means flavor or taste according to Visva. He has a body bright with the enchanting or tasty (madhura) influence (dhama) of millions of Cupids.

Madhura means a taste, the opposite of poison. It is tnadhuratn in the neuter also. Madhura, rasavat and svadu are synonyms according to the writer of Visvalocana.

Dhama means body, house, ray, place, birth and influence according to Visva.

This means he has a most enchanting form. He is the ornament (uttarhsaK) of the sannyasis (yatinam). He has cloth which shines like the rays of the morning sun (tarani-kara). This means his cloth is dyed orange. He defeats (abhibhavan) intense beauty (laksmt-bharam) of gold by his bodily complexion (angika-ruca). Ruci means beautiful appearance, light, complexion, flashing and shining according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 5

*hare kṛṣṇety uccaiḥ sphurita-rasano nāma-gaṇanā-*  
*kṛta-granthi-śreṇī-subhaga-kaṭi-sūtrojjvala-karaḥ*  
*viśālākṣo dīrghārgala-yugala-khelāñcita-bhujaḥ*  
*sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When will Caitanya, on whose tongue dance loudly the words “Hare Krsna,” whose shining left hand holds a beautiful thread tied around his waist and knotted in order to count his japa, who has wide eyes and arms beautiful as iron bars, appear before my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

His tongue (rasandh) danced (sphuritd) by uttering the thirty-two syllables made of sixteen names. His left hand shone with a beautiful (subhagd) thread tied with knots around his waist (kati-siitra) for counting his utterance of names. His eye spread to his ears (visaldksah). He has arms endowed with the beauty of two long door bolts. This means that his arms extend to his knees. Argala means a door bolt according to Halayudha. The alankara is nidarsana (example).

### Text 6

*payorāśes tīre sphurad-upavanālī-kalanayā*  
*muhur vṛndāraṇya-smaraṇa-janita-prema-vivaśaḥ*  
*kvacit kṛṣṇāvṛtti-pracala-rasano-bhakti-rasikaḥ*  
*sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Will Caitanya, tasting bhakti-rasa, his tongue restless with repeating Krsna’s name, overwhelmed with prema arising from constantly remembering Vrndavana on seeing the trembling groves on the ocean’s shore, again appear before my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

He was unsteady because of remembering Vrndavana constantly by seeing the groups of trembling gardens on the shore of the ocean (payoraseh). His tongue was quivering by repeatedly chanting Krsna’s name at some place since he was a taster of bhakti-rasa.

### Text 7

*rathārūḍhasyārād adhipadavi nīlācala-pater*  
*adabhra-premormi-sphurita-naṭanollāsa-vivaśaḥ*  
*sa-harṣaṁ gāyadbhiḥ parivṛta-tanur vaiṣṇava-janaiḥ*  
*sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Will Caitanya, overwhelmed with joyful dancing, which manifested towering waves of prema on the path near the chariot of Jagannatha, while his body was surrounded by joyfully singing devotees, again appear before my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

Caitanya was overwhelmed by intensely dancing (natanollasa), which manifested with huge (adabhra) waves of prema on the path (adhipadavi) near (ardt) the chariot of Jagannatha. Adhipadavi an indeclinable compound used as an inflected word. Ardt can mean both near and far according to Amara-kosa. Adabhra means “many” according to Halayudha. The rest of the verse is clear.

### Text 8

*bhuvaṁ siñcann aśru-śrutibhir abhitaḥ sāndra-pulakaiḥ*  
*parītāṅgo nīpa-stabaka-nava-kiñjalka-jayibhiḥ*  
*ghana-sveda-stoma-stimita-tanur utkīrtana-sukhī*  
*sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Will Caitanya, joyful with kirtana, sprinkling the ground everywhere with streams of tears, his hairs standing on end all over his body, thus defeating new filaments of kadamba clusters, whose body was damp with profuse perspiration, again appear before my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

Sprinkling the ground everywhere with streams of tears (asru-Srutibhih), his bodily hairs stood intensely on end. His hairs standing on end is described. They conquered fresh stamens on kadamba clusters (nipa-stavaka). Nlpa means kadamba according to Amara-kosa. Stavaka is a cluster. Kinjalka means filaments or stamens. His body was damp with profuse perspiration.

### Text 9

*adhīte gaurāṅga-smaraṇa-padavī-maṅgalataraṁ*  
*kṛtī yo viśrambha-sphurad-amala-dhīr aṣṭakam idam*  
*parānande sadyas tad-amala-padāmbhoja-yugale*  
*parisphārā tasya sphuratu nitarāṁ prema-laharī \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May great waves of prema for the most blissful, pure lotus feet of Caitanya immediately and constantly manifest for the person of pure intelligence bright with faith who recites this astaka, auspicious as a means of attaining Gauranga.**

**Комментарий:**

He describes the result of reciting the astaka. May waves of prema for the Lord’s pure lotus feet, manifest for the learned person (krti) who recites this astaka concerning Caitanya-deva. This is a bestowal of blessing on the reader. The astaka is described. It is most auspicious as a path to meditation on Gauranga. The learned person is described. He has pure intelligence shining with faith (yisrambha). Visrambha means trust, intimacy and playful dealings according to MedinL Parisphara means broad.

The meter of this and the next astaka is in sikharini.

*rasai rudaiś chinnā yamanasabhalāgaḥ śikhariṇī*

**With caesuras at sixth (rasa) and eleventh (rudra) syllables, sll 111 sss ssl Iss si (ya, ma, na, sa, bha, la, gu) constitutes sikharini.**

The ganas in meter should be understood.

*sarvagururmaḥ kathito bhajasā gurvādimadhyāntāḥ \|*  
*chandasi naḥ sarvalaghuryaratā laghvādimadhyāntāḥ \|\| iti \|*

**Lil is ma. In bha, ja and sa the long syllable is at the beginning, middle and end (Iss, sis, ssl). Na is sss. Ya is sll, ra is Isl and ta is Ils.**

These are ganas in varna meters.

The ganas in matra meters are described as follows:

*jñeyāḥ sarvādimadhyāttaguravo'tra catuṣkalāḥ \|*  
*gaṇāścaturlaghūpetāḥ pañcāryādiṣu saṁsthitāḥ \|\|*

**The four kalas are understood to be all long syllables (111), a long syllable at the beginning (Iss), middle (sis) and end (ssl) and four shorts syllables (sss). These five are established in arya and other meters.**

Thus, the first astaka on Caitanya has been explained.

## dvitīyaṁ caitanyāṣṭakam

### Text 1

*kalau yaṁ vidvāṁsaḥ sphuṭam abhiyajante dyuti-bharād*  
*akṛṣṇaṁ kṛṣṇāṅgaṁ makha-vidhibhir utkīrtanamayaiḥ \|*  
*upāsyaṁ ca prāhur yam akhila-caturthāśrama-juṣāṁ*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the form of Caitanya, worshipped by all, whom the wise worship directly as Krsna with a golden complexion, by the devotional yajna of sankirtana and whom they describe as worthy of worship among all sannyasis, be most merciful to us.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to Caitanya. In the second astaka Caitanya is described as going from Puri and coming to Bengal to see his mother.

May that form of Caitanya be merciful to us. Caitanyakrtih means a spiritual form (caitanya). Medinl says that the word akrti in the feminine means an ordinary body by itself. Or caitanyakrtih means the form named Caitanya, the son of Saci. He is worshipped by all (devah) and desires to conquer the pasandis. Who is he?

The wise in Kali-yuga worship him directly (sphutam) by the yajnas of bhakti (makha-vidhibhih) predominated by sankirtana (utklrtana-mayaih). The wise are those who understand the true meaning of the verse krsna-varnam tvisdkrsnam (SB 11.5.32).

He is described. He has a black, sapphire hued body (krsnangam) and because of his effulgence (tvisa) has a golden form. It is said krsna-varnam tvisakrsnam in Bhagavatam. Though this could refer to any pale complexion, in the Tenth Canto in Garga’s statement, the word pita is clearly used in describing the Lord in Kali-yuga. Thus akrsnam means pita (golden).

*āsanvarṇāśrayo hāsya gṛhato'nuyugaṁ tanuḥ \|*  
*śuklo raktastathā pīta idānīṁ kṛṣṇatāṁ gataḥ \|\|*

**Your son Krsna appeared in previous yugas (according to the avatara he worshipped) with three different colors— white, red and yellow—and now he has appeared in a blackish color. (SB 10.8.13)**

Wise persons like Bhisma say that he is worthy of worship among all sannydsis. He describes the king of sannydsis with the words:

*saṁnyāsakṛcchramaḥ śānto niṣṭhā śāntiḥ parāyaṇam*

**He takes sannydsa. He reflected on the confidential pastimes of the Lord (samuh). He was detached from everything except Krsna (sdntah). He was fixed in the sacrifice of chanting the Lord’s names (nistha). He pacified the advaitins who were against bhakti by performing kirtana (sdntah). He was the highest refuge for person of various bhavas, up to mahabhava (parayanam).**

### Text 2

*caritraṁ tanvānaḥ priyam aghavadāhlādana-padaṁ*  
*jayodghoṣaiḥ samyag-viracita-śacī-śoka-haraṇaḥ \|*  
*udañcan-mārtaṇḍa-dyuti-hara-dukūlāñcita-kaṭiḥ*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the form of Caitanya, who displays an affectionate nature, who gives bliss to the sinful, who is worthy of worship, who removed Saci’s lamentation with shouts of victory, who wore a reddish cloth on his waist that defeated the brilliance of the rising sun, be merciful to us.**

**Комментарий:**

He displays (tanvanah) affectionate nature (priyam caritram) -spreading kirtana at the houses of all devotees and on the road in Santipura. His nature is further described. He gave bliss to the sinful who should have suffered. He is the deliverer of the most fallen.

He is most worshippable (devah). That is further described. By loudly shouting “Victory to Krsna, deliverer of the fallen,” he removed the lamentation of his mother Saci, who was suffering from his separation. He wore a reddish cloth on his waist that defeated the brilliance of the rising sun.

There is another meaning. Vamana appeared in order to carry out actions for Indra. He displayed actions of cheating and tying up Bali. He arranged for the bliss of dear Indra (priya-maghavad-ahladana-padam) since Indra was his elder brother and his devotee. When Bali was bound up, he removed the lamentation of Indra’s wife Saci by proclaiming victory for the devatas. The rest of the verse has the same meaning.

### Text 3

*apāraṁ kasyāpi praṇayi-jana-vṛndasya kutukī*  
*rasa-stomaṁ hṛtvā madhuram upabhoktuṁ kam api yaḥ \|*  
*ruciṁ svām āvavre dyutim iha tadīyāṁ prakaṭayan*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|3\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

May the form of Caitanya, who, stealing the inconceivable, abundant madhurya-rasa of the gopis to taste that mood, covered his complexion and manifested their complexion, be merciful to us.

“The yugavatara of the fourthyuga is black as previously stated in krte suklo dharma-miirtih. Why should Caitanya the yugavatara be golden?” That is explained in this verse.

Stealing the abundant inconceivable (kam) madhura-rasa (also called srngara-rasa) of one (kasya) group of gopis (pranayi-jana-vrndasya), an affectionate group of devotees, in order to taste personally by that mood, he covered (avavre) his own complexion (svam rucim) and manifested the complexion (dyutim) of that group (tadiyam). A thief will hide his form and steal. That is well known. Sruti also indicates this.

*yadāpaśyaḥ paśyati rukmavarṇaṁ*  
*kartāramīśaṁ puruṣaṁ brahmayonim \|*  
*tada vidvan punya pope vidhuya*  
*niranjandh paramam samyam upaiti \|\|*

**When the seer sees the Lord of resplendent complexion, who is the creator of the world, the ruler of the world, and who is the material cause, that learned person is free of all sin and piety, and being pure, attains a form similar to the Lord’s. (Mundaka Upanisad 3.1.2)**

Why did he do this? He was eager to taste the gopis’ bhava (kutuki). Halayudha says that kutuki (kutuhala) means eagerness or curiosity.

Even though smrtis say that the Kali-yuga avatara is black, at the junction of Kali-yuga in the twenty-eighth yuga cycle of Vaivasvata Manvantara, Svayam Bhagavan Krsna appeared, covering his own complexion and mood by the complexion and mood of his beloved Radha. This should be accepted. This is understood from krsnavarnam (SB 11.5.32), asan varnas trayah (SB 10.8.13), etc., and from the statement of Prahlada in the Seventh Canto:

*chinnaḥ kalau yad abhavan triyugo'tha sat tvam*

**Since you will appear covered in Kali-yuga, you are called Tri-yuga. (SB 7.9.38)**

### Text 4

*anārādhyaḥ prītyā ciram asura-bhāva-praṇayināṁ*  
*prapannānāṁ daivīṁ prakṛtim adhidaivaṁ trijagati \|*  
*ajasraṁ yaḥ śrīmāñ jayati sahajānanda-madhuraḥ*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the form of Caitanya, who is not accepted as the Lord by persons of demonic nature, but who is accepted as such by those of devotional nature in the three worlds, who, as the husband of Laksmi remains ever victorious, filled with natural blissful sweetness, be merciful to us.**

**Комментарий:**

“Though Caitanya was defined as being directly the Lord, why did some of the local brahmanas^f various places not accept him, though they were favorable .to his taking sannyasa?”

He was not accepted as/ihe direct Lord (anaradhyah) with affection for a long time by persons of demonic nature (asura-bhava-pranayinam), who worshipped tamasic devatas. But he was worshipped as the Lord (adhidaivarri) by those who were endowed with spiritual nature (daivim prakrtim). He remains victorious at all times (ajasram). He was accepted as the Lord by many residents of sattvika nature in the three worlds (trigate), not just in the single bhil-mandala. He was the husband of Laksmi.

*dvī bhūtasargau loke'smin daiva āsura eva ca \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktiparo daiva āsurastadviparyayaḥ \|\|*

**There are two types of created beings in this world—the divine and demonic. Those having bhakti to Visnu are the divine and those who are opposite are the demonic. (Visnu-dharma)**

There is no harm if some do not accept Caitanya’s real nature.

### Text 5

*gatir yaḥ pauṇḍrāṇāṁ prakaṭita-navadvīpa-mahimā*  
*bhavenālaṁkurvan bhuvana-mahitaṁ śrotriya-kulam \|*  
*punāty aṅgīkārād bhuvi paramahaṁsāśrama-padaṁ*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the form of Caitanya, most worshipable, who delivered the people of Pundra, who revealed the glories of Navadvipa, who ornamented a brahmana family, celebrated on earth by his birth, and who purified the sannyasa asrama by accepting its symbols, be merciful to us.**

**Комментарий:**

South of Navadvipa at the edge of Kullna-grama is a place called Pundra. The people living there are called paundras. Most worshippable (devah), he was the deliverer, the means and goal (gatih) of the inhabitants of Pundra. All those residents worshipped him directly as the Lord. He is further described. He manifested the glories of Navadvipa in its true nature, though it was already ornamented with Gahga-devI and groups of scholars. It is worshipped as a special manifestation of Vrndavana by those who know the truth. He ornamented the family of Vedic brahmanas by his birth (bhavena). He purified the sannyasa asrama by accepting its symbols. He had no goal for himself in accepting sannyasa. He purified it by honoring bhakti.

### Text 6

*mukhenāgre pītvā madhuram iha nāmāmṛta-rasaṁ*  
*dṛśor dvārā yas taṁ vamati ghana-bāṣpāmbu-miṣataḥ \|*  
*bhuvi premṇas tattvaṁ prakaṭayitum ullāsita-tanuḥ*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the form of Caitanya, most worshippable, of joyful body, who, having drunk with his mouth the sweet rasa of the name, vomited it through his eyes on the pretext of profuse tears in order to reveal the tattva of prema to the world, be merciful to us.**

**Комментарий:**

Caitanya’s mood is now described in detail. Having first drunk the sweet rasa of the name by his mouth, he vomited that rasa through his eyes on the pretext of profuse tears. Why? In order to make understand (prakatayitum) the svarUpa (tattvam) of prema on earth. Tattvam means musical instrument, svarupa or the Lord according to Visva. He made it understood that hlrtana of the holy names of the Lord would transform into prema.

The word vomit should not be taken as vulgar, since one does not accept it as vulgar in its secondary meaning. It is apahnuti alankara. In the act of drinking the sweet rasa of the name, tears are denied and made similar to the drinking of nectar. Apanhuti means using a simile in other than its true application.

### Text 7

*tanūm āviṣkurvan nava-puraṭa-bhāsaṁ kaṭi-lasat-*  
*karaṅkālaṅkāras taruṇa-gaja-rājāñcita-gatiḥ \|*  
*priyebhyo yaḥ śikṣāṁ diśati nija-nirmālya-rucibhiḥ*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the form of Caitanya, most worshippable, showing his form of molten gold, decorated with a coconut shell water pot shining at his waist, walking like the king of young elephants, and teaching his devotees by respecting the Lord’s garlands, be merciful to us.**

**Комментарий:**

Caitanya is described as he went on pilgrimage.

He showed a form whose complexion was that of newly smelted gold (nava-puratd). His mercy is indicated since he shows everyone his form when he travelled on the road. He had a water pot made of coconut shell (karahka') shining on his waist. Karanka means coconut according to Haima. He taught his devotees by appreciating (rucibhih) the prasada garlands of the Lord. He taught them to respect the garlands.

### Text 8

*smitālokaḥ śokaṁ harati jagatāṁ yasya parito*  
*girāṁ tu prārambhaḥ kuśala-paṭalīṁ pallavayati \|*  
*padālambaḥ kaṁ vā praṇayati nahi prema-nivahaṁ*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the form of Caitanya, most worshippable, whose smiling glance destroys the lamentation of all people of the world, whose words spread all auspiciousness and whose feet, accepted as a shelter, produce abundant prema for all, be merciful to us.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse describes that he was the cause of all auspiciousness.

His glance of mercy while smiling removes lamentation of the living beings in this world (jagatam). Just by beginning to speak, he spreads all auspiciousness (kusala-patalim). Taking shelter of his feet will deliver abundant prema to all.

### Text 9

*smitālokaḥ śokaṁ harati jagatāṁ yasya parito*  
*girāṁ tu prārambhaḥ kuśala-paṭalīṁ pallavayati \|*  
*padālambaḥ kaṁ vā praṇayati nahi prema-nivahaṁ*  
*sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May possessor of Laksmi, the son of Saci, who gives affection to his lotus feet, bring happiness at all times to the person who, with affectionate heart, recites this as taka, which is filled with the fresh fragrance of flower clusters glorifying Caitanya.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of reciting this astaka is described.

May the son of Saci, possessor of Laksmi, giving affection (pranayitam) to his lotus feet, bring happiness at all times (anupadam) to the person who recites this astaka concerning Caitanya.

## tṛtīyaṁ caitanyāṣṭakam

### Text 1

*upāsita-padāmbujas tvam anurakta-rudrādibhiḥ*  
*prapadya puruṣottamaṁ padam adabhram udbhrājitaḥ \|*  
*samasta-nata-maṇḍalī-sphurad-abhīṣṭa-kalpa-drumaḥ*  
*śacī-suta mayi prabho kuru mukunda mande kṛpām \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О son of Saci! О master! О Mukunda! О Lord whose lotus feet are worshipped by Siva and others with affection, who shine profusely on attaining the place called Puri, who manifests as a desire tree cherished by all the devotees, give mercy to me, this fool.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to Caitanya-candra. Seeing Caitanya shining in Puri, he praises him. О son of Saci! О master! О Mukunda! О Lord, whose lotus feet are worshipped by Siva and others with affection, who shines profusely attaining the place called Puri! Give mercy to me, this fool (mande).

The Lord is then described. Your lotus feet are worshipped by Siva and others situated as Advaitacarya and others, who are attracted to him.

Attaining the ksetra of Puri, you shine excellently (adabhram). Or attaining the form of Jagannatha, appearing in that manner you shine, or appear beautiful (udbhrajitah).

Nata-mandall means all his devotees. Mandali means a group according to Medinikara.

### Text 2

*nu varṇayitum īśate gurutarāvatārāyitā*  
*bhavantam uru-buddhayo na khalu sārvabhaumādayaḥ \|*  
*paro bhavatu tatra kaḥ paṭur ato namas te paraṁ*  
*śacī-suta mayi prabho kuru mukunda mande kṛpām \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О son of Saci! О master! О Mukunda! Sarvabhauma and others, acting as gurus of all sages and avataras, most intelligent, cannot describe you. What other person is skillful? All I can do is offer respects to you. Give mercy to me, this fool.**

**Комментарий:**

The author expresses his inability to praise Caitanya. О son of Sacl! Sarvabhauma and others are not capable of describing you. They are described.

They are gurus of all sages (gurutara) and avataras such as Dattatreya, and Vyasa. They conduct themselves like gurus and avataras (gurutaravatarayita). The suffix ayita indicates they acted in this manner. They had very fine intelligence. Still, they cannot describe Caitanya. What other person (parah) is skillful (patuh)l No one is skillful. I, being devoid of intelligence, can only (param) offer respects to you. And I have no impetus to describe you.

### Text 3

*na yat katham api śrutāv upaniṣadbhir apy āhitaṁ*  
*svayaṁ ca vivṛtaṁ na yad gurutarāvatārāntare \|*  
*kṣipann asi rasāmbudhe tad iha bhākta-ratnaṁ kṣitau*  
*śacī-suta mayi prabho kuru mukunda mande kṛpām \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О son of Saci! О master! О Mukunda! О ocean of rasa! You scatter on earth the jewel of bhakti, which was not offered by the Upanisads, heads of the Vedas, and which was not uncovered when gurus among sages and avataras appeared. Give mercy to me, this fool.**

**Комментарий:**

“Why are such people incapable of describing him?” This verse answers.

That jewel of bhakti was not offered (ahitam) by any means in order to reveal the svarupa of bhakti, by the Upanisads, the head of the Vedas (srutau). This means the Upanisads did not describe bhakti.

*tā hi śraddhā-bhakti-dhyāna-yogād avaiti*

**One meets the Lord by faith, bhakti and meditation. (Kaivalya Upanisad 2)**

*yasya deve parā bhaktir yathā deve tathā gurau \|*  
*tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ \|\|*

**To the great soul who has great bhakti for the Lord and guru, the meanings of what was spoken are revealed. (Svetasvatara Upanisad 6.23)**

*bhaktir asya bhajanam*

**Bhakti to Krsna is bhajana. (Gopala Tapani Upanisad)**

The Upanisads establish bhakti in a contracted manner. The jewel of bhakti was not revealed by Svayam Bhagavan Krsna when Dattatreya, Vyasa and others acting as great avataras appeared. It can however be obtained by uncovering pure bhakti deep within the statements of karma, yoga and the shadow of Advaita. You seem to throw the svarUpa of bhakti, like pile of wealth, on the earth. Distributing the jewels of bhakti hidden by the Vedas and by the Lord indicates Caitanya’s great generosity. This is impossible for all others.

It is said:

*ka sā niraṅkuśa-kṛpā kva tad-vaibhavam adbhutam \|*  
*kva sā vatsalatā śaure yādṛg-gaure tavātmani \|\|*

**О Krsna! Where is your unrestrained mercy? Where is your astonishing power? Where is your affection? Where are all these, to the extent that they are present in your form as Gauratiga? (Prabodhananda Sarasvati, Caitanya-candramrta)**

### Text 4

*nija-praṇaya-visphuran-naṭana-raṅga-vismāpita*  
*trinetra-nata-maṇḍala-prakaṭitānurāgāmṛta \|*  
*ahaṅkṛti-kalaṅkitoddhata-janādi-durbodha he*  
*śacī-suta mayi prabho kuru mukunda mande kṛpām \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Lord who astonishes Siva by knowledge of dancing manifested out of affection for Krsna! О Lord, who revealed the sweetness of devotion among all the devotees! О Lord who cannot be understood by vain persons contaminated with pride! О son of Saci! О master! О Mukunda! Give mercy to me, this fool.**

**Комментарий:**

He addresses the Lord with three statements. О Caitanya who astonished Siva (trinetra) by astonishing knowledge (rahga) of dancing, which manifested when overwhelmed with bhava for Krsna (nija-pranaya). He astonished Advaitacarya. Rahga means astonishing knowledge according to Visva. О Lord, who cannot be understood by vain people contaminated with pride in birth or learning. Kalahkita means spoiled according to Amara-kosa.

*ahaṁkāraviyuktānāṁ keśavo na hi dūragaḥ \|*  
*ahaṁkārayutānāṁ tu madhye parvatakoṭayaḥ \|\|*

**Kesava does not go far from those devoid of pride. There are millions of mountains between him and those affected by pride. (Brahma-vaivarta Purana)**

The rest is clear.

### Text 5

*bhavanti bhuvi ye narāḥ kalita-duṣkulotpattayas*  
*tvam uddharasi tān api pracura-cāru-kāruṇyataḥ \|*  
*iti pramuditāntaraḥ śaraṇam āśritas tvām ahaṁ*  
*śacī-suta mayi prabho kuru mukunda mande kṛpām \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You deliver even the persons who are born in low families on earth because of your great attractive mercy. Thus, joyful in heart, I have taken shelter of you. О son of Sacl! О master! О Mukunda! Give mercy to me, this fool.**

**Комментарий:**

“How can 1 show mercy to you, a fool?”

You deliver most sinful persons who are born in bad families on earth. Because they are born in degraded families, they commit sins. This reason is given. It is because of your great, attractive (caru) mercy. Because of this, I, with joyful heart, have attained your shelter. Thus, even I can be delivered.

### Text 6

*mukhāmbuja-pariskhalan-mṛdula-vāṅ-madhūlī-rasa-*  
*prasaṅga-janitākhila-praṇata-bhṛṅga-raṅgotkara \|*  
*samasta-jana-maṅgala-prabhava-nāma-ratnāmbudhe*  
*śacī-suta mayi prabho kuru mukunda mande kṛpām \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Lord who greatly astonishes the devotee bees who are deeply attached to the flowing honey of your soft sweet words trickling from your lotus mouth. О ocean of jewels in the form of the names which causes all types of auspiciousness for people. О son of Sacl! О master! О Mukunda! Give mercy to me, this fool.**

**Комментарий:**

He calls out to the Lord with two statements.

О Lord who greatly astonishes the devotee (pranata) bees (bhrga) who are deeply attached (prasanga') to the flowing honey (madhuli) of your soft sweet words trickling (pariskhalat) from your lotus mouth. О ocean of jewels in the form of the names which causes (prabhdva) all types of auspiciousness for people.

### Text 7

*mṛgāṅka-madhurānana sphurad-anidra-padmekṣaṇa*  
*smita-stavaka-sundarādhara viśaṅkaṭoras-taṭa \|*  
*bhujoddhata-bhujaṅgama-prabha manoja-koṭi-dyute*  
*śacī-suta mayi prabho kuru mukunda mande kṛpām \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Lord, having a face attractive because of effulgence and joy. О Lord with eyes like shining, blossoming lotuses! О Lord with beautiful lips like flower clusters of gentle smiles! О Lord with a broad chest! О Lord with upraised arms like effulgent snakes! О Lord with the splendor of millions of Cupids! О son of Saci! О master! О Mukunda! Give mercy to me, this fool.**

**Комментарий:**

He calls out, describing the Lord’s form. О Lord having a face attractive because of effulgence and joy (madhuram). О Lord with eyes like shining (sphurat), blossoming (anidra) lotuses! О Lord with beautiful lips like flower clusters (stavaka) of gentle smiles. О Lord with a broad (visankata) chest! Visankata means broad according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 8

*ahaṁ kanaka-ketakī-kusuma-gaura duṣṭaḥ kṣitau*  
*na doṣa-lava-darśitā vividha-doṣa-pūrṇe’pi te \|*  
*ataḥ pravaṇayā dhiyā kṛpaṇa-vatsala tvāṁ bhaje*  
*śacī-suta mayi prabho kuru mukunda mande kṛpām \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Lord, golden as a kanaka-ketaki flower! I am the most wicked on earth. But you do not see any fault in a person though he may be filled with all faults. Thus, I worship you with humble intelligence. О Lord affectionate to the miserable! О son of Saci! О master! О Mukunda! Give mercy to me, this fool.**

**Комментарий:**

Though most sinful, I have a joyful heart, thinking myself successful on seeing your nature. О Lord, golden like a kanaka-ketaki flower! I am the most wicked on earth, afflicted by lust and anger. You do not see any fault at all, though a person may be full of various faults. I worship you with humbled intelligence (pravanaya dhiya) because I believe you have a relationship with me because of your generosity, since you are the deliverer. О Lord affectionate to the most miserable! Be merciful to me, a fool.

### Text 9

*idaṁ dharaṇi-maṇḍalotsava bhavat-padāṅkeṣu ye*  
*niviṣṭa-manaso narāḥ paripaṭhanti padyāṣṭakam \|*  
*śacī-hṛdaya-nandana prakaṭa-kīrti-candra prabho*  
*nija-praṇaya-nirbharaṁ vitara deva tebhyaḥ śubham \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O joy to the earth! O joy to the heart of Saci! O moon of great fame! O master! Bestow to those persons who, absorbed in the marks on your feet, recite this astaka, a wealth of your prema, most auspicious.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of reciting this astaka is described. O joy to the earth! O joy to the heart of Saci! O moon of great fame! O master! Bestow to those persons who, absorbed in the marks on your feet (padarikesu), recite this astaka, a wealth of your prema (nija-pranaya-nirbharam), most auspicious (subham). The astaka is in prthvi meter.

*jasau jasayalā vasu-graha-yatis tu pṛthvī guruḥ*

**sls ssl sls ssl sll s l (ja, sa, ja, sa, ya, la, gu), with caesura after the eighth syllable and nine syllables following.**

Thus, the third astaka on Caitanya has been explained.

## ānanda-stotram

**śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ**

**I offer respects to Sri Krsna**

### Text 1

*śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ paramānando govindo nanda-nandanaḥ \|*  
*tamāla-śyāmala-ruciḥ śikhaṇḍa-kṛta-śekharaḥ \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna is the highest bliss, the king of the cows, Govinda, and the son of Nanda. He has the complexion of a dark tamala tree and wears a peacock feather on his head.**

**Комментарий:**

Therefore, Krsna is the supreme being. One should meditate on him. (Gopala-tapanl Upanisad)

*krsnastu bhagavan svayam*

**Krsna is Bhagavan svayam (SB 1.3.28)**

*mattah parataram nanyat*

**There is no one superior to me. (BG 7.7)**

Sri Krsna is mentioned because this is the chief of all names. The Lord says:

*nāmnāṁ mukhyataraṁ nāma kṛṣṇākhyaṁ me parantapa*

**О conqueror, the chief of all my names is that of Krsna. (Prabhasa-khanda)**

The word Krsna is used to indicate his eternally blissful state.

*kṛṣir bhū-vācakaḥ śabdo ṇaś ca nirvṛti-vācakaḥ \|*  
*tayor aikyaṁ paraṁ brahmā kṛṣṇa ityabhidhīyate \|\|*

**Krsi means “existence” and na means “bliss.” Combined together, the two roots indicate that Krsna is the supreme form of God.**

Sometimes Krsna indicates his dark complexion.

*kṛṣṇo varṇaś ca me yasmāt tasmāt kṛṣṇo'ham arjuna*

**Since I am black in complexion, I am called Krsna, О Arjuna. (Mahabharata 12.330.14)**

He is supreme and blissful (paramanandah). Sruti says vijnanam anandam brahma: the supreme Brahman is knowledge and bliss. (Brhad-aranyaka Upanisad 3.9.28)

Or he is the highest bliss since he is similarly composed of all knowledge and is all-pervading, or he is the very form of bliss. One must accept that he is the very form of bliss since he has inconceivable nature, just as he is the very form of raga, and since he is described as such in sruti. He is the king of the cows, Govinda. Sukadeva says priyan na indro gavam: May Govinda, the Lord of the cows be pleased. (SB 10.26.25) He is Nanda-nandana (son of Nanda) because he was born from Nanda in Yasoda’s womb. Nandana means a son according to Dhananjaya. Later it will be said:

*yaśodā khani-māṇikyam*

**He is the ruby in the mine of Yasoda.**

“Krsna cannot be the son of Yasoda because in the Tenth Canto the clear meaning contradicts that.” That is not so.

*niśīthe tama udbhūte jāyamāne janārdane \|*  
*devakyāṁ deva-rūpiṇyāṁ viṣṇuḥ sarva-guhāśayaḥ \|*  
*āvirāsīd yathā prācyāṁ diśīnduriva puṣkalaḥ \|\|*

**Then the Supreme Lord Visnu, who is situated in the core of everyone’s heart, appeared from the heart of Devaki in the dense darkness of night, like the full moon rising on the eastern horizon, because Devaki was of the same category as Sri Krsna. (SB 10.3.8)**

Here Sukadeva says that Krsna was born from Yasoda since Devaki is another name of Yasoda.

*dvināmnī nandabhāryā yā yaśodā devakīti ca \|*  
*ataḥ sakhyamabhūttasyā devakyā śaurijāyayā \|\|*

**“The wife of Nanda had two names, Yasoda and Devaki. Therefore, it was natural that she \[the wife of Nanda\] developed friendship with Devaki, the wife of Sauri \[Vasudeva\].” (Brhad-visnu Purana)**

The meaning is that the word Devaki means both Devaki and Yasoda according to dehali-pradlpa-nyaya.

Therefore, in middle of the night spread with the darkness while Krsna was born in Yasoda, he also appeared in Devaki, wife of Vasudeva. He was born simultaneously to both mothers.

*garbhakāle tvasaṁpūrṇe aṣṭame māsi te striyau \|*  
*devakī ca yaśodā ca suṣuvāte rāmaṁ tadā \|\|*

**Without the pregnancy period being completed, in the eighth month Devaki and Yasoda gave birth at the same time. (Hari-vamsa)**

After that, Durga was bom to Yasoda. Sukadeva says:

*tataśca śaurirbhagavatpracoditaḥ sutaṁ samādāya sa sūtikāgṛhāt \|*  
*yadā bahirgantumiyeṣa garhyajā yā yogamāyājani nandajāyayā \|\|*

**Thereafter, exactly when Vasudeva, being inspired by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, was about to take the newborn child from the delivery room, Yogamaya, the Lord’s spiritual energy, took birth as the daughter of the wife of Maharaja Nanda. (SB 10.3.47)**

Thus, Yasoda bore two children, one after the other, a son and a daughter. Neither Vasudeva nor Yasoda saw both children. Thus, the fault of Krsna being born only in Devaki’s womb is destroyed.

*yaśodā nandapatnī ca jātaṁ paramabudhyata \|*  
*na tadveda pariśrāntā nidyāpagatasmṛtiḥ \|\|*

**Exhausted by the labor of childbirth, Yasoda was overwhelmed with sleep and unable to understand what kind of child had been born to her. (SB 10.3.53)**

Thus, Krsna was born to Yasoda. According to another version, both Devaki and Yasoda understood that the Supreme Lord had been born from their wombs. They were unaware of the signs that Vasudeva came, etc. Another Purana says that Krsna was born to both.

*nandagopagṛhe jāto yaśodāgarbhasaṁbhavaḥ*

**Krsna was born in the house of Nanda and from the womb of Yasoda.**

Thus, it is proper to say that Nanda gave birth to a son and his sister was Durga (SB 10.4.9).

There is no fear of taking a secondary meaning of the words as in the case of the statement upaguhyatmajam: Devaki hugged her daughter (Durga). (The female child was not her daughter. (SB 10.4.7) Since this Krsna is one with Vasudeva (son of Vasudeva), there is no doubt about the clear meaning (Krsna is the son of Nanda), in his going to Mathura (as Vasudeva’s son) and later his return to Vraja (as Nanda’s son). Thus, Krsna is Yasoda’s son. The rest of the verse is clear in meaning.

### Text 2

*pīta-kauśeya-vasano madhura-smita-śobhitaḥ \|*  
*kandarpa-koṭi-lāvaṇyo vṛndāraṇya-mahotsavaḥ \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He wears yellow cloth the color of lightning. He is decorated with a sweet smile. He has beauty greater than a million Cupids. He has a great festival in Vrndavana.**

### Text 3

*vaijayantī-sphurad-vakṣāḥ kakṣātta-laguḍottamaḥ \|*  
*kuñjārpitaratir guñjā-puñja-mañjula-kaṇṭhakaḥ \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His chest shines with a vaijayanti garland. He carries a stick under his arm. He delights in the bowers. He wears a gunja berry necklace around his neck.**

**Комментарий:**

He shines with a garland of flowers of five colors (vaijayanti) on his chest. He carries a fine stick under his armpit. Kaksa is the armpit according to Amara-kosa. Laguda is stick according to Haima. He delights in (ratih) the bowers. On his charming neck is a necklace of gunja berries. A kunja is an area enclosed by trees according to Haima. Gunja is a black and red berry according to Halayudha.

### Text 4

*karṇikārāḍhya-karṇa-śrīr-dhṛta-svarṇābha-varṇakaḥ \|*  
*muralī-vādana-paṭur ballavī-kula-vallabhaḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is beautiful with ears embellished by karnika flowers. He wears gold colored cosmetics. He is skillful at playing the flute. He is beloved of the gopis.**

**Комментарий:**

He is beautiful (srih) with ears decorated with karnika flowers. Karnika is a golden campaka tree according to Halayudha. He wears gold colored cosmetics (varnakah). Varnaka means cosmetic ointments according to Amara-kosa. The rest is clear in meaning.

### Text 5

*karṇikārāḍhya-karṇa-śrīr-dhṛta-svarṇābha-varṇakaḥ \|*  
*muralī-vādana-paṭur ballavī-kula-vallabhaḥ \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He holds a great festival for attaining Radha. He is skillful at dressing Radha. These are the twenty names of Krsna.**

**Комментарий:**

He holds a great festival for attaining (apti) Radha (gandharva) or on attaining Radha. Parva means festival according to Visva. He is skillful (pesalah) at dressing Radha when she acts independently as svadhlna-bhartrka. Pesala means skillful according to Haima.

### Text 6

*ānandākhyaṁ mahā-stotraṁ yaḥ paṭhec chṛṇuyāc ca yaḥ \|*  
*sa paraṁ saukhyam āsādya kṛṣṇa-prema-samanvitaḥ \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The person who recites or hears this great stotra which gives bliss, attains the highest happiness, and becomes filled with krsna-prema.**

**Комментарий:**

This great stotra gives happiness (saukhyam) by reciting it.

### Text 7

*sarva-loka-priyo bhūtvā sad-guṇāvali-bhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*vraja-rāja-kumārasya sannikarṣam avāpnuyāt \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Becoming dear to all people, decorated with a host of good qualities, one attains nearness to the son of Nanda.**

**Комментарий:**

One will become his associate (sannikarsam).

## līlāṁṛta-stotram

līlāmṛtākhyaṁ nāmadaśakam - Ten names called Lilamrta

**śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ**

**I offer respects to Sri Krsna**

### Text 1

*rādhikā-hṛdayonmādi-vaṁśī-kvāṇa-madhu-cchaṭaḥ \|*  
*rādhā-parimalodgāra-garimākṣipta-mānasaḥ \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He continually releases sweet sounds from his flute, which madden Radha’s heart. His mind is attracted to the great outpouring of Radha’s fragrance.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises Krsna with ten names. Parimala means fragrance according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 2

*kamra-rādhā-mano-mīna-vaḍiśīkṛta-vibhramaḥ \|*  
*prema-garbāndha-gāndharvā-kilakiñcita-rañjitaḥ \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His amorous gestures act as a fishhook for the fish of charming Radha’s mind. He is attracted to the kilakincita of Radha who is intoxicated with prema and pride.**

**Комментарий:**

His amorous gestures act as a hook to catch (badisi-krta) the fish-like mind of charming (kamra) Radha. Badisam means a fishhook according to Amara-kosa. Pastimes which are the cause of the greatest bliss become a hook in the heart during separation. There is feeling of great thirst at that time. He is attracted to the kilakincita of Radha, who is intoxicated (andha) with pride and prema.

*garva-smitābhilāṣāder kopādeś ca miśraṇam \|*  
*pramodāt preyasaḥ saṅge kathyate kilakiñcitam \|\|*

**The mixture of pride, smiling, desire, etc., and anger out of joy on meeting the lover is called kilakincita. (Kavya-kaustubha)**

### Text 3

*lalitā-vaśya-dhīrā-dhāmānābhāsa-vaśīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*rādhā-vakrokti-pīyūṣa-mādhurya-bhara-lampaṭaḥ \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is controlled by the shadow of pride of Radha’s intelligence, controlled by her playfulness. He is greedy for the intense sweetness of Radha’s crooked, but sweet words.**

**Комментарий:**

He is controlled by the shadow of pride in Radha whose intelligence is controlled by playfulness. He is greedy (lampatah) for the great sweetness of the nectar of Radha’s crooked words. “What do we have to do with you, the plaything of Candravall, though we are controlled by you?” Hearing those words, he is never satiated.

### Text 4

*mukhendu-candrikodghūrṇa-rādhikā-rāga-sāgaraḥ \|*  
*vṛṣabhānu-sutā-kaṇṭha-hāri-hāra-harin-maṇiḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**By the moonlight of his face he agitates the ocean of Radha’s raga. He is the emerald center jewel on the charming necklace on the neck of Radha.**

**Комментарий:**

By the moonlight of his face he agitates the ocean of Radha’s raga. He is the emerald center jewel on the charming (hari) necklace on the neck of Radha. Harin-mani means an emerald according to Haima. He is worn on her neck like a center jewel.

### Text 5

*phulla-rādhā-kamalinī-mukhāmbuja-madhuvrataḥ \|*  
*rādhikā-kuca-kastūrī-patra-sphurad-uraḥ-sthalaḥ \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is a bee on the darkened lotus mouth of blossoming Radha. His chest shines with the musk from Radha’s breasts because of embracing her.**

**Комментарий:**

He kisses her. He is a bee on the darkened lotus mouth of blossoming Radha. His chest shines with the musk from Radha’s breasts because of embracing. This indicates that they have united. It is not a fault that in the verses Radha’s name is repeated many times since the names can only be completed by referring to her.

### Text 6

*iti gokula-bhūpāla-sūnu-līlā-manoharam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhen nāma-daśakaṁ so’sya vallabhatāṁ vrajet \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He who recites the ten names indicating Krsna’s attractive pastimes will attain the status of a gopi.**

**Комментарий:**

The results of reciting the stotra are described.

The person who recites the ten names will attain (vrajet) the status of a beloved of Krsna (asya). What are these names? They are attractive with five verses describing the pastimes of Krsna with Radha. Asya refers to Krsna (who is mentioned within the compound of the previous line).

*samastasyāsamastena nityākāṇkṣeṇa saṁgatiḥ*

**A word inside a compound can be considered connected with a word outside the compound if their meanings are unavoidably connected by a semantic expectation. (Harinamamrta-vyakarana 6.104)**

## premendu-sāgara-stotram

premendusāgarākhyaṁ śrīkṛṣṇa nāmāṣṭottaraśatam - The ocean of the moon of Prema. A hundred and eight names of Krsna

**śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ**

**I offer respects to Sri Krsna**

### Text 1

*kalahāntaritā-vṛttā kācid ballava-sundarī \|*  
*virahottāpa-khinnāṅgī sakhīṁ sotkaṇṭham abravīt \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**One gopi, in the mood of kalahantarita, her limbs thin from the fire of separation, spoke with longing to a sakhi.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises Krsna by a hundred and eight names. He begins by explaining the method for producing these names.

One gopi, in the mood of kalahantarita (separated from her lover because of a quarrel), with longing, spoke to a sakhi. She is described. She was thin because of separation.

### Text 2

*hanta gauri sa kiṁ gantā panthānaṁ mama netrayoḥ \|*  
*śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ karuṇā-sindhuḥ kṛṣṇo gokula-vallabhaḥ \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Oh! Golden friend! Has he gone from my vision? Krsna is an ocean of mercy. Krsna is the beloved of Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

What did she say?

Oh! This expresses lamentation. О friend! Has he (sah), Krsna, gone from the path of my eyes? The word krsna means the form of knowledge and bliss, as stated in krsir bhu-vacakah sabdah:

the syllable krs indicates existence and the syllable na indicates bliss. He is the lord of all and dear. Will I suddenly see him? Kim indicates a question. Kim indicates a question or something despised according to Haima.

One should not say that the gopls do not know their dear lover in truth. From their words one cannot say that some beings on eating sugar cannot taste the sweetness. In such awareness (expressed in this verse) there is no restriction of their nature, but rather nourishment. He is then described. Since he is merciful, he will accept me, not considering my low nature. The word krsna means he has the complexion of an atasi flower (blue). I am very attached to him.

Since he acts for the benefit of all Vraja he should not remain hidden from me since I am included in the people of Vraja.

### Text 3

*govindaḥ paramānando nanda-mandira-maṅgalam \|*  
*yaśodā-khani-māṇikyaṁ gopendrāmbhodhi-candramāḥ \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is Govinda, the highest bliss, auspiciousness in the house of Nanda, a ruby in the mine of Yasoda, and the moon in the ocean of Nanda.**

**Комментарий:**

What was stated is expanded. In the pastime of lifting Govardhana, he easily defeated Indra who flooded Vraja with rain, and protected Vraja. Indra then bathed him ceremoniously, making him king of the cows (Govinda).

He is the highest and is bliss. This means his body is eternal bliss. One should not say that there is fault of repetition since the word krsna also indicates bliss. There is no fault of repetition of meaning since all names indicate one entity. The commentator on Vaisampayana’s sahasra-nama-stotra explains it in this way.

His is the very form of auspiciousness in Nanda’s house. He is the ruby in the mine of Yasoda. Khani in the feminine means a mine according to Amara-kosa. The comparison is given of a jewel in her womb (the mine). Bhisma also recited the name ratna-garbha. He is like a moon in the ocean of Nanda (gopendrd). He was born from Nanda like the moon is born from the ocean, and gave joy to Nanda as the moon gives joy to the ocean.

### Text 4

*navāmbhodhara-saṁrambha-viḍambi-ruci-ḍambaraḥ \|*  
*kṣipta-hāṭaka-śauṭīrya-paṭṭa-pītāmbarāvṛtaḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His effulgence disregards the fury of a fresh cloud. He wears a yellow cloth that derides the pride of gold.**

**Комментарий:**

He has a great effulgence (nt ci-dambarah) that disregards the anger (samrambha) of a new cloud, since the cloud cannot equal him. He wears a yellow cloth that derides (ksipta) the pride (sautirya) of gold (hataka) in its beauty.

### Text 5

*kandarpa-rūpa-saṁdarpa-hāri-pāda-nakha-dyutiḥ \|*  
*dhvajāmbhoruha-dambholi-yavāṅkuśa-lasat-padaḥ \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The beauty of his toenails destroys Cupid’s pride in his beauty. His feet shine with the marks of the flag, lotus, thunderbolt, barley corn and goad.**

**Комментарий:**

The beauty of his toenails destroys (hari) Cupid’s pride (sandarpa) in his beauty (rupu). Rupa means beauty or splendor according to Visva. The rest is clear. The marks listed represent others as well such as the umbrella.

### Text 6

*pada-pañjara-siñjāna-mañju-mañjīra-khañjanaḥ \|*  
*masāra-saṁpuṭākāra-dhāri jānu-yugojjvalaḥ \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He has charming khanjana bird ankle bells jingling on his cage-like feet. He shines with knees like sapphire caskets.**

**Комментарий:**

He has charming khanjana bird ankle bells jingling on the cages (panjard) of his feet. Manjlra means ankle bell according to Amara-kosa. Kanjana is the wagtail bird. This is the alankara of rupaka. He is bright with knees holding (dhari) a resemblance (akara) of sapphire (masard) caskets (samputd). Akara means a gesture, appearance or expression according to writer of Visvalocana.

### Text 7

*śauṇḍa-stamberamoddaṇḍa-śuṇḍāramyoru-sauṣṭhavaḥ \|*  
*maṇi-kiṅkiṇi-saṁkīrṇa-viśaṅkaṭa-kaṭi-sthalaḥ \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He has attractive thighs beautiful as excellent trunks of drunk elephants. On his broad hips are jeweled bells.**

**Комментарий:**

His attractive thighs have beauty like excellent trunks (sunda) of drunk elephants (saunda-stamberamd). Saunda means drunk. Stamberama is an elephant. Sunda is an elephant trunk according to Haima. He has broad (visankata) hips spread (sahkirna) with jeweled bells. Uru in masculine means thigh. Saustava means praiseworthy according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 8

*madhyamādhurya-vidhvasta-divya-siṁha-madoddhatiḥ \|*  
*gārutmata-giri-grāva-gariṣṭhoras-taṭāntaraḥ \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The sweetness of his waist defeats the pride of a celestial lion. His broad chest is like a slab from an emerald mountain.**

**Комментарий:**

The great pride of celestial lions is defeated (vidhvastd) by the beauty of waist (madhyd). The middle (tatantarah) of his broad chest is like a slab from a mountain of emeralds. Grava means stone according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 9

*kambu-kaṇṭha-sthalālambi-maṇi-samrāḍ alaṅkṛtiḥ \|*  
*ākhaṇḍala-maṇi-stambha-spardhi-dor-daṇḍa-caṇḍimā \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is ornamented with the Kaustubha on his conch-like neck. His passionate arms create envy in sapphire pillars.**

**Комментарий:**

His neck is like a conch (kambu) because it has three lines. He is ornamented with the Kaustubha gem (mani-samrat) resting on his conch-like neck. Kambu-griva means a neck with three lines according to Amara-kosa.

His passionate (candima) arms or arms with intense beauty create envy in sapphire (akhanda-mani) pillars. Canda means sharp or angry according to Visvalocana.

### Text 10

*khaṇḍitākhaṇḍa-koṭīndu-saundarya-mukha-maṇḍalaḥ \|*  
*lāvaṇya-laharī-sindhuḥ sindūra-tulitādharaḥ \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His face defeats the beauty of a million full moons. He is an ocean with waves of beauty. His lips are red like sindura.**

**Комментарий:**

His face defeats the beauty of a million full (akhanda) moons. He is an ocean with waves of beauty. All his limbs have increasing beauty. His lips are equal to sindura. His lips are very red. Sindura means red power according to Visva.

### Text 11

*phullāravinda-saundarya kandalī-tundilekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*gaṇḍānta-tāṇḍava-krīḍā-hiṇḍan-makara-kuṇḍalaḥ \|\|11\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His eyes nourish the fresh beauty of blossoming lotuses. His fickle makara earrings dance at the edge of his cheeks.**

**Комментарий:**

His eyes nourish (tundila) the new (kandali) beauty of blossoming lotuses. Kandala means newly born according to Amara-kosa. His fickle (hindani) makara earrings dance (tandava-krida) at the edge of his cheeks.

### Text 12

*navīna-yauvanārambha-jṛmbhitojjvala-vigrahaḥ \|*  
*apāṅga-tuṅgitānaṅga-koṭi-kodaṇḍa-vikramaḥ \|\|12\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is the very form of madhurya-rasa manifested at the beginning of kaisora period. The edges of his eyes have the great prowess of a million arrows of Cupid.**

**Комментарий:**

He has a form of madhurya-rasa manifested (jrmbhita) during the first part of kaisora age (navlna-yauvana). Ujjvala means madhurya-rasa according to Amara-kosa. The tips of his eyes show the great (tungita') prowess (yikrama) of a million arrows of Cupid. The tips of his eyes shower sharp arrows that pierce the heart. Apanga is the edge of the eye according to Amara-kosa. His glances agitated the hearts of the young gopis which are like deer, pierced by arrows.

### Text 13

*sudhā-niryāsa-mādhurya-dhurīṇodāra-bhāṣitaḥ \|*  
*sāndra-vṛndāṭavī-kuñja-kandarā-gandha-sindhuraḥ \|\|13\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His generous words are laden with sweetness of the essence of nectar. He is an intoxicated elephant in the dense bowers and caves of Vrndavana.**

**Комментарий:**

His generous (udara) words, giving bliss, carry (dhurina) sweetness which is the essence (niryasa) of nectar. He is an intoxicated (gandha) elephant (sindhurah) in the caves and dense bowers of Vrndavana. This means he plays at will in these places.

### Text 14

*dhanya-govardhanottuṅga-śṛṅgotsaṅga-navāmbudhaḥ \|*  
*kalinda-nandinī-keli-kalyāṇa-kalahaṁsakaḥ \|\|14\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is a fresh cloud on the high peaks of fortunate Govardhana. He is an auspicious swan while playing the waters of Yamuna.**

**Комментарий:**

He is a fresh cloud among (utsanga) the towering (uttunga) peaks of Govardhana, the best of Krsna’s servants, who possesses wealth in the form of Krsna. Sniga means a peak according to Visva. He is like a cloud on the peak, showering his beauty which is to be drunk. He is like an auspicious swan while playing in the waters of Yamuna. He moves about freely there.

### Text 15

*dhanya-govardhanottuṅga-śṛṅgotsaṅga-navāmbudhaḥ \|*  
*kalinda-nandinī-keli-kalyāṇa-kalahaṁsakaḥ \|\|15\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He becomes blissful in Nandisvara. He dances beside Bhandira. He killed $ankhacuda. He lifted Govardhana like a ball.**

**Комментарий:**

He takes bliss in Nandisvara, Nanda’s capital city, ornamented with various tree and creepers endowed with flowers and fruits, many waterfalls, and plateaus with colorful gems. He dances at the side of a banyan tree called Bhandira, situated on the other side of the Yamuna. He killed Sankhacuda, a Yaksa and servant of Karhsa. He lifted Govardhana (g)risvarah) like a ball used for playing. Genduka means a ball according to Haima.

### Text 16

*vārīndrārbudha-gambhīraḥ pārīndrārbuda-vikramī \|*  
*rohiṇī-nandanānandī śrīdāmoddāma-sauhṛdaḥ \|\|16\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is deeper than ten million oceans. He is more valiant than ten million lions. He gives bliss to Balarama. He has great friendship with Sridama.**

**Комментарий:**

He is deeper than ten million oceans (varindra). He is more valiant than ten million lions (parindra). This means he has unlimited strength. Pafindra means a lion according to Haima. He gives joy to Balarama by his service. He has great (uddama) friendship with Sridama, brother of Radhika.

### Text 17

*vārīndrārbudha-gambhīraḥ pārīndrārbuda-vikramī \|*  
*rohiṇī-nandanānandī śrīdāmoddāma-sauhṛdaḥ \|\|17\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

He has Subala as his priya-narma-sakha. He is attractive to the other cowherd boys. He is fixed on increasing the joy of the people of Vraja.

He has a dear friend named Subala, a priya-narma-sakha, an excellent young cowherd. He is attractive (hrdayangamah) to the best of the cowherd boys such as Subhadra, Mandalibhadra and Devaprastha. He is their friend according to their bhava. He is fixed (mahd-vratl) in increasing (sandipana) the bliss of the people of Vraja like a gardener of trees.

### Text 18

*śṛṅginī-saṅgha-saṁgrāhi-veṇu-saṁgīta-maṇḍalaḥ \|*  
*uttuṅga-puṅgavārabdha-saṅgarāsaṅga-kautukī \|\|18\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He plays many songs on his flute in order to gather all the cows together. He takes pleasure in seeing the huge bulls when they begin to fight.**

**Комментарий:**

He plays many songs on his flute to gather all the cows (snigini) together. Snigini means cow according to Amara-kosa. He takes pleasure when the huge bulls begin fighting.

### Text 19

*visphurad-vanya-śṛṅgāraḥ śṛṅgārābhīṣṭa-daivatam \|*  
*udañcat-piccha-viñcholī-lāñchitojjvala-vigrahaḥ \|\|19\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He wears clove flowers which blossom in the forest. He is the deity of madhurya-rasa. His form shines with a line of peacock feathers of variegated beauty.**

**Комментарий:**

He is decorated with blossoming forest flowers such as clove flowers. He is the presiding deity (abhlsta-daivatam) of madhurya-rasa. Daivatam could be taken as daivatah. Srngdra means being decorated with powdered sindura and clove flowers according to writer of Medini. His form is decorated with a line of peacock feathers with variegated beauty (udancat). Vincholikd means a line according to Trikanda-sesa. He has a peacock feather crown on his head.

### Text 20

*saṁcarac-cañcarīkāli-pañca-varṇa-srag-añcitaḥ \|*  
*suraṅga-raṅgaṇa-svarṇa-yūthi-grathita-mekhalaḥ \|\|20\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is worshipped by a Vaijayanti garland where bees hover. He wears a belt made of colorful rangana and svarna-ytithi flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

He is worshipped by a Vaijayanti garland where swarms of bees (cancankali) hover (sancarat). Cancarikali means bees according to Halayudha. He wears a belt made of nicely colored (suranga) rangana and svarna yuthi flowers. Ranga means color according to Haima. He is decorated with a belt of colorful flowers.

### Text 21

*dhātu-citra-vicitrāṅga-lāvaṇya-laharī-bharaḥ \|*  
*guñjā-puñja-kṛtākalpaḥ keli-talpita-pallavaḥ \|\|21\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His various limbs radiate waves of beauty with their colorful mineral patterns. He is decorated with gunja berry ornaments. He has beds made of shoots for pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

His various limbs (vicitranga) like chest, arms, forehead, are laden with waves of beauty because of the patterns made by mountain minerals (dhatu) colored red, yellow, etc. He has, decorations such as necklaces and bracelets made of gunja berries. Akalpa means decorations according to Amara-kosa. He has beds for play made of shoots.

### Text 22

*vapur-āmoda-mādhvīka-vardhita-pramadā-madaḥ \|*  
*vṛndāvanāravindākṣī-vṛnda-kandarpa-dīpanaḥ \|\|22\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He increasingly intoxicates the young women with the scented honey of his limbs. He excites love in the many lotus eyed women of Vrndavana.**

**Комментарий:**

He increasingly intoxicates (madah) the young women (pramadd) with the scented honey on his limbs. The rest is clear.

### Text 23

*mīnāṅka-saṁkulābhīrī-kuca-kuṅkuma-paṅkilaḥ \|*  
*mukhendu-mādhurī-dhārā-ruddha-sādhvī-vilocanaḥ \|\|23\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His chest is covered with kuhkuma from the breasts of gopis who are overwhelmed with love. The sweetness of his moonlike face obstructs the eyes of the chaste women.**

**Комментарий:**

He is heavily anointed with the kuhkuma from the breasts of the gopis (dbhifi) who are inundated (sahkula) with love (minanka). His chest is smeared with the kuhkuma. He obstructs the eyes of the chaste women with the abundant (dhara) sweetness of his moon-like face. Dhara means an assembly according to Visva. Their eyes are like cakora birds (which drink the nectar of the moon).

### Text 24

*kumārī-paṭa-luṇṭhākaḥ prauḍha-narmokti-karmaṭhaḥ \|*  
*amanda-mugdha-vaidagdhyadigdha-rādhā-sudhāmbudhiḥ \|\|24\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He steals the young girls’ clothing. He is most skillful at joking. He plunges Radha into an ocean of nectar by his most attractive clever words.**

**Комментарий:**

He steals (lunthakah) the clothing situated on the riverbank, belonging to the young girls performing Katyayani vrata. He is skillful (karmathah) at joking and logical words. He said the girls had offended the water devatas by bathing naked. They should atone for the offense by placing their hand on their heads. Karmatha means clever according to Amara-kosa. He increases (digdha) the ocean of nectar for Radha by his attractive (mugdha) cleverness (vaidaghya). She sinks in an ocean of nectar because of his joking words on being brought by the young girls and hearing him talk of atonements. This is how she is nourished by his joking.

### Text 25

*cāru-candrāvalī-buddhi-kaumudī-śarad-āgamaḥ \|*  
*dhīra-lālitya-lakṣmīvān kandarpānanda-bandhuraḥ \|\|25\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is the arrival of autumn for the moonlight of attractive Candravali. He is strongly marked with the qualities of the dhira-lalita hero. He is attractive with the joy of love.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the arrival of autumn for the moonlight of attractive (caru) Candravali’s intelligence. Just as the moonlight manifests in autumn, Candravali’s intelligence awakens when Krsna comes. He is endowed with the qualities of the dhira-lalita hero. The qualities are stated as follows:

*parihāsapaṭurmṛdula kalākalāpāñcitastaruṇaḥ \|*  
*kāntāvaśagaścintārahitaḥ kathito'tra dhīralalito'yam \|\|*

**The dhira-lalita hero is clever at joking, soft, skillful in many arts, youthful, controlled by his lover and devoid of worry. (Kavya-kaustubha)**

He is attractive (bandhurah) with the joy of love.

### Text 26

*candrāvalī-cakorendro rādhikā-mādhavī-madhuḥ \|*  
*lalitā-keli-lalito viśākhoḍu-niśākaraḥ \|\|26\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is the moon for the cakora Candravali. He is the spring for the madhavi creeper, Radha. He is charming in playing with Lalita. He is the moon for the star Visakha.**

ced iyaṁ preyasā hātuṁ kṣaṇam apy atiduḥśakā \| paramapremavaśyatvānmādhavīti tadocyate \|\|

*If Krsna cannot give up his lover for even a moment because he is controlled by her prema, the svadhina-bhartrha is called madhavi. (Ujjvala-nila-mani 5.94)*

**Комментарий:**

He gives joy to her like the spring season (madhu). In both cases with the double meaning of the words (spring and honey, madhavi flower and madhavi woman) the ornament of rupaka (metaphor) is used. He is charming (.lalita) when playing with Lalita. He is attractive in playing at verbal wars or love battles with her.

He is the moon (nisakarah) for the star Visakha. Udu means star according to Amara-kosa. As the moon makes the constellation Visakha beautiful, Krsna makes Visakha sakhi beautiful.

### Text 27

*padmā-vadana-padmāliḥ śaibyā-sevya-padāmbujaḥ \|*  
*bhadrā-hṛdaya-nidrāluḥ śyāmalā-kāma-lālasaḥ \|\|27\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is a bee on the lotus mouth of Padma. His lotus feet are served by Saibya. He sleeps on the heart of Bhadra. He is greedy to fulfill the desires of Syamala.**

**Комментарий:**

The first sentence is clear. It is understood that Padma and Saibya are sahhis of Candravali. Bhadra and Syamala are heads of yuthas (groups). He is thirsty for Syamala’s desire to serve him. When her desires are known to him, he thinks himself successful.

### Text 28

*lokottara-camatkāra-līlā-mañjari-niṣkuṭaḥ \|*  
*prema-sampad-ayaskānta-kānta-kṛta-kṛṣṇāyasa-vrataḥ \|\|28\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is a garden of creepers of most amazing pastimes. He is iron attracted to the magnet of a wealth of prema.**

**Комментарий:**

He is a garden (niskutah) full of creepers of pastimes which cause the greatest astonishment (lokottara-camatkara). Mahjari means a creeper and niskutd means a garden according to Amara-kosa. He is the shelter of most amazing pastimes. He is like iron (dyasa) attracted by the magnet (ayaskanta) of a wealth of prema.

He is attracted by prema just as iron is attracted by a magnet.

### Text 29

*muralī-caura-gaurāṅgī-kuca-kañcuka-luñcanaḥ \|*  
*rādhābhisāra-sarvasvaḥ sphāra-nāgaratā-guruḥ \|\|29\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He tears the bodices from the breasts of the gopis who stole his flute. His highest treasure is meeting Radha. He is the teacher of great cleverness.**

**Комментарий:**

He tears (luncanah) the bodices on the breasts of the golden gopis who have stolen his flute (murali-caura). Radha meeting him is the all and all of his life (sarvasvah). He is the teacher of extensive (sphdra) clever arts (nagarata). Nagara means cleverness according to Visva.

### Text 30

*rādhā-narmokti-śuśrūṣā-vīrun-nīruddha-vigrahaḥ \|*  
*kadamba-mañjarī-hāri-rādhikā-rodhanoddhuraḥ \|\|30\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He hides himself in a creeper bower, desiring to hear Radha joking with her friends. He proudly stops Radha from taking the kadamba flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

He covers himself (niruddha) with the creeper (yirut) of the desire to hear (susrusa) Radha’s joking words. He is most eager to hear her. Virut means a creeper according to Amara-kosa. He proudly (uddhurah) stops Radha from stealing the kadamba flowers. Or he hides himself among the creepers with desire to hear or to serve (susrtisd) Radha’s joking with her friends, ^usrusa means desire to hear or to serve according to Visvalocana. He is proud (uddhurah) in preventing Radha from taking kadamba flowers. Uddhura or uddhatah means proud according to Dhananjaya.

### Text 31

*kuḍuṅga-kroḍa-saṁgūḍha-rādhā-saṅgama-raṅgavān \|*  
*krīḍoḍḍāmara-dhīrādhā-tāṭaṅkotpala-tāḍitaḥ \|\|31\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He comes to a place for meeting Radha who hides within a bower. He is struck by the lotus ear ornament of Radha who is skillful at playing.**

**Комментарий:**

He comes to the place (ranga) to meet Radha who hides within the bower (kudunga). He understands where she is by hints from sakhis or experiences astonishment because of that news. He is struck by the lotus ear ornament of Radha whose intelligence has become skillful (uddamara) at playing. She beats him by saying, “You torment me when I hide in fear of you.”

### Text 32

*anaṅga-saṅgarodgāri-kṣuṇṇa-kuṅkuma-kaṅkaṭaḥ \|*  
*tribhaṅgi-laṅgimākāro veṇu-saṅgamitādharaḥ \|\|32\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He breaks Radha’s kunkuma armor during the war of love. His charming form is bent in three places. He places the flute on his lips in order to play it.**

**Комментарий:**

He destroyed Radha’s kunkuma armor when the war of love (sangara) manifested (udgari). Kankatah means armor according to Amara-kosa. His form is attractively (langima) bent at three places—neck, waist and feet. He places his flute on his lips to play it (sangamita).

### Text 33

*veṇu-vistṛta-gāndharva-sāra-sandarbha-sauṣṭhavaḥ \|*  
*gopī-yūtha-sahasrendraḥ sāndra-rāsa-rasonmadaḥ \|\|33\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When he plays his flute, he displays the beauty of the highest musical scriptures.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the leader of thousands of groups of gopis. He is intoxicated with the rasa of the intimate rasa dance.

He is distinguished by beauty of the highest (sara) musical (gandharvd) scriptures (sandarbhd) when playing the flute. He is the king of thousands of groups of gopis. Though у iitha means a creeper or a group, usually it means a group. This is stated by Halayudha and others.

### Text 34

*veṇu-vistṛta-gāndharva-sāra-sandarbha-sauṣṭhavaḥ \|*  
*gopī-yūtha-sahasrendraḥ sāndra-rāsa-rasonmadaḥ \|\|34\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**His side glances cause agitation like millions of Cupids. He begins to dance within groups on the bank of the Yamuna.**

**Комментарий:**

His side glances cause agitation like millions of Cupids. He begins to dance in the areas (mandalesu) on the bank of the Yamuna (candamsu-nandini).

### Text 35

*vṛṣabhānu-sutā-bhṛṅgī-kāmadhuk-kamalākaraḥ \|*  
*gūḍhākūta-parīhāsa-rādhikā-janita-smitaḥ \|\|35\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is a lotus pond for fulfilling the desires of the bee Radha. He smiles at Radha’s jokes filled with hidden intentions.**

**Комментарий:**

He is a lotus pond (kamalakarah) that fulfills the desires (kamadhuka) of the bee Radha. Padmakara means a pond according to Amara-kosa.
