He smiles when Radha jokes with hidden intentions. “Do not add any other ingredients, since I desire to eat the sweets displayed in your mind.” Akuta means intention according to Halayudha.

### Text 36

*nārī-veśa-nigūḍhātmā vyūḍha-citta-camatkṛtiḥ \|*  
*karpūrālambi-tāmbūla-karambita-mukhāmbujaḥ \|\|36\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He disguises himself in woman’s clothing. He becomes most astonished in his heart. His lotus mouth is endowed with betel nut mixed with camphor.**

**Комментарий:**

Meaning is clear. He disguises himself in woman’s clothing. He becomes astonished in his heart. “It is good that I have come to this house, filled with clever people, unnoticed by others, disguising myself, a man, in woman’s dress.” His lotus mouth is endowed with betel nut mixed with camphor.

### Text 37

*māni-candrāvalī-dūtī-kḷpta-sandhāna-kauśalaḥ \|*  
*chadma-ghaṭṭa-taṭī-ruddha-rādhā-bhrū-kuṭi-ghaṭṭitaḥ \|\|37\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Skillfully he arranges a meeting with respectable Candravali through a messenger. He makes Radha frown when he stops her at the toll gate.**

**Комментарий:**

The next verse explains the intention of frowning.

### Text 38

*dakṣa-rādhā-sakhī-hāsa-vyājopālambha-lajjitaḥ \|*  
*mūrti-mad-ballavī-premā kṣemānanda-rasākṛtiḥ \|\|38\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He is shamed by the scolding on the pretext of joking by a skillful sakhi of Radha. He is personified prema experienced by the gopis. He is the very form of auspicious madhurya-rasa.**

**Комментарий:**

He is shamed by the scolding (upalambha) through a pretense (yyajd) of joking by Radha’s clever sakhi.

She starts to scold, “You have become the toll collector at this ordinary forest. How have you become the controller here? The bee does not obtain the fragrance of the lotus woman by fraud, devoid of humility and politeness.” By this he becomes shamed. He is the personified (miirti-mat) prema of the gopis. He is the object of their love. He has a form which is nondifferent from madhurya-rasa (ananda-rasa'), filled with auspiciousness (ksema). Raso vai sah: the Lord is rasa. (Taittiriya Upanisad 2.7.1)

### Text 39

*abhisārollasad-bhadrā-kiṅkiṇī-ninadonmukhaḥ \|*  
*vāsa-sajjībhavat-padmā-prekṣyamāṇāgra-paddhatiḥ \|\|39\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He eagerly listens for the sound of ankle bells of Bhadra, who is joyful to come for a meeting. Padma, dressing herself, peers at the path waiting for him to come.**

**Комментарий:**

He eagerly listens for the sound of ankle bells of Bhadra who is joyful (ullasat) to come for a meeting. The qualities of the woman going for a meeting are described:

*yā paryutsukacittātimadena madanena vā \|*  
*ātmanābhisaretkāntaṁ sā bhavedabhisārikā \|\|*

**She who with eager heart, goes to meet her lover with great passion and intoxication is the abhisarika, the woman going to meet her lover. (Gitavali)**

Padma, decorating herself, looks at the path for his coming. The quality of the vasaka-sajja are described:

*bhavedvāsakasajjāsau sajjitāṅgaratālayā \|*  
*niścityāgamanaṁ bharturdvārekṣaṇaparāyaṇā \|\|*

**The vasaka-sajja decorates herself at home and continually peers at the path by which her lover will come. (Gitavali)**

### Text 40

*utkaṇṭhitārta-lalitā-vitarka-padavīṁ gataḥ \|*  
*vipralabdha-viśākhoru-vilāpa-bhara-vardhanaḥ \|\|40\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He causes Lalita, in pain and longing, to worry when he does not appear for a meeting. He causes ever-increasing lamentation in Visakha when she is cheated.**

**Комментарий:**

The qualities of the utkanthita woman are described:

*sā syādutkaṇṭhitā yasyā vāsaṁ naiti drutaṁ patiḥ \|*  
*tasyānāgamane hetuṁ cintayantyāḥ śucā bhṛśam \|\|*

**The utkanthita woman worries about the cause of her lover not coming and laments profusely when he does not quickly come to her residence. (Gltavall)**

He causes Visakha who has been cheated to greatly increase her lamentation. The qualities of the vipralabdha woman are described:

*yasyā dūtīṁ svayaṁ preṣya samaye nāgataḥ priyaḥ \|*  
*śocantī taṁ vinā duḥsthā vipralabdhā tu sā smṛtā \|\|*

**The vipralbadha woman laments when after sending a messenger personally, her lover does not come on time and feels miserable. (Gltavali)**

### Text 41

*kalahāntaritā-śyāmā-mṛgyamāṇa-mukhekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*khaṇḍitoccaṇḍadhī-śaivyā-roṣokti-rasikāntaraḥ \|\|41\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He causes Syama to search for the sight of his attractive face. His heart longs to hear the angry words of Saibya who is unsteady with anger at not having her lover.**

**Комментарий:**

He causes Syama to search for seeing his attractive face. The qualities of the kalahantarita are described.

*nirasto manyunā kānto namannapi yayā puraḥ \|*  
*sānutāpayutā dīnā kalahāntaritā bhavet \|\|*

**The kalahantarita woman rejects her lover out of anger and then feels remorse, offering him respect. (Gltavall)**

His heart (antara) longs to hear (rasika) the angry words of Saibya who is unsteady with anger on not attaining her lover. Antara means inside something according to Halayudha. The qualities of the khandita woman are described:

*anyayā saha kāntasya dṛṣṭe saṁbhogalakṣaṇe \|*  
*īrṣyākaṣāyitātmāsau khaṇḍitā khalu kathyate \|\|*

**The khandita woman becomes inundated with anger on seeing marks on her lover that indicate that he has enjoyed with someone else. (Gitavali)**

### Text 42

*viśleṣa-viklavac-candrāvalī-sandeśa-nanditaḥ \|*  
*svādhīna-bhartṛkotphulla-rādhā-maṇḍana-paṇḍitaḥ \|\|42\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

He was overjoyed at a message from Candravali who was upset in separation. He is expert at dressing joyful Radha, who brought Krsna under her control.

He was overjoyed at a message from Candravali who was upset (viklavat) in separation (vislesa). Viklava means disturbed according to Halayudha.

He was skillful (panditah) at dressing Radha who was joyful and who brought Krsna under her control (svadhina-bhartrka) by joyful pastimes. The qualities of the svadhina-bhartrka are described:

*yasyāḥ premaguṇākṛṣṭaḥ priyaḥ pārśvaṁ na muñcati \|*  
*vicitravibhramāsaktā sā syātsvādhīnabhartṛkā \|\|*

**The svadhina-bhartrka. is endowed with coquetry so that her lover, attracted by her qualities of prema does not leave her side. (Gitavali)**

### Text 43

*cumba-veṇu-glaha-dyuti-jayi-rādhā-dhṛtāñcalaḥ \|*  
*rādhā-prema-rasāvarta-vibhrama-bhramitāntaraḥ \|\|43\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

The end of his garment was grasped by Radha when she won at dice where the wager was a kiss and his flute. His heart was agitated by the whirlpools of the amorous gestures of Radha’s prema-rasa.

The end of his garment was grasped by Radha when she won in the dice game (dyiiti) where the wager (glaha) was a kiss and his flute. Glaha means a wager and ancala means end of the cloth according to Halayudha. “If you conquer me then you can take a kiss from Lalita and if I win, then I take your flute.” That was the wager. When Radha won she pulled his cloth in order to take his flute. His mind was confused by the amorous gestures of Radha’s prema-rasa which was like a whirlpool. Avarta means a whirlpool according to Amara-kosa. This means that he was controlled by her flow of prema.

### Text 44

*ity eṣonmatta-dhīḥ premnā śaṁsantī kaṁsa-mardanam \|*  
*sphurantaṁ purataḥ prekṣya prauḍhānandotsavaṁ yayau \|\|44\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

This beautiful cowherd girl, praising Krsna by these names, saw him manifest in front of her and attained a festival of deep bliss.

The work concludes by showing the results of the stotra. This beautiful cowherd girl (esd), praised (samsanti) Krsna by these names. By the power of that sanhirtana, she saw him manifest in front of her (sphurantam) and she attained a festival of deep bliss. She experienced the happiness of uniting with him.

### Text 45

*premendu-sāgarākhye’smin nāmnām aṣṭottare śate \|*  
*vigāhayantu vibudhāḥ prītyā rasana-mandaram \|\|45\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

О learned devotees! With great taste may you immerse the churning mountain of your tongue in the hundred and eight names, called the ocean which produces the moon of prema.

What is necessary for the devotees at present is explained.

О learned devotees (vibudhah) or devatas! With great taste (pritya) may you immerse the churning mountain of your tongue (rasana-mandaram) in the hundred and eight names, called the ocean which produces the moon of prema.

Just as the devatas manifested the moon which destroys all suffering from the ocean of milk by using Mandara mountain as the churning rod, prema should manifest from this stotra which the devotees receive by their tongues.

## keśavāṣṭakam

**śrīkeśavāya namaḥ**

**I offer respects to Kesava.**

### Text 1

*nava-priyaka-mañjarī-racita-karṇa-pūra-śriyaṁ*  
*vinidratara-mālatī-kalita-śekhareṇojjvalam \|*  
*darocchvasita-yūthikā-grathita-valgu-vaikakṣakaṁ*  
*vraje vijayinaṁ bhaje vipina-deśataḥ keśavam \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship Kesava, as he returns in the evening from a forest, who is made attractive with ear ornaments made of fresh kadamba flowers, who is beautiful with a crown made of blossoming jasmines, and who has a charming upper garment woven with blossoming yuthika flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises Kesava with eight verses. I worship Kesava, who returns most pleased (vijayinam) to the Vraja village in the evening from the forest. He is further described. He is made attractive with ear ornaments made of fresh kadamba flowers. He is beautiful with a crown made (kalita) of blossoming (yinidratara) jasmines. He has a charming (valgu) upper garment (vaikaksakam) woven with slightly blossoming yuthika flowers. Vaikaksaka is a cloth worn over the chest according to Halayudha.

### Text 2

*piśaṅgi maṇika-stani praṇata-śṛṅgi piṅgekṣaṇe*  
*mṛdaṅga-mukhi dhūmale śavali haṁsi vaṁśī-priye \|*  
*iti svasurabhi-kulaṁ taralam āhvayantaṁ mudā*  
*vraje vijayinaṁ bhaje vipina-deśataḥ keśavam \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship Kesava as he returns in the evening from a forest, who joyfully calls his restless herd of cows, “O Pisangi! О Manika-stam! О Pranata-srrigi! О Piheksana! О Mrdanga-mukhi! О Dhumala! О Savaii! О Hams!! О Vamsi-priya!”**

**Комментарий:**

He calls out names of nine cows whose meanings are clear. He calls out to his herd of cows of one variety to assemble them. Surabhi means a cow and kula means a group of similar nature according to Haima.

### Text 3

*ghana-praṇaya-medurān madhura-narma-goṣṭhī-kalā*  
*vilāsa-nilayān milad-vividha-veśa-vidyotinaḥ \|*  
*sakhīn akhila-sārayā pathiṣu hāsayantaṁ girā*  
*vraje vijayinaṁ bhaje vipina-deśataḥ keśavam \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship Kesava as he returns in the evening from a forest, who, by his excellent words on the path, causes laughter in his friends, who are full of deep affection, who are abodes of cleverness in conversations of sweet jokes, and who shine with various types of clothing.**

**Комментарий:**

He makes his friends laugh by excellent words (akhila-saraya gird) on the path. Sara means the best according to Haima. The friends are described. They are full of (meduran) deep affection (ghana-pranaya). They are abodes which manifest cleverness in conversations of sweet joking. Gosthl means a discussion according to Visva. They are endowed (milat) with special beauty (yidyotinah) from their variety of clothing.

### Text 4

*śramāmbu-kaṇikāvalī-dara-vilīḍha-gaṇḍāntaraṁ*  
*samūḍhāgiri-dhātubhir likhita-cāru-patrāṅkuram \|*  
*udañcad-ali-maṇḍalī-dyuti-viḍambi-vakrālakaṁ*  
*vraje vijayinaṁ bhaje vipina-deśataḥ keśavam \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship Kesava as he returns in the evening from a forest, whose cheeks are delicately decorated with small drops of perspiration, whose body is decorated with attractive patterns made from mountain minerals, whose curly locks of hair deride a swarm of fickle bees.**

**Комментарий:**

The center of his cheeks are ornamented, seemingly being slightly licked (dara-vilidha) with drops of perspiration. His body is decorated with patterns (patrahkuram) made from fragrant mountain minerals, yellow, red, white and blue. His curly locks of hair deride the beauty of a swarm of fickle (udancat) bees.

### Text 5

*nibaddha-nava-tarṇakāvali-vilokanotkaṇṭhayā*  
*naṭat-khura-puṭāñcalair alaghubhir bhuvaṁ bhindatīm \|*  
*kalena dhavalā-ghaṭāṁ laghu nivartayantaṁ puro*  
*vraje vijayinaṁ bhaje vipina-deśataḥ keśavam \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship Kesava as he returns in the evening from a forest, who by the sound of his flute quickly brings in front the herd of cows, which tear the earth with their heavy, dancing hooves because of desire to see their new calves tied in the cow pens.**

**Комментарий:**

He quickly (laghu) brings back the herd of cows (dhavala-ghatam) by the sound of his flue (kalena). Dhavala means cow according to Medinikara. Ghata means a group according to Haima. Laghu means fast according to Amara-kosa. The herd is described. Eager to see the new calves (nava tarnakavali) tied in the pens, the cows tear up (bhindatim) the earth with the tips of their dancing hooves (khura-puta). Tarnaka is a calf according to Halayudha.

### Text 6

*padāṅka-tatibhir varāṁ viracayantam adhva-śriyaṁ*  
*calat-tarala-naicikī-nicaya-dhūli-dhūmra-srajam \|*  
*marul-lahari-cañcalī-kṛta-dukūla-cūḍāñcalaṁ*  
*vraje vijayinaṁ bhaje vipina-deśataḥ keśavam \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship Kesava as he returns to the village from the forest, who improves the beauty of the road by the marks on his feet, whose garland becomes grey from the dust raised by the moving, restless cows, and whose cloth and crown quiver in the gusts of wind.**

**Комментарий:**

He makes the beauty of the road most excellent by the many marks on his feet. His garland becomes grey (dhiimra) with dust from the herd of moving, restless cows. Naicikt means an excellent cow. Dhiimra means smoke-colored according to Amara-kosa. The edge of his yellow cloth and his head ornament quiver because of the gusts of gentle wind (marul-lahari).

### Text 7

*vilāsa-muralī-kala-dhvanibhir ullasan-mānasāḥ*  
*kṣaṇād akhila-ballavīḥ pulakayantam antar gṛhe \|*  
*muhur vidadhataṁ hṛdi pramuditāṁ ca goṣṭheśvarīṁ*  
*vraje vijayinaṁ bhaje vipina-deśataḥ keśavam \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship Kesava as he returns to Vraja from the forest, who makes Yasoda, happy in mind, constantly joyful within, and causes the hairs of all the elder women in the house to instantly stand on end by the sweet sound of his playful flute.**

**Комментарий:**

The elder women become joyful in the distance. That is described. He makes the hairs of the elder cowherd women (akhila-ballavih), associates of Yasoda, in the houses suddenly (ksanat) stand on end by the sweet sound (kala-dhvanibhih) of his playful flute. He gives joy in the heart constantly to Yasoda, his mother, who is joyful in heart (ullasan manasah) because of the festival of Krsna’s coming.

### Text 8

*upetya pathi sundarī-tatibhir ābhir abhyarcitaṁ*  
*smitāṅkura-karambitair naṭad-apāṅga-bhaṅgī-śataiḥ \|*  
*stana-stavaka-saṁcaran-nayana-cañcarīkāñcalaṁ*  
*vraje vijayinaṁ bhaje vipina-deśataḥ keśavam \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship Kesava as he returns to Vraja from the forest, who is worshipped on the path by the gopis who have climbed on the roofs, through their many dancing side glances endowed with amorous gestures, and whose bee-like eyes hover over their flower-clustered breasts.**

**Комментарий:**

He meets directly with the dear gopis who have intense love for him. He is worshipped by those gopis who have climbed on the roofs, with their many dancing side glances. Abhih indicates that he directly met them. The glances are further described. The glances were endowed with buds of smiles. This means they displayed many alluring gestures. He responded to them. The edges of his bee-like eyes wandered to their flower cluster breasts. Their breasts were ornamented with colorful bodices which made them appear like flower clusters. This is an example of luptopama (where an element of the comparison is missing) rather than rupaka (metaphor). The bodices obstruct his wandering bee-like eyes.

### Text 9

*idaṁ nikhila-ballavī-kula-mahotsavollāsanaṁ*  
*krameṇa kila yaḥ pumān paṭhati suṣṭhu padyāṣṭakam \|*  
*tam ujjvala-dhiyaṁ sadā nija-padāravinda-dvaye*  
*ratiṁ dadad-acañcalāṁ sukhayatād viśākhā-sakhaḥ \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Visakha’s friend, bestowing bhava for his lotus feet, give happiness to the person of shining intelligence who recites intently in order this astaka which is a joyous festival for all the gopis.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of reciting this astaka is described. May the friend of Visakha give happiness to the person who recites this astaka with concentration (susthu). Susthu means intensely according to Amara-kosa. The friend of Visakha is the hero who acts as a friend, Krsna. What does he do? He makes that person attain fixed bhava for his lotus feet. The rest is clear in meaning. The meter is prthivl.

Thus Kesavastaka has been explained.

## prathamaṁ kuñjavihāryaṣṭakam

**namaḥ kuñjavihāriṇe**

**I offer respects to Kunja-vihari.**

### Text 1

*indranīla-maṇi-mañjula-varṇaḥ*  
*phulla-nīpa-kusumāñcita-karṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇalābhir a-kṛśorasi hārī*  
*sundaro jayati kuñja-vihārī \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The beautiful son of Nanda, who plays in the bowers, who has the charming beauty of a sapphire, who has ears decorated with blossoming kadambas, and who wears a necklace of gunja berries on his chest, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises Krsna, who plays in the bowers, in two sets of eight verses.

The son of Nanda, who plays in the bowers (kunja-vihari'), attractive to the dear gopis (sundarah), remains victorious. He is described. He has a charming beauty (varna) like a sapphire. Varna means color and beauty according to Visva. He has a necklace (hard) of gunja berries (krsnalabhih) on his broad (akrsa) chest. The rest is clear.

### Text 2

*rādhikā vadana-candra-cakoraḥ*  
*sarva-ballava-vadhū-dhṛti-cauraḥ \|*  
*carcarī-caturatāñcita-cārī*  
*cāruto jayati kuñja-vihārī \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who plays in the bowers, who is the cakora gazing at the moon-like face of Radha, who steals the composure of all the gopis, who is attractive at skillfully dancing to carcari rhythm, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

His attractiveness is made clear. He is attractive (canitah) at dancing (carl), being skillful (caturata) at carcarl rhythm. The rest is clear.

### Text 3

*sarvataḥ prathita-kaulika-parva*  
*dhvaṁsanena hṛta-vāsava-garvaḥ \|*  
*goṣṭha-rakṣaṇa-kṛte giridhārī*  
*līlayā jayati kuñja-vihārī \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who plays in the bowers, who destroyed the pride of Indra by preventing Indra’s worship which was a well-known family tradition, and lifted Govardhana to protect Vraja, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

He was disinterested in his follower (Indra) who created obstacles to his pastimes and developed absorption in other desires. He destroyed Indra’s pride (yasava-garvah) in being a controller of the world, by stopping worship of Indra (parva) which was a tradition in Nanda’s family (kaulikam) and was most famous (prathitd). What did he do when Indra, deprived of his festival, tormented Vraja? Gostha means Vraja according to Halayudha. He easily lifted Govardhana to protect Vraja. There was a great festival in which the gopls could have the rare opportunity of seeing him.

### Text 4

*rāga-maṇḍala-vibhūṣita-vaṁśī*  
*vibhrameṇa madanotsava-śaṁsī \|*  
*stūyamāna-caritaḥ śuka-śārī*  
*śreṇibhir jayati kuñja-vihārī \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who plays in the bowers, who promises a festival of love to the gopis by playing on this flute, which is ornamented with various ragas, and whose actions are praised by flocks of parrots, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

Having defeated Indra, the obstacle, Krsna, again played with passion. He makes a promise (samsi) of a festival of Cupid to his beloveds by the pastimes (vibhramena) of his flute decorated with a host of various ragas. His actions are praised by flocks of parrots and other birds who are attracted by the sweetness of the flute. They praise him as the supreme singer.

### Text 5

*śātakumbha-ruci-hāri-dukūlaḥ*  
*koki-candraka-virājita-cūlaḥ \|*  
*navya-yauvana-lasad-vraja-nārī*  
*rañjano jayati kuñja-vihārī \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who plays in the bowers, whose cloth derides the beauty of gold, whose head shines with a peacock feather and who attracts the Vraja women effulgent with new youth, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

He wears a cloth which derides the beauty of gold (satakumbha). Satakumbha means gold according to Halayudha. Dukulam means loose cloth according to Medini. A peacock feather shines on his head (cudah). Cudah is synonymous with culah (hair). The da and la are interchangeable. Candraka here does not mean the moon since it is combined with the word keki (peacock). The rest is clear. He contacts the women who are attracted to the sound of his flute.

### Text 6

*sthāsakī-kṛta-sugandhi-paṭīraḥ*  
*svarṇa-kāñci-pariśobhi-kaṭīraḥ \|*  
*rādhikonnata-payodhara-vārī*  
*kuñjaro jayati kuñja-vihārī \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who plays in the bowers, who is anointed with fragrant sandalwood, whose waist is attractive with a golden belt, who is an elephant bound by the ropes of Radha’s raised breasts, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

He is anointed (sthasaki) with fragrant sandalwood. Sthasaka

means putting on unguents according to Amara-kosa. The unadi sutra kr-sf-pr-kati-pati-sautibhya Iran explains patlrah and katirah. His waist is attractive (parisobhi) with a golden belt.

Kanci means a belt according to Halayudha. Katiram means the waist. He is an elephant bound by the rope (van) of Radha’s raised breasts. Vari is a rope for tying elephants according to Amara-kosa. He is bound to the beauty of her breasts like an elephant tied up. Payodhara can also mean kanti-dhara, holder of beauty.

### Text 7

*gaura-dhātu-tilakojjvala-bhālaḥ*  
*keli-cañcalita-campaka-mālaḥ \|*  
*adri-kandara-gṛheṣv abhisārī*  
*subhruvāṁ jayati kuñja-vihārī \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who plays in the bowers, whose forehead is bright with yellow mineral tilaka, who wears a campaka garland trembling with play, who meets the gopis in mountain caves, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

His forehead shines with tilaka made of yellow minerals. Bhala means forehead according to Visva. He meets the gopis in mountain caves (adri-kandara). Kandara is a cave according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 8

*vibhramoccala-dṛg-añcala-nṛtya-*  
*kṣipta-gopa-lalanākhila-kṛtyaḥ \|*  
*prema-matta-vṛṣabhānu-kumārī*  
*nāgaro jayati kuñja-vihārī \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who plays in the bowers, who makes the gopis give up their household duties by the amorous movements of the dancing tips of his eyes, who tastes Radha, intoxicated with prema, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

He makes the gopis give up (ksipta) their household duties (krtyah) by the amorous movements (vibhramoccald) of the dancing tips of his eyes. Nagara means rasika.

### Text 9

*aṣṭakaṁ madhura-kuñja-vihārī*  
*krīḍayā paṭhati yaḥ kila hāri \|*  
*sa prayāti vilasat-para-bhāgaṁ*  
*tasya pāda-kamalārcana-rāgam \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The person who recites this astaka attractive with the sweet pastimes of Kunja-vihari will attain the shining excellence of attraction for worshipping Krsna’s lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of recitation of the astaka is described. The person who recites this astaka attractive (hart) with the sweet pastimes of kunja-vihari, attains attraction (ragam) for worshipping the lotus feet of Krsna. The attraction is described. The attraction produces shining excellence (parabhagam). Parabhaga means excellence of qualities according to Haima. The meter is svagata.

svagata ra na bha gair guruna ca

Svagata: Isl sss Iss 11 (ra, na, bha, gu, gu)

Thus, the first kunja-vihari astaka has been explained.

## dvitīyaṁ kuñjavihāryaṣṭakam

**namaḥ kuñjavihāriṇe**

**I offer respects to Kunja-viharl.**

### Text 1

*avirata-rati-bandhu-smeratā-bandhura-śrīḥ*  
*kavalita iva rādhāpāṅga-bhaṅgī-taraṅgaiḥ \|*  
*mudita-vadana-candraś candrakāpīḍa-dhārī*  
*mudira-madhura-kāntir bhāti kuñje vihārī \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, endowed with attractive beauty because of his amorous smiles, who seems devoured by the waves of Radha’s side glances, who has joyful moon-like face, who wears a peacock feather head ornament and whose sweet beauty surpasses that of a cloud, shines in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

The son of Nanda (vihari) shines in the bower (kunje). He is described.

He has charming (bandhura) beauty because of constant amorous (rati-bandhu) smiles. Bandhura means attractive according to Haima. He seems to be devoured (kavalitah) by the waves of Radha’s side glances. He has a joyful (mudita) moon-like face. He wears a head ornament made of peacock feathers. His beauty is sweeter than a cloud (mudira).

### Text 2

*tata-suṣira-ghanānāṁ nādam ānaddha-bhājāṁ*  
*janayati taruṇīnāṁ maṇḍale maṇḍitānām \|*  
*taṭa-bhuvi naṭarāja-krīḍayā bhānu-putryā*  
*vidadhad-atula-cārīr bhāti kuñje vihārī \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, performing incomparable dance steps on the bank of the Yamuna, while the groups of ornamented women produce ragas using vinas, flutes, karatalas and drums, shines in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

His enjoyment in dancing with the gopis is described. Performing incomparable dance steps (vidadhad-atula-carih), with supreme dancing pastimes (nataraja-kridaya) on the bank of the Yamuna, he shines in the bower. Other details are described. The group of gopis (mandale) situated all around produce ragas from playing drums (anaddha-bhajam) and the vina, flutes and brass cymbals. Tata means string instruments like vina, etc., anaddham means drums, and susira means wind instruments like flutes, etc. Kamsya means brass cymbals, etc., which are used to keep the beat. This is according to Amara-kosa. The women are described. They are decorated (manditanam). From top of the head to the feet they are ornamented with various decorations.

### Text 3

*śikhini kalita-ṣaḍje kokile pañcamāḍhye*  
*svayam api nava-vaṁśyoddāmayan grāma-mukhyam \|*  
*dhṛta-mṛga-mada-gandhaḥ suṣṭhu gāndhāra-saṁjñaṁ*  
*tribhuvana-dhṛti-hārīr  bhāti kuñje vihārī \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, fragrant with musk, unsettling the three worlds, playing on his flute and giving the peacock and the cuckoo joy, without restriction playing the principal grama called gandhara on a new flute, shines in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

He not only gives bliss to the gopis but to all the living beings of Vrndavana.

The peacocks sing the seven notes of the scale. The cuckoos sing the fifth note.

Playing on his flute, he gives the peacock and the cuckoo joy. Without restriction, he plays the principal grama called gandhara on a new flute. Svara is based on sruti and echoes it. It is said in Sangita-sastra:

*śrutyanantarabhāvī yaḥ snigdho'nuraṇanāsmakaḥ \|*  
*svato rañjayati śrotuścittaṁ sa svara ucyate \|\| iti \|*

**That which is based on srutis is pleasing and spontaneously attracts the heart of the listener is called svara.**

Sruti is a specialized word that makes up svara. It is said:

*śrutyanantarabhāvī yaḥ snigdho'nuraṇanāsmakaḥ \|*  
*svato rañjayati śrotuścittaṁ sa svara ucyate \|\| iti \|*

**The sound which is the smallest interval on first hearing is known as sruti and constitutes the svara.**

The srutis are enumerated:

*catuścatuścatuścaiva ṣaḍjamadhyamapañcamāḥ \|*  
*dve dve niṣādagāndhārau tristriṁṝṣabhadhaivatau \|\|*

**Sadja, madhyama and pancama have four divisions each. Nisada and gandhara have two divisions each and rsabha and dhaivata have three divisions each.**

*śrutibhyaḥ syuḥ svarāḥ ṣaḍjarṣabhagāndhāramadhyamāḥ \|*  
*pañcamo dhaivataścātha niṣāda iti saptame \|\|*

**From the srutis appear the seven svaras: sadja, rsabha, gandhara, madhyama, pancama, dhaivata and nisada.**

These are also known as sa, re, ga, ma, pa, dha, and ni. The characteristics of grama are given:

*yathā kuṭumbinaḥ sarve'pyekībhūtā bhavanti hi \|*  
*tathā svarāṇāṁ saṁdoho grāma ityabhidhīyate \|\|*  
*ṣaḍjagrāmo bhavedādyo madhyamagrāma eva ca \|*  
*gāndhāragrāma ityetadvāmatrayamudāhṛtam \|\|*  
*nandāvarto'tha jīmūtaḥ subhadro grāmakāstrayaḥ \| ṣaḍjamadhyamagāndhārāstrayāṇāṁ janmahetavaḥ \|\| iti \|*

**Just as family members become one unit, the combination of svaras are called grama. Sadja-grama is the first, then madhayma-grama and then gandhara-grama. These are the three gramas. The three gramakas - nandavarta, jirnUta and subahdra arise from the three gramas - sadja, madhyama and gandhara.**

The characteristics of miircha are stated:

*kramātsvarāṇāṁ saptānāmārohaścāvarohaṇam \|*  
*sā mūrchetyucyate grāmasthā etāḥ sapta sapta ca \|\| iti \|*

**The ascending and descending scale of seven svaras, based on the gramas, is called miircha. There are seven for each grama.**

The sadja, madhyma and gandara gramas are based on different combinations of svaras. The miirchana consists of ascending and descending scales on each note. In each grama there are seven miirchanas. The total is twenty-one miirchanas.

### Text 4

*anupama-kara-śākhopātta-rādhāṅgulīko*  
*laghu laghu kusumānāṁ paryaṭan vāṭikāyām \|*  
*sarabhasam anugītaś citra-kaṇṭhībhir uccair*  
*vraja-nava-yuvatībhir bhāti kuñje vihārī \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, holding the fingers of Radha’s right hand in his left hand, strolling slowly in the flower garden with her, as he is joyfully and loudly praised by her sakhis in sweet, amazing voices, shines in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

He wanders in Vrndavana with his dear associates. He holds the fingers of Radha’s right hand in the fingers (kara-sakha) of his incomparable left hand. Kara-sakha means finger according to Amara-kosa. He slowly wanders about with her in the flower garden (yatikayam). He is praised joyfully (sarabhasam) and loudly by the young girls of Vraja, Radha’s sakhls, in astonishing, sweet voices. Rabhasa means either quickly or joyfully according to Haima.

### Text 5

*ahiripu-kṛta-lāsye kīcakārabdha-vādye*  
*vraja-giri-taṭa-raṅge bhṛṅga-saṅgīta-bhāji \|*  
*viracita-paricaryāś citra-tauryatrikeṇa*  
*stimita-karaṇa-vṛttir bhāti kuñje vihārī \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, served by amazing musical performance at the arena on a plateau of Govardhana, where peacocks dance, bamboos sound in the wind, and bees sing, causing his senses to melt, shines in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

Govardhana, the best servant, sometimes satisfied Krsna accompanied by the gopis where there was song, dance and instrumental music. He is served (viracita-paricaryah) by dance, instruments and song at the arena on the plateau of Govardhana. Ranga means dancing arena. Taurya-trikam means performance of dancing, singing and instrumental music according to Amara-kosa. This performance is produced using the arena on Govardhana. At that place there is dancing (lasya) done by the peacocks (ahi-ripu). Lasyam means dancing according to Amara-kosa. At that place there is instrumental music of hollow bamboos (kicaka). Kicdka means bamboo. The wind produces sound in it according to Amara-kosa. There, the bees sing by their buzzing. His sense functions become moist on experiencing the performance.

### Text 6

*diśi diśi śuka-śārī-maṇḍalair gūḍha-līlāḥ*  
*prakaṭam anupaṭhadbhir nirmitāś carya-pūraḥ \|*  
*tad atirahasi vṛttaṁ preyasī-karṇa-mūle*  
*smita-mukham abhijalpan bhāti kuñje vihārī \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, who is fully amazed by the parrots and sari birds that recite the couple’s intimate pastimes in all directions, and who, with smiling face, whispers their conversations in Radha’s ear in a solitary place, shines in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

He experiences amazement from the flocks of parrots and saris playing in all directions. The reason is explained. They repeat clearly his secret pastimes. In private (atirahasi) he speaks those conversations of the parrots in Radha’s ear while smiling (smita-mukham). He smiles in amazement, wondering how the parrots knew about their gambling match since they were not there.

### Text 7

*tava cikura-kadambaṁ stambhate prekṣya kekī*  
*nayana-kamala-lakṣmīr vandate kṛṣṇa-sāraḥ \|*  
*alir alam alakāntaṁ nauti paśyeti rādhāṁ*  
*sumadhuram anuśaṁsan bhāti kuñje vihārī \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, praising sweet Radha by saying, “The peacock, seeing your hair bound up, becomes stunned; the deer offers respects to the beauty of your lotus eyes; and the bee profusely praises your locks,” shines in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna praises Radha’s limbs using indirect words. He speaks to Radha these words (iti). О Radha! The peacock (kekl), seeing your hair, becomes stunned.

“Her hair decorated with flowers derides my peacock tail.” Thus, the peacock becomes stunned. The deer offers respects (vandate) to the beauty of your lotus eyes. “Her eyes are more beautiful than my eyes.” Thus, the deer offers respects. The bee praises (nauti) your locks of hair. “Her locks are fickler than my fickleness.” Thus, the bee praises her. This is comparison by exclusion.

### Text 8

*madana-tarala-bālā-cakravālena viṣvag-*  
*vividha-vara-kalānāṁ śikṣayā sevyamānaḥ \|*  
*skhalita-cikura-veśe skandha-deśe priyāyāḥ*  
*prathita-pṛthula-bāhur bhāti kuñje vihārī \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda, served devotedly by the group of gopis unsteady with love, teaching him various excellent arts, whose broad arm is offered to Radha’s shoulder where her locks had fallen, shines in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

He is served with complete devotion (visvak) by groups (cakravalena) of girls like Lalita (bald), unsteady with love (madana-tarala), teaching various excellent arts.

Tarala means unsteady according to Visva. Being taught by the group of girls indicates that he is most skillful at learning. One should not say that since he is omniscient it is inappropriate to teach him the arts. There is no fault since his svardpa-sakti makes these far-sighted arrangements. Sukadeva says:

*tad eva dhruvam unninye tasyai mānaṁ ca bahvadāt*

**When another gopi sang in the dhruva style, Krsna praised her even more. (SB 10.33.9)**

The special beauty is described. Prathitah means offered.

### Text 9

*idam anupama-līlā-hāri kuñje-vihārī*  
*smaraṇa-padam adhīte tuṣṭa-dhīr aṣṭakaṁ yaḥ \|*  
*nija-guṇa-vṛtayā śrī-rādhayā rādhitas taṁ*  
*nayati nija-padābjaṁ kuñja-sadmādhirājaḥ \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, king of the bowers, worshipped by Radha, surrounded by her friends, brings to his lotus feet the person who studies this astaka, a place attractive with incomparable pastimes for remembering Krsna in the bower.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of studying this astaka is described.

Krsna, king of the bowers, brings the person who studies this astaka to his lotus feet. The astaka is described. It is the place (padam), attractive with incomparable pastimes, because they relate to Radha’s group, for remembering the player in the bower. Krsna is worshipped by Radha, the queen of the bower. The meter is malini.

*nanamayayayuteyaṁ mālinī bhogilokaiḥ*

**Malini: sss sss 111 sll sll (па, na, ma, ya, ya) with caesura after the eighth syllable and seven syllables following it.**

This and the following astaka are in this meter.

Thus, the second kunja-vihari astaka has been explained.

## mukundāṣṭakam

**śrīmukundāya namaḥ \|**

**I offer respects to Mukunda.**

### Text 1

*balabhid-upala-kānti-drohiṇi śrīmad-aṅge*  
*ghusṛṇa-rasa-vilāsaiḥ suṣṭhu gāndharvikāyāḥ \|*  
*sva-madana-nṛpa-śobhāṁ vardhayan deha-rājye*  
*praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ  mukundaḥ \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, who increases his amorous beauty on the kingdom of Radha’s body when her kunkuma gets smeared on his limbs which defeat the beauty of a sapphire, be visibleto my eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises Mukunda in this astaka.

May Mukunda bestow the cherished fulfillment of my eyes. May Mukunda be visible to my eyes. Mukunda means he whose smile is like kunda flowers shining in his mouth (mukha). Or it means “he who gives (da) liberation (mukti).” Because of suffering in separation, he becomes visible, or because of suffering in samsara he becomes the object of meditation. This is proper usage (mukti-da = mukunda) according to prsodaradlni yathopadistam: The elision, augment and mutation of letters to be seen in prsodara, etc., though not found taught in treatises of Grammar, are valid, to that extent and in the mode, as taught by the usage of the sages. (Panini Sutras 6.3.109)

What does he do? By her kunkuma (ghusrna-rasa) smeared on his limbs, he increases the beauty of his passion (king Cupid) on the kingdom of Radha’s body. His limbs include his forehead and chest. Ghusrna means kunkuma according to Halayudha. The

asangati alankara is used. It is explained in Kavya-kaustubha as follows:

*asaṁgatirbhavedbhinnadeśatve hetukāryayoḥ*

**When two things related to each other as cause and effect are simultaneously residing in two totally different places, it is termed disconnection (asangati).**

His limbs are described. They conquer the beauty of sapphires (balabhid-upala). This means his limbs shine more brilliantly than sapphires.

### Text 2

*udita-vidhu-parārdha-jyotir ullaṅghi-vaktro*  
*nava-taruṇima-rajyad-bālya-śeṣātiramyaḥ \|*  
*pariṣadi lalitālīṁ dolayan kuṇḍalābhyāṁ*  
*praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, whose face derides the light of billions of rising moons, who is attractive with new youth in the last years of childhood, who makes Radha in her group unsteady by his earrings, be visible to my eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

His face derides the light of billions of rising moons. His face is incomparably beautiful. Jyoti means light according to Nanartha-varga. He is charming because he is at the end of childhood, which is attractive (rajyat) with new youth. He makes Radha, the friend of Lalita (.lalitallm), situated among the assembly of young women (parisadi), tremble by the beauty of his earrings.

### Text 3

*kanaka-nivaha-śobhānandi pītaṁ nitambe*  
*tad-upari navaraktaṁ vastram itthaṁ dadhānaḥ \|*  
*priyam iva kila varṇaṁ rāga-yuktaṁ priyāyāḥ*  
*praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, who wears a yellow cloth, defeating the beauty of heaps of gold, with red cloth placed above that, as if showing by that color the love of Radha, which stimulates his affection, be visible to my eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

His absorption in Radha is described. He wears a yellow cloth on his hips and above that a red upper cloth. There is comparison with the complexion of Radha (yellow), which is combined with her attraction (red in color). Why does he wear the cloth? It is endowed with the color of her attraction causing affection in him (priyam).

Though nitamba is used in Amara-kosa to mean a woman’s hips, it refers to hips in general. That is meaning given by Halayudha and others.

### Text 4

*surabhi-kusuma-vṛndair vāsitāmbhaḥ-samṛddhe*  
*priya-sarasi nidāghe sāyam ālī-parītām \|*  
*madana-janaka-sekaiḥ khelayann eva rādhāṁ*  
*praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, who plays with Radha and her sakhis in the summer evening at Radha-kunda, full of fragrant flowers and fragrant water, by splashing water which inflamed their love, be visible to my eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

He plays with his beloveds in Radha-kunda. He plays with Radha accompanied by her sakhis at Radha-kunda (priya-sarasi) in the summer (nidaghe), by splashing water released from instruments, which stimulates their love. The pond is described. It was filled with fragrant flower clusters and fragrant water (vasitambhah).

### Text 5

*parimalam iha labdhvā hanta gāndharvikāyāḥ*  
*pulakita-tanur uccair unmadas tat-kṣaṇena \|*  
*nikhila-vipina-deśān vāsitān eva jighran*  
*praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, whose hairs stand on end by smelling Radha’s fragrance, who becomes immediately frenzied, and who smells the perfumes from all the forests, be visible to my eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

When Radha comes to Vrndavana, he is delighted by her fragrance. The meaning is clear. He became frenzied (unmadah).

### Text 6

*praṇihita-bhuja-daṇḍaḥ skandha-deśe varāṅgyāḥ*  
*smita-vikasita-gaṇḍe kīrtidā-kanyakāyāḥ \|*  
*manasija-jani-saukhyaṁ cumbanenaiva tanvan*  
*praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, who places his arm on Radha’s shoulder and spreads amorous bliss by kissing her on her cheek while she breaks into a smile, be visible to my eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

He searches for Radha because of her fragrance and finding her, plays with her.

He places his rod-like arm on the shoulder of Radha, daughter of Kirtida, wife of King Vrsabhanu. He spreads amorous, agitating (manasi-ja-jani) bliss by a kiss on her cheek, which blossoms with a smile. These actions show his skill. The alankara is vibhavana. (By describing effects, the causes can be imagined.) Such bliss may arise even without intimate amorous love.

### Text 7

*pramada-danuja-goṣṭhyāḥ ko’pi saṁvarta-vahnir*  
*vraja-bhuvi kila pitror mūrtimān sneha-puñjaḥ \|*  
*prathama-rasa-mahendraḥ śyāmalo rādhikāyāḥ*  
*praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, who is the fire of destruction for a host of wild demons, who is a pile of affection for his parents in Vraja and who is the dark presiding deity of madhurya-rasa for Radha, be visible to my eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

Constantly the object of affection for his loving mother and father, as a courageous hero, he is the cause of great attraction for the beautiful women. He is the fire of final devastation (samvarta-vahnih) for the host of wild demons (danuja). Samvarta means pralaya according to Amara-kosa. He is the very form of abundant affection of his father and mother, Nanda and Yasoda (pitroh). Pitroh expresses both father and mother according to pita, matra: the word pitr (father), when spoken of along with matr (mother), is optionally left alone. (Panini Sutras 1.2.70) He is the presiding deity of madhurya-rasa (prathama-rasa-mahendra) for Radha. He is experienced in this way by Radha.

### Text 8

*svakadana-kathayāṅgīkṛtya mṛdvīṁ viśākhāṁ*  
*kṛta-caṭu lalitāṁ tu prārthayan prauḍha-śīlām \|*  
*praṇaya-vidhura-rādhā-māna-vidhvaṁsanāya*  
*praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, who, accepting mild Visakha by speaking of his own misery, prays to stubborn Lalita using sweet words for breaking the anger of Radha who suffers with affection, be visible to my eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

Sometimes he personally is busy dissolving the anger of Radha. Accepting mild Visakha by speaking of his own misery, getting her on his side, he prays to stubborn Lalita using sweet words (catu). Catu means affectionate words according to Halayudha.

“O Lalita! You are my only benefactor. Radha is merciless with me. If you too become like a thunderbolt, what shelter do I have, though I am in great pain and accept her as my beloved.” He speaks pleasing words, making his request. The result of these actions is described. The purpose is for breaking the anger of Radha who suffers with affection. “Since Krsna is in love with other women, Radha’s anger should make him happy.” That cannot be. If one gives up drinking a cooling drink and instead drinks an astringent drink, the maker of the cooling drink, who has made that drink to make him happy will become angry.

### Text 9

*paripaṭhati mukundasyāṣṭakaṁ kākubhir yaḥ*  
*sakala-viṣaya-saṅgāt saṁniyamyendriyāṇi \|*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājo darśayan svaṁ sa-rādhe*  
*svajana-gaṇana-madhye taṁ priyāyās tanoti \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The son of Nanda shows himself and counts among the associates of Radha that person who, withdrawing his senses from all sense objects, recites the Mukundastaka in a choked voice with joy.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of reciting this astaka, which produces qualities like mental control, is explained. The person, withdrawing into the mind his ear, skin, eye, tongue and nose, which are attached to sound, touch, form, taste and smell, from those objects, and just maintaining his body, while concentrating his mind on Mukunda with Radha, should recite the Mukundastaka in a choked voice with joy. The son of Nanda accepts (tanoti) that person as one among the associates of Radha. Sruti also indicates that the devotee develops mental control.

*tasmād evaṁ vicchānto dānta uparatas titikṣuḥ śraddhāvitto bhūtvātmany evātmānaṁ paśyed*

**Knowing this, having faith, peace, control of the senses and mind, and tolerance, he sees the Lord in the self. (Brhad-aranyaka Upanisad 4.4.23)**

Thus, Mukundastaka has been explained.

## vraja-navayuva-rājāṣṭakam

**namaḥ śrīgokulayuvarājāya \|**

**I offer respects to the prince of Gokula.**

### Text 1

*mudira-madam udāraṁ mardayann aṅga-kāntyā*  
*vasana-ruci-nirastāmbhoja-kiñjalka-śobhaḥ \|*  
*taruṇima-taraṇīkṣāviklavad-bālya-candro*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājaḥ kāṅkṣitaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja, who crushes the great pride of the cloud by the beauty of his limbs, whose lustrous cloth defeats the beauty of lotus stamens, whose kaisora sun terrifies the moon of his childhood, fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises the youthful prince of Vraja in this astaka. May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja (vraja-nava-yuva-rajah'), fulfill my desires (kanksitam krsista). He was given responsibility for the kingdom by his father since Nanda was capable of giving all things. Mudira means cloud. Kinjalka means stamens. The moon of his childhood (balya-candrah) is terrified on seeing the appearance of the sun of the first state of his kaisora age (tarunima). He now gives up his fickle nature. Youth is superior to childhood because of its extraordinary features.

### Text 2

*pitur aniśama-gaṇya-prāṇa-nirmanthanīyaḥ*  
*kalita-tanur ivāddhā mātṛ-vātsalya-puñjaḥ \|*  
*anuguṇa-guru-goṣṭhī-dṛṣṭi-pīyūṣa-vartir*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājaḥ kāṅkṣitaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja, who is worthy of worship by unlimited pranas of Nanda, who is a heap of affection for his mother, being as if directly embraced by her, who is sweet collyrium for the eyes of favorable elders, fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

Affection of his father and others increases when he is made the ruler of Vraja. He is worthy of being worshipped (in aratrika) by unlimited pranas of Nanda at every moment. He is a heap of affection for Yasoda. He is as if being directly (addha) held (kalita-tanuh). He is a sweet cosmetic mark (vartih) for the eyes (drsti) of the favorable (anuguna) elders. Varti means ointment or collyrium according to Medini. The comparison is rupaka. He gives happiness and is bright like collyrium.

### Text 3

*akhila-jagati jāgran-mugdha-vaidagdhya-caryā-*  
*prathama-gurur udagra-sthāma viśrāma-saudhaḥ \|*  
*anupama-guṇa-rājī-rañjitāśeṣa-bandhur*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājaḥ kāṅkṣitaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja, who is the first guru for attractive arts praised in all the worlds, who has an excellent glorious palace for relaxing, who attracts unlimited relatives by his many incomparable qualities, fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the first teacher of charming arts praised (jagrat) in all the world. The arts arose from him. He has a huge palace (saudhah) for happily residing, which is most glorious or strong (udagra-sthama). Sthama means prana, strength or glory according to Halayudha. Saudha is a palace according to Amara-kosa. All his relatives are attracted by his many most excellent qualities like friendship and good disposition.

Bandhu means relative and associates according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 4

*api madana-parārdhair duṣkaraṁ vikriyormiṁ*  
*yuvatiṣu nidadhāno bhrū-dhanur dhūnanena \|*  
*priya-sahacara-varga-prāṇa-mīnāmbu-rāśir*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājaḥ kāṅkṣitaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja, who, just by moving his bow-like brow, produces in the gopis waves of transformations that cannot be replicated by billions of Cupids, and who is the life of his dear friends like the ocean is for fish, fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

He offers (nidadhanah) to the gopis, by shaking his bow-like brow, waves of transformations (vikiryortnitn) which crush the heart and cannot be replicated by billions of Cupids. This is the alankara of vibhdvand. Without using arrows, he can pierce their hearts. The rest is clear. He is a place of happiness for his followers like the ocean is for the fish.

### Text 5

*nayana-śṛṇi-vinoda-kṣobhitānaṅganāgon*  
*mathita-gahana-rādhā-citta-kāsāra-garbhaḥ \|*  
*praṇaya-rasa-marandāsvāda-līlā-ṣaḍ-aṅghrir*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājaḥ kāṅkṣitaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja, who agitates Radha’s lake-like heart through the elephant of love deep within, by striking it with the goad of his eyes, who is a bee absorbed in pastimes of tasting the honey of Radha’s rasa of love, fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

He agitates the unfathomable depths of Radha’s lake-like (kasard) heart by the elephant of love disturbed by the beating of the goad (srnt) of his glances. Srni is a goad according to Amara-kosa. Kasara is a lake. Her heart is very deep (garbhah). He is a bee in the pastimes of tasting honey (maranda) of Radha’s rasa of affection. Maranda means honey according to Haima.

### Text 6

*anupadam udayantyā rādhikāsaṅga-siddhyā*  
*sthagita-pṛthur athāṅga-dvandva-rāgānubandhaḥ \|*  
*madhurima-madhu-dhārā-dhoraṇīnām udanvān*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājaḥ kāṅkṣitaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja, an ocean with many waves of charming sweetness, the effects of whose separation from Radha, increasing at every moment, stuns the attachment of a cakravaka couple, fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of his not meeting Radha, which manifests at every moment, stuns the attachment of a couple of excellent (prthu) cakravaka birds. Rathanga means cakravaka. His attachment derides the attachment of the cakravakas, since they experience separation only at night. He is an ocean (udanvan) of many (dhoraninam) waves of charming sweetness (madhurima-madhu) of his form, words and actions. Dhorani means a row according to Haima. Udanvan is the ocean according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 7

*alaghu-kuṭila-rādhā-dṛṣṭi-vārī-niruddha-*  
*trijagad-aparatantroddāma-ceto-gajendraḥ \|*  
*sukha-mukhara-viśākhā-narmaṇā smera-vaktro*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājaḥ kāṅkṣitaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja, whose strong, elephant-like heart, unfettered by the three worlds, is controlled by the ropes of Radha’s excellent, crooked glances, and who smiles at the jokes of joyfully loquacious Visakha, fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

The strong (uddama) elephant of his heart, uncontrolled by three worlds, is controlled by the ropes of Radha’s excellent (alaghu) crooked glances.

He smiles because of the jokes of Visakha, who talks plentifully with joy (sukha-mukhara) since she understands that he is controlled by Radha. Many times, you have said, “I am not controlled by the gopis’ triumphant hearts. I am independent minded.” Why do you now request me repeatedly for touching Radha’s limbs? We should worship the independent heart of you, who are like a wild horse. He smiles when he hears her jokes. I have been conquered by her. Thus, he smiles.

### Text 8

*tvayi rahasi milantyāṁ sambhramanyāsabhugnāpy*  
*uṣasi sakhi tavālī-mekhalā paśya bhāti \|*  
*iti vivṛta-rahasyair hrepayann eva rādhāṁ*  
*vraja-nava-yuva-rājaḥ kāṅkṣitaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, enthroned by Nanda as the authority in Vraja, who embarrasses Radha by revealing intimate pastimes, saying, “O Visakha! Look! This belt of bells, put on crookedly out of fear at dawn when she met you privately, shines nicely,” fulfill my desires.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse describes Krsna joking with Visakha whom he meets after he has played with Radha who had been dressed by Visakha.

“O Visakha! Your friend Radha, like lightning on a cloud, has been fickle with me. Your friend’s belt of bells is crooked (bhugna) since it was put on in haste out of fear, on your meeting her in a solitary place.” It actually becomes more beautiful according to the saying, “How can anything beautiful become ugly?” Bhugna means crooked according to Halayudha. Look! Seeing this, you can understand her and my character. In this way, he embarrasses Radha by revealing the intimate pastimes.

### Text 9

*vraja-nava-yuva-rājasyāṣṭakaṁ tuṣṭa-buddhiḥ*  
*kalita-vara-vilāsaṁ yaḥ prayatnād adhīte \|*  
*parijana-gaṇanāyāṁ nāma tasyānurajyan*  
*vilikhati kila vṛndāraṇya-rājñī-rasajñaḥ \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The rasika of Vnidavana’s queen, becoming attracted to him, writes among his associates the name of that person who carefully studies the astaka of Vraja’s youthful prince, which describes excellent pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

The result of reciting the astaka is described. Kalita means described. The astaka describes excellent pastimes. The rasika (rasajnah) of the queen of Vrndavana is Krsna.

Thus Vraja-nava-yuva-rajastaka has been explained.

## praṇāma-praṇaya-stavaḥ

**namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇāya \|**

**I offer respects to Sri Krsna.**

### Text 1

*kandarpa-koṭi-ramyāya sphurad-indīvara-tviṣe \|*  
*jagan-mohana-līlāya namo gopendra-sūnave \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the son of Nanda, more attractive than a million Cupids, possessing the complexion of shining sapphire, performing pastimes that enchant the universe.**

**Комментарий:**

The author pleases Krsna by offering respects (pranama) since Krsna is fond of pranamas offered by the devotee. I offer respects to Krsna, the son of Nanda. One remembers the phrase pasupangajaya (son of the cowherd) in (SB 10.14.1. Krsna was Nanda’s legitimate son. The rest is clear.

### Text 2

*kṛṣṇalā-kṛta-hārāya kṛṣṇa-lāvaṇya-śāline \|*  
*kṛṣṇākūla-karīndrāya kṛṣṇāya karavai namaḥ \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna, who wears a necklace of gunja berries, who has the beauty of sapphire, who is an elephant playing on the bank of the Yamuna.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsnala means gunja berry. He is like a central jewel made of sapphire (krsnadavanya). He is an elephant (karindraya) on the bank of the Yamuna (krsna). In Padma Parana, Yamuna is described as nllotpala-dala-syamam: dark like the petal of a blue lotus. He plays on the bank in that form.

### Text 3

*sarvānanda-kadambāya kandamba-kusuma-sraje \|*  
*namaḥ premāvalambāya pralambāri-kanīyase \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna whose form is the total of all bliss, who wears a garland of kadamba flowers, who supports his devotee’s prema and is the younger brother of Balarama.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the form of all types of bliss (sarvananda-kadambaya). Sarva means all or complete according to Haima. He is full, concentrated happiness. Or Krsna is he from whom comes all types of bliss. He is the cause of all happiness. I offer respects to Krsna who is the support for the devotee’s prema (premavalambaya). Prema is the cause of attaining him. Or he gives life to the prema of his devotee.

*visṛjati hṛdayaṁ na yasya sākṣād dharir avaśābhihito'py aghaugha-nāśaḥ \| praṇaya-rasanayā dhṛtāṅghri-padmaḥ sa bhavati bhāgavata pradhāna uktaḥ \|\|*

**He who binds the lotus feet of the Lord by ropes of love, and whose heart the Lord, destroyer of heaps of sin, does not leave, even if beckoned accidentally, is called the best of devotees. (SB 11.2.55)**

He is the younger brother of Balarama (pralambari).

### Text 4

*kuṇḍala-sphurad-aṁsāya vaṁśāyatta-mukha-śriye \|*  
*rādhā-mānasa-haṁsāya vrajottaṁsāya te namaḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to you, whose shoulders shine from the luster of your earrings, whose mouth is made beautiful by the flute, who swims like a swan in Radha’s heart, who is the head ornament of the people of Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

His shoulders become beautiful from the luster of his earrings. His mouth is beautifully contracted by playing the flute. He is a swan in the lake-like heart of Radha. He swims like a swan in her heart. Manasa means heart and also a lake called Manasa in the

Himalayas. This is riipaka alankara with a pun. He is the head ornament made of flowers (uttamsdya) of Vraja’s people.

### Text 5

*namaḥ śikhaṇḍa-cūḍāya daṇḍa-maṇḍita-pāṇaye \|*  
*kuṇḍalī-kṛta-puṣpāya puṇḍarīkekṣaṇāya te \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to you, whose top knot is decorated with a peacock feather, whose hand holds a stick, who wears flowers as earrings, whose eyes are like lotuses.**

**Комментарий:**

Your hair is kissed by a peacock feather. Ciida means hair tied on the head according to Amara-kosa. His hand is decorated with a stick embedded with gems (danda). He makes flowers into earrings. He ornaments his ears with flower earrings. He has lotus eyes.

### Text 6

*rādhikā-prema-mādhvīka-mādhurī-muditāntaram \|*  
*kandarpa-vṛnda-saundaryaṁ govindam abhivādaye \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Govinda, whose heart is joyous from the sweetness of Radha’s intoxicating prema, who possesses the beauty of a host of Cupids.**

**Комментарий:**

Abhivadaye means I offer respects.

### Text 7

*śṛṅgāra-rasa-śṛṅgāraṁ karṇikārātta-karṇikam \|*  
*vande śriyā navābhrāṇāṁ bibhrāṇaṁ vibhramaṁ harim \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Hari, who is the ornament of madhurya-rasa, who wears karnika flowers as ear ornaments, who is mistaken for fresh clouds because of his bodily beauty.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the ornament (srhgaram) of madhurya-rasa (srngara-rasa'). He has karnika ear ornaments made of karnikara flowers. Karnika is an ear ornament according to Amara-kosa. He is mistaken (vibhrama) for fresh clouds (navabhranam) because of the beauty of his form (sriya). Vibhrama means mistake according to Visvalocana.

### Text 8

*sādhvī-vrata-maṇi-vrāta-paśyato-hara-veṇave \|*  
*kahlāra-kṛta-cūḍāya śaṅkha-cūḍa-bhide namaḥ \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to he whose flute steals in plain sight the gems of vows of the chaste girls, who wears water lilies on his head, and who killed Sarikhactida.**

**Комментарий:**

His flute steals before the eyes (pasyato hard) the heap of jewels (mani-vrata) of the chaste gopts’s steadiness in dharma (yratd). The person who steals while being seen is called pasyatoharah according to Haima. The genitive pasyatah is not dissolved in the compound. He attracts the young girls by force using his flute. He makes a head ornament from white water lilies (kdhlard). Kahlara is water lily according to Amara-kosa. He destroyed the Yaksa Saiikhacuda, servant of Kamsa.

### Text 9

*rādhikādhara-bandhūka-makaranda-madhuvratam \|*  
*daitya-sindhura-pārīndraṁ vande gopendra-nandanam \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the son of Nanda who is a bee in the honey of Radha’s lips which are red like bandhujiva flowers, who is a lion for the elephant-like demons.**

**Комментарий:**

He is a bee in the honey of Radha’s lips which are red like bandhujiva (bandhiika) flowers. He is a lion (parindram) for the elephant-like (sindhura) demons. He destroys them.

### Text 10

*barhendrāyudha-ramyāya jagaj-jīvana-dāyine \|*  
*rādhā-vidyud-vṛtāṅgāya kṛṣṇāmbhodāya te namaḥ \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who is attractive with rainbow-like peacock feathers, who gives life to the universe, who is a black cloud whose limbs are surrounded by the lighting of Radha.**

**Комментарий:**

He is attractive with a peacock feather like a rainbow (indrayudha). Barha means peacock feather and ayudha means weapon according to Amara-kosa. He gives life in the form of water to the universe. This is rupaka concerning all the items mentioned in the verse, with a combination of various components (rainbow, rain, cloud).

### Text 11

*premāndha-ballavī-vṛnda-locanendīvarendave \|*  
*kāśmīra-tilakāḍhyāya namaḥ pītāmbarāya te \|\|11\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who is the moon for the lotus eyes of all the gopis blinded by prema, who wears kunkuma tilaka and yellow cloth.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the moon (indave) for the lotus eyes of all the gopis blinded by prema. He makes their eyes blossom. He is endowed (adhyayd) with tilaka made of kunkuma (kdsmira'). Kasmlra means kunkuma according to Visva.

### Text 12

*gīrvāṇeśa-madoddāma dāva-nirvāṇa-nīradam \|*  
*kandūkī-kṛta-śailendraṁ vande gokula-bāndhavam \|\|12\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the cloud who destroyed the great forest fire of Indra’s pride, who made Govardhana into a toy ball, and who is the friend of Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

He is a cloud (nlradam) who destroys the great (uddama) forest fire of Indra’s pride. Ddva means forest fire according to Halayudha. The rest is clear.

### Text 13

*dainyārṇave nimagno’smi mantu-grāva-bharārditaḥ \|*  
*duṣṭe kāruṇya-pārīṇa mayi kṛṣṇa kṛpāṁ kuru \|\|13\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I am submerged in an ocean of misfortune. O ocean of mercy! I am pained by a load of stones in the form of offenses. Please be merciful to me.**

**Комментарий:**

Revealing his own faults, the author prays for mercy. I am submerged in an ocean of misfortune (dainyarnave). О ocean of mercy (karunya-parina)! I am pained by a load of stones (grava) in the form of offenses (mantu). Mantu means offense according to Amara-kosa. Be merciful to me, wicked (duste), because of the fault of offenses, since you are an ocean of mercy. This is a confession (vijnapti) expressing dainya. It becomes a prayer (samprarthanatmika) and expression of longing (lalasamayi prarthana).

It is said in Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu:

*samprārthanātmikā dainyabodhikā lālasāmayī \|*  
*ityādirvividhā dhīraiḥ kṛṣṇe vijñaptirīritā \|\|*

**The wise have explained that there are various types of entreaties to Krsna, such as prayers, admission of incompetence and expressions of longing. (BRS 1.2.152)**

*ādhāro’py aparādhānām aviveka-hato’py aham \|*  
*tvat-kāruṇya-pratīkṣo’smi prasīda mayi mādhava \|\|14\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Though I am a mine of offenses and afflicted by lack of good judgement, I expect your mercy. Please be merciful to me, О Madhava!**

**Комментарий:**

“Why should I show mercy to you, who are so wicked?”

Though I am a mine of offenses, afflicted with lack of discrimination of what is the essence and what is not the essence, I observe (pratiksa) your mercy devoid of considering low or high. О Madhava! Show mercy to me, such a person. If your mercy is not given, those who speak of you, the devotees would be shamed.

Thus, the stava called pranama-pranaya has been explained.

## hari-kusuma-stavakam

**śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ**

**I offer respects to Sri Krsna.**

### Text 1

*gati-gañjita-mattatara-dviradaṁ*  
*rada-nindita-sundara-kunda-madam \|*  
*madanārbuda-rūpa-mada-ghna-ruciṁ*  
*rucira-smita-mañjari mañju-mukham \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna, whose gait derides that of an intoxicated elephant, whose teeth criticize the pride of beautiful jasmine flowers, whose beauty destroys billions of Cupids’ pride in their beauty, whose face is radiant with a blossoming smile.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to Hari (verb is in verse eleven). How is he described? By his gait (gati) he derides (ganjita) an intoxicated elephant (dviradam). By his teeth he criticizes the pride of beautiful jasmine buds. His beauty destroys billions of Cupids’ pride in their beauty. His face is attractive with a radiant (rucira'), blossoming smile (smita-manjari).

### Text 2

*mukharīkṛta-veṇu-hṛta-pramadaṁ*  
*mada-valgita-locana-tāmarasam \|*  
*rasa-pūra-vikāsaka-keli-paraṁ*  
*paramārtha-parāyaṇa-loka-gatim \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who attracts the women by playing his flute, whose lotus eyes are red with intoxicating youth, who is absorbed in pastimes which manifest a variety of rasas and who is the shelter of devotees having understanding of tattva.**

**Комментарий:**

He attracts the women by playing (mukhari-krta) his flute. He has lotus (tamarasam) eyes attractive with redness (yalgita) of intoxicating youth (mada). He is absorbed (param) in pastimes which reveal waves of rasa such as sakhya and hasya. He is the shelter (method and goal) of surrendered persons on the path of bhakti with understanding of tattva (paramartha).

### Text 3

*gati-maṇḍita-yāmuna-tīra-bhuvaṁ*  
*bhuvaneśvara-vandita-cāru-padam \|*  
*padakojjvala-komala-kaṇṭha-rucaṁ*  
*rucakātta-viśeṣaka-valgutaram \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who decorates the land on the bank of the Yamuna with the marks on his feet as he walks, whose attractive feet are worshipped by all devatas, the beauty of whose neck shines with a padaka, and who is most attractive with gorocana tilaka.**

**Комментарий:**

He decorates the land on the bank of the Yamuna with the marks on his feet, flag, thunderbolt, etc., when he walks (gati). His attractive (caru) feet are worshipped by Brahma, Siva and other controllers of the world. He is beautiful with a tender neck bright with a padaka ornament on his chest. He is attractive (valgutaram) with tilaka (visesaka) made of gorocana (rucaka). Rucaka means gorocana according to Visva. Visesaka means tilaka according to Halayudha.

### Text 4

*tarala-pracalāka-parīta-śikhaṁ*  
*śikharīndra-dhṛti pratipanna-bhujam \|*  
*bhujagendra-phaṇāṅgaṇa-raṅga-dharaṁ*  
*dhara-kandara-khelana-lubdha-hṛdam \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna whose head is decorated with a trembling peacock feather, whose left arm boldly lifts Govardhana, who makes a dancing arena on Kaliya’s hoods, whose heart is greedy to play in the mountain caves.**

**Комментарий:**

The hair on his head is endowed (pafita) with a trembling (tarala) peacock feather (pracalaka). Pracalaka means peacock feather according to Halayudha. His left arm is endowed with boldness to lift Govardhana (sikharindra). He made the arena of the hoods of Kaliya a place for performing dancing and singing (ranga-dharam). His heart is greedy to play in the mountain caves (dhara-kandara).

### Text 5

*hṛdayālu-suhṛd-gaṇa-datta-mahaṁ*  
*mahanīya-kathā-kula-dhūta-kalim \|*  
*kalitākhila-durjaya-bāhu-balaṁ*  
*bala-ballava-śāvaka-saṁnihitam \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who gives joy to his affectionate friends, who destroys Kali-yuga by his worshippable topics, whose arms are unconquerable in strength, who is accompanied by Balarama and cowherd boys.**

**Комментарий:**

He gives joy (maham) to his affectionate (hrdayalu) friends. Hrdayalu means good hearted according to Amara-kosa. Maha means joyous festival. He destroys Kali-yuga, the last yuga by many worshippable stories of his exploits. Kali is the last yuga according to Haima. Or he destroys quarrels (kali) among the gopis. The strength of his arms cannot be conquered by anyone. He is accompanied by Balarama and by cowherd boys (ballava-savaka).

### Text 6

*hita-sādhu-samīhita-kalpa-taruṁ*  
*taruṇī-gaṇa-nūtana-puṣpa-śaram \|*  
*śaraṇāgata-rakṣaṇa-dakṣatamaṁ*  
*tam asādhu-kulotpala-caṇḍa-karam \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who fulfills the desires of the favorable devotees, who is a new Cupid for the young girls, who is most skillful at protecting the surrendered, who is the harsh sun for the lotus-like demons.**

**Комментарий:**

He fulfills the desires (samihita) of the devotees following him (hita). He is fresh Cupid (puspa-saram) for the young girls. He is most skillful at protecting those who are surrendered. He is the sun (candakaram) for the blue lotuses who are groups of demons. Utpala is a blue lotus according to Halayudha. He restricts the demons.

### Text 7

*kara-padma-milat-kusuma-stavakaṁ*  
*baka-dānava-matta-karīndra-harim \|*  
*hariṇī-gaṇa-hāraka-veṇu-kalaṁ*  
*kala-kaṇṭha-ravojjvala-kaṇṭha-raṇam \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who holds in his lotus hands clusters of flowers, who is a lion tearing apart the mad elephant called the Бака demon, who attracts the women with the sound of his flute, whose voice is more brilliant than the cuckoo’s song.**

**Комментарий:**

He holds flower clusters(stavakam) in his lotus hands. He holds flower clusters in his right hand. Kusuma-stavakam also indicates meter of the work, also called danddka. This is called mudra alankara as explained in Kavya-kaustubha.

*dyotārthadyotanaṁ mudrā śabdaiḥ prakṛtavācibhiḥ*

**Indicating another meaning (such as author or title of work) by words having a different meaning in the context of the poem is called mudra.**

He is a lion tearing up the Baka demon, like a mad elephant. With the sound of his flute he attracts all the women (deer). Kala-kantha is cuckoo according to Halayudha.

### Text 8

*raṇa-khaṇḍita-durjana-puṇya-janaṁ*  
*jana-maṅgala-kīrti-latā-prabhavam \|*  
*bhava-sāgara-kumbha-janām aguṇaṁ*  
*guṇa-saṅga-vivarjita-bhakta-gaṇam \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who destroys the wicked demons in battle, whose fame spreads auspiciousness throughout the world, whose single quality dries up the ocean of ignorance like Agastya, whose devotees are free of the touch of the material gunas.**

**Комментарий:**

He destroyed the wicked Raksasas (punya-janam) in battle. Punya-jana means a Raksasa according to Amara-kosa. He produces (prabhavam) a creeper of fame which is auspicious for the world. His fame produces auspiciousness for the world.

His qualities are Agastya (kumbhaja) for the ocean of material existence. Just one designated (nama) quality dries up the ocean of ignorance, just as Agastya swallows the ocean. What to speak of all his qualities. His devotees are devoid of the touch of material gunas.

### Text 9

*gaṇanātiga-divya-guṇollasitaṁ*  
*smita-raśmi-sahodara-vaktra-varam \|*  
*vara-dṛpta-vṛṣāsura-dāra-ghanaṁ*  
*ghana-vibhrama-veśa-vihāramayam \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who has manifested attractive, unlimited qualities, whose excellent face is brother of the moon, who is a cloud for the forest fire of proud Vrsasura, whose pastimes and ornaments are intensely beautiful.**

**Комментарий:**

He has manifested (ullasitam) qualities related to his svariipa (divya) such as omnipotence, omniscience, friendship and mercy which are unlimited (gananatiga). He is excellent (varam) for his face which is like the brother of the moon (smita-rasmi). He is a cloud for the forest fire of extremely proud (vara-drpta) Vrsasura. He destroys the demon. His pastimes like activities in the bower and his decorations are profoundly (ghana) beautiful (.vibhrama).

### Text 10

*maya-putra-tamaḥ-kṣaya-pūrṇa-vidhuṁ*  
*vidhurīkṛta-dānava-rāja-kulam \|*  
*\[…\]*  
*kula-nandanam atra namāmi harim \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna who is the full moon which destroys the darkness of Vyomasura, who brings disaster to the dynasty of demons, and who gives joy to his family.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the full moon which destroys the darkness of Vyomasura (maya-putra).

He brought disaster (vidhuri-krta) to the dynasty of demons (danava-raja-kulam). Vidhura means trouble according to Dhananjaya. 1 offer respects to Krsna who gives joy to his family (kulam). The alankara is chekanuprasa (alliteration).

The characteristics of dandaka are given (of which Kusuma-stavaka is a subtype):

*sagaṇaḥ \| sakalaḥ khalu yatra bhavet tam iha pravadanti budhāḥ kusuma-stavakam*

**The wise call a dandaka with all sa ganas (ssl ssl ssl ssl, etc.) as kusuma-stavaka.**

Here there are 156 sa ganas in total, or four lines with 40 sa ganas (ssl) each.

### Text 11

*urasi parisphurad-indiram indindira-mandira-srajollasitam \|*  
*harim aṅganātimaṅgala-maṅgala-sac-candanaṁ vande \|\|11\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Hari who shines with Laksmi on his chest, who is beautiful with a garland which is the abode of bees, who is most auspicious for the young women and whose limbs shine with sandalwood.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises the Lord with arya dandaka.

I offer respects to Hari. He is described. The mark of Laksmi shines brightly on his chest. He is beautiful (ullasitam) with a Vaijayanti garland (sraja), the abode of bees (indindira). He is most auspicious for the young women (arigana). He attracts them. He shines with sandalwood on his limbs. Yamaha alankdra is used. It is described as follows:

*bhinnārthā saṁbhavatyarthe svaravyañjanasaṁhatiḥ \|*  
*krameṇa tena cedgacchedāvṛttiṁ yamakaṁ tadā \|\|*

**Repetition of phrases with same sound with different meaning is called yamdka. (Kavya-kaustubha)**

Thus hari-kusuma-stavaka has been explained.

## gāthā-cchandaḥ stavaḥ

**śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ**

**I offer respects to Sri Krsna**

### Text 1

*paritoṣita-gopa-vadhū-paṭalaṁ*  
*paṭalaṅghita-kāñcana-sāra-cayam \|*  
*racayantam udāra-vilāsa-kalāṁ*  
*sakalāñcita-pādam agādha-balam*  
*dhavalaṁ nava-kīrti-kulair amitam \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I remember Krsna who satisfies all the gopis, whose cloth derides a pile of fine gold, who manifests great playful arts, whose feet are worshipped by the devatas who has unfathomable strength, who is white with all types of fresh fame, who is all-pervading.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises Krsna using gatha meter.

I meditate upon Krsna, who gives great joy to the group (patalam) of gopis by his embraces, etc. The word Krsna should be supplied (which the phrases modify), according to the dictum:

*asādhāraṇāni viśeṣaṇāni viśeṣyaṁ lakṣayanti*

**Unusual adjectives indicate the object of depiction.**

An example is this following:

*ayamudayati mudrābhañjnaḥ padminīnāṁ*

**The sun is the breaker of the locks of the lotuses. (Sat-ukti-karnamrtam compiled by Sridhara dasa)**

The verb smarami should be added to the verse as in grham bhunksva: enter the house and eat, or pravisa pindim: enter and accept an oblation. By his cloth (pata) he derides (langhita) a heap (cayam) of the best gold. He wears a bright yellow cloth.

He manifests (racayantam) charming arts which are great (udara) or fulfilling all desires. His feet are worshipped (ancita) by all devatas, etc. He is the Lord of all. He is white (dhavalam) with fresh fame, though black in complexion. He is all-pervading (amitam). The meter is gatha.

The meter is gatha. since there are five lines of totaka.

*iha toṭakamambudhisairgaditam*

**Totaka is four (ambudhi) x ssl (sa) i.e. ssl ssl ssl ssl.**

Because of the irregular number of lines (five instead of four) it is classed as gatha. This will be written in Gitavali.

Thus, the gatha-chandah stava has been explained.

## tribhaṅgī-cchandaḥ-stavaḥ

**śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ**

**I offer respects to Sri Krsna.**

### Text 1

*yamalārjuna-bhañjanam āśrita-rañjanam ahigañjana-ghana-lāsya-bharaṁ paśupāla-purandaram abhisṛta-kandaram atisundaram aravinda-karam \|*  
*vara-gopa-vadhū-jana-viracita-pūjanam uru-kūjana-nava-veṇu-dharaṁ*  
*smara-narma-vicakṣaṇam akhila-vilakṣaṇa-tanu-lakṣaṇam atidakṣataram \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, who broke the two aijuna trees, who is attractive to those who take shelter, who danced intently on Kaliya, who is the king of the cowherds, who meets the gopis in caves, who is most beautiful, who has lotus hands, who is worshipped by the fine gopis, who holds a new flute which sounds exquisite, who is expert at amorous joking, who has outstanding marks on his body, and who is most expert at all activities.**

**Комментарий:**

The author praises Krsna using tribhangi meter. The verb vandemahi is in the fifth verse. О Damodara! Let us worship you. He is described. You broke the pair (.yamala) of arjuna trees. Yamala means two according to Haima. He revived them as Nalakuvara and Manigriva, after they had been cursed by Narada to become two arjuna trees, freeing them from the curse. He danced (Iosya) expertly (ganjana-ghana) on Kaliya (ahi). He has meetings in caves (kandaram). He is worshipped by gopis having excellent forms and qualities, after they meet in the caves. This means he offers his youth to them. He holds a new flute whose excellent (uru) sound (kiijana) enchants the heart. He is expert at amorous jokes. He has most outstanding marks on his body. Some parts are red and some are raised and there are marks of the wheel and lotus, etc., on his hands and feet. These are not seen in other avataras. Thus, the marks are outstanding. He is most skillful in all actions (atidaksataram). The rest is clear.

### Text 2

*praṇatāśani-pañjaram nambara-piñjaram arikuñjara-harim indumukhaṁ*  
*go-maṇḍala-rakṣiṇam anukṛta-pakṣiṇam atidakṣiṇam amitātma-sukham \|*  
*guru-gairika-maṇḍitam anunaya-paṇḍitam avakhaṇḍita-puruhūta-makhaṁ vraja-kamala-virocanam alika-surocana-gorocanam atitāmra-nakham \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, who are a covering of thunderbolts for the devotees, who wear yellow cloth, who are a lion in relation to the elephant-like enemies, who have a moon-like face, who protect all the cows, who imitate the birds, who are most honest, who experience unlimited happiness, who are decorated with fine minerals, who are learned at pacifying, who stopped Indra’s sacrifice, who are the sun for the lotus of Gokula, who wear attractive gorocana tilaka on your forehead, whose fingernails are colored excellent red.**

**Комментарий:**

You are a cage of thunderbolts for protecting the surrendered. You are a place where the devotee has no fear. You wear yellow (pinjaram) cloth. Pinjara means yellow according to Visva. You are a lion for the enemies who are elephants (kunjara). You protect the herds of cows. You imitate the birds like parrots and swans with similar actions and voices. You are most honest (atidaksinam). Daksina means honest according to Visvalocana. You feel unlimited happiness of pastimes in the self (amitatma-sukham). You are decorated with minerals excellent in color and fragrance. You look beautiful with the colorful patterns made by the minerals. You are expert at pleasing friends, brahmanas and angry persons. You stopped the sacrifice of Indra (puruhuta). You are the sun for the lotus of Gokula. You reveal Gokula. You have most beautiful (surocand) gorocana tilaka on your forehead. You have praiseworthy red fingernails. Ati means praiseworthy according to Visva.

### Text 3

*unmada-rati-nāyaka-śāṇita-sāyaka-vinidhāyaka-cala-cilli-latam*  
*uddhata-saṅkocanam ambuja-locanam agha-mocanam amarāli-natam \|*  
*nikhilādhika-gauravam ujjvala-saurabham atigaurabha-paśupīṣu rata*  
*mṛdu-pada-pallavam abhram u vallabha-ruci-durlabha-sa-vilāsa-gatam \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**
