О queen of Vrndavana! When will the sound of your vina become guests of my ears for a moment? The sound is described. It produces (pravalayan) breakage of the notes of Krsna’s flute and stuns them. When Krsna becomes bewildered on hearing the sound of her vina, the flute stops producing sound.

He prays to hear their songs together. О excellent lords (prabhu-varau)l That day will happen for which person? Va is an ornament of speech. At that time, your soft songs, manifesting together, will destroy the impurity of my ear. The songs are described. They swell with towering (unnaman) sweet waves.

*parimala-saraṇir vāṁ gaura-nīlāṅga-rājan-*

He prays to experience the fragrance of their limbs. О charming lords! Will a continuous streams (saranih) of fragrance be a festival for the bee of my nose? Sarani means a line or path according to Visvalocana. The paths give (anugrahinl) fragrance of musk and kurikuma shining on your golden and black limbs.

*pradeśinīṁ mukha-kuhare vinikṣipañ*

It is impossible for me to have the fortune of close contact. May I meet you from far off! Pradesini means forefinger according to Amara-kosa. It is next to the thumb. Placing his forefinger into his mouth, he shouts (phutkaroti). The rest is clear. The couple have beauty (chavih) like lightning and a cloud.

**Перевод:**

**О ornament of the sweet people of Vraja! This person prays to you. May the moonlight from your toenails astonish my eyes for even a moment!**

**Комментарий:**

He prays, desiring to see their toenails. The meaning is clear.

### Text 33

*atarkita-samīkṣaṇollasitayā mudā śliṣyator*  
*nikuñja-bhavanāṅgane sphurita-gaura-nīlāṅgayoḥ \|*  
*rucaḥ pracurayantu vāṁ puraṭa-yūthikā-mañjarī-*

**Перевод:**

**As you embrace with intense joy on suddenly seeing each other, with shining gold and black limbs, attractive as a bee on golden yuthika bud, may your complexions deepen the astonishment of my eyes, in the yard of the bower pavilion.**

**Комментарий:**

He prays, desiring to see suddenly the couple together. May your complexions deepen (pracurayantu) the astonishment of my eyes, in the yard (angane) of the bower pavilion. The couple is described. They embrace with increased joy on suddenly (atarkita) seeing each other. They are further described. They shine golden and black. They are described with metaphor. They are attractive, like a bee situated on golden yuthika bud.

### Text 34

*sākṣātkṛtiṁ bata yayor na mahattamo'pi*

*jantur vijitya nijagāra bhiyaṁ hriyaṁ ca \|\|34\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

Realizing his incompetence, he shows regret. Bata indicates surprise. Even a person endowed with all sadhanas (mahattamah), the best devotee, cannot (prabhutam na upaiti) directly meet even slightly the two lords made of knowledge and bliss. Desiring to see you two (icchan nayanayoh pathi), this person, foolish, wicked, and possessing a material body, has conquered and swallowed (nijagara) fear and shame. He is without fear and shame.

### Text 35

*athavā mama kiṁ nu dūṣaṇaṁ*

*yuvayor guṇa-mādhurī navā*

**О lords of Vrndavana! What sin have I not committed? Does not the attractiveness of your fresh qualities intoxicate all people?**

**Комментарий:**

In praying though he has explained that he is a fool, he suggests that he still prays because of the sweetness of the couple. The attractiveness of your ever fresh (nava) qualities (guna-madhuri), such as delivering the fallen, will not intoxicate what person? The greed of a beggar for a desirable object is the cause of the object’s attractiveness.

О two lords (adhlsau)! Will astonishment of my ears be produced by the joy (ksvelibhih) in pastimes of your love quarrels? Kim indicates a question. This is further described. The joy is increased (unnatabhih) by assisting actions (parsni-graha-carya) of your associates. This is further described. They are compact (sugahana-ghatanabhih) with crooked bombast or pride (varkimadambarena).

О killer of Agha! When will you give satisfaction to my eyes? He is described. You ask, “Who stole my flute?” while sending eager (utka) eyes in all directions, when the flute was stolen by Radha in a solitary place (nibhrtam). He is cheated by the sakhis who say that Radha did not steal it. The sakhis are described. Their faces have variegated (Sabalo) smiles. My eyes will be satisfied on seeing you cheated directly by the sakhis, though you are the king of cheaters.

О Radha (devi)! Having wounded his own petal-like lip by his teeth, Krsna says to her friend Lalita, “Your friend has done this.” When will the beauty of your face at this time offer (upadhasyati) me joy? The beauty is described. The tip of the eye is variegated with a smile. The brow is slightly raised because of Krsna’s clowning nature. It indicates Radha’s anger when he speaks lies.

**Комментарий:**

He again speaks with humility. О protectors from pain (arta-nathau)! This fallen person should not desire at all such good fortune of service. The service is described. It is desired by great devotees (uttamarham). The effulgence of your mercy shines most excellently (jayatitaram). It is devoid of considering good from bad (guru-laghu-ganana ujjhita). Though I am most fallen, by your mercy I can desire this.

### Text 40

*vṛtte daivād vraja-pati-suhṛn-nandinī-vipralambhe*  
*saṁrambheṇollalita lalitā-śaṅkayodbhrānta-netraḥ \|*  
*tvaṁ śārībhiḥ samaya-paṭubhir drāg upālabhyamānaḥ*  
*kāmaṁ dāmodara mama kadā modam akṣṇor vidhātā \|\|40\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Damodara! When will you, in separation from Radha, your eyes terrified out of fear of Lalita who is enflamed with rage, while the sari birds, knowledgeable of circumstance, quickly scold you, give pleasure to my eyes?**

**Комментарий:**

He prays for results of th at mercy. О Damodara! When will you give pleasure to my eyes, as much as you desire (kama)? Krsna is described. There is separation from Radha (vraja-pati-suhrn-nandini) by Cupid’s desire (daivat). Daiva means Krsna’s friend called Ujjvala, or the devata Cupid. His action is called daiva. Daivat means by his desire. His desire acts to manifest pastimes. His eyes are in terror (udbhranta) out of fear of Lalita who is blazing (ullalita) with anger (samrambhena). He is scolded suddenly by the sari birds knowledgeable of the situation (samaya-patubhih). "Though you have a most beautiful form and you are the prince, you do not have beauty of intelligence. You have cheated your princess full of incomparable qualities.” In this way they scold him. They request that he give pleasure to Radha. Radha requests, “If I make these rough entities, the birds, favorable to you by my skills, you should accept me.”

**Комментарий:**

О Radha! Seeing you in the distance in Vrndavana, will I quickly (acirat) offer the pride in my heart? Radha is described. Giving up all the lotus eyed gopis at the beginning of the shining rasa dance, brought by Kesava to a solitary place, you are worshipped by him, in the form of being decorated with flowers by him (arcitangim). Kesava is described. He has attained the position (pada) of decorating you with flowers, as a lover dependent on you. He follows your orders.

### Text 42

*ramyā śoṇa-dyutibhir alakair yāvakenorja-devyāḥ*

**Комментарий:**

О lord of Vraja! When will the beauty of your face produce pride (sammadam) and joy in me? Mada means pride according to Halayudha. The beauty is described. It is attractive with the red luster of lac, stuck to his face as he offers obeisance to please her. The eyes are suddenly (sadyas) fatigued and lazy, closed by sleep. Sadyah means immediately according to Amara-kosa. The face is seen with crooked stares in the morning by Candravali’s pale followers.

### Text 43

*vyātyukṣī-rabhasotsave'dhara-sudhā-pāna-glahe prastute*  
*jitvā pātum athotsukena hariṇā kaṇṭhe dhṛtāyāḥ puraḥ \|*  
*īṣac-choṇima-mīlitākṣam anṛju-bhrū-valli-helonnataṁ*  
*prekṣiṣye tava sa-smitaṁ sa-ruditaṁ tad devi vaktraṁ kadā \|\|43\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Radha! When will I see your face, smiling and weeping, with slightly red eyes and brows crooked out of disrespect, when Krsna eagerly holds your throat to drink the nectar after winning, where the prize was drinking the nectar of your lips during the impetuous festival of squirting water?**

**Комментарий:**

О Radha (devi)! When will I see your face in an impetuous (rabhasd) festival of splashing water? Vyatyuksl means sprinkling each other with water using syringes.

*karma-vyatihāreṇa ca striyām*

**The affix пае comes after a root in denoting reciprocity of action, and the word so formed is in the feminine gender. (Panini Sutras 3.3.43)**

This is a festival endowed with impetuosity (rabhasa). It is described. The wager (glahe) was drinking the nectar from the lips. Radha is described. Your throat was held by Krsna out of enthusiasm to drink the nectar of your lips when he won (jitva). The face is described. It was slightly red with closed eyes. The brows became crooked because of increased disrespect (helonnatam). Here the three bhavas kilakincita, kuttamita and bibboka are described. They are defined as follows:

*garvasmitābhilāṣādorbhīkopādeśca miśraṇam \|*  
*pramodātpreyasaḥ saṅge kathyate kilakiñcitam \|\|*

**Meeting the lover out of joy with a mixture of pride, smiling, desire, tears, fear, anger, etc., is called kilakincita.**

*dayite kucasaṁsparśamukhacumbādi kurvati \|*  
*hṛdyānando bahiḥ kopaḥ smṛtaṁ kuṭṭamitaṁ budhaiḥ \|\|*

**External anger while being blissful in the heart, when the lover touches the breasts and kisses the mouth is called kuttamita by the wise.**

*vibbokaḥ kathyate garvādiṣṭe vastunyanādare \|\|*

**Bibboka is disrespecting desired things out of pride.**

These symptoms should be seen in the verse.

Sahasa means unexpected according to Amara-kosa. You smile broadly (gudha-smitasyam).

**The words para (across), and madhya (middle) may optionally be compounded with a word ending in the sixth case-affix, when they take the forms pare and madhye, and the compound so formed is indeclinable.**

**(Panini Sutras 2.1.18) The couple is described. They joke with each other (vyavahaslm) excessively with a desire to win (jaya-kalanaya). Vyavahaslm is explained like vyatyuksl (sprinkling each other with water). The rest is clear.**

**Комментарий:**

O Radha! When will I, understanding the intentions of your words (sdkutam vacanam), having increased intelligence (ucchalita-dhih), stop Krsna, crest jewel of the cowherds (gopa-pravaram), with cheating loud words (chalatopaih)? What are your words? He is a cheater (sathd). Externally by pleasing words he attracts, but internally he has no liking for us. He should not be seen by me, having a wealth of pride (mana-dhanaya). Looking closely, the friend of Subala, enters in my bower wearing a woman’s clothing. Forbid him with false words. Radha says, “Subala cheats our elders by wearing a woman’s clothing. This knowledge was attained from Krsna. He has been prevented with harsh words. The deception has been discovered.”

“To fool the intelligence of the demons, you previously disguised yourself as a woman (Mohini). There is no demon here. Quickly manifest yourself. Disguised as a woman, you are recognized by my clever associates standing around my mistress. There is no opportunity to enter. Meditating on your deception, you should return to your own clothing.” These are the cheating loud words.

### Text 59

*aghahara balīvardaḥ preyān navas tava yo vraje*  
*vṛṣabha-vapuṣā daityenāsau balād abhiyujyate \|*  
*iti kila mṛṣā-gīrbhiś candrāvalī-nilaya-sthitaṁ*  
*vanabhuvi kadā neṣyāmi tvāṁ mukunda mad-īśvarīm \|\|59\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“O killer of Agha! Your favorite young bull has been attacked forcefully by the demon with a bull body.” O Mukunda! When will I lead you, hiding at Candravali’s house, to my mistress staying in the forest, using these false words?**

**Комментарий:**

О Mukunda! When will I lead you, hiding at Candravali’s house, to my mistress staying in the forest, using false words? What are the false words? О killer of Agha! Your favorite young bull has been attacked forcefully by the demon with a bull body. Though 1 am not fond of telling lies, if I please you by these false words, you will accept me.

### Text 60

*nigirati jagad uccaiḥ sūci-bhedye tamisre*  
*bhramara-ruci-nicolenāṅgam āvṛtya dīptam \|*  
*parihṛta-maṇi-kāñcī-nūpurāyāḥ kadāhaṁ*  
*tava navam abhisāṛaṁ kāṛayiṣyāmi devi \|\|60\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Radha! When will I arrange your fresh meeting, covering your limbs, shining like lightning, with a cape, black like a bee, while you discard your jeweled belt and ankle bells, in the thick darkness which swallows the world?**

**Комментарий:**

О Radha (devi)! When will 1 arrange your fresh meeting, covering your limbs, shining like lightning (dlptam) with a cape black like a bee, in the thick (suci-bhedye) darkness which swallows the world? Nicola is a covering cloth according to Amara-kosa. Radha is described. She has given up her jeweled belt and ankle bells.

### Text 61

*āsye devyāḥ katham api mudā nyastam āsyāt tvayeśa*  
*kṣiptaṁ parṇe praṇaya-janitād devi vāmyāt tvayāgre \|*  
*ākūtajñas tad atinibhṛtaṁ carvitaṁ kharvitāṅgas*  
*tāmbūlīyaṁ rasayati janaḥ phulla-romā kadāyam \|\|61\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О my two lords! When will this person, deformed, but understanding your hint, taste in a secret place your chewed betel nut, which was placed affectionately and insistently in Radha’s mouth by you, and was thrown by Radha in front onto a leaf, out of affectionate obstinacy?**

**Комментарий:**

О my two lords! When will this person taste your chewed betel nut in a secret place (atinibhrtam)? The person is described. This person has deformed limbs (kharvitangah). The person understands your intention (akuta-jnah): “This recipient of my mercy should eat our prasada” The persons’s hairs stand on end on tasting the betel nut. The chewed betel nut is described. O lord of Vraja (isa)! It was placed by you into the mouth of Radha (devyah) with affection (muda) and insistence (katham). O Radha (devi)! You threw the betel nut onto a leaf from your mouth out of affectionate obstinacy saying, “I will not eat your leftovers.”

### Text 62

*parasparam apaśyatoḥ praṇaya-māninor vāṁ kadā*  
*dhṛtotkelikayor api svam abhirakṣator āgraham \|*  
*dvayoḥ smitam udañcaye nudasi kiṁ mukundāmunā*  
*dṛganta-naṭanena mām uparamety alīkoktibhiḥ \|\|62\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You both display affectionate anger, both long to see each other, both nourish stubbornness, and thus you cannot see each other. By uttering false words, “O Mukunda! Why do you force me, by the dancing of your side glance? Give this up,” when will I make you two smile?**

**Комментарий:**

O my two lords! When will I make you two smile? The two are described. You both have causeless anger (pranaya-maninoh). Both have longing to see each other (dhrtotkalikayoh). But you cannot see each other (apasyatoh) since you nourish own stubbornness (agraham).

“By what method will you make us smile?”

“O Mukunda! Why do you force me by the dancing of your side glance? The angry woman will not accept your prayer. Therefore, give up this attempt.” These are the false words (alika uktibhih).

The meaning is this. Hearing the words, “Why do you insist?”

Krsna becomes depressed and Radha smiles. Radha then becomes depressed because Krsna approaches her sakhi on his behalf. Then he smiles.

### Text 63

*kadāpy avasaraḥ sa me kim u bhaviṣyati svāminau*  
*jano'yam anurāgataḥ pṛthuni yatra kuñjodare \|*  
*tvayā saha tavālike vividha-varṇa-gandha-dravyaiś*  
*ciraṁ viracayiṣyati prakaṭa-paktra-vallī-śriyam \|\|63\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When will I have the opportunity, where, out of affection, in a large bower, I will for a long time draw beautiful patterns on your foreheads using substances of various colors and fragrance, assisted by you?**

**Комментарий:**

О lords! When will I have the opportunity? Avasara means opportunity according to Visvalocana. It also means moment according to Haima. Assisted by you, Radha, this person will out of love make beautiful clear patterns on Krsna’s forehead with various colored fragrant materials. And I will make patterns on Radha’s forehead assisted by Krsna. The colors are yellow, blue, red and white. The scents are sandalwood, musk, saffron and aguru.

### Text 64

*idaṁ sevā-bhāgyaṁ bhavati sulabhaṁ yena yuvayoś*  
*chaṭāpy asya premṇaḥ sphurati nahi suptāv api mama \|*  
*padārthe'smin yuṣmad-vrajam anu nivāsena janitas*  
*tathāpy āśā-bandhaḥ parivṛḍha-varau māṁ draḍhayati \|\|64\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О excellent masters! The splendor of prema by which good fortune of service to you becomes easily available does not manifest in me even in dreams. But hope for that service, born from living in your Vraja, makes me more determined.**

**Комментарий:**

Though I am not qualified to request this service, by attaining residence in Vraja, I have hope. О best masters (parivrdha-varau)1. Parivrdha means master according to Halayudha. The splendor of prema by which (yena) it will be easy to attain the good fortune of service to you two does not appear to me even in dreams. “Therefore, give up hope.” In answer to this he says, “Even though that is true, because of living in your Vraja, my hope for the object (padarthe), good fortune of service, makes me more determined.”

### Text 65

*prapadya bhavadīyatāṁ kalita-nirmala-premabhir*  
*mahadbhir api kāmyate kim api yatra tārṇaṁ januḥ \|*  
*kṛtātra kujaner api vraja-vane sthitir me yayā*  
*kṛpāṁ kṛpaṇa-gāminīṁ sadasi naumi tām eva vām \|\|65\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Though I have a low birth, by staying in Vraja, where, attaining your service, great persons who have developed pure bhava desire birth as grass, I praise in the assembly your mercy which is directed to the fallen.**

**Комментарий:**

I have inferred that my living in Vraja is the only method of attaining your mercy. Therefore, that good fortune of service will be attained. That is indicated in this verse. Attaining your service (.bhavadiyatam), birth as grass is desired by great persons like Uddhava, who have developed pure bhava.

*āsāmaho caraṇareṇujuṣāmahaṁ syāṁ vṛndāvane kimapi gulmalatauṣadhīnām*

**Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers or herbs in Vrndavana, because the gopis trample them and bless them with the dust of their lotus feet. (SB 10.47.61)**

By being situated in the Vraja forest, though being born in a low family (kujaneh), I praise the mercy of you two in the assembly. Januh means birth according to Amara-kosa. That mercy is directed to the fallen (krpana-gaminim).

### Text 66

*mādhavyā madhurāṅga kānana-pada-prāptādhirājya-śriyā*  
*vṛndāraṇya-vikāsi-saurabha-tate tāpiñcha-kalpa-druma \|*  
*nottāpaṁ jagad eva yasya bhajate kīrti-cchaṭā-cchāyayā*  
*citrā tasya tavāṅghri-saṁnidhi-juṣāṁ kiṁ vā phalāptir nṛṇām \|\|66\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О sweet limbed Krsna embraced by a madhavi creeper, whose beauty rules the forest! О you whose abundant fragrance spreads in the forest of Vrndavana! О tamala tree that fulfills all desires! By the mere shadow of this tree’s great fame the world does not experience pain. Is it astonishing that men who reside at the base of this tree attain fruits?**

**Комментарий:**

By attaining understanding of the strength of bhakti, he attains strength with confidence. This is expressed in two verses (66-67). О you whose sweet- limbs—trunk and branches- with the madhavi creeper which embraces you from foot to head (madhavya madhuranga)! The creeper is described. Its beauty rules over the kingdom (pada) of the forest. О you whose abundant fragrance spreads (vikasi) in the forest of Vrndavana! О tamala (tapincha) desire tree (kalpa-druma). Is it surprising that persons who attain the base of this tree, by the shadow of whose splendid fame the universe does not experience pain (uttapam), attain fruits? It is not surprising.

*aprastutapraśaṁsā yā sā saiva prastutāśrayā \|*  
*kārye nimitte sāmānye viśeṣa prastute sati \|\|*  
*tadanyasya vacastulye tulyasyeti ca pañcadhā \|\|*

**When irrelevant topics are introduced in reference to the topic at hand, it is called aprastuta-prasamsa. There are five types: stating the effect when the cause is the subject, stating the cause when the effect is the subject, stating the general when the particular is the subject, stating the particular when the general is the subject, and stating similarity. (Kavya-prakasa 10.99)**

Chayaya employs a pun (beauty and shadow), which then creates a metaphor, in line with the comparison of Radha and Krsna to a madhavl creeper and tamala tree.

### Text 67

*tval-līlā-madhu-kulyayollasitayā kṛṣṇāmbudasyāmṛtaiḥ*  
*śrī-vṛndāvana-kalpa-valli-paritaḥ saurabhya-visphārayā \|*  
*mādhuryeṇa samastam eva pṛthunā brahmāṇḍam apyāyitaṁ*  
*nāścaryaṁ bhuvi labdha-pāda-rajasāṁ parvonnatir vīrudhām \|\|67\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О desire creeper of Vrndavana (Radha)! The whole universe is pleased by the great sweetness caused by the river of your sweet pastimes, swelling with the sweet water from the dark cloud, spreading fragrance everywhere. It is not surprising that the creepers which have attained your foot dust experience great joy on earth.**

**Комментарий:**

О desire creeper of Vrndavana! The whole universe is pleased (apyayitam) by the great (prthuna) sweetness caused by the river (kulyaya) of your sweet pastimes, swelling with the sweet water from the dark cloud. It is not surprising that the creepers which have attained your foot dust experience great joy or elevation of their limbs (parvonnatih). Attaining foot dust means taking shelter of your feet. The river is described. The river swells (ullasitaya) with sweet water from the dark cloud (krsnambudasya), or from the sweet pastimes of the cloud, Krsna. It is also an alahkara. Others say it is the first type of atisayokti (hyperbole), the first part having a pun. That should be considered.

### Text 68

*paśupāla-vareṇya-nandanau*  
*varam etaṁ muhur arthaye yuvām \|*  
*bhavatu praṇayo bhave bhave*  
*bhavator eva padāmbujeṣu me \|\|68\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О son and daughter of the two kings who are best of the cowherds! I beg this boon from you two. May I have affection for your lotus feet birth after birth.**

**Комментарий:**

The good fortune of service prayed for is difficult for me to attain. But for one who has developed bhakti to your lotus feet may it happen. Thus, he prays. О son and daughter of the two kings who are best of the cowherds! Bhave bhave means birth after birth. The rest is clear.

### Text 69

*udgīrṇābhūd utkalikā-vallarir agre*  
*vṛndāṭāvyāṁ nitya-vilāsa-vratayor vām \|*  
*vāṅ-mātreṇa vyāharato'py ullalam etām*  
*ākarṇyeśau kāmita-siddhiṁ kurutaṁ me \|\|69\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О lords! The creeper of longing for you two, who play eternally in Vrndavana, has manifested in front of you. Hearing it, bestow my desired goal from reciting it while trembling.**

**Комментарий:**

He begs for attaining his desire from recitation of the stotra. О two lords (isau)! The creeper (vallarih) of longing for you two has manifested (udgirnabhUt). Vallarl means creeper according to Dhananjaya. Hearing it (akarnya), bestow my desired goal from reading (vyaharatah) these verses by voice or in the mind. The couple is described. They eternally play in Vrndavana.

### Text 70

*candrāśva-bhuvane śāke pauṣe gokula-vāsinā \|*  
*iyam utkalikā-pūrvā vallarī nirmitā mayā \|\|70\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**This work Utkalika-purva-vallari was composed by me, living in Gokula, during Pausa month, 1471 saka era.**

**Комментарий:**

He describes the time and place of the stotra’s creation. The numbers are counted in reverse (candra=l, asva=7 and bhuvana=14). The stotra was created in 1471 in Salivahana’s era or saka era. The commentary was written in 1686 saka. By calculating Salivahana’s era, one can understand Vikramaditya’s era also.

*vikramādityarājyasya pañcaviṁśottaraṁ śatam \|*  
*pātayitvā bhavecchākaḥ sa nṛpaḥ śālivāhanaḥ \|\|*

**Subtracting 125 years from Vikramaditya’s era produces the era of the saka king Salivahana.**

May the Utkalika-vallari, elevated, refined in poetic skill, explained by Vidyabhusana, remain always the wealth of the devotees.

## sri-sri-radha-krsnayoh kunjad vesmagamanam

**Radha and Krsna return to their houses from the bower**

### Text 1

*srastaṁ srastam udañcayanty adhiśiraḥ śyāmaṁ nicolāñcalaṁ*  
*hastena ślatha-durbalena lulitākalpāṁ vahantī tanum \|*  
*muktārdhām avarudhya veṇim alasa-spande kṣipantī dṛśau*  
*kuñjāt paśya gṛhaṁ praviśya nibhṛtaṁ śete sakhī rādhikā \|\|1\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

With her weak, tired hand, she raised her blue cape over her head as it falls repeatedly. She carries a body with ornaments in disarray. She ties her half-undone braids. She casts glances here and there, while quivering with fatigue. Look! My sakhi Radhika, entering alone the house from the bower, lies down.

When the lovers return from the bower to their houses in the dawn, someone speaks to some resident of the house. This is expressed in two verses. Look! My sakhi Radhika entering alone the house from the bower, lies down. She is described. She pulls a blue cape on her head with her tired hand, though it falls off continually. She has a body with ornaments in disarray. She ties up her half-undone braid with her hand. She casts glances here and there, quivering with fatigue.

### Text 2

*mlānām utkṣipya mālāṁ truṭita-maṇi-saraḥ kajjalaṁ bibhrad-oṣṭhe*  
*saṅkīrṇāṅgo nakhāṅkair diśi diśi vikiran ghūrṇite netra-padme \|*  
*paśya mlānāṅga-yaṣṭiḥ sphuṭam aparicito gopa-goṣṭhībhir agre*  
*goṣṭhaṁ goṣṭhendra-sūnuḥ praviśati rajanau dhvaṁsam āsādayantyām \|\|2\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

Look! Nanda’s son enters the village at the end of night before anyone has risen, unnoticed by the cowherds, discarding his faded garland, with broken jewel necklace, collyrium on his lips, nail marks on his chest, and withered arms, as he looks in all directions with rolling lotus eyes.

Krsna is described. The son of Nanda enters Vraja village before the people have risen (agre). О friend! Look! When is this? It is when the night (rajanau) is being destroyed (dhvamsam asadayantyam). What is he doing? He throws off his Vaijayanti garland, wilted from being crushed by his lover’s breast. He has a broken jewel necklace. He has collyrium on his lips from kissing Radha’s eyes. His chest is covered with her nail marks. He casts his rolling lotus eyes in all directions, thinking, “No one should see me.” His arms (anga-yasti) are spotted from contacting the kunkuma on his lover’s body and are withered from fatigue of pastimes. He is unseen (aparicitah) clearly by the group of cowherds who are waking up because of his quick entrance.

One should not say that by repetition of the word withered (mlana), there is actual withering, since the word is used for a certain goal in the description. This should be understood elsewhere as well.

## srī-govinda-virudāvaliḥ

*oṁ namaḥ kṛṣṇāya \|*

**I offer respects to Sri Krsna.**

*gauḍodayamupayātastamaḥ samastaṁ nihanti yo yugapat \|*  
*jyotiśca yo'tiśītaḥ pītastamupāsmahe kṛtāñjalayaḥ \|\|*

**With folded hands we worship he who appeared in Bengal, simultaneously destroys all darkness and is effulgent, pale and golden.**

*satkāvyasadmasu ya eva haripriyeṣu śabdārtharatnanikaraistanute'tibhavyaiḥ \|*  
*śilpakriyāṁ bahuvidhāṁ kaviviśvakarmā rūpābhidho rasikacittaharaḥ sa jīyāt \|\|*

**May Rupa, the rasika who attracts the heart, Visvakarma among poets, who produced many types of art with heaps of jewels in meanings of words with great beauty, in the abodes of pure poetry dear to the Lord, manifest all excellence.**

*adhītya virudāvalyā lakṣaṇaṁ granthakṛtkṛtam \|*  
*etāṁ cetpaṭhati prājñastadā bodho'sya puṣkalaḥ \|\|*

**If the wise person reads the work after studying the characteristics of virudavali which the author has created, then his understanding will be thorough.**

*sāmānyavirudāvalyā govindavirudāvalau \|*  
*yo'bhyadhāyi viśeṣastaiḥ sa tāvadiha likhyate \|\|*

**What detail was set forth in Govinda-virudavali by Samanya-virudavali (Rupa Gosvami’s work describing the virudavali form) is written here.**

*kalikā ślokavirudairyutā vividhalakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*kīrtipratāpaśauṭīryasaundaryonmeṣaśālinī \|\|*  
*kalikādyantasaṁsargipadyā doṣavivarjitā \|*  
*śabdāḍambarasaṁbaddhā kartavyā virudāvalī \|\|*

**The virudavali poem with kalikas at the beginning and end, with kalikas, sloka, and viruda having various characteristics, should be composed—manifesting fame, splendor, strength and beauty, devoid of fault, and filled with pleasurable words.**

*syurmahākalikārambhe ślokāstu yugaśaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*anyāsāṁ kalikānāṁ tu bhavantyekaikaśo hi te \|*  
*pūrtau dvau kalikābhistu virudāstulyasaṁkhyakāḥ \|\|*

**At the beginning of the mahd-kalika (a work with several kalikas) there should be two verses of introduction. In other kalikas there will be one each. There are two verses at the end. The viruda is equal in number to the kalikas.Characteristics of the kalika:**

*kalā nāma bhavettālaniyatā padasaṁtatiḥ \|*  
*kalābhiḥ kalikā proktā tadbhedāḥ ṣaṭ samīritāḥ \|\|*  
*kalikā caṇḍavṛttākhyā dvigādigaṇavṛttakā \|*  
*tathā tribhaṅgīvṛttākhyā madhyā miśrā ca kevalā \|\|*

**Kala means a collection of padas regulated by meter (tala). The kalika is said to consist of these kalds. There are six types: canda-vrtta, dvigadi-gana-vrttaka, tribhangi, madhya, misra and kevala.**

**There are ten types of combined consonants in canda-vrtta:**

*atra saṁyuktavarṇānāṁ niyamo daśadhā ca te \| madhuraśliṣṭaviśliṣṭaśithilahrādinastvamī \|\|*

**The rules from combinations of constants are ten: madhura, Elista, vislista, sithila and hradl (for short and long each).**

*bhidyante hrasvadīrghābhyāṁ te darśyante sphuṭaṁ yathā \|*  
*hrasvānmadhurasaṁyogāḥ śaṅkarāṅkuśakiṁkarāḥ \|\|*

**These are preceded by either short or long vowels to produce ten types. The type madhura, with short vowel, consists of words like sahkarankusa, kimkarah. (combination of a nasal with a consonant)**

*tasmāttu śliṣṭasaṁyuktā darpakarparasarpavat \|\|*

**Slista combination is darpa, karpara, sarpa. (initial r with a consonant)**

*tato viśliṣṭasaṁyuktā bhallakalyāṇacillayaḥ \|\|*

**Vislista combination is bhalla, kalyana, cillayah. (I + consonant)**

*tathā śithilasaṁyuktāḥ paśyakaśyapavaśyavat \|*

**Examples of sithila combination are pasya, kasyapa, vasya. (final y)**

*proktā hrādiyutā mahyaṁ  sahyaṁguhyaṁprasahyatavat \|\|*

**Examples of hradi combination are mahyam, sahyam, guhyam, prasahyata. (initial h)**

*garhādīnhrādisaṁyuktabhedānkecitsamūcire \|*  
*dīrghāttu gāṅgaṁ kārpāsaṁ bālyaṁ viśvaś ca  bāhyakam \|\|*

**Some say the words like garha (h after a consonant) are also classed as hradi and examples of long vowels before the conjunct consonants are gahga, karpasa, balyam, vaioya and bahyakam.**

*kalāparimāṇamuktam—*

**The extent of the kalas (lines):**

*adhikāśceccatuḥṣaṣṭirnyūnā dvādaśa tāḥ kalāḥ \|*  
*etābhyo nādhikā kāryā nyūnāścāpi na paṇḍitaiḥ \|\|*

**There should be up to sixty-four kolas and at least twelve.**

**More or less than this is not done by the learned.**

**There are two types of canda-vrttakalika: nakha and visikha. There are twenty types of nakha such as rana, of which nine are accepted here, starting with vardhita.**

*vardhitaṁ vīrabhadraśca samagro cyuta utpalam \|*  
*taraṅgaḥ śrīguṇaratistathā mātaṅgakhelitam \|\|*  
*tilakaśceti kalikā nakhasyehoditā nava \|\|*

**The nine are vardhita, vlrabhadra, samagra, cyuta, utpala, taranga, gunarati, matanga-khelita, and tilaka.**

**Комментарий:**

There are five types of visikha: padma, kunda, campaka, vanjula, and bakula. Among them padma has six types: pankeruha, sitakanja, pandutpala indivara, arunambhoruha and kahldra.

Bakula has two types: bhasura and mangala.

Thus there are eleven visikha types.

In total there are twenty types of canda-vrtta kalikas accepted.

There are five types of dvigadi-gana-vrttaka kalikas also called manjaris: koraka, gucchaka, samphulla, kusuma and gandha. Of these koraka, guccha and kusuma will be accepted (three).

There are six types of tribhangi kalikas starting with sikharini.

Of these dandaka and vidagha are accepted (two).

Misra-kalika has alternative types: gadya-samprkta or sapta-vibhaktika.

Kevala has two types: aksaramayl and sarva-laghu (two).

Within the six maha-kalikas (major types), there are twentyeight accepted here.

Eleven types of nakha, two types of manjari (samphulla and gandha), four types of tribhangl (sikharim, turaga, bhujanga and tigma) and madhya-kalika are not presented, because they are not too charming.

Slokas are well known. Virudas have two, four or six or ten kalas. The rules of samyukta are the same as previously described. They have descriptions with excellence of qualities, etc.

It is said:

*vāśikaḥ kalpitaśceti virudo dvividho mataḥ \|*  
*saṁyuktaniyamo hyatra varṇitaḥ pūrvavabudhaiḥ \|\|*  
*dvicatuḥṣaḍdaśaścātra kalāstu virude matāḥ \|*  
*daśabhyo nādhikāḥ kāryāḥ kalāstu virude budhaiḥ \|\|*  
*kalikābhyastu virude bhidhāsāveva kīrtitā \|*  
*virudaṁ kavayaḥ prāhurguṇotkarṣādivarṇanam \|\| iti \|*  
*virudaḥ kalikā cānte dhīravīrādiśabdabhāk \|*

**There are two varieties of viruda: vasika and kalpita. The rules for samyukta were described previously here by the wise. The viruda consists of two, four, six or ten kalas. The wise do not put more than ten kalas in a viruda. The virudas are distinguished from the kalikas. The poets say that the viruda is a description with excellence of qualities. At the end of the viruda and kalika is the word dhira or vlra, etc.**

### Text 1

*iyaṁ maṅgala-rūpā syād govinda-virudāvalī \|*  
*yasyāḥ paṭhana-mātreṇa śrī-govindaḥ prasīdati \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Govinda-virudavali is the form of auspiciousness. Just by reciting it Govinda is pleased.**

**Комментарий:**

In order that the listener develop taste for the stotra, the result of reciting the work and the svariipa of the work are explained. The meaning is clear. There is a tradition in this work. Pleased with the beauty of the form of deva-virudavall when recited by a poet of South India, Govinda gave him the garland from his neck.

“How can the Supreme Lord be pleased with deva-viruda?” Because of this doubt, the Lord spoke to Rupa who was sleeping. “Make a form of virudavali for me.” Thus, he wrote this work.

### Text 2

*brahmā brahmāṇḍa-bhāṇḍe sarasija-nayana-sraṣṭum ākrīḍanāni*  
*sthānur bhaṅktuṁ ca khelākhuralita-matinā tāni yena nyayoji \|*  
*tādṛk-krīḍāṇḍa-koṭī-vṛta-jala-kuḍavā yasya vaikuṇṭha-kulyā*  
*kartavyā tasya kā te stutir iha kṛtibhiḥ projjhya līlāyitāni \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Lotus-eyed Govinda! Other than reciting your pastimes, what praises should be made by the learned of you, who are absorbed in pastimes, by whom Brahma is engaged in creating places for pastimes in the universe, by whom Siva is engaged in destroying them, and whose Viraja River is but a handful of water full of millions of universes?**

**Комментарий:**

At the beginning of the canda-vrtta-maha-kalika, the first among the six major kalikds (sanna-kalika), he writes two verses.

О lotus-eyed Govinda! Brahma has been established (nyayoji) by you (yena) to create pastime places (akrldanani) within the universe. Siva (sthanuh) has been established to destroy (bhanktum) these places.

*sṛjāmi tanniyukto'haṁ haro harati tadvaśaḥ*

*I create under his order, and Siva destroys under his order. (SB 2.6.32)*

“Why do I create?” This is then described. You intend to engage in playing (kheld-khuralita-matina). You are absorbed in playing.

Your river of Vaikuntha called Viraja, surrounding the spiritual sky, is a handful (kudava) of water containing millions of universes for pastimes (kridanda). Kudava means handful according to Visva. Avoiding those activities (lllayitani), what stuti, praising your supreme powers and vibhutis can be done by the learned (krtibhih)? This means that the pastimes should be sung by those who are incapable.

### Text 3

*niviḍataraturāṣāḍantarīṇoṣma-saṁpad-*  
*vighaṭana-paṭu-khelāḍambarormi-cchaṭasya \|*  
*sagarima-giri-rāja-cchatra-daṇḍāyita-śrīr*  
*jagad idam aghaśatroḥ savya-bāhur dhinotu \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the left hand, a beautiful stick for the umbrella of towering Govardhana, belonging to Krsna, whose multitude of great waves of skillful pastimes destroyed the condensed wealth of pride in Indra’s heart, give pleasure to the world.**

**Комментарий:**

He describes the pastimes. May Krsna’s left arm please the world. Krsna is described. He has numerous, vast (adambara) waves of skillful pastimes that destroy the concentrated (nividatara) wealth of pride (usma-sampat) in Indra’s (turasad) heart (antarina). His left arm is described. His arm has beauty by acting as a stick (dandayita) of an umbrella in the form of Govardhana, high and broad (sagarima) to prevent Indra’s attack using lightning. Dandayita also means giving protection.

*caṇḍavṛttamahākalikāyā nakhe vardhitam \|*

Vardhita type of nakha in the canda-vrtta kalika

Describing the Lord’s pastimes in kalika form, he indicates the name of the kalika.

This canda-vrtta is vardhita in the nakha class. Canda-vrtta-mahd-kalika has two types: nakha and visikha. Of the nine types of nakha (presented in this work), vardhita is described. The vardhita form of canda-vrtta consists of the following:

*bhanajairjana laghunā baddhairaṁśaiḥ samanvitam \|*  
*ekāṣṭaikādaśasthāne śliṣṭasaṁyogaśālibhiḥ \|*  
*caṇḍavṛttamidaṁ nāmnā vardhitaṁ kavayo viduḥ \|\|*

**Iss sss sis sis s (bha, na, ja, ja, la) with slista sathyogas in the first, eighth, and eleventh syllable (r or s + consonant). The poets know this canda-vrtta by the name vardhita.**

In analyzing the compounds, I have not formed them into satnbodhana (vocative form) in order to keep the commentary short. The intelligent people can do so.

*abhram upatimamada-mardi-pada-krama*  
*vibhrama-parimala-lupta-suhṛc-chrama \|*  
*duṣṭa-danuja-bala-darpa-vimardana*  
*tuṣṭa-hṛdaya-sura-pakṣa-vivardhana \|*  
*darpaka-vilasita-sarga-nirargala*  
*sarpa-tulita-bhuja karṇaga-kuṇḍala \|*  
*nirmala-malayaja-carcita-vigraha*  
*narma-lalita-kṛta-sarpa-vinigraha \|*  
*duṣkara-kṛti-bhara-lakṣaṇa-vismita-*  
*puṣkara-bhava-bhaya-mardana-susmita \|*  
*vatsala-haladhara-tarkita-lakṣaṇa*  
*vatsara-virahita-vatsa-suhṛd-gaṇa \|*  
*garjita-vijayi-viśuddhatara-svara*  
*tarjita-khala-gaṇa-durjana-matsara \|\| vīra \|\|*

**O Krsna, whose gait crushes the pride of Airavata. O Krsna, who relieves friends of fatigue by his beauty and fragrance! O Krsna, who crushes the pride of wicked demons! O Krsna, who increase the strength of devatas with satisfied hearts! O Krsna, who is independent in conjugal pastimes charming with love! O Krsna, whose arms are like snakes, long and round! O Krsna, who has earrings in the ears! O Krsna, whose form is anointed with pure sandalwood! O Krsna, charming with jokes! O Krsna, who destroyed the snake demon! O Krsna, who gained a name by doing what is impossible! O Krsna, by whose smile Brahma was relieved of fear! O Krsna, whose real form was guessed by affectionate Balarama! O Krsna, who was separated from his friends and calves for a year! O Krsna, whose pure voice conquers thunder! O Krsna, who conquers the envy of wicked demons.**

Paksa means strength according to Visvalocana. He received the name liberator of Agha, since he gave him liberation, which is difficult to give. Laksana means name according to Haima.

*dṛṣṭvāghāsuramokṣaṇaṁ prabhavataḥ prāptaḥ paraṁ vismayam*

**Brahma had observed the activities of the most powerful Krsna in killing and delivering Aghasura, and he was astonished. (SB 10.13.15)**

Brahma, surprised at the liberation of Agha, offended the Lord by stealing the calves to test him. By his smile he destroyed the fear in Brahma who had acted unfavorably by testing Krsna. He lost his fear, understanding the Lord was merciful because he smiled. After Brahma stole all the calves Krsna took those forms in Vraja and the forest and performed pastimes. His form of power and bliss in the calves was guessed by affectionate Balarama. For a year Krsna was separated from the calves and boys, since they were sleeping on the bed of maya created by Brahma. He has a pure voice which conquers the rumbling of thunder. His voice is deep like thunder. The rest is clear.

### Text 4

*tava muralī-dhvanir amarī*  
*kāmāmbudhi-vṛddhi-śubhrāṁśuḥ \|*  
*acaṭula-gokula-kulajā*  
*dhairyāmbudhi-pāna-kumbhajo jayati \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The sound of the flute is a moon which increases the ocean of desire in the devata’s wives. It is Agastya which drinks up the ocean of composure of the sober girls of Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

He composes one verse at the end of the kalika. The sound of your flute, a moon (subhrdmsuh) which increases the ocean of desire of the devata women, remains glorious.

*devyo vimānagatayaḥ smaranunnasārā bhraśyatprasūnakabarā mumuhurvinīvyaḥ*

**When the demigods’ wives flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of him and hear his resonant flutesong, their hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair and their belts loosen. (SB 10.21.12)**

The flute is Agastya, drinking up the ocean of composure of sober (acatula) young girls of Vraja. The flute is a moon increasing the ocean of desire, and is Agastya, drying up the ocean of the gopis’ composure. This is virodhabhasa.

*dhṛta-govardhana surabhī-vardhana*  
*paśupāla-priya racitopakriya \|\| dhīra \|\|*

**О upholder of Govardhana! О increaser of cows! О Krsna, dear to the cowherds!**

After the verse he makes a viruda. The meaning is clear. He helps the devotees (racitopakriya).

### Text 5

*bhujaṅga-ripu-candraka-sphurad-akhaṇḍa-cūḍāṅkure*  
*niraṅkuśa-dṛgañcala bhrami-nibaddha-bhṛṅga-bhrame \|*  
*pataṅga-duhitus taṭī-vana-kuṭīra-keli-priye*  
*parisphuratu me muhus tvayi mukunda śuddhā ratiḥ \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Mukunda! May I always manifest pure rati for you, whose hair shines with peacock feather, whose uncontrollable wandering glances stun the wandering of bees, who is fond of playing in the cottages on the bank of the Yamuna.**

**Комментарий:**

This is a verse at the beginning of virabhadra-kalika.

O Mukunda! May my pure rati, without any material desires, manifest for you.

Krsna is described. The front ofyour full hair (akhanda-cudarikure) shines with a peacock feather (candraka). The moving of bees is stunned (nibaddha) by the unrestrained wandering of the tip of your eye. You are fond of playing in cottages on the bank of the Yamuna (patanga-duhituh). Patanga means a moth or the sun.

**vīrabhadraḥ \|**

Virabhadra is a type of nakha within canda-vrtta. It is described as follows:

*mabhanairnena baddhābhiścatuḥśliṣṭayutādibhiḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamātrāchidābhistu kalābhirupakalpitam \|*  
*vīrabhadratayā khyātaṁ caṇḍavṛttaṁ pracakṣate \|\|*

**III Iss sss sss (ma, bha, na, nd) with four slistas (r or s conjunct) or other conjuncts and with caesura at the eighth matra is called the Virabhadra form of canda-vrtta.**

*udyad-vidyud-dyuti-paricita-paṭa*  
*sarpat-sarpa-sphurad-uru-bhuja-taṭa \|*  
*svastha-svastha-tridaśa-yuvati-nuta*  
*rakṣad-dakṣa-priya-suhṛd-anusṛta \|*  
*mugdha-snigdha-vraja-jana-kṛta-sukha*  
*navya-śravyasvara-vilasita-mukha \|*  
*hasta-nyasta-sphuṭa-sarasija-vara*  
*sarjad-garjat-khala-vṛṣa-mada-hara*  
*yuddha-kruddha-pratibhaṭa-laya-kara*  
*varṇa-svarṇa-pratima-tilaka-dhara \|*  
*ruṣyat-tuṣyad-yuvatiṣu kṛta-rasa*  
*bhakta-vyakta-praṇaya-manasi vasa vīra \|\|*

**О Krsna whose cloth is recognized by its lightning effulgence! О Krsna whose excellent arms shine like straight-moving snakes! О Krsna, praised by happy young women of Svarga situated in the sky! О Krsna, followed by dear friends skillful as protectors! О Krsna, whose rasa in pastimes is revealed by the beautiful, affectionate people of Vraja! О Krsna, whose face shines with musical notes which give fresh happiness to the ears! О Krsna, holding a blossoming lotus in your hand! О Krsna, who destroyed the pride of the evil bull which produced anger and bellowed! О Krsna, who destroys enemies who show anger in fighting! О Krsna, wearing tilaka colored bright yellow! О Krsna, attracted to the young girls who are angry sometimes and are satisfied by your treatment! О hero! Please reside in the minds of the devotees manifesting affection.**

His cloth is known (paricita) by lightning (vidyut) effulgence (udyat). О Krsna, wearing cloth yellow like lightning. Your excellent (uru) arms shine like snakes moving straightly (sarpat). You are praised (nut) by happy (svastha) young women of Svarga (tridasa) situated in the sky (svastha). You are followed by dear friends skillful (daksa) as protectors (raksad). The rasa of your pastimes is revealed by the beautiful, affectionate people of Vraja.

Your face shines with musical notes which give fresh (navyd) happiness to the ears (sravyena). The next line is clear. You destroy the pride of the evil bull which produced anger (sarja) and bellowed (garjan). You killed the bull demon. Sarja means to emit according to Kavi-kalpa-druma. You destroy (laya) enemies (pratibhata) who show anger in fighting. You wear tilaka bright yellow (svarna-pratima) in color (varna). You are attracted (rasa) to the young girls who are angry sometimes and satisfied by your treatment. Rasa means attraction according to Medinikara. Please reside in the minds of those manifesting affection, the devotees. О hero (vira)!

### Text 6

*pracura-paramahaṁsaiḥ kāmam ācamyamāne*  
*praṇata-makara-cakraiḥ śaśvad ākrānta-kukṣau \|*  
*aghahara jagad-aṇḍāhiṇḍi-hillola-hāse*  
*sphuratu tava gabhīre keli-sindhau ratir naḥ \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О killer of Agha! May we manifest attraction to the deep ocean of your pastimes, an ocean which is sipped as much as they desire by the profound jnani-bhaktas standing at the edge, an ocean whose center is frequented by surrendered makara devotees, an ocean whose waves of laughter rock the whole universe.**

**Комментарий:**

A verse follows the kalika.

May we manifest attraction to the ocean of your pastimes. The ocean is described. It is drunk fully (kamam) by the profound paramahamsa jnani-bhaktas or the best swans situated on the shore. Its central area is approached always by groups (cakraih) of surrendered dasa bhaktas, who are makaras, special fish. In it there are wave of laughter which rocks the whole universe. Hillola means wave. The alahkara is rupaka.

*udgīrṇa-tāruṇya vistīrṇa-kāruṇya*  
*guñjā-latā-piñcha-puñjāḍhya-tāpiñcha dhīra \|\|*

**О Krsna, manifesting youth and great mercy! О Krsna, a tamala tree laden with gunja berries and madhavi creepers.**

After the verse there is this viruda. Your youth has suddenly manifested. You have abundant mercy. You are a tamala tree endowed with abundant gunja berries and madhavi creepers. Tapincha means madhavi creeper according to Amara-kosa.

### Text 7

*ucitaḥ paśupaty alaṅkriyāyai*  
*nitarāṁ nandita-rohiṇī-yaśodaḥ \|*  
*tava gokula-keli-sindhu-janmā*  
*jagad uddīpayati sma kīrti-candraḥ \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The moon of your fame, born from the ocean of Gokula pastimes, ornamenting the cowherds and giving joy to Rohini and Yasoda at all times, illuminates the world.**

**Комментарий:**

This is a verse introducing the samagra-kalika. О Krsna! The moon of your fame illuminates the world. The moon is described. It arose from the ocean of pastimes in Gokula. It is suitable for decorating the cowherds (pasupati). It makes them glorious. It gives joy to Rohini and Yasoda. The moon is suitable to ornament Siva (pasupati). The moon gives fame (yasodah) to the blissful Rohini constellation. This is rupaka with puns as its anga.

**samagraḥ \|**

In nakha, a type of canda-vrtta, there is a type called samagra. It is described as follows.

*jarābhyāṁ kalpitair aṅgais turyān madhura-śālibhiḥ \|*  
*śliṣṭair antyādvitīyāc ca sarvānte laghu-śālibhiḥ \|\|*  
*baddhaḥ samagra-nāmāyaṁ caṇḍo mādhava-vallabhaḥ \|\|*

**Composed of parts comprised of the sequence sis Isl (ja, ra), with a madhura samyoga (nasal) after the fourth syllable, and slista samyogas (r or s) two syllables later, and with a laghu syllable at the end. This canda-vrtta named samagra is dear to Madhava.**

*ariṣṭa-khaṇḍana sva-bhakta-maṇḍana*  
*prayukta-candana prapanna-nandana \|*  
*prasanna-cañcala sphurad-dṛg-añcala*  
*śruti-pralambaka bhramat-kadambaka \|*  
*prakṛṣṭa-kandara-praviṣṭa sundara*  
*sthaviṣṭha-sindhura-prasarpa-bandhura \|\| deva \|\|*

**О killer of Arista! Decoration of your devotee! Wearer of sandalwood. Joy to the surrendered! Krsna with side glances manifesting pleasing fickleness! Krsna with swaying kadamba flowers hanging from your ears! О Krsna, who enters a fine cave! О Lord, having attractive swaying gait of a beautiful, solid elephant!**

О Krsna, who killed Arista! The next four are clear in meaning. He has swaying kadamba flowers hanging from his ears (sruti). He has entered a fine cave (kandara). He is attractive (bandhura) with praiseworthy crooked gait of a beautiful, solid elephant (sindhura). О deva!

### Text 8

*vṛndāraka-taru-vīte vṛndāvana-maṇḍale vīra \|*  
*nandita-bāndhava-vṛnda sundara vṛndārikā ramaya \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Valorous, beautiful Krsna, giver of joy to all your friends! Enjoy with the attractive young girls in Vrndavana area, thick with excellent trees.**

**Комментарий:**

After the kalika, a verse is added.

О beautiful one! О valorous one! Enjoy the attractive girls (vrndarikd) in Vrndavana area. Vrndaraka means attractive according to Visva. Vrndavana is thick (vite) with (vrndaraka') trees (taru). By the power of words, it is suggested that the gopis are like the devata woman, by comparing Vrndavana to Nandana garden of Svarga. And thus, Krsna is compared to Indra.

*khalinī-ḍumbaka muralī-cumbaka*  
*jananī-vandaka-paśupī-nandaka vīra \|\|*

**О tormentor of the wicked. О kisser of the flute! О giver of respect to your mother! О giver of joy to the gopis!**

A virudha verse is added. You torment (dumbaka) all the rascals (khalini). The root du means to torment. You offer respects to mother Yasoda. You give joy to the gopis (pasupi).

### Text 9

*anudinam anuraktaḥ padminī-cakravāle*  
*nava-parimalam ādyac-cañcarīkānukarṣī \|*  
*kalita-madhura-padmaḥ ko’pi gambhīra-vedī*  
*jayati mihira-kanyā-kūla-vanyā-karīndraḥ \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The indescribable king of elephants in the pools of water of the Yamuna, who is attracted daily to the groups of lotuses (women), who attracts bees intoxicated with his fresh fragrance, who has a lotus in his hand, who is inscrutable and restless, remains victorious.**

**Комментарий:**

This is a verse before the acyuta-kalika.

Indescribable in qualities and form (kah), the king of elephants remains victorious in the water pools (kula-vanya) of the Yamuna (mihira-kanya-kula), putting his body in the water. He is described. He is daily attracted to the groups (cakravale) of padtnini women (or flowers). He attracts the bees (cancarika) intoxicated with his fresh fragrance. He has a sweet line of Laksmi (madhura-padmah) or carries a sweet lotus. He is inscrutable

(gambira-vit) or is restless like an elephant, according to Haima. The alankara is samasokti.

*samāsoktiryadi śliṣṭaiḥ paroktiḥ syādviśeṣaṇaiḥ*

**Describing a different object with descriptive elements having another meaning is called samasokti.**

This refers to Krsna.

**acyutaḥ \|**

A type of nakha in canda-vrtta is called acyuta is described.

*najābhyāṁ kalpitair aṁśaiḥ pañcame dīrgha-śālibhiḥ \|*  
*antyāc-chliṣṭayutopetaiś caṇḍam acyutam ūcire \|\|*

**Acyuta is the canda-vrtta with the portion sss sll (na, ya) with the fifth syllable long and slista at the end (r or s conjunct after the sixth syllable).**

*jaya jaya vīra smara-rasa-dhīra*  
*dvija-jita-hīra pratibhaṭa-vīra \|*  
*sphura-uru-hāra priya-parivāra*  
*cchurita-vihāra sthira-maṇi-hāra \|*  
*prakaṭita-rāsa stavakita-hāsa*  
*sphuṭa-paṭa-vāsa sphurita-vilāsa \|*  
*dhvanad-ali-jāla-stuta-vana-māla*  
*vraja-kula-pāla praṇaya-viśāla \|*  
*pravilasad-aṁsa bhramad-avataṁsa*  
*kvaṇad-uru-vaṁśa-svana-hṛta-haṁsa \|*  
*praśamita-dāva praṇayiṣu tāvad*  
*vilasita-bhāva stanita-virāva \|*  
*stana-ghana-rāga-śrita-para-bhāga*  
*kṣata-hari-yāga tvarita-dhṛtāga vīra \|\|*

**О vira! О Krsna steady in madhurya-rasa! May you remain victorious. О Krsna, whose teeth defeat diamonds, who show valour against rivals! О Krsna, performer of pastimes with friends wearing huge shining necklaces. О wearer of jewel necklaces! О manifestor of the rasa dance! Krsna with blossoming smile! О manifestor of pastimes with profuse perfumed powders! О Krsna, whose garland is praised by swarms of humming bees! О protector of Vraja’s families! О greatly affectionate one! О Krsna, with earrings swinging over your lustrous shoulders! О attractor of the hamsas by playing your excellent flute! О extinguisher of the fire in the grass, manifesting love for dear ones! О Krsna, with voice like rumbling thunder! О Krsna whose upper body is ornamented with thick kunkuma from the breasts of the gopis. О destroyer of Indra’s sacrifice! О holder of the mountain! О Krsna endowed with action!**

О hero with ear ornaments (vlra)! О Krsna, steady in madhurya-rasa! May you remain victorious. Your teeth defeat diamonds. You are courageous against rivals. You have pastimes with dear friends wearing huge shining necklaces. You always were jewel necklaces. You manifest the rasa dance (prakatita-rasa). You have a blossoming smile (stavakita-hasa).

Your pastimes manifest with extensive powered perfumes (pata-vasa). Pata-vasa is perfumed power according to Amara-kosa. You have a garland praised by swarms of humming (dhvanat) bees. The next two are clear. (You protect the families of Vraja. You have great affection.)

You have earrings (avatamsa) swinging over your lustrous shoulders (amsa).

You attract the hamsas by playing (kvanat) your excellent flute. You extinguished the fire in the grass thicket. You show affection (bhava) for your friends. Tavat is an ornament. You swallowed the fire because of love for your friends. Your voice is like rumbling thunder (stanita-rava). Stanita means the sound of clouds according to Amara-kosa. The upper part of your body (para-bhaga) is ornamented with thick kunkuma from the breasts of the gopis. You destroyed Indra’s (hara) sacrifice. You held up the mountain (agah) to stop the disturbance of Indra. О Krsna endowed with impelling action (vlra)!

### Text 10

*sthiti-niyatim atīte dhīratā-hāri-gīte*  
*priya-jana-parivīte kuṅkumālepa-prīte \|*  
*kalita-nava-kuṭīre kāñcy-udañcat-kaṭīre*  
*sphuratu rasa-gabhīre goṣṭha-vīre ratir naḥ \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May our rati manifest for the hero of Vraja, possessing deep rasa, who is beyond the rules of the Vedas, who steals the gopis’ resolve by his songs, who is surrounded by his dear friends, who becomes yellowish from the gopis’ kunkuma, who makes fresh bowers, who wears an golden belt!**

**Комментарий:**

This is this verse after the kalika.

May our rati manifest for the hero of Vraja (gostha-vlre)!

Krsna is described. He is beyond the rules of the Vedas (sthiti-niyatim) since he plays with the cowherds’ wives. He has a fresh cottage for playing with them. His waist is beautiful with a golden belt. The rest is clear.

*ambā-vinihita cumbāmalatara*  
*bimbādhara-mukha-lambālaka jaya deva \|\|*

**О Krsna, with locks hanging over your face endowed with pure bimba lips kissed by your mother! О lord! May you be victorious.**

Viruda verse concludes after that verse.

You have locks hanging over your face which has pure (amalatara) bimba lips kissed by your mother. O Lord! May you be victorious!

### Text 11

*dṛṣṭvā te pada-nakha-koṭi-kānti-pūraṁ*

**Комментарий:**

This verse appears at the beginning of the utpala-kalikd.

O killer of Mura! Seeing the waves of beauty from the tips of your toenails, Cupid, losing all pride in his beauty, became detached and made his body disappear (asarlratam ayasli). The rest is clear. What poet can bind your form to poetic expression?

**utpalam \|**

The utpala form of nakha within canda-vrtta is described.

*bhābhyāṁ vinirmitairaṁśairādyāttu śliṣṭayogataḥ \|*  
*caturthācca tathā dhīrā utpalākhyaṁ pracakṣate \|\|*

**The wise say that utpala is composed of a portion with Iss (bha) twice with a slista (r or s conjunct) after the first and fourth syllable.**  
**Iss Iss Iss Iss (bha, bha, bha, bha)**

*nartita-śarkara-kṛta-karkara*  
*vṛddha-marud-bhara-tardana nirbhara \|*  
*duṣṭa-vimardana śiṣṭa-vivardhana*  
*sarva-vilakṣaṇa mitra-kṛta-kṣaṇa  \|*  
*sad-bhuja-lakṣita-parvata-rakṣita*  
*niṣṭhura-garjana khinna-suhṛj-jana \|*  
*ruṣṭa-divaspati-garva-samunnati-*  
*tarjana-vibhrama nirgalita-bhrama \|*  
*śakra-kṛtas tava visphurad-utsava vīra \|\|*

**О Krsna, who destroyed the wind demon named Trnavarta, full of intense wind which stirred up hard lumps of earth which turned into fine gravel. О destroyer of the wicked who do not accept the Vedas. О nourisher of the followers of the Vedas. О Lord, distinguished from all others by remarkable qualities! О Krsna made joyful by friends. О Krsna, who protected friends who were tormented by the thundering clouds by lifting the mountain in your fine arms. О Krsna who performed the pastime of deriding the great pride of angry Indra. О Krsna, who was praised by Indra whose illusion was dispelled. О Krsna, installed as Govinda in a festival held by Indra.**

You destroyed (tardana) the wind demon named Trnavarta, full of intense wind which stirred up hard lumps of earth (karkara) which turned into fine gravel (sarkara). Sarkara means stones broken into small pieces according to Visva.

Carkrtis imitates the sound of the stones. You destroy the most wicked, who do not accept the Vedas (nirbhara-dusta). You nourish the followers of the Vedas (sista). These are all in the vocative.

You have qualities contrary to the baddha-muktas and nitya-muktas. О Supreme Lord! This means Krsna is the cause of all. You are made joyful (ksana) by friends. You protected, by the mountain held by your fine arms (sad-bhuja), your friends afflicted by the thundering clouds. He performed the pastime (vibhramah) of deriding the great pride of angry Indra. He was praised (stave) by Indra whose illusion that Krsna was a material human was dispelled, saying, “You are our master. Protect us, your servants.” You were subject of a festival installing you as Govinda by Indra.

### Text 12

*buddhīnāṁ parimohanaḥ kila hriyām uccāṭanaḥ stambhano*

**Комментарий:**

This is this verse after the kdlika.

О swan playing in the Yamuna! May the king of mantras composed of the fifth note of your flute be victorious. The qualities of the mantra are described. They think, “How will we go to him today?” It stuns fear of dharma in the most excellent (udagra) gopis. It brings under its control the elephants of their minds. And it attracts the bodies of the gopis. Here the powers of mantra to bewilder, drive away, control and stun are described one after the other.

О Krsna who meets (adrsta) the gopis attracted by the skill of the fine (kakali) sound arising in the forest! Kakali means fine according to Amara-kosa.

О Krsna satisfied with Radhika, who is endowed with cleverness (caturi). О friend (paksa) of the women (bhavini)\] The rest is clear.

**О Krsna, with earrings of swaying jasmines! О decorator of the circle of excellent women! О Krsna, who fought Kaliya! О Krsna, who defeated Kaliya, fearful to the whole world. О Krsna, worshipped by Siva and Brahma! О Krsna, overjoyed when your servants praise you a little! О Krsna, who defeated proud Indra! О Krsna, most capable of controlling those who afflict brahmanas and cows! О Krsna, defeating an elephant by your charming gait! О Krsna, whose neck is fragrant with sandalwood! О Krsna, with armbands shining on your beautiful arms! О Krsna, destroyer of attachment to other things! О Krsna, who astonish your friends with your beauty! О Krsna, with jingling jeweled bracelets! О Krsna, with large rangana flowers swaying in your hair! О Krsna, whose cloth shines yellow with kunkuma! О Krsna, with abundant, attractive fragrance! О Krsna, form of auspiciousness in Nanda’s house! О Krsna, golden with attractive kunkuma! О Krsna, whose soles are red in color! О Krsna, who has increasing prema for the gopis! О Krsna, having scented musk ointment always! Give auspiciousness to me!**

You have earrings of moving jasmines (yicalikd). You decorate the circle of excellent women (yaru-tanu). You fought (sangard) with the snake Kaliya. You defeated Kaliya, fearful to the whole world.

The next three items are clear in meaning. You are most capable (dhurandhara) of controlling those who afflict brahmanas and cows (cancala). The next three items are clear in meaning. You destroy attachment to other things (sanga-da). Da stands for dyati: destroying. You astonish your friends with your beauty (sakhi-gana-ranga-da).

You have jeweled bracelets that jingle. You have large rangana flowers moving in your hair. Your cloth shines yellow with kunkuma. You have abundant, attractive (laiigima) fragrance. The next two items are clear. (You are most auspicious in Nanda’s house. You become golden with attractive kunkuma.) The soles of your lotus feet are red (pinguid) in color. You have increasing (sancitd) prema for the gopis. The rest is clear in meaning.

**The kama-rupa-bhakti of the gopis has become famous simply as prema. (BRS 1.2.285) —**

Spread (santanu) auspiciousness to me.

### Text 15

*undita-hṛdayendu-maṇiḥ pūrṇa-kalaḥ kuvalayollāsī \|*

**Перевод:**

**The moon of Vrndavana, melting the moonstone hearts of the devotees, being full in sixteen phases, giving joy to the blue lotuses, destroying the darkness everywhere, shines.**

**Комментарий:**

A verse introduces the guna-rati-kalika.

The moon shines in Vrndavana. The author explains Krsna’s moon-like nature. It liquifies the moonstone hearts of the devotees. It has sixteen phases (kalah) or sixty-four arts. It brings joy to the blue lotuses (kuvalaya) or the earth.

He destroys the darkness and violence (sarvard). Varvara means great darkness according to Visva. This is prathamatisayokti with rupaka and pun as members.

Krsna is compared to the moon. Liquifying the moonstone hearts is rupaka. Puns are the full moon or full in arts, the joy to the lotus or earth and destroying darkness or demons.

Guna-rati type of nakha in canda-vrtta should be described:

**The canda-vrtta called guna-rati is endowed with ssl sss s (sa, na, la) as its portion, with the third syllable long.**

*kalaśī-dadhi-hara kala-śīlita-mukha*  
*lalitā-rati-kara lalitāvali-para dhīra \|\|*

**О Krsna, revealer of good qualities! О Krsna, destroyer of the cart demon! О Krsna, holder of a fresh stick! О Krsna, wanderer in all the forests! О Krsna, performer of dance pastimes! О Krsna, sweetness personified! О Krsna, who makes the forests fragrant! О Krsna, who care for the cows! О Krsna, holding your buffalo horn you steal the composure of the cows! О Krsna, controlling the universe by practicing on your shining flute! О Krsna, with red lips! О Krsna, with fresh youth! О Krsna, with long arms! О Krsna, having great mercy like an ocean! О Krsna, who made Pralambha like a grasshopper by the strength of Balarama, like a baby elephant! О Krsna, holding a lotus in your hand! О Krsna, filling people with rasa! О Krsna, stealing yogurt from a pot! О Krsna, whose mouth produces sweet sounds of an infant! О Krsna, producing rati in Lalita! О Krsna, attached to the group of attractive women! О intelligent Krsna!**

He reveals qualities like mercy and affection. He destroyed the carl with the demon. He destroyed the cart by moving his strong, tender foot. He keeps a new stick near, in his hand. He wanders in all the forests. He performs dance pastimes (nata-lila). He is sweet. He makes the forests fragrant by his bodily fragrance. He cares for the cows. With buffalo horn in his hand he steals the composure of the cows.

He controls the universe by practicing (khurali) on his shining flute. He has red lips. He has fresh youth (nava-taruna). He has long arms.

He has great (parimala) mercy like the ocean (varunalayd). By strength of a baby elephant (kalabhayita), as Balarama (bala) he made Pralambha like a grasshopper (salabhdyita). The next three items are clear. His mouth is served (sllita) by sweet sounds of a child. He produces rati in Lalita. He is attached to the group of attractive women (lalitavali). О clever one (dhlra).

The matanga-khelita type of ndkha in canda-vrtta should be described.

**The canda-vrtta called matanga-khelita is composed of parts comprised of the sequence Isl 1 s (ra, gu, la) with a long vowel in the first and third syllables, and a madhura (nasal conjunct) or slista (r or s conjunct) after the fourth syllable.**

*nātha he nanda-gehinī-śanda*  
*pūtanā-piṇḍa-pātane caṇḍa*  
*dānave daṇḍa-kārakākhaṇḍa-*

*sauhṛdāśaṅka-yoṣitām aṅka-*

*mālikā-kaṇṭha kautukākuṇṭha*  
*pāṭalī-kunda-mādhavī-vṛnda-*  
*sevitottuṅga-śekharotsaṅga*  
*māṁ sadā hanta pālayānanta vīra \|\|*

**О master! Giver of auspiciousness to Yasoda! О Krsna, filled with anger when throwing the body of Putana! О punisher of the demons! О Krsna, acting unsteadily in pastimes of pauganda, during which you displayed continuous strength! О Krsna, hiding near the gates of Gokula. О Krsna, giver of bliss to excellent Radha. О Krsna, whose limbs play with Cupid who is stimulated with an angry shower of arrows on glancing at the cane and madhavi groves! О Krsna, playing like an elephant on seeing the pastimes of the gopis! О Krsna, detached from results in pastimes! О Krsna who embrace the fearless women who desire only your happiness! О Krsna, on whose neck is a garland full of intelligent bees! О Krsna, tireless in pastimes! О Krsna whose central high crown is served by patali, jasmine and madhavi flowers! О unlimited one! Please protect me always. О valiant one!**

О master (natha)! О giver of auspiciousness (sanda) to Yasoda by your birth! Angrily you threw the body (pinda) of Piltana outside of your kingdom. Pinda in masculine means body according to Nanartha-varga. You punished the demons (danave). You acted unsteadily (uddanda) in pastimes of pauganda, ending in the tenth year, during which you displayed continuous strength (sard). You hid on the porches of Gokula. Alinda means an outer door according to Amara-kosa. (O Govinda!)

He is then addressed according to his kaisora activities. He gives excellent Radha full bliss.

Your limbs play with Cupid who is stimulated with an angry shower of arrows, on glancing at the cane and madhavi groves. Vetasi means cane according to Halayudha. You play like an elephant on seeing the pastimes (ranga) of the gopis (gopa-sarahga). Sarahga means a cataka bird, bee, deer or elephant according to Visva.

You are detached from results in pastimes (khelitasahga). You embrace (ahga-palika) the fearless (asanka) women who desire only your happiness (sauhrda). Sahka means doubt according to Haima. Anga-pali means embrace according to Halayudha.

You have on your neck a garland with intelligent (caru) bees. You are tireless (akuntha) in pastimes (kautuka). The middle portion (utsangd) of your high crown is served by patali, jasmine and madhavi flowers. О unlimited one! Please protect me always. О valiant one!

О Govinda! Give me joy by the fragrance of your lotus feet. О root of the shoots of condensed happiness. Kanda is a root according to Haima.

*kunda-daśana baddha-raśana*  
*rukma-vasana ramya-hasana \|\| deva \|\|*

**О Krsna with teeth like jasmine flowers! О Krsna bound at the waist with a belt! О Krsna, wearing golden cloth! О Krsna, with attractive smile. О lord!**

A viruda follows.

You have a belt bound to your waist (baddha-rasana'). You have a garment yellow like gold (rukma). The rest is clear.

**Комментарий:**

This verse introduces the tilaka-kalika.

О Madhava! May the beauty of your freshly sprouting (kadamba) smile nourish (bibhartu) my bliss (mudam). Kadamba means a stalk of a plant. Dambara means wise. The rest is clear.

**tilakam \|**

The tilaka type of nakha in canda-vrtta should be described.

*nanastanaiḥ kṛtairaṁśairnavamānmadhurojjvalaiḥ \|*  
*nibaddhaṁ caṇḍavṛttaṁ tu tilakākhyamathocire \|\|*

**The canda-vrtta called tilaka has a series of sss sss ssl sss sss (na, na, sa, na, na) where the ninth syllable has madhura (nasal) conjunct.**

**O Krsna, whose dancing eyes defeat a flock of khanjana birds! O Krsna, whose feet are skillful at destroying the beauty of perfect lotuses! O Krsna, whose skillful dancing destroyed the pride of Kaliya! O Krsna, most effulgent with the beauty of fresh blue lotuses! O Krsna, wearing charming cloth like condensed lightning! O Krsna, best attractive dancer on the bank of the Yamuna! O Krsna, whose arms are fragrant with sandalwood! O Krsna, whose flute sound gives joy to the gopis! O Krsna, whose side glances shine with the sweetness of new intoxication! O Krsna, whose fragrant face is surrounded by swarming bees! O Krsna, whose excellent face is the full moon in autumn! O Krsna, happy with golden makara earrings! O Krsna, whose arms are a cage for the parrot-like hearts of the gopis! O Krsna, whose hair is attractive with jasmines. O Krsna, skillful at kissing the moon-like faces of the gopis! O Krsna, whose rough battles destroy the intense pride of the demons!**

Generally the meaning is clear. You are skillful at dancing in the southern style (natana-patima). Your cloth is comparable to concentrated lighting (ghana-tadit).

Your eyes defeat all (parikara) khanjana birds. Parikara means all according to Medini. Your face is the full moon (upacita) of autumn. You give happiness to observers to your hair (sirasija). You have sharp (khara) battles to destroy (dumbana) the strong pride of the demons.

### Text 20

*raṇati hare tava veṇau*  
*nāryo danujāś ca kampitāḥ khinnāḥ \|*  
*vanam anapekṣita-dayitāḥ*  
*kara-bālān projjhya dhāvanti \|\|20\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna! When your flute sounds, the women and demons, tremble and perspire, and forgetting about their spouses, giving up actions at hand, run to the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse follows the kalika.

О Hari! When your flute sounds (ranati), both the gopis and the demons run to the forest. The gopis give up holding their hair in their hands for dressing it and run to you situated in the forest. The demons give up their swords held in their hands (kara-bdldn) for fighting and enter the depths of the forest. They are described. The women are ornamented with sdttvika-bhdvas, trembling and perspiring (kampitah khinndh), arising from rati. The demons tremble and become depressed from fear of death. The women forget their husbands (anapeksita-dayitah). The demons forget their wives. This is the alankdra of pun (.slesa).

Since madhurya-rasa and bhaydnaka-rasa are suggested, there is no contradiction from the different subjects. The astonishing nature of the flute is suggested from its producing contrary states simultaneously.

*kuṅkuma-puṇḍraka gumphita-puṇḍraka*  
*saṅkula-kaṅkaṇa kaṇṭhaga-raṅgaṇa \|\| deva \|\|*

After this follows a viruda.

You have kunkuma tilaka (pundraka). О Krsna with golden bracelets filled with madhavi flowers (pundrakd). Thus, the nine types of nakha were illustrated.

О attractive goblet for drinking by the bee-like eyes of the gopis.

Bhrngara means a golden goblet according to Amara-kosa. О deity of madhurya-rasa (srngaradhisvara)! I praise you, dressed beautifully (srngaram).

**caṇḍavṛttasya viśikhe paṅkeruham \|**

The pankeruha of the visikha type of canda-vrtta should be described.

*syāt pañcadhā sa viśikhaḥ padmaṁ kundaṁ ca campakam \|*  
*vañjulaṁ bakulaṁ ceti kāmasyāmī śarā matāḥ \|\| iti \|*

**There are five types of viSikha: padma, kunda, campaka, vanjula and bakula.**

Padma is described:

*acyutas tu bhavet padma pañcamādyukta-saṁyutam \|*

**Acyuta becomes padma when it has a conjunct after the fifth syllable (instead of the sixth).**

Acyuta is described. This was previously described.

*nayābhyāṁ kalpitair aṁśaiḥ pañcame dīrghaśālibhiḥ \| antyācchliṣṭayutopetaiścaṇḍamacyutamūcire*

**Acyuta is the canda-vrtta with the portion sss sll (na, ya) with the fifth syllable long and slista at the end (r or s conjunct after the sixth syllable).**

Padma has six types like pankeruha, etc., previously mentioned. Pankeruha is now described.

*syāccetkavargyamadhuraṁ pūrvapañcamavarṇakam\|*  
*padmaṁ paṅkeruhaṁ proktaṁ kalikāvedibhirbudhaiḥ \|\|*

**If the syllable after the fifth syllable there is a conjunct with ka-varga and nasal, it is called the pankeruha type of padma.**

*madhu-rasa-piṅga-grathita-lavaṅga*

**О fearless one! О place of prema! О Krsna, roaming about with your friends! О Krsna whose gentle smile conquers a conch! О Krsna, producing joy by the deep sound of your horn! О Krsna, whose limbs dance with joy! О Krsna, followed by the affectionate deer in Vraja! О Krsna, with lavanga flowers yellow and filled with honey swinging on your ears! О Krsna, who wounded Kaliya’s head by your intense waves of dancing. О Krsna, whose love arises by the loud waves of sound of bees humming on the high tops of land lotus trees with flower clusters! О Krsna, who play new songs because of the soft movements of the joyful does’ eyes, wandering like huge bees! О Krsna with slightly crooked eyes! О Krsna, sleeping on the laps of the gopis who have come for a new meeting! О Krsna, whose face is praised as a faultless moon! О Krsna with lotus feet! Give mercy to me, poor and sinful.**

О fearless one (gata-sanka)! О place of prema. Vitanka means a dove or place according to Amara-kosa. You roam about with your friends. Your gentle smile conquers a conch. You produce joy by the sound of your horn which spreads far and is sweet and deep (sphutatara). Your limbs dance with joy (ksana). О Krsna, full of joy! Ksana means a festival according to Haima. You are followed by the affectionate deer (kuranga) in Vraja. You have lavanga flowers yellow (pinga) and filled with honey swinging (riiigat) on your ears. О Krsna with moving lavanga ear ornaments! You split (vranita) Kaliya’s head by your intense waves of dancing.

Your love arises (prabalad) by the loud waves of sound of bees humming on the high tops (srnga) of land lotus trees with flower clusters. Srnga means a peak according to Medinl. The sound of bees stimulates your love. You play new songs because of the soft movements of the joyful does’ eyes, wandering like huge bees. You play songs because of remembering the gopis on seeing the does’ eye movements. This is the alankara of smarana. This is described in Kavya-kaustubha.

*sadṛśānubhavādvastusmṛtiḥ syātsmaraṇaṁ matam \|*

**Remembrance of an object from experiencing a similar object is called smarana.**

О Krsna with slightly (dara) crooked eyes! You sleep on the laps (anke) of the gopis who have come for a new meeting (sanketa-ga). Your face is praised as a faultless (sa-kalariketara) moon (prsad-arika). Prsat means spotted. O Krsna with lotus feet! Give mercy to me, poor (rarike) and sinful (sa-parike). Rarika means poor according to Amara-kosa. One should examine the parikeruha with distinctive features as described.

You make fine sounds with the jeweled bells on your waist.

**May you manifest excellence! О Krsna, shining with peacock feather and sweet flower clusters spread with sweetness and increasing in beauty, moving in the wind on top of your hair! О Krsna, praised by Brahma! О Krsna whose ankle bells sound like swarms of buzzing bees in the mountain bowers! О Krsna, who disrespected Kaliya! О Krsna, yellow with pollen from the wind humming sweetly carrying fresh honey, blowing gently in the groves! О Krsna, who destroyed the strong grass fire! О Krsna, fond of gunja berries! О Krsna, taking shelter of bowers on the mountain! О Krsna, wide awake for having amorous affairs! О Krsna, whose hands are purer than red lotuses! О Krsna, driving away the wind and rain! О Krsna, who conquered Siva’s pride in his sense control and power by the host of arrows of fresh Cupid, who has been revived by the fragrance and the sound of your ankle bells! О Krsna, most clever!**

You shine with peacock feather and sweet flower clusters spread (panca) with sweetness and increasing in beauty, moving in the wind on top of your hair.

The soft sounds of your ankle bells quickly becomes swarms of buzzing bees in the mountain bowers. The sound of your ornament resembles the buzzing of bees.

You disrespected (ganjana) Kaliya. You become yellow with pollen from the wind humming sweetly, carrying fresh honey, blowing gently (khanjan) in the groves. Manjan means sweet sound according to Kavi-kalpa-druma. You destroyed the strong grass fire. You are fond of gunja berries. You take shelter of bowers on the mountain. You are wide awake for having amorous affairs. Your hands are purer than red lotuses (kanja). You drive away the wind and rain (jhanjhanila). Jhanjhavata means with rain according to Halayudha

You conquer Siva’s pride in his sense control and power by the host of arrows of fresh Cupid, who has been revived by the fragrance and the sound of your ankle bells. Cupid was revived by the abundant (panji) sound of Krsna’s ankle bells and his bodily fragrance. With fresh youth, with his great strength, he pierced Siva, his previous enemy with the glances of youth. This is kavi-praudhokti. This indicates the great attractiveness of Krsna’s ankle bells and fragrance. Panji means a lot. The root is paj given in the sutras. The roots have many meanings. Similarly pac means to cook and to reveal. As pac (becoming panji) means to manifest, its meaning is clear.
