**Victory! Victory! О Krsna fond of a stick! О Krsna with peacock feather in your crown! О Krsna whose cheeks have a smile like the son of the half moon! O beehive of affection! O Krsna with a moon-like face! O lake of madhurya-rasa! Crusher of Kaliya’s many hoods! O Krsna with uncountable universes situated separately in your belly! O Krsna, with jingling bells on your belt! O Krsna, bold in great battles! O Krsna, beating the ferocious demons by your arms like huge elephant trunks. O Krsna, who defeat your army of friends by arguments produced from scripture! O Krsna, fond of the bhandira tree. O Krsna, who broke the pots of yogurt white like fresh sea foam! O Krsna, whose sweet flute sound defeats all the cuckoos! O Krsna, dear to the gopis with pearl necklaces! O Krsna, excellent lion in battle! O clever one!**

O Krsna, fond of a stick! You have a peacock feather in your crown. Your cheeks have a smile like the son of the half moon. Sapinda means son according to Visvalocana. O beehive of affection (karanda). Karanda means beehive according to Visva. You have a moonlike (dvijapati) face (tunda). O lake of madhurya-rasa!

Crusher of Kaliya’s many hoods (phana)! You have uncountable universes situated separately in your belly (picanda). You have jingling bells on your belt.

You are bold (ghanta) in great battles. You beat the ferocious demons by your arms like huge elephant trunks. You defeat your friend’s army (bala) by arguments (vitanda) produced from scripture (panda). You are fond of Bhandira.

You broke (khandi-krta) the pots of yogurt like fresh sea foam. As a fickle child you broke the yogurt pots. Hindira means foam according to Amara-kosa.

Your sweet flute sound defeats all the cuckoos. You are dear to the gopis with pearl necklaces. Or they are dear to you. You are an excellent lion (kanthlrava) in battle. You defeat all enemies.

After the kalika, this verse appears.

О lotus-eyed Krsna! Decorate my heart with the beauty of your face (tunda-sriya).

The beauty is described. The beauty defeats many (ghataya) rising (udyat) moons (acanda). Krsna is described. He has a stick in his hand (dandi). He is endowed (slistah) with great valor (candima-dambarena) of excellent (uddanda) arms similar to rodlike (kanda) snakes. Bhoga means snake according to Medinl. Kanda means a stick according to Amara-kosa. He is beautiful with thick sandalwood tilaka. Srikhanda means sandalwood according to Halayudha.

*kandarpa-kodaṇḍa-darpa-kriyoddaṇḍa-*  
*dṛg-bhaṅgi-kāṇḍīra saṁjuṣṭa-bhāṇḍīra \|\| dhira \|\|*

**О Krsna, firing arrows of your glances in activities of pride that conquer the world from your brows which are Cupid’s bows! О Krsna, playing at Bhandira! О clever one!**

A viruda follows the verse.

О Krsna, firing arrows of your glances in activities of pride that conquer the world (darpa-kriya) ofyour brows which are Cupid’s bows! О Krsna who frequents the Bhandira tree! Kandira means archery, firing arrows, according to Amara-kosa. O Krsna who plays at (samjusta) Bhandira!

The indiravara type of viSikha in canda-vrtta should be described.

**Ta-varga with a nasal appears after the fifth syllable in indivara.**

*madhurima-santarpita-jagad-antar-*

**May you be victorious! О destroyer of enemies! О Krsna, who satisfies the world with your beauty! О soft-hearted Krsna! Krsna, fond of spring! О Krsna with pearl-like teeth! О Krsna with fickle glances! О Krsna whose news is widespread! О Krsna with Balarama as your friend! О Krsna who liberates the devotees! О Supreme Lord! О son of Nanda! О Krsna, the root of qualities! О Krsna, with complexion of a fresh black cloud! О Krsna with teeth shining like jasmine buds! О Krsna, holding the universe in your belly! О Krsna whose hair is worshiped by clusters of fresh mandara flowers endowed with fresh fragrance and sprouting in Vrndavana! О Krsna, praised by excellent groups, who offer respects! О Krsna whose activities give happiness to Nanda! О Krsna whose eyes deride beautiful blue lotuses blossoming by the moon! May you be victorious, clever one!**

Jaya is repeated for showing respect. Hanta indicates joy. О destroyer (abhihantar) of enemies! You satisfy the world with your beauty! You have a soft heart (antar). You are fond of spring. You have teeth white like pearls. You have fickle glances.

Your news (udanta') spreads everywhere. You have Ananta as your friend because of your powers. Or you are Ananta’s friend. The devotees, having bhava for you are delivered or liberated. О Supreme Lord (prabhuvara)! О son of Nanda! You are the root of qualities like friendliness and mercy (guna-kanda). You have the color of a black fresh cloud (nava-kanda). You have teeth (radd) shining like jasmine buds (kunda). Because of writing details of his form, there is no fault of repetition. You hold the universe in your belly (tunda).

Your hair is worshiped by clusters of fresh mandara flowers endowed with fresh fragrance, growing in Vrndavana. Mandara is the deva-taru tree. You are praised by excellent groups such as devatas and brahmanas, who offer respects (yandaru). Vandina means reciters of praise according to Amara-kosa. Your activities (ihita) give happiness (nandi) to Nanda. Your eyes deride beautiful blue lotuses blossoming by the moon (yidhu). Be victorious! О clever one!

**aruṇāmbhoruham \|**

The arundmbhoruha type of visikha in canda-vrtta should be described.

**Every fifth syllable is pa-varga with a nasal in arunambhoruha.**

*jaya rasa-sampad-viracita-jhampa*  
*smara-kṛta-kampa priya-jana-śampa*  
*pravaṇita-kampa-sphurad-anukampa*  
*dyuti-jita-śampa-sphuṭa-nava-campa-*

*nmukha-lasad-ambhoruha-mukha lambo*  
*dbhaṭa-bhuja lambodara-vara-kumbho*  
*pama-kuca-bimboṣṭha-yuvati-cumbo*  
*dbhaṭa-parirambhotsuka kuru śaṁ bhos*  
*taḍid-avalamborjita-milad-ambho-*  
*dhara-suviḍambodbhura nata-śambho*  
*parijita-dambholi-garima-sambhā-*

*ka-manasi sampādaya mayi taṁ pā-*  
*kimam anukampā-lavam iha \|\| dhira \|\|*

**Victory! О Krsna, jumping in the ocean of madhurya and other rasas! О Krsna trembling from love! О Krsna, protecting the auspiciousness of the devotees! О Krsna, merciful to Varuna who offered respects! О Krsna, hair tied with fresh blooming campakas conquering lightning! О Krsna, whose face is praised by two blossoming kadambas hanging from your ears! О Krsna, affectionate to the babies of the cowherds! О Krsna, whose face is like a shining lotus blossoming in the rising sun! О Krsna, with long excellent arms! О Krsna, boldly kissing the gopis endowed with bimba lips and breasts like the forehead bumps of Ganesa! О Krsna, enthusiastically embracing the gopis! О Lord! Give auspiciousness to the devotees! О Krsna, deriding the pride of clouds flashing with lightning! О Krsna, to whom Siva bows! О Krsna, defeating the pride of Indra whose arms are famous for the power of the thunderbolt! Give to my mind, greedy for material enjoyment, a particle of ripe mercy!**

You submerge yourself (jhampa) in the ocean of madhurya and other rasas. Jhampa means jumping into according to Haima. You protect the auspiciousness (sampa) of the devotees. You showed mercy to Varuna (kampa) who offered respects (pravanita). Your hair is tied with fresh blooming campakas, shining and conquering lightning (.sampa). Campa means campaka, a golden flower according to Amara-kosa. Your hair is woven with campakas. Your face is praised by two blossoming kadambas hanging from your ears. You are affectionate to the babies of the cowherds (dimbha).

Your face is like a shining lotus blossoming (parijrmbhonmukha) in the rising sun.

You have long excellent arms. You boldly kiss the gopis with bimbalips and breasts like the forehead bumps of Ganesa (lambhodara). You enthusiastically embrace the gopis. Utsuka means zealous according to Amara-kosa. O Lord! Give auspiciousness (sum) to the devotees. The pride of clouds flashing with lightning is derided by your form with yellow cloth. Siva bows to you (nata-sambho).

You defeated the pride of Indra (jambhahita) whose arms are famous (sambhavita) for the power of the thunderbolt (dambholi).

Give to my mind greed for material enjoyment (lampaka manasi) a particle of mercy. Lampaka means greedy according to Haima. That mercy is ripe (pdkimam).

Krsna is described. He has the pride of an intoxicated elephant (madira stambarema). This means he is unrestrained in pastimes. He defeats a pile of collyrium by the beauty of his very black limbs.

Phullambhuja type of visikha in canda-vrrta should be described. This is also called kahlara.

**A conjunct with I after the fifth syllable is called kahlara.**

*vraja-pṛthu-pallī-parisara-vallī-*  
*vana-bhuvi tallī-gaṇa-bhṛti mallī-*

**Situated in the creeper groves at the edge of the great cowherd village of Vraja, filled with water bodies, served by jasmines, sivamalli which conquer Cupid’s arrows, and excellent lotuses, resounding with many crickets, О Krsna, absorbed joyfully in dancing with women in a circle! О Krsna, defeating Cupid’s pride by your fickle, joyful eyebrows! О Krsna, with charming tilaka! О Krsna, equal to hundreds of skillful Cupids! О Krsna, destroyer of trembling demons in a small stream of warfare! О Krsna, of auspicious actions!**

You are situated in the creeper groves at the edge (parisara) of the great cowherd village (prthu-pall) of Vraja. Palli means a cowherd according to Amara-kosa. Parisara means the border according to Amara-kosa. The place has many water bodies (talli-gana). Talia means a water body according to Haima. The i ending indicates small. There are many water bodies there. It is served by jasmines (malli), sivamalli, which conquer the arrows of Cupid, and excellent lotuses (kumuda-matalli). It has a swarm of crickets (jhilli).

You are engaged in a mass (jhalli) of joy by dancing with women in a circle (hallisaka). That is the meaning of halltsaka according to Haima. You defeat the pride of Cupid who holds rati to his chest (malli-mada bhara) by your joyful fickle eyebrows. Malla means to hold according to Kalpa-druma. You have charming tilaka. You are equal hundreds of Cupids, expert in arts (kalya). You churn up masses of trembling demons in the joyful rivers of battles. You cross all the battles like crossing a small stream. О Krsna, with auspicious actions!

By your music (sumadhura kala) you attract flocks of deer (rallaka).

Your hair is surrounded by a garland of red halldka lotuses.

The campaka types of visikha of canda-vrtta should be described.

*sānuprāsaiḥ pratiyugamādāvante ca campakam \|\|*

**Campdka is defined as having Iss sss (bha and na) as its portion, with repetition of similar syllables in the two Iss portions and the two sss portions.**

**(Iss sss Iss sss Iss sss Iss sss)**

*sañcalad-aruṇa-cañcala-karuṇa-sundara-nayana kandara-śayana*  
*ballava-śaraṇa pallava-caraṇa maṅgala-ghusṛṇa-piṅgala-masṛṇa*

*śaṁ vara-valaya ḍambara kalaya \|\| deva \|\|*

**О Krsna, endowed with beautiful, merciful, red eyes which enter the hearts of the gopis! О Krsna, sleeping in a cave! О Krsna, shelter of the cowherds! О Krsna, with bud-like feet! О Krsna, shining red with auspicious kunkuma! О Krsna, decorated with sandalwood! О Krsna, whose words cause joy! О Krsna, breaker of the cart! О Krsna, punisher of the fearsome, proud demons! О Krsna, giving joy to the people! О Krsna, protector of cows! О Krsna, holding a buffalo horn!**

**О Krsna, subduer of Kaliya! О Krsna, lifter of the saintly hill! О Krsna, charming in appearance! О Krsna, with the gait of an elephant! О Krsna, abode of words that generate love! О Krsna, wearing an attractive crown! О Krsna, holding an asoka stick in your hand! О Krsna, whose prowess defeats a host of sarabhas! О Krsna, whose faces is endowed with earrings! О Krsna, whose beauty gives joy to the Yamuna! О Krsna, with forest flowers in your hair! О Krsna, the destroyer of fear of the cowherd boys, fearful of the forest fire! О Krsna, surrounded by calves! О Krsna, charming with catuhsama! Please produce auspiciousness! О wearer of excellent bracelets! О Krsna endowed with extensive pastimes!**

You have beautiful, merciful, red eyes which enter (sancalat) the hearts of the gopis. The next seven items are clear. You punish the fearsome (vikata), proud demons (danuja). You make people joyful (parvitd). You protect the cows. You hold a buffalo horn (gavald). You defeated Kaliya (pannagd). You lifted the saintly hill (sannaga). You have a charming appearance (ydland). You walk like an elephant (sindhurd). You are the abode (sadana) of words that generate love (madand).

You wear an attractive crown. Your hand is decorated with a stick made of asoka woods (yanjuld). Vanjula means asoka tree and karabha means the hand from the wrist to the little finger according to Amara-kosa. Your prowess defeats a host of sarabhas (eight footed creatures according to Haima). Your face Gapand) is endowed (sanditd) with swaying earrings. Lapana means face according to Amara-kosa. Your beauty gives joy to the Yamuna (tapana-kanyakd). You have forest flowers in your hair (garbhakd). Garbhaka means in the hair according to Halayudha.

You are the destroyer of fear (sarana) of the cowherd boys, who shouted out fear of the forest fire (viranat). You are surrounded (kavalitd) by calves (tarnd). You are charming with catuhsama (varnaka). This means sandalwood, aguru, musk and kunkuma according to Haima. Please produce auspiciousness (sam). О wearer of excellent bracelets (yalayd)\\ О Krsna endowed with extensive pastimes (dambard)!

*tvam atra caṇḍāsura-maṇḍalīnāṁ*  
*raṇḍāvaśiṣṭāni gṛhāṇi kṛtvā \|*  
*pūrṇānyakārṣīr vraja-sundarībhir*  
*vṛndāṭavī-puṇḍraka-maṇḍapāni \|\|35\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Making the demons’ wives into widows, you have filled the pundraka pavilions of Vrndavana with gopis.**

**Комментарий:**

This verse introduces vanjula-kalika.

О Lord! Making the demons’ wives into widows (randa), you have filled the pundraka flower pavilions of Vrndavana with gopis. Killing the demons, you play with your beloved who are then without worries. Randa means widow according to Medini. Pundraka is the vasantl plant.

**vañjulam \|**

Vanjula type of visikha in canda-vrtta should be described.

*najalair ghaṭitair aṁśair madhurottara pañcamaiḥ \|*  
*nibaddhaṁ vañjulaṁ nāma kalikāvedināṁ matam \|\|*

**According to the wise, vanjula type of kalika has sss sis s (na, ja, la) as its portion, with nasal conjunct after the fifth syllable.**

*jaya jaya sundara-vihasita mandara-vijita-purandara nija-giri-kandara-*  
*rati-rasa-śandhara maṇi-yuta-kandhara guṇa-maṇi-mandira hṛdi valad-indira gati-jita-sindhura parijana-bandhura paśupati-nandana tilakita-candana vidhi-kṛta-vandana pṛthu-haricandana-parivṛta-nandana-madhurima-nindana-madhuvana vandita-kusuma-sugandhita-vana-vara-rañjita rati-bhara-sañjita śikhi-dala-kuṇḍala-sahakṛta-bhaṇḍila nava-sita-tandula-jayi-rada-maṇḍala rati-raṇa-paṇḍita vara-tanu-bhaṇḍita nakha-pada-maṇḍita daśana-vikhaṇḍit \|\| dhira \|\|*

**О Krsna, who smiles with beauty! О Krsna, defeating Indra by lifting the mountain! О Krsna, experiencing happiness by the rasa of love in the caves of Govardhana! О Krsna, with jewels on your neck! О Krsna, a temple of jewel-like qualities! О Krsna, having Laksmi on your heart! О Krsna, defeating an elephant by your gait! О Krsna, affectionate to your friends! О Krsna, giving joy to Siva! О Krsna, wearing sandalwood tilaka! О Krsna, respected by Brahma! О Krsna, whose Madhuvana derides the sweetness of Indra’s Nandana forest surrounded by huge, celestial hari-candana trees! О Krsna, pleased by Vrndavana which is fragrant with respected flowers! О Krsna, controlled by the intense prema of the forest! О Krsna, wearing srisa flowers with your earrings and peacock feather! О Krsna, whose teeth defeat by their brilliance new white rice grains! О Krsna, acting like clown in front of the gopis! О Krsna, whose chest is decorated with their nail marks! О Krsna, wounded by their teeth! О clever one!**

О Krsna, who smiles with beauty! You defeated Indra by lifting the mountain (mandard). You experience happiness (sandhard) by the rasa of love in the caves of Govardhana! The next eight items are clear. Pasupati means Siva.

His Madhuvana derides the sweetness of Indra’s nandana forest surrounded by huge, celestial haricandana trees. He is pleased (rafijita) by Vrndavana (yana-vard) which is fragrant with respected flowers. You are controlled (sanjita) by the intense prema of the forest. Sirisa flowers accompany your peacock feather and earrings. Bhandila means Sirisa flower according to Amara-kosa. You wear sirisa flowers with your earrings and peacock feather. Your teeth (rada-mandala) defeat by their brilliance new white rice grains (tandula). You acted like clown (bhandita) in front of the gopis. You became embarrassed using vulgar words. Your chest is decorated with their nail marks. You are wounded by their teeth. О clever one (dhira)!

### Text 36

*nininda nijam indirā vapur avekṣya yāsāṁ śriyaṁ*  
*vicārya guṇa-cāturīm acalajā ca lajjāṁ gatā \|*  
*lasat-paśupa-nandinī-tatibhir ābhir ānanditaṁ*

**О master of Gokula! We offer respects to you, most beautiful, who give joy to the gopis shining with qualities, seeing whose beauty Laksmi criticized her own body, considering whose qualities and actions, Parvati became ashamed.**

**Комментарий:**

“The devatas such as Indra enjoy with their wives. If I do so what is significant?” That is rare even in your avataras, what to speak devatas. That is indicated here.

О master of Gokula! We offer respects to you (yandemahi). Krsna is described.

You are pleased with the group of gopis shining with incomparable qualities and form. The gopis are described. Seeing (aveksya) their beauty, Laksmi, wife of Visnu criticizes her own body, since she cannot take a body in the pastimes of Vraja. Parvati (acalaja) wife of your avatara Siva, considering their skill in singing and dancing, and your qualities, becomes shamed. She was not equal to them in skill and qualities. Even among your associates you have no compare. You are most beautiful.

*lāvaṇya sāram asamordhvam ananya siddham*

**With their eyes they always drink the nectar of Lord Krsna’s form, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. (SB 10.44.14)**

The details were previously stated. Thus, you are beyond compare. There is no one like you anywhere.

*rasaparipāṭī sphuṭataruvāṭī manasijadhāṭī priyanavaśāṭīhara jaya \|\| vira \|\|*

A viruda follows that verse.

О Krsna, fond of succession of rasas like madhurya. Paripatl means succession according to Amara-kosa. Fond of garden of flowering groves, fond of amorous assaults (dhati) and stealer of the new dresses of the young gopis. О valiant one! May you be victorious.

**Перевод:**

**Комментарий:**

Before kunda-kalika there is this verse.

О killer of Mura! May the sound of your flute give happiness to us. The sound is described. It is worshipped by the respected (sambhrantaih) Vedas along with its six angas (sasad-anga-patam). It is placed reverently (gauravat) on their heads by the deities of the Upanisads. It is praised by joyful omkara with offering obeisance. The glory of the flute’s sound cannot be indicated by such poetic words.

Remembering the experience of Brahma and Siva, the sound is naturally respected because of the bliss of Parabrahman.

**kundam \|**

The kuncla type of visikha in canda-vrtta should be described.

*bhajābhyāṁ kalpitairaṁśaiḥ prāyaśchinnairdviśo'kṣaraiḥ \|*  
*ādyapañcamayoryuktottaritaiḥ kundamucyate \|\| iti \|*

**When there is Iss sis (bha,ja) as its component, with two syllable words (generally), and conjuncts after the first and fifth syllables it is called kunda.**

*nanda-kula-candra lupta-bhava-tandra kunda-jayi-danta duṣṭa-kulahanta-*  
*riṣṭa-suvasanta miṣṭa-sasu(mu)danta sandalita-mallikandalita-valli-*  
*guñja-dali-puñja-mañjutara-kuñja-labdha-rati-raṅga hṛdya-jana-saṅga-*  
*śarma-lasad-aṅga harṣa-kṛd-anaṅga matta-para-puṣṭa-ramya-kala-ghuṣṭa gandha-bhara-juṣṭa puṣpa-vana-tuṣṭa kṛtta-khala-yakṣa yuddha-nayad-akṣa valgu-kaca-pakṣa-baddha-śikhi-pakṣa piṣṭa-nata-tṛṣṇa tiṣṭha hṛdi kṛṣṇa \|\| vira \|\|*

**О moon of Nanda’s family. О Krsna, who destroy the illusion of samsara! О Krsna whose teeth defeat the jasmine! О Krsna, destroying the demon families! О Krsna, fond of spring! О Krsna, whose beautiful topics are sweet! О Krsna, having amorous pastimes in the bowers most charming with blossoming jasmines, newly sprouting creepers and humming swarms of bees! О Krsna whose limbs shine with happiness from association with charming persons! О Krsna, having love which produces joy! О Krsna, the sweet sounds from whose throat are attractive like an intoxicated cuckoo! О Krsna, laden with fragrance! О Krsna, satisfied with the flowering forest! О Krsna, who killed Sankhacuda! О Krsna, skillful in the conduct of war! О Krsna, with a peacock feather bound in your attractive hair! О Krsna, destroying material desires in your devotees! О Krsna! Reside in my heart. О clever Krsna!**

You destroy the illusion (tandra) of samsara (bhava). The next three items are clear. Your beautiful (sat) topics (udanta) are sweet (mista). Udanta means news according to Amara-kosa. You obtain amorous pastimes (rati-ranga) in the bowers most charming (manjutara) with blossoming jasmines, newly sprouting creepers and humming swarms of bees (ali-punja). Your limbs shine with happiness (sarma) from association with charming (hrdya) persons. Your love produces joy (harsa-krt). The sweet sounds from your throat (kala-ghusta) are attractive like an intoxicated cuckoo (para-pusta). The next four items are clear. The yaksa is Sankhacuda. You have a peacock feather bound in your attractive hair. Kaca means hair according to Amara-kosa. You destroy (pista) other desires in your devotees (nata). О Krsna! Reside in my heart.

**bakulabhāsuram \|**

Bakula-bhasura type of visikha in canda-vrtta should be described.

*śṛṅkhalā vandha ghaṭitaṁ bakulaṁ paricakṣate \|*  
*bhāsuraṁ maṅgalaṁ tuṅgāmiti syādbakulaṁ tridhā \|\|*

**Lines which are bound together by repeated sound groups (rhyme) are called bakula. There were three types: bhasura, mangala and tuhga.**

Tunga is not represented here. Bhasura’s characteristics are described as follows:

*mithaḥ śṛṅkhalitairvadvaṁ bhāsuraṁ pajjhaṭīpadaiḥ iti \|*

**Bhasura has repeated sound groups at the end of one line and beginning of the next line, having pajjhati or sixteen matrihas.**

*jaya jaya vaṁśī-vādya-viśārada śārada-sarasīruha-paribhāvaka-*

*bhāsura-kuṭila-kacārpita-candraka candrakalāpa-rucābhyadhikānana*

*rocanayā kṛta-cāru-viśeṣaka śeṣakamala-bhava-sanaka-sanandana-*

**О Krsna, skilled at playing the flute! О Krsna, whose wandering eyes full of desire defeat autumn lotuses! О Krsna, stealer of the determination of the wives of siddhas and caranas! О Krsna, whose earrings are worshipped by the beauty of necklaces! О Krsna, living on the land Govardhana which shines with ponds! О Krsna, whose form of condensed knowledge decorates your ornaments! О Krsna, killer of Vrsabhasura in battle! О Krsna, with a peacock feather in your shining, curly hair! О Krsna, with face more attractive than a host of moons! О Krsna, performing love battles in the cottage bowers in the forests! О Krsna, whose snake-like arms are passionate for enjoyment of embraces! О Krsna, a moving, young tamala tree! О Krsna, sincere in awarding the desires of the cowherds! О Krsna, holding a stick in your right hand! О Krsna, conquering millions of suns and moons by your radiance! О Krsna, with tilaka attractively made of gorocana! О Krsna, whose qualities give joy to Ananta, Laksmi, Siva, Sanaka and Sanandana! Please increase my bhakti. О beautiful Krsna!**

You conquer millions of suns (virocana) and moons by your radiance (bha).

О Krsna, skilled at playing the flute! Your wandering eyes full of desire (bhava-kalita) defeat autumn lotuses. You steal (haraka) the determination of the wives of siddhas and caranas by your beauty. Your earrings are worshipped by the beauty of necklaces made of pearl and coral. You live (usita) on the land (bhii) in the valley and on top of Govardhana which shines with ponds.

Kunda means water body according to Visva. Your form of condensed knowledge decorates your ornaments.

*bhūṣaṇabhūṣaṇāṅgam*

**Krsna’s body is the ornament of all ornaments. (SB 3.2.12)**

*sac-cid-ānanda-rūpāya*

**I offer respects to Krsna, the form of eternity, knowledge and bliss. (Gopala-tapam Upanisad)**

You killed Vrsabhasura in battle (yigraha). Vigraha means body and war according to Visva. You place a peacock feather on your shining (bhasura), curly hair.

Your face is more attractive than a host (kalapa) of moons. You have love battles in the cottage bowers in the forests. Your snakelike arms are passionate (uddhara) for enjoyment of embraces (sanga-rasa). This is upama alankara.

You are like a moving (jangama), young tamala tree (naga).

You are sincere in awarding the desires of the cowherds. You have a stick in your right hand. You conquer millions of suns (yirocana) and moons by your radiance (bha). Your tilaka is attractively made of gorocana. Your qualities like mercy give joy to Ananta and others. Please increase (nandaya) my bhakti. О beautiful Krsna!

### Text 40

*bhavataḥ pratāpa-taraṇāv udetum iha lohitāyati sphīte \|*  
*danujāndhakāra-nikarāḥ śaraṇaṁ bhejur guhā-kuharam \|\|40\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Lord! When your powerful sun turns red in order to rise, the demons go to the cave.**

**Комментарий:**

After the kalika there is this verse.

О Lord! When your powerful sun turns red (lohitayati) in order to rise, the demons go to the cave. The verb lohitayati is explained in the following sutra.

*lohitādiḍājbhyaḥ kyap*

**The affix kyas in the sense of becoming what the thing previously was not, is employed after the words lohita, etc., and after those that end with the affix ac, when these words do not take the affix cvi. (Panini Sutras 3.1.13)**

The rest is clear. Since it is impossible for the sun to be red when it is showing its intense power (pratapa), it becomes kavi-praudhokti (boldness of poetic speech).

*pulina-dhṛta-raṅga-yuvati-kṛta-saṅga*  
*madana-rasa-bhaṅga-garima-lasad-aṅga \|\| vira \|\|*

**О embracer of the gopis engaged in pastimes on the riverbank! О Krsna, whose limbs shine with great waves of madhurya-rasa!**

After the verse there is this viruda.

You embrace the gopis engaged in pastimes on the riverbank.

Your limbs shine with great waves of madhurya-rasa.

**О Kesava, with excellent locks of hair! Be victorious! О Krsna, whose many qualities are praised by Brahma, Siva, and Ananta! О Krsna, outstanding in powers! О Krsna, understood to be svayam Bhagavan by marks on your feet! О Krsna, skillful at pastimes! О Krsna, excited in fighting Kaliya! О Krsna, giving joy to Vraja! О Krsna, you give great bliss to those who vow to respect Nanda! О Krsna, bewilderer of Cupid! О Krsna, destroyer of the fresh pride of proud women! О Krsna, taking shelter of the arts of the rasa dance! О Krsna, surrounded by golden women with raised breasts! О Krsna, residing with them in hundreds of bowers! О Krsna, satisfier of the young women! О Krsna, honored by Radhika, with the highest beauty. О Krsna, dependent on gopis! О Krsna, whose crown falls off from performing intense pastimes! О Krsna, eyes thirsty but tired with many pastimes! О Krsna, whose glance gives liberation to the cruel demons, red-eyed with anger! О Krsna, offered respects by the world! О Krsna, protector of the assembly of cowherds! О Krsna, giver of happiness to those who think of you! О abode of mercy! Protect me О valiant one!**

О Kesava, with excellent locks of hair. Be victorious. О Krsna, whose many qualities are praised by Brahma (ka), Siva (isa) and Ananta (bala)\\ Outstanding (vilaksana) by vlrya, maintaining the universe, by controlled transformation of prakrti, etc., no one else is comparable. You are understood to be Svayam Bhagavan by marks on your feet described in samudrika scriptures and Puranas. You are skillful (nagard) at pastimes. You are excited in fighting Kaliya or Kuvalayapida (naga). You give joy to Vraja. You offer respects to Nanda (nati-vratd). Or you give great bliss to those who vow to respect Nanda. You bewilder Cupid (darpdka) by your beauty and cleverness. You destroy the fresh pride of proud women (manavatl) by your unequalled beauty. You take shelter of the arts of the rasa dance. You are surrounded by golden women with raised breasts. You reside (usita) with them in hundreds of bowers.

He satisfied the previously mentioned young women (yauvata') by his embraces, etc.

Among the golden women you are, as you desired, honorably treated (arcitd) by Radhika, with the highest beauty. You are dependent on gopis like Lalita (bhlru).

Your crown falls off (lambita) from the intense pastimes with the gopis.

Your eyes are thirsty (lalasa) but tired (alasa) with many pastimes (keli-kuld).

Your glance gives liberation to the cruel demons red-eyed with anger.

*yamiha nirīkṣya hatā gatāḥ svarūpam*

**Those who saw him on the Battlefield of Kuruksetra attained their original forms after death. (SB 1.9.39)**

You are offered respects by the world. You protect (avdkd) the assembly of cowherds. You give happiness (sarma-da) to the those who think of you (bhavaka). Hanta expresses joy. О abode of mercy! Protect me О valiant one!

### Text 42

*parābhavaṁ phenila-vaktratāṁ ca*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, with peacock feather in your crown! After defeating the enemies inflicting the pa-vargas defeat, foam, bondage, fear and death, you give them liberation, not pa-varga.**

**Комментарий:**

After the kalika, there is this verse.

O Krsna, with peacock feather in your crown! After defeating the enemies (satravanam), etc., inflicting the pa-vargas (pa, pha, ba, bha, ma-defeat, foam, bondage, fear and death) on them, you give them liberation, not pa-varga. This is virodhabhasa. Thus, you are astonishing. You are most merciful in giving liberation, the purusartha, freeing them from the pa-vargas, which are not the purusartha. This is the alankara of anukula.

*anukūlaṁ prātikūlyādyati syād anukūlatā*

**Making the unfavorable favorable is called anukula.**

From the unfavorable bondage, etc., they ^receive the favorable, liberation.

*praṇaya-bharita-madhura-carita*  
*bhajana-sahita-paśupa-mudi(mahi)ta \|\| deva \|\|*

**O Krsna, performing sweet actions filled with prema for your devotee! O Krsna, worshipped by the cowherds with service!**

*madbhaktānāṁ vinodārtha karomi vividhāḥ kriyāḥ*

**I perform various actions to give pleasure to my devotees. (Padma Purana)**

You are worshipped by the cowherds with service.

Counting bakula as two, though they are one, there are eleven types of visikha. With the two types of canda-vrtta, nakha (nine types) and visikha, twenty types starting with vardhita have been described.

**Комментарий:**

Having described the beautiful creeper, his power is now described. Kandisika means running away in fear according to Amara-kosa. Piercing the universe, they fled. They disappeared in the eight thick coverings of darkness. They have great fear. This is praudhokti. They attained the dense darkness beyond Lokaloka mountain range.

**mañjaryāṁ korakaḥ \|**

The koraka in the manjari class should be understood. The manjari or dvigadi-gana-vrtta, the second type of mahd-kalika, is first defined. There are five types such as koraka. It is said:

*dvigādigaṇavṛttākhyā kalikātha nigadyate \|*  
*eṣā tu kalikābhijñaiḥ kathyate mañjarītyapi \|\|*  
*pañcadheyaṁ dvigādiśca rādirmādiśca kīrtitā \|*  
*caturthī syānna kalikā gānākhyā pañcamī matā \|\|*  
*korako gucchakaścaiva saṁphullaṁ kusumaṁ tathā \|*  
*gandhaśceti dvigādyādikalikākhyāḥ smṛtāḥ kramāt \|\|*

**Dvigadi-gana-vrtta kalika is here explained. It is called by knowers of kalikas as manjari. There are five types: dvigadi, radi, madi, the fourth is called na-kalika. The fifth is called gdna. The five dvigadi kalikas are also known as koraka, gucchaka, samphulla, kusuma and gandha.**

The rules of samyoga (conjunction of consonants) in canda-vrtta do not apply here. The characteristics of the first, called dvigadi-kalika, are described.

*dvigādi-kalikāṁ dhīrāḥ korakākhyāṁ pracakṣate \|*  
*dviga-bhasnala-sandarbhair ananya-gaṇa-pātibhiḥ \|*  
*svecchāvasānaiḥ saṁkḷptāṁ dvigādikalikāṁ viduḥ*

**When any of the segments 11 Iss ssl sss s (ga, ga, bha, sa, na, la) are included, placed freely, with rhymes at the end, is called dvigadi-kalika or koraka by the wise.**

An example of the ganas is the following:

*śaure mādhava bhagavan murahara*

**O Sauri! O Madhava! O Lord! O killer of Mura!**

*mānavatī-mada-hāri-vilocana dānava-saṁcaya-dhūka-virocana \|*  
*ḍiṇḍima-vādi-surāli-sabhājita caṇḍima-śāli-bhujārgala-rājita \|*  
*dīkṣita-yauvata-citta-vilobhana-vīkṣita susmita-mārdava-śobhana \|*  
*parvata-saṁdhṛti-nirdhuta-pībara-garva-tamaḥ-parimugdha-śacī-vara\|*

**О Krsna, whose glance destroys the pride of proud women! О Krsna, the sun for the owl-like demons! О Krsna, worshiped by all the devatas who sound drums in great joy. О Krsna, shining with arms like heroic wooden door latch! О Krsna, whose glance attracted the hearts of the young wives of the brahmanas performing sacrifices! О Krsna, beautiful with a slight, natural smile! О Krsna, defeating Indra, whose ignorance was nourished by pride, by lifting Govardhana!**

Your glance destroys (hari) the pride (madd) of proud women. You are the sun (virocana) for the owl-like (ghuka) demons. You give suffering to demons like the sun gives suffering to the owl. Ghuka is owl according to Halayudha. You are worshiped by all the devatas who sound drums (dindima) in great joy. You shine with arms like wooden door latch which are heroic (candima-sali). The alankara is parinama. (the door bolts become heroic). Your glance attracted the hearts of the young women, wives of the brahmanas performing sacrifices (diksita).

You are beautiful with a slight (mardavd) natural (su) smile. He secretly smiled at the brahmanas’ wives. Indra whose ignorance was nourished (plbara) by pride was defeated by your lifting Govardhana.

*rañjita-mañju-parisphurad-ambara gañjita-keśi-parākrama-ḍambara \|*  
*komalatāṅkita-vāg-avatāraka soma-lalāma-mahotsava-kāraka \|*  
*haṁsa-ratha-stuti-śaṁsita-vaṁśaka kaṁsa-vadhū-śruti-nunna-vataṁsaka \|*

**О Krsna, with cloth shining attractively with kunkuma! О Krsna, destroyer of Kesi’s ferocious attack! О Krsna, speaking soft words! О Krsna, who celebrated a great festival for Siva! О Krsna, whose dynasty is praised by Brahma! О Krsna, remover of the earrings of Kamsa’s wives!**

You wear cloth shining attractively with kunkuma. You destroyed Kesi’s ferocious attack. You speak soft words. You celebrated a great festival for Siva (soma-lalama). Your dynasty is praised by Brahma (hamsa-ratha). You removed the earrings of Kamsa’s wives (made them widows).

*raṅga-taraṅgita-cāru-dṛg-añcala saṅgata-pañca-śarodaya-cañcala \|*  
*luñcita-gopa-sutā-gaṇa-śāṭaka saṁcita-raṅga-mahotsava-nāṭaka \|*  
*tāraya mām uru-saṁsṛti-śātana dhāraya locanam atra sanātana \|\| dhira \|\|*

**О Krsna, with attractive eyes trembling in the dancing arena! О Krsna, trembling when love arises on attaining the gopis! О Krsna, stealer of the gopis’ clothing! О Krsna, propagating dramas depicting your great, astonishing festivals, through poets! О Krsna, destroyer of the deep ocean of samsara! Please deliver me. Look at me once. О eternal form! О clever one!**

Your attractive eyes tremble in the dancing arena (rangd). You tremble when love (panca-sard) arises on attaining the gopis (sangata). You stole (luncita) the gopis’ clothing (sataka). Your great astonishing festivals are propagated (sancitd) by the devotee poets in special scriptures or dramas (natakd). Оdestroyer (satana) of the deep ocean of samsara! О pilot! Please deliver me. Let me to the shore,  destruction of samsara. Look at me once. О eternal form (sanatand)!

Formation of palitankarani is explained by the following sutra.

*āḍhya-subhaga-sthūla-palitanagnāndha-priyeṣu cvyartheṣvacvau kṛñaḥ karaṇe khyun*

**.The affix khyun, when the sense of the word to be formed is that of an instrumental agent, comes after the verb kr (to make), when the following words are in composition with it as objects: adhya (rich), subhaga (fortunate), sthiila (big), palita (grey), nagna (naked), andha (blind) and priya (pleasant), provided that these words have the sense of the words formed by the affix cvi, though not actually ending in the affix cvi. (Panini Sutras 3.2.56)**

**gucchaḥ \|**

### Text 51

*citraṁ murāre sura-vairi-pakṣas*  
*tvayā samantād anubaddha-yuddhaḥ \|*  
*amitram uccair avibhidya bhedaṁ*  
*mitrasya kurvann amṛtaṁ prayāti \|\|51\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O enemy of Mura! This is most astonishing. The demons, enemies of the devatas, constantly waging war against you, not piercing their enemy, pierce their friend, and attain nectar.**

**Комментарий:**

O enemy of Mura! This is most astonishing (citram). What is astonishing?

The enemies of the devatas are constantly engaged in battle with you. Not piercing you, who are not their friend, they pierce their friend or kill their friend, and attain nectar. For the sinful to gain punya and attain nectar is contrary. This is virodhabhasa. The real meaning is this. The Lord has the quality of giving an eternal destination to the enemies he kills. The demons killed by you, Svayam Bhagavan, pierce the sun globe (mitra) and attain liberation. In this way the contradiction is resolved.

**tribhaṅgyāṁ daṇḍakatribhaṅgī \|**

The dandaka-tribhangl among the tribhangls.

The tribharigi is described.

*atha tribhaṅgīvṛttākhyā kalikā procyate'dhunā \|*  
*vṛtteṣu kalikānāṁ ca viśeṣe sā sphuṭībhavet \|\|*  
*trayāṇāmiha bhaṅgānāṁ samāhārastribhaṅgikā \|*

*The tribhagl-vrtta kalika is now explained. This becomes clear in the functions of the kalikds and its details. The collection of three bhangas makes it tri-bhanga.*

*bhaṅgo'nuprāsarūpeṇa varṇāvṛttiriheṣyate \|\|*  
*saṁyuktaścātra dīrghaśca dvayameva satāṁ matam \|*  
*mālā bālā ca śālā ca mallī vallī ca cillikā \|*

**A bhanga here is accepted as a repetition of similar sounds (anuprasa). The wise say that the bhanga should consists of two syllables which have a conjunct consonant or a long vowel. They are called mala, bala, sala, malli, valli and cillika.**

These six types are called sikharinl, turaga, dandaka, bhujanga, tigma and vidaghda. Here dandaka and vidagdha are taken up. The qualities of the dandaka are as follows.

*daṇḍakeṣu ca sarvatra daśame bhaṅga īritaḥ \|*  
*taccaturthāttacaturthe taccaturthātkramādiha \|\|*

**In all dandakas, there is said to be a bhanga at the 10th syllable, in the fourth after that, and the fourth after that, and the fourth after that in order.**

*yāvatkalāvivṛddhiḥ syāttāvadbhaṅgāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*etādṛśeṣu vṛttepu tribhaṅgītyupalakṣaṇam \|*  
*caturbhaṅgī pañcabhaṅgī ṣaḍbhaṅgī caiva kīrtitā \|\| iti \|*

**As much as the number of ganas is increased. That many more bhangas are added. In such meters as these, the term tribhangl is a general indication. Poems with four, five, and six bhangas are glorified.**

An example of tribhangl is given with a dandaka called arnava. The dandaka is called arnava if it has sss sss (na, no) and nine Isl (ra). (sss sss Isl Isl Isl Isl Isl Isl Isl Isl Isl) '

*śritam agha-jaladher vahitraṁ caritraṁ sucitraṁ vicitraṁ*  
*phaṇitraṁ samitraṁ pavitraṁ lavitraṁ rujām \|*  
*jagad-aparimita-pratiṣṭhaṁ paṭiṣṭhaṁ baliṣṭhaṁ gariṣṭhaṁ*  
*variṣṭhaṁ mradiṣṭhaṁ suniṣṭhaṁ daviṣṭhaṁ dhiyām \|*  
*nikhila-vilasite’bhirāmaṁ sa-rāmaṁ mudā mañju-dāman-*  
*nabhāmaṁ lalāmaṁ dhṛtāmanda-dhāman-naye \|*

**I always worship you, who take the form of a boat in the ocean of sin, which is astonishing because you deliver those in ignorance, who deliver the snakes, who deliver from battle, who destroy ignorance, who cut the pains of samsara, who have unlimited fame in the universe, are skillful, strong, are the best teacher because you are the greatest and very tender, fixed in vows, far beyond the material mind, attractive in pastimes, accompanied by Balarama, devoid of anger and are the ornament of the world. О attractive form! О brilliant form!**

О killer of Madhu, О Hari, О Murari, О killer of Kesi, 1 always worship you. Krsna is then described. You took the form of a boat in the ocean of sin. The act was most astonishing (citram). You deliver (tra) those who have no spiritual knowledge (vicit). You deliver the Vidyadhara who had a snake form (phanitram). You deliver the person who remembers you from battle (samitram). You destroy ignorance (pavitram). You cut (lavitram) the pains of persons bewildered by the household.

You have unlimited fame in the universe (pratistham). You are very skillful (patistham). You have great strength (balistham). You are the best guru, teaching everything (garistham) because you are greater than the greatest (varistham) and also very soft (mradistham). You do not waiver in your vows (sunistham). You are far from (davistham) the material mind. You are attractive in all pastimes (vilasite). You are accompanied by Balarama (sa-ramam). О lord with beautiful form (manju-dhaman)! You are not angry (abhamam). You are the ornament of the world (lalamam). О Krsna, having a bright form (dhrtamanda-dhaman). Aye expresses tenderness.

*madhumathana hare murāre purārer apāre sasāre*  
*vihāre surārer udāre ca dāre prabhum \|*  
*sphurta-mina-sutā-taraṅge vihaṅgeśa-raṅgeṇa gaṅgeṣṭa-*  
*-bhaṅge bhujaṅgendra-saṅge sad-aṅgena bhoḥ \|*

**О killer of Madhu! О Hari! O^Murari! О Lord beyond Siva! О Lord with fixed expansions! О performer of pastimes! О Krsna, generous to the demons! О destroyer! I worship you with pure limbs that astonished Garuda.**

I worship you, shining in the Yamuna’s waves which deride the ocean, and which touched Kaliya.

О Krsna, unapproachable by Siva (purarer apare)! Krsna, having fixed expansions (sasare), having eternal pastimes (vihare), generous with the demons! Krsna, the great destroyer (dare)! You are capable (prabhum). You shine in the waves of the Yamuna (ina-suta) with your pure limbs (sad-angena). You appeared to chastise Kaliya in Yamuna’s lake. Ina means the sun according to Dhananjaya. The waves were touched by Kaliya (bhujangendra-sange) and derided (bhanga) the ocean (gangesta), in depth and blackness. His pure limbs were astonishing to Garuda (vihangesa). Though Garuda eternally carries Visnu, seeing Krsna’s limbs he became astonished. Or on the pretext of killing Kaliya, Kaliya became frightened of dying.

*śikhari-vara-darī-niśāntaṁ prayāntaṁ sa-kāntaṁ vibhāntaṁ*  
*nitāntaṁ ca kāntaṁ praśāntaṁ kṛtāntaṁ dviṣām \|*  
*danuja-hara bhajāmy anantaṁ sudantaṁ nudantaṁ dṛgantaṁ*  
*hasantaṁ vasantaṁ bhajantaṁ bhavantaṁ sadā \|\| vira \|\|*

**О killer of demons! I always worship you, who made palaces in the caves of Govardhana, who made appointments in those rooms with your beloveds, who shone brilliantly, who are most attractive, devoid of hatred and the form of time for the demons, who are all-pervading, with shining teeth, and stimulate the gopis by your glance, while laughing and serving the spring seasons.**

He made palaces (nisantam) out of the caves in Govardhana. Nisantam means a house according to Halayudha. He made appointments in these rooms (praydntam) with his beloveds (sakantam). He shone with beauty and grace (vibhdntam). He was most attractive (bantam), devoid of hatred (prasantam), and death or the form of time (krtantam) to the demons. He is devoid of hatred, because he protects and gives them liberation when they die. He is all-pervading (anantam). His teeth are like rows of shining pearls. He stimulates (nudantam) his beloveds by his glance. His face smiles (hasantam). He serves (bhajantam) the spring, king of seasons. This is gatha meter because of having seven padas (of three syllables).

### Text 53

*saṁsārāmbhasi dustarormi-gahane gambhīra-tāpa-trayī-*

*dīpreṇ(pte)nādya sudarśanena vibudha-klānti-cchidākāriṇā*  
*cintā-santati-ruddham uddhara hare mac-citta-dantīśvaram \|\|53\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Hari! Deliver my mind, Gajendra, shouting out of internal fear and choked by constant worry, caught by the crocodile of the intense three miseries, with cruel intelligence, in the deep lake of samsara, full of unsurpassable waves, by the brilliant Sudarsana which destroys the exhaustion caused by the Gandharva’s curse.**

**Комментарий:**

There is this verse before the vidagdha-tribhangi kalika.

О Hari! Deliver my mind, Gajendra, caught by the crocodile of the three miseries in the deep lake of desire for material pleasure (samsarambhasi) by the Sudarsana. Take me from this lake. Kumbhlra is crocodile according to Amara-kosa. Sudarsana, meaning pleasant to see, is the Lord’s cakra. The water of samsara is described. It is full of waves difficult to escape, full of (gahana) hunger, thrist, lamentation, illusion, old age and death. The crocodile is cruel intelligence (ugra-matina) which causes violence and slandering. The heart which is like Gajendra is screaming from inner fear. It is choked by a multitude of worries. They equally afflict the heart. Sudarsana is effulgent (dlprena). It destroys the curse on the Gandharava Huhu (vibudhasya) by the sage Devala, which causes the exhaustion—in the experience of Gajendra with the crocodile. Or it destroys my exhaustion from attempts to attain material objects. I see as enjoyable objects which are useless since 1 am unintelligent (vibudha). The cakra destroys material thirst. This is rupaka with ahgas of puns.

**vidagdha-tribhaṅgī \|**

Vidagdha-tribhangi in the tribhaiigl-kalika group should be described.

*dvitīyāṣṭamayoḥ sthāne bhaṅgaścaiva caturdaśe \|*  
*bha-dvaye sādhvanuprāso yatraikā kalikedṛśī \|\|*

*yasyām evaṁ vidhaṁ lakṣma sā vidagdha-tribhaṅgikā \|\|*

**There are bhangas after the second, eight and fourteenth syllables and anuprasa in this type of hdlika. There should be no sll (ya). And Iss Iss (bha, bha) should be repeated three times. It has from eight to the sixteen kalas. This is called vidagdha tribhangika.**  
**(Ils sss Iss sss Ils sss Iss Iss)**

О Krsna, respected by Siva (candi-priya)! By you, the wives (vallabha) of the demons are made widows (randi-krta) by your fierce (candl-krta) strength. О cowherd (ballava)! You wear silk clothing. О king (bhattaraka)! Bhattaraka means king according to Visva. О killer of Baka (baka-kuttdka). You are ornamented by experts attractive with all knowledge (lalita).

*nandīśvara-pati-nandī-hita-bhara sandīpita-rasa-sāgara nāgara*

Your great actions give prosperity (nandi) to Nanda. You are an ocean of shining rasa. О clever lover (nagara)! You appreciate new songs (sangltaka). Human beauty is surpassed by a drop of your excellent gestures. This indicates prominence of his bhava.

*ūrvī-priyakara kharvī-kṛta-khala-darvī-kara-pati-garvita-parvata*  
*gotrā-hita-kara gotrāhita-daya gotrādhipa-dhṛti-śobhana-lobhana*

You give happiness of the earth (urvl). Urvl means earth according to Amara-kosa.

You destroyed the mountain of pride of the cruel king of snakes (darvlkara-pati).

You benefit all the cows (gotra). You show compassion to families (gotra). You cause greed in people’s minds by your beauty when lifting Govardhana (gotradhipa).

*vanyā-sthita-bahu-kanyā-paṭa-hara dhanyāśaya-maṇi-cora manorama*

**O stealer of the clothing of many gopis situated in the water! O stealer of the jewel of the hearts of the most fortunate of the gopis! O performer of pastimes in the minds of the fortunate! O Krsna, whose cloth shines like lightning! O Krsna, deliverer of persons suffering from samsara! O Krsna, full of joy! Be joyful! O clever one!**

Vanya means a lot of water according to Amara-kosa. You stole the clothing of many gopis situated in the water (vanya). You steal the jewel of the heart (asaya) of the most fortunate of the gopis (dhanya). Asaya means container according to Visva. 0 performer of pastimes in the minds of the fortunate (manorama)! Your cloth shines like lightning (sampa). You deliver persons suffering from samsara by a particle of your presence. You

are full of joy (phulla). Be joyful (samullasa). This means “Be victorious!”

After the kalika, there is this verse.

The grinding stone is described. It was smooth, devoid of bumps (akutile). The host of demons is described. They clearly afflicted (arati-karam) the cows and cowherds (carukanam). Krsna is described. The two lines are clear. He destroyed the jackal (bhuri-maya) demons. You decorate your body attractively and faultlessly.

Among the six forms of tribhangi, dandaka and vidagdha were described. The other four such as tikharinl have been omitted. Giving up the fourth or madhya-kalika, the fifth, misra-kalika is next described.

**miśrakalikā \|**

The fifth type of kalika, misra-kalika should be described.

*tila-tandula-vad yatra kalikā-gadyayoryutiḥ \|*  
*sā miśrakalikā nāma ṣaṇmukhena prakīrtitā \|\|*  
*atha vā miśrakalikā nānāvidhakalāśritā \|*  
*vibhakti saptakālambi saṁbuddhy antā budhaiḥ smṛtā \|\|*

**When there is a combination of prose with kalika, like sesame and rice it is called misra-kalika by Sanmukha. Or misra-kalika has various types of kalds, using the seven vibhaktis, with sambodhana at the end.**

*duṣṭa-durdamāriṣṭa-kaṇṭhīr avakaṇṭha-vikhaṇḍana-khelad-aṣṭāpada navīnāṣṭāpada vispardhi-paṭṭāmbara-parīta gariṣṭha-gaṇḍa-śaila-sapiṇḍa-vakṣaḥ-paṭṭa \|*

**О Krsna, sarabha playing at piercing the throat of lion-like, evil, infatuated Arista! О Krsna, who wears silk cloth which defeats fresh gold! О Krsna, whose chest is like the firm stone of a great mountain!**

This is the first type of misra-kalika. О Krsna, sarabha (astapada) playing at piercing the throat of lion-like, evil, infatuated Arista. You wear silk cloth which defeats fresh gold (astapada'). Astapada means gold or an eight footed creature according to Medini. Your chest is like the firm stone of a great mountain. Ganda-saila means a slab fallen from a mountain according to Amara-kosa. The text following this is prose.

*pāṭava-daṇḍita-caṭula-bhujaṅgama kanduka-vilasita-laṅgima bhaṇḍila-vicakila-maṇḍita saṅgara-viharaṇa-paṇḍita dantura-danuja-viḍambaka kuṇṭhita-kuṭila-kadambaka \|*

**О Krsna, punishing the agitated snake with great skill! О Krsna, attractively playing ball! О Krsna, decorated with sirisa and jasmine flowers! О Krsna, skillful at fighting pastimes! О Krsna, destroyer of demons with crooked teeth! О Krsna, crippier of the crooked!**

О Krsna, by whose skill you punished the agitated snake (Kaliya)! О Krsna, attractively play ball! Krsna, decorated with sirisa (bhandila) and jasmine flowers! Krsna, skillful at fighting pastimes! Destroyer of demons with crooked teeth (dantura). Dantura means prominent or crooked teeth according to Haima. You make the crooked weak (kunthita).

*khacitākhaṇḍalopala-virājad-aṇḍaja-rāja-kuṇḍala-maṇḍita-mañjula-gaṇḍa-sthala viśaṅkaṭa-bhāṇḍīra-taṭī-tāṇḍava-kalā-rañjita-suhṛn-maṇḍala*

**О Krsna, whose attractive cheeks are decorated with makara (andaja-raja) earrings made of sapphire! О Krsna, attracting your circle of friends by dancing at the extensive Bhandira tree!**

Your attractive cheeks are decorated with makara (andaja-raja) earrings made of sapphire (akhandalopala). King of the fish (andaja) means makara. Andaja means fish according to Amara-kosa. He attracts his circle of friends by his dancing at the extensive Bhandira tree. Here the prose section ends.

*nanda-vicumbita-kunda-nibha-smita gandha-karambita śanda-viceṣṭita tunda-parisphurad-aṇḍaka-ḍambara \|*

**О Krsna, kissed by Nanda! О Krsna, whose smile is like the jasmine flower! О Krsna, thoroughly perfumed! О Krsna whose actions give happiness! О Krsna, manifesting the vast universe in your belly!**

After this the kalika is clear in meaning. You manifest vast universes in your belly (tunda).

*durjana-bhojendra-kaṇṭaka-kandoddhāraṇoddāma-kuddāla vinamra-vipad-dāruṇa-dhvānta-vidrāvaṇa-mārtaṇḍopama-kṛpā-kaṭākṣa śārad-ācaṇḍa-marīci-mādhurya-viḍambi-tuṇḍa-maṇḍala, loṣṭhī-kṛta-maṇi-koṣṭhī-kula-muni-goṣṭhīśvara madhuroṣṭhī-priya parameṣṭhīḍita parameṣṭhī-kṛta-nara \|\| dhira \|\|*

**О Krsna, a giant spade for uprooting the thorn of wicked Karhsa! О Krsna, whose merciful glance is the sun that destroys the great darkness of danger to the devotees! О Krsna, whose face mocks the sweetness of the autumn moon! О Krsna, worshipped by the group of sages who take a chest of gems to be dirt! О Krsna, dear to the gopis who have bimba-like lips! О Krsna, worshipped by Brahma! О Krsna, arranging for men to attain the status of Brahma! О clever one!**

You are a giant spade (kuddala) for uprooting the thorn of wicked Kamsa.

Your merciful glance is the sun that destroys the great darkness of danger to the devotees (.vinamra'). Your face mocks the sweetness of the autumn moon (sarad-acanda-manci-madhurya-vidambi-tunda-mandala'). This is the end of a prose section.

You are worshipped by the group of sages who take a chest of gems to be dirt. This means you are the crest jewel of the renounced. You are dear to the gopis with bimba-like lips who have love only for you. You are worshipped by Brahma. You have men attain the status of Brahma by pious actions.

*yaṁ kāmaye taṁ tamugraṁ kṛṇoti taṁ brahmāṇaṁ tamṛṣiṁ taṁ sumedhām \|\|*

*sva-dharma-niṣṭhaḥ śatajanmabhiḥ pumānvirañcatāmeti tataḥ paraṁ hi mām*

**A person who executes his sva-dharma properly for one hundred births becomes qualified to occupy the post of Brahma. (SB 4.24.29)**

The second type of misra-kalika (with seven vibhaktis) should be described. The qualities were previously mentioned.

*yaḥ sthira-karuṇas tarjita-varuṇas tarpita-janakaḥ saṁmada-janakaḥ \|*  
*praṇata-vimāyaṁ jagur anapāyaṁ ghana-ruci-kāyaṁ sukṛta-janā yam \|*  
*sujana-kalita-kathanena prabala-danuja-mathanena*  
*praṇayiṣu ratam abhayena prakaṭa-ratiṣu kila yena \|*

**You who are merciful to your parents, you scolded Varuna, you had your father worshipped, and you gave joy to Nanda; whom, with complexion of a cloud, the learned praise as eternally being without coy/ring for the devotees; by whom, without fear, the destroyer of strong demons, as narrated by the devotees, there arise pastimes with devotees, please manifest the highest excellence.**

The long sentence with the seven vibhaktis ends in the last line with “manifest the highest excellence (sa tvamjayajaya)." Krsna is described in the preceding lines.

You were most merciful to your parents. You scolded Varuna. “O foolish frog! Why have you brought my father here?” He made Varuna worship his father to get relief for his offense. Bringing back his father, he gave joy (sammada) to his father, showing Goloka to the people of Vraja. And giving mercy, he gave joy to Varuna. This is the first vibhakti (nominative).

Learned men (sukrta-jana) praise (jaguh) him (yam) as being visible to the devotees without covering (vimayam). Or they praise him for having sincere (vimaya) devotees (pranata). He is eternal (anapayam). This is the second vibhakti (accusative).

By him (yena), whose actions are related by the devotees, there are pastimes (ratam) with the affectionate devotees (prakata-ratisu). This is the third vibhakti (instrumental).

*yasmai paridhvasta-duṣṭāya cakruḥ spṛhāṁ mālya-juṣṭāya*  
*divyāḥ striyaḥ kelituṣṭāya kandarparaṅgeṇa puṣṭāya \|*  
*ghṛtotsāha-pūrād-dyuti-kṣipta-sūrād yato’rir vidūrād bhayaṁ prāpa śūrāt \|*  
*yasyojjvalāṅgasya saṁcāry-apāṅgasya veṇur lalāmasya haste’bhirāmasya \|*

**You, wearing a garland, destroyer of demons, satisfied with pastimes, ovetjoyed by the autumn festival, for whom the devatas’ wives developed desire, should manifest excellence. You, eager to kill the demons, shining greater than the sun, endowed with power, situated far off, from whom Kamsa developed fear, should manifest excellence. You, with shining limbs, wandering glance, the crest jewel of all beings, having a flute in your hand, most delightful, should manifest excellence.**

The wives of the devatas showed desire for him (yasmai).

*devyo vimāna-gatayaḥ smara-nunna-sārā*

**The heavenly women became agitated. (SB 10.21.12)**

Krsna is further described. The meaning is clear. He was overjoyed (pustaya) by the autumn festival (kandarpa-rangena). This is the fourth vibhakti (dative).

From him full of prowess (surat) even far away (vidurat), eager to destroy his enemy (dhrtotsaha-purat), by whom the sun (surat) lost its powers, Kamsa (arih) developed fear. This is the fifth vibhakti (ablative).

In his hand there is a flute. His glances spread sideways (sancdri). He is the crest jewel of all things (laldmasya). This is the sixth vibhakti (genitive).

*smita-visphurite’jani yatra hite ratir ullasite sudṛśāṁ lalite \|*  
*sa tvaṁ jaya jaya duṣṭa-pratibhaya bhakti-sthira-daya lupta-vraja-bhaya \|\| vira \|\|*

**You, with blossoming smile,joyful, affectionate, desired by the gopis, in whom rati for the gopis developed, should manifest excellence. O fearful to demons! O steady in mercy to the devotees! O destroyer of fear in Vraja!**

In him, rati for the gopis developed (ajani). Manifest the highest excellence (jay a jay a). O Krsna, inciting fear (pratibhaya) in the demons! Pratibhaya means dreadful according to Halayudha. (This is locative). The rest is clear. It ends with the vocative.

### Text 58

*haṁsottamābhilaṣitā sevaka-cakreṣu darśitotsekā \|*  
*mura-jayinaḥ kalyāṇī karuṇā-kallolinī jayati \|\|58\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna’s auspicious river of mercy, desired by the jnani-bhaktas, submerging the dasa-bhaktas, manifests the highest excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

After the kalika there is this verse.

The river of mercy belonging to Krsna manifests excellence (jayati). The river is described. It is desired by all the jnani-bhaktas (hamsottama) but cannot be attained by them. It bathes the assembly of dasa-bhaktas, who are like cdkravakas.

It is the very form of auspiciousness. This means it uproots samsara.

*mitra-kulodita-narma-sumodita*  
*rañjita-rādhika śarma-bharādhika \|\| vira \|\|*

**O Krsna, pleased with jokes uttered by your group of friends! O Krsna, attracted to Radhika! O Krsna, overjoyed by attaining Radha!**

After the verse there is this viruda.

You are pleased by jokes uttered by your group of friends. Krsna, attracted to Radha! О Krsna, becoming joyful by attaining Radha’s association (sarma-bharadhika). Thus, the two type of misra-kalika, the fifth type have been described.

### Text 59

*madhureśa mādhurīmaya mādhava muralī-matallikā-mugdha \|*  
*mama madana-mohana mudā mardaya manaso mahā-moham \|\|59\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О master of Mathura! О Krsna, filled with sweetness! О Madhava! О Krsna, attractive with an excellent flute! О Madana-mohana! Destroy the great illusion in my mind by the bliss of realizing your tattva.**

**Комментарий:**

At the beginning of the sixth kalika, which has two types, aksara-mayi and sarva-laghvl, there is this verse. О master of Mathura! О Krsna, filled with sweetness! О Madhava! О Krsna, attractive with an excellent flute! О Madana-mohana! Destroy (mardaya) the great illusion in my mind by the bliss (muda) of realizing your tattva.

**akṣaramayī \|**

The a-ksara-mayi starts with the vowel a and ends with ksa.

*acyuta jaya jaya ārta-kṛpā-maya indra-makhārdana īti-viśātana*  
*ujjvala-vibhrama ūrjita-vikrama ṛddhi-dhuroddhara ṝbhu-dayā-para*  
*ḷdiva-kṛpekṣita ḷvada-lakṣita edhita-ballava aindava-kula-bhava*  
*ojaḥ-sphūrjita augrya-vivarjita aṁsa-viśaṅkaṭa aṣṭāpada-paṭa*

**О Acyuta! Manifest all excellence! О Krsna, merciful to the suffering! O Krsna, who stopped Indra’s sacrifice! Destroyer of suffering! O Krsna, shining with beauty! O Krsna, with great prowess! O Krsna, unrestrained in great wealth! O Krsna, merciful to the Rbhus. O Krsna, ascertained by mercy! O Krsna, invisible like L. O giver of prosperity to the cowherds! O Krsna, appearing in the moon dynasty! O Krsna, full of power! O Krsna, devoid of anger! O Krsna with broad shoulders! O Krsna with golden cloth!**

The first three items are clear in meaning. Sandhis are not used in this work because of the attractiveness without sandhis. He destroys sufferings (iti-visatana). The sufferings are described.

*ativṛṣṭiranāvṛṣṭiḥ śalabhā mūṣikāḥ khagāḥ \|*  
*svacakraṁ paracakraṁ ca saptaitā ītayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\|*

**The seven sufferings are too much rain, no rain, locust plague, mice, birds (or grasshoppers), people in one’s group, and people in other groups.**

You have shining beauty or pastimes (vibhrama). You are unrestrained (uddhara) with great wealth. You are merciful to the Rbhus. Rbhu means the Adityas according to Amara-kosa. They are born (bhu) from Aditi. R means the mother of the devatas according to Aksara-kosa.

You are seen by mercy like the letter L is seen only in kjpta. As L is seen in the root krpa, which become klpta, so you are seen by mercy. L and R are often equated.

*nityāvyakto'pi bhagavānīkṣate nijaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*tāmṛte paramātmānaṁ kaḥ paśyetāmitaṁ prabhum \|*

**The Lord, eternally invisible, is seen by his will. Without that, who can see the Lord, the Paramatma? (Narayanadhyatma)**

Without mercy you cannot be seen, just as L is not seen (l-vat dldksita).

You give prosperity (edhita) to the cowherds. You appeared in the moon dynasty (aindava), since Vasudeva and Nanda were both Yadavas. You shine with heroic energy (ojah). You are devoid of ferocity (augrya).

Arosano hy asau devah: the Lord is devoid of anger. (Mahabharata 12.323.15)

Though Krsna shows anger towards demons, it is not considered anger since it is for their benefit. You have broad (visarikata) shoulders (amsa). Your cloth is like gold (astapada). О Krsna, with yellow upper cloth.

*kaṅkaṇa-yuta-kara khaṇḍita-khala-vara gati-jita-kuñjara ghana-ghusṛṇāmbara*  
*ṅuta-muralī-rata cala-cillī-lata chalita-satī-śata jalajodbhava-nuta*  
*jhaṣa-vara-kuṇḍala ñoṅūyita-dala ṭaṅkita-bhūdhara ṭhani-bhānana-vara*  
*ḍamara-ghaṭāhara ḍhakkita-karatala ṇakhara-dhṛtācala tarala-vilocana*  
*thūtkṛta-khañjana danuja-vimardana dhavalā-vardhana nanda-sukhāspada*

**О Krsna, wearing bracelets on your wrists! О Krsna, best destroyer of demons. О Krsna, walking like an elephant! О Krsna, whose upper cloth and turban are smeared with thick kunkuma! О Krsna, attached to playing the flute! О Krsna, with moving eyebrows! О Krsna, deceiver of chaste women! О Krsna, praised by Brahma! О Krsna, with makara earrings! О Krsna, play music using leaves! О Krsna, holding the mountain! О Krsna, excellent with face like the disk of the moon! О Krsna, who drove away a gathering of clouds! О Krsna, whose hands proclaim your fame like drums! О Krsna, holding Govardhana on the tip of the little finger of your left hand! О Krsna, deriding the khanjana bird by your two restless eyes! О Krsna, crusher of demons! О Krsna, increaser of cows! О Krsna, abode of Nanda’s joy!**

The next three are clear in meaning.

Your upper cloth and turban are smeared with thick kunkuma (ghusrn).

You are attached to playing (nutd) the flute. Nu is in the bhvadi class.

You have moving eyebrows (cilll-latd). You deceive the chaste women (sati).

You are praised by Brahma (jalajodbhavd). You have makara (jhasa-vard) earrings. You play music (nonuyita) using leaves (data). This is the verb nu in the causative form. It means to make music.

You are excellent with face (anand) like (nibhd) the disk of the moon (tha). Tha means the moon disk according to Aksara-kosa.

You drove away a gathering of clouds (damara). You have drumlike (dhakkd) hands. As a drum makes loud noise so your hands proclaim your fame as a donor. You held up Govardhana on the tip of the little finger of your left hand. You deride (thiitkrta) the khanjana bird by your two restless eyes. You are the receptacle of Nanda’s happiness.

*paṅkaja-sama-pada phaṇi-nuti-modita bandhu-vinodita bhaṅguritālaka*  
*mañjula-mālaka yaṣṭi-lasad-bhuja ramya-mukhāmbuja lalita-viśārada-*  
*vallava-raṅgada śarmada-ceṣṭita ṣaṭpada-veṣṭita sarasīruha-dhara*  
*haladhara-sodara kṣaṇada-guṇotkara*  
*\|\| vira \|\|*

**O Krsna, with feet like lotuses! O Krsna, pleased with Kaliya’s prayers! O Krsna, happy with friends! O Krsna, with curly locks of hair! O Krsna, with attractive garland! O Krsna, with stick in your hand! O Krsna, with attractive lotus face! O Krsna, giving pleasure to the attractive gopis skillful in the knowledge of all scriptures! O Krsna, whose actions give joy! O Krsna, holding a lotus surrounded by bees! O Krsna, brother of Balarama! O Krsna, whose excellent qualities which give joy!**

You were pleased with Kaliya’s prayers (nuti). You are happy with friends. You have curly (bharigurita) locks of hair. You have excellent qualities which give joy.

You give pleasure to the attractive gopis skillful in the knowledge of all scriptures. The other phrases are clear in meaning.

He wanders on Yamuna’s bank. He steals the clothing of the golden gopis performing Katyayani vrata in the hemanta season. Pata-bhara (carrier of the cloth) is sometimes seen. He has hands which steal cloth.

*premoru-haṭṭa-hiṇḍaka kakkhaṭa-subhaṭendra-kaṇṭha-kuṭṭāka \|*

You go to (hindaka) the great market (hatta) with prema. This means he is dependent on prema. You cut the throats of the tough, skillful warriors.

О wearer of yellow cloth! О great Lord tyhattarakdll Dance in my heart.

sarva-laghuh I

The sarva-laghu variety of kalika, has only short syllables in the whole kalika.

*caraṇa-calana-hata-jaraṭha-śakaṭaka*  
*rajaka-dalana vaśa-gata-para-kaṭaka*  
*naṭana-ghaṭana-lasad-aga-vara-kaṭaka*  
*sakanaka-marakata-maya-nava-kaṭaka*

**О Krsna, destroying the rough cart with the movement of your foot! О Krsna, slayer of the washerman! О Krsna, subduer of enemy troops! О Krsna, making the ridge of Govardhana shine by your dancing! О Krsna, wearing new bracelets of emerald with gold!**

You destroyed the rough (jaratha) cart with the movement of your foot. Jaratha means hard or rough according to Visvalocana. You killed the washerman (rajaka). You controlled the enemy troops (kataka). The ridge (katakajof Govardhana (aga-vara) shone because of your dancing. You wore new bracelets (kataka) of emerald with gold. Kataka means ridge, bracelet and group according to Nanartha-varga.

*kapaṭa-rudita naṭad-akaṭhina-pada-taṭa-*  
*vighaṭita-dadhi-ghaṭa-niviḍita-suśakaṭa*  
*ruci-tulita-puraṭa-paṭala-rucira-paṭa-*  
*ghaṭita-vipula-kaṭa kuṭila-cikura-ghaṭa*

**О Krsna, crying falsely breaking the yogurt pot with the tip of your moving, tender foot! О Krsna, giving the demon disguised as a cart the bliss of liberation! О Krsna, whose hip is endowed with attractive cloth with the color of piles of gold! О Krsna, with tied up curly locks of hair!**

You cried falsely when your mother went to remove the overflowing milk and then broke (vigh atita) the yogurt pot with the tip of your moving (natal), tender foot out of anger. This is an occasional pastime. You gave the demon disguised as a cart the bliss of liberation (nividita). Your hip is endowed with attractive cloth with the color of piles of gold (purata-patala). Kata means hips according to Amara-kosa. You tie up your curly locks of hair.

*ravi-duhitṛ-nikaṭa-luṭhada-jaraṭha-jaṭa-*  
*viṭapani-cita-vaṭa-taṭa-paṭutara-naṭa*  
*nija-vilasita-haṭha-vicaṭita-suvikaṭa-*  
*caṭulad-anuja-ghaṭa jaya yuvatiṣu śaṭha \|\| vira \|\|*

**О Krsna, skillfully dancing near the Bhandira tree endowed with branches and hanging soft secondary roots near the Yamuna river! О Krsna, killing the terrible, trembling, despised demons with force in your pastimes! О deceiver of the gopis! Manifest with excellence!**

You skillfully dance near the Bhandira tree endowed with branches (vitapani) and hanging soft secondary roots near the Yamuna river. Jata means secondary roots according to Visva. You kill the terrible (suvikata), trembling (catula), despised (vicatita) demons with force in your pastimes.

### Text 63

*vivṛta-vividha-bādhe bhrānti-vegād agādhe*  
*balavati bhava-pūre majjato me’vidūre \|*  
*aśaraṇa-gaṇa-bandho he kṛpā-kaumudīndo*  
*sakṛd-akṛta-vilambaṁ dehi hastāvalambam \|\|63\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О shelter of those with no shelter, who showers moon rays of mercy! Just once, without delay, give a supporting hand to me, drowning in the currents of samsara which gives many types of suffering, deep and strong from the force of illusion, which is not so far from you.**

**Комментарий:**

There are two verses in conclusion. Thinking the Lord is pleased with being praised, the author prays for his deliverance. O friend of those with no shelter (asarana)! Shelter of those with no shelter! O showerer of moon rays of mercy! Give a supporting hand to me, drownifig in the currents of samsara without delay (akrta-vilambam) or quickly. Otherwise these two names have no meaning. Give support just once (sakrt). Just that will deliver me. The ocean of samsara is described. It gives many types of suffering.

“Just wait a minute!” Because of the force of the whirlpools of illusion, the thought that useless things are of value is very strong (balavati), destroying determination, etc. I cannot remain in such a situation. Quickly deliver me. In delivering me, you do not have any difficulty. It is not far away. Situated in your place you should deliver me. The alankaras are alliteration (anuprasa), puns (slesa) and rupaka.

He reinforces his prayer.

O Lord! Your names produce a great festival by prema (.pranayena) manifesting through worship, for the devotees expert at worshipping you (sukrtinam).

The luster of your limbs, dark like a cloud, produce salve for the eyes. The luster sticks to their eyes like ointment. The sounds of your flute, your dear words, ornament their ears. They hear the sounds. With these three items our desires are no longer attractive. Why? The reason is given. Our minds are pained by material desires. Being merciful, our shelter, deliver us.
