*bhavati madābhāso’pi svātijalaṁ mukti-muktāyāḥ \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the name of Murari, a fresh lotus with the honey of prema,**  
**whose abhasa produces pearls of liberation as a side effect, manifest excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

Describing the Lord’s pastime, Rupa invokes auspiciousness with the excellence of the Lord’s names. What is the name? It is a lotus with the honey of prema. This means that when chanted it reveals prema. “It is said that it manifests liberation.”

From its abhasa the pearls of liberation are easily achieved (svatijalam).

Just as pearls are produced in oysters by small drops of water, liberation arises for persons by incidental chanting such as sahketya, etc. It is achieved as a secondary result.

*sāṁkelyaṁ pārihāsyaṁ vā stomaṁ helanameva vā \| vaikuṇṭhanāmagrahaṇamaśeṣāghaharaṁ viduḥ*

**Chanting the name of the Lord while indicating someone else or while joking in a friendly manner, or chanting the Lord’s name in order to fill up space while chanting verses or chanting with neglect destroys unlimited sins and desires. (SB 6.2.14)**

The details will be explained in the stotra.

### Text 2

*nandotsavādayas tāḥ kaṁsa-vadhāntā harer mahā-līlāḥ \|*  
*chandobhir lalitāṅgair aṣṭādaśabhir nirūpyante \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord’s great pastimes, starting with Nanda’s celebration of Krsna’s birth, ending with the killing of Kamsa, are described in eighteen attractive meters.**

**Комментарий:**

He makes a declaration. The meaning is clear.

### Text 3

*danuja-tṛṇaka-damboddāma-dāvāgni-rāśe*  
*kusumita-ravi-kanyā-tīra-vanyā-karīndra \|*  
*madakala-paśupālī-locanedīvarendo*  
*bhavatu tava caritraṁ mad-girāṁ maṇḍanāya \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О forest fire for the proud groups of grass-like demons! О elephant in the flowering forest on the bank of the Yamuna! О moon for the blue lotus eyes of the gopis mad with prema! May your pastimes decorate my words.**

**Комментарий:**

In speaking about the Lord’s pastimes, he prays that his words will ornament the pastimes. О moon for the blue lotus eyes of the gopis mad with prema. He manifests their love. Madakala means most intoxicated according to Amara-kosa. The rest is clear. He is death for the demons. He plays with the cowherds on the bank of the Yamuna. He has pastimes with the gopis. These pastimes should be described.

### Text 4

*mūlotkhāta-vidhāyinī bhavataroḥ kṛṣṇānya-tṛṣṇākṣayāt*  
*kheladbhir muni-cakravāka-nicayair ācamyamānā muhuḥ \|*  
*karṇānandi-kala-svanā vahatu me jihvā-taṭī-prāṅgaṇe*  
*ghūrṇat-tuṅga-rasāvalis tava kathā-pīyūṣa-kallolinī \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna! May the sweet river of your pastimes, which uproots the tree of samsara by destroying other tastes, which is constantly sipped by the many trembling cakravaka sages, whose gentle sound gives bliss to the ears and is full of great currents of swirling rasa, flow on my tongue.**

**Комментарий:**

He prays that the pastimes full of rasa will flow strongly on his tongue.

О Krsna, son of Nanda! May the sweet river of your pastimes (katha) flow on my tongue (jihva-tati-prangane). He describes the pastimes in terms of similarity with the river. It uproots the tree of samsara by destroying thirst for anything other than Krsna. Thirst for other things makes the tree of samsara grow. By drinking the sweet river of pastimes, the thirst is destroyed.

Thus, the tree cannot grow.

The river is drunk constantly by the group of cakravaka sages who play about. That river makes a soft sound joyful to the ears. The word kallola suggest the singer has a river of topics flowing from his mouth. The river has many rasas whirling about. This means there are currents of vatsalya, madhurya, vira, hasya, etc.

## tatra nandotsavādi-caritam

**The Pastime of Nanda’s festival**

### 1

*nija-mahima-maṇḍalī-vraja-vasati-rocanaṁ*  
*vadana-vidhu-mādhurī-ramita-pitṛ-locanam \|*  
*śruti-nipuṇa-bhūsura-vraja-vihita-jātakaṁ*  
*tanu-jalada-tarpita-svajana-gaṇa-cātakam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О fickle mind! Worship the son of Nanda, who illuminates Vraja by all his glories, who pleased his parent’s eyes by his moonlike face, who had his chart drawn up by the expert brahmanas of Vraja, and whose body was the cloud to satisfy his cataka bird relatives.**

**Комментарий:**

First, he speaks of the birth pastime.

О fickle mind! Worship the son of Nanda! This sentence at the end connects with all the words. Accomplishing all your goals by service to Krsna will destroy the fickleness of the mind. Krsna is described. He gives radiance to Vraja by his collection of glories.

Thus, Sukadeva says:

*avādyanta vicitrāṇi vāditrāṇi mahotsave \|*  
*kṛṣṇe viśveśvare'nante nandasya vrajamāgate \|\|*

**Now that the all-pervading, unlimited Lord Krsna, the master of the cosmic manifestation, had arrived within the estate of Maharaja Nanda, various types of musical instruments resounded to celebrate the great festival. (SB 10.5.13)**

*tata ārabhya nandasya vrajaḥ sarvasamṛddhimān \|*  
*harernivāsātmaguṇai ramākrīḍamabhūnnṛpaḥ \|\|*

**О Maharaja Pariksit, the home of Nanda Maharaja is eternally the abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and his transcendental qualities and is therefore always naturally endowed with the opulence of all wealth. Yet beginning from Lord Krsna’s appearance there, it became the place for the pastimes of the goddess of fortune. (SB 10.5.18)**

Previous to his appearance Vraja shone. Before the sun rises, the light appears in the east. He gave pleasure to his parent’s eyes by his sweet moon-like face. His parents attained great joy on seeing his moonlike face. His birth chart was drawn up by brahmanas like Bhaguri, who knew the rules of the Vedas. Sukadeva says:

*nandasvātmaja utpanne jātāhlādo mahāmanāḥ \|*  
*āhūya viprāndaivajñānsnātaḥ śuciralaṁkṛtaḥ \|\|*  
*vācayitvā svastyayanaṁ jātakarmātmajasya vai \|*  
*kārayāmāsa vidhivatpitṛdevārcanaṁ tathā \|\|*

**Nanda Maharaja was naturally very magnanimous, and when Lord Sri Krsna appeared as his son, he was overwhelmed by jubilation. Therefore, after bathing and purifying himself and dressing himself properly, he invited brahmanas who knew how to recite Vedic mantras. After having these qualified brahmanas recite auspicious Vedic hymns, he arranged to have the Vedic birth ceremony celebrated for his newborn child according to the rules and regulations, and he also arranged for worship of the demigods and forefathers. (SB 10.5.1-2)**

By this it is clear that Krsna is the real son of Nanda. The details were previously stated and should be consulted. He satisfied all his relatives, like catdka birds, by his body resembling a cloud. He produces satisfaction in all people of Vraja when they saw him.

### 2

*subahu-vidhadānakṛj-janaka-kṛta-kautukaṁ*  
*nikhila-paśupāvalī-samupahṛta-yautukam \|*  
*jani-samaya-maṇḍitī-kṛta-puruṣa-yoṣitaṁ*  
*rajani-rasa-gorasa-kṣapaṇa-jana-toṣitam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О fickle mind! Worship the son of Nanda, whose father gave many donations at his birth, who was offered gifts by all the cowherd people, whose birth caused the men and women to decorate themselves, and was happy when the people sprinkled milk products mixed with turmeric.**

**Комментарий:**

At his birth ceremony (kautukam) his father gave many types of donations. Sukadeva says:

*dhenūnāṁ niyute prādādviprebhyaḥ samalaṁkṛte \|*  
*tilādrīnsapta ratnaughaśātakaumbhāmbarāvṛtān \|\|*

**Nanda Maharaja gave two million cows, completely decorated with cloth and jewels, in charity to the brahmanas. He also gave them seven hills of grain, covered with jewels and with cloth decorated with golden embroidery. (SB 10.5.3)**

Niyute means two hundred thousand or according to others two million.

*saumaṅgalyagiro viprāḥ sūtamāgadhabandinaḥ \|*  
*gāyakāśca jagurnedurbheryo dundubhayo muhuḥ \|\|*

**The brahmanas recited auspicious Vedic hymns, which purified the environment by their vibration. The experts in reciting old histories like the Puranas, the experts in reciting the histories of royal families, and general reciters all chanted, while singers sang and many kinds of musical instruments, like bhefis and dundubhis, played in accompaniment. (SB 10.5.5)**

*vrajaḥ saṁsṛṣṭasaṁsiktadvārājiragṛhāntaraḥ \| citradhvajapatākāsrakcailapallavatoraṇaiḥ \|\|*

**Vrajapura, the residence of Nanda Maharaja, was fully decorated with varieties of festoons and flags, and in different places, gates were made with varieties of flower garlands, pieces of cloth, and mango leaves. The courtyards, the gates near the roads, and everything within the rooms of the houses were perfectly swept and washed with water. (SB 10.5.6)**

The characteristics of sutas and others is described:

*sūtāḥ paurāṇikāḥ proktā māgadhā vaṁśaśaṁsakāḥ \|*  
*bandinastvamalaprajñāḥ prastāvasadṛśoktayaḥ \|\| iti \|*

**Siitas recite Puranas. Magadhas praise the dynasty. Bandls, having pure intelligence, produce compositions similar to prastavas.**

All the cowherds offered him gifts. At the time of his birth he inspired men and women to decorate themselves. Sukadeva says:

*mahārhavastrābharaṇakañcukoṣṇīṣabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*gopāḥ samāyayū rājannānopāyanapāṇayaḥ \|\|*

**О King Pariksit, the cowherd men dressed very opulently with valuable ornaments and garments such as coats and turbans. Decorated in this way and carrying variouspresentations in their hands, they approached the house of Nanda Maharaja. (SB 10.5.8)**

*gopyaścākarṇya muditā yaśodāyāḥ sutodbhavam \|*  
*ātmānaṁ bhūṣayāṁcakrurvastrākalpāñjanādibhiḥ \|\|*

**The gopi wives of the cowherd men were very pleased to hear that mother Yasoda had given birth to a son, and they began to decorate themselves very nicely with proper dresses, ornaments, black ointment for the eyes, and so on. (SB 10.5.9)**

*navakuṅkumakiñjalkamukhapaṅkajabhūtayaḥ \|*  
*balibhistvaritaṁ jagmuḥ pṛthuśroṇyaścalatkucāḥ \|\|*

**Their lotus-like faces extraordinarily beautiful, being decorated with saffron and newly grown kunkuma, the wives of the cowherd men hurried to the house of mother Yasoda with presentations in their hands. Because of natural beauty, the wives had full hips and full breasts, which moved as they hurried along. (SB 10.5.10)**

*gopyaḥ samṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalaniṣkakaṇṭhyaścitrāmbarāḥ pathi śikhācyutamālyavarṣāḥ \|*  
*nandālayaṁ savalayā vraja tīvirejurvyālolakuṇḍalapayodharahāraśobhāḥ \|\|*

**In the ears of the gopis were brilliantly polished jeweled earrings, and from their necks hung metal lockets. Their hands were decorated with bangles, their dresses were of varied colors, and from their hair, flowers fell onto the street like showers. Thus while going to the house of Maharaja Nanda, the gopis, their earrings, breasts and garlands moving, were brilliantly beautiful. (SB 10.5.11)**

He was satisfied with the people who sprinkled each other with milk and yogurt mixed with turmeric and fragrant oils (rajani-rasa). Rajani means turmeric according to Amara-kosa. He attained happiness by seeing the festival.

### 3

*bahula-dadhi-paṅkilī-kṛta-vilasad-aṅganaṁ*  
*pramada-bhara-lolita-prakaṭa-naṭad-aṅganam \|*  
*janaka-paritoṣita-sphurad-akhila-ballavaṁ*  
*vraja-janita-padmajāvibhava-bhara-pallavam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О fickle mind! Worship the son of Nanda, because of whom the yards became muddy with yogurt and shone, who caused the women to dance conspicuously unsteadily with great joy, who made everyone, who were given gifts by Nanda, tremble with bliss on seeing him, by whose birth the desire creeper of Laksmi manifested in Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of him, the yards, made muddy by the profuse yogurt, shone because of being studded with jewels. At his birth ceremony the yard became muddy with yogurt up to the knees. Because of him the women of Vraja danced conspicuously unsteadily with great joy (pramada). He made all the cowherds and gopis (vallabham), who were given gifts of valuable cloth and ornaments by joyful Nanda, tremble in bliss on seeing him. Sukadeva says:

*tā āśiṣaḥ prayuñjānāściraṁ pāhīti bālake \|*  
*haridrācūrṇatailādbhiḥ siñcantyo janamujjaguḥ \|\|*

**Offering blessings to the newborn child, Krsna, the wives and daughters of the cowherd men said, “May You become the King of Vraja and long maintain all its inhabitants.” They sprinkled a mixture of turmeric powder, oil and water upon the birthless Supreme Lord and offered their prayers. (SB 10.5.12)**

*gopāḥ parasparaṁ hṛṣṭā dadhikṣīraghṛtāmbubhiḥ \|*  
*āsiñcanto vilimpanto navanītaiśca cikṣipuḥ \|\|*

**In gladness, the cowherd men enjoyed the great festival by splashing one another’s bodies with a mixture of curd, condensed milk, butter and water. They threw butter on one another and smeared it on one another’s bodies. (SB 10.5.14)**

*nando mahāmanāstebhyo vāso'laṁkāragodhanam \|*  
*sūtamāgadhavandibhyo ye'nye vidyopajīvinaḥ \|\|*  
*taistaiḥ kāmairadīnātmā yathocitamapūjayat \|*  
*viṣṇorārādhanārthāya svaputrasyodayāya ca \|\|*

**The great-minded Maharaja Nanda gave clothing, ornaments and cows in charity to the cowherd men in order to please Lord Visnu, and thus he improved the condition of his own son in all respects. He distributed charity to the sutas, the magadhas, the vandis, and men of all other professions, according to their educational qualifications, and satisfied everyone’s desires. (SB 10.5.15-16)**

Tebhyah in the Bhdgavatam verse also refers to the cowherds and the cowherd women. He gave according to the qualities of the recipient (.yathocitam). Because of him the shoots manifested great wealth by Mahalaksmi who followed him. By his birth, the desire creeper of Laksmi manifested to fulfill the desires of Vraja’s people. When her master Krsna was born, she followed him.

*tata arabhya nandasya vrajah sarva-samrddhiman*  
*harer nivasatma-gunai ramakridam abhiin nrpa*

**O Maharaja Pariksit, the home of Nanda Maharaja is eternally the abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and his transcendental qualities and is therefore always naturally endowed with the opulence of all wealth. Yet beginning from Lord Krsna’s appearance there, it became the place for the pastimes of the goddess of fortune. (SB 10.5.18)**

The festival of Nanda has been described.

### 4

*kapaṭa-paṭu-pūtanākaṭu-nayana-vīkṣitaṁ*  
*vraja-bhaya-danur jana-vraja-nidhana-dīkṣitam \|*  
*viṣama-baka-pūrvajākuca-savidha-śāyinaṁ*  
*tad-asuparimiśrita-stana-jarasapāyinam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О fickle mind! Worship the son of Nanda, who was gazed upon by the sharp eyes of duplicitous Putana, who vowed to destroy all the demons giving fear to Vraja, who lay down next to the breast of murderous Putana, and drank her breast milk along with her life airs.**

**Комментарий:**

The killing of Putana is described.

He was seen by the very sharp eyes of Putana, skillfully disguised, attractively dressed and showing false motherly affection, sent by Kamsa, when Nanda went to pay the yearly tax after Krsna’s birth celebration. Devotees should not fear Putana. The son of Nanda will kill all the wicked people. That is explained. Krsna made a firm vow to destroy all the wicked persons who gave fear to Vraja. He lay near the breast of murderous Putana, elder sister of Baka. He lay with closed eyes to kill her when she took him from the bed, disrespecting the mother and showing false affection. Then what happened? He drank her breast milk mixed with her life airs (asu). He drank her milk with her life airs.

### 5

*tad-urutara-vigraha-druma-nivaha-pātanam*  
*pṛthuka-ripu-rākṣasī-vividha-bhava-śātanam \|*  
*nipuṇa-paśupāṅganākula-kalita-rakṣaṇaṁ*  
*praṇaya-kṛta-gorajaḥ-śakṛd-amala-lakṣaṇam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О fickle mind! Worship the son of Nanda, who crushed Kamsa’s groves by her huge body, who destroyed the thick samsara of Putana, his great enemy, who was protected by the expert cowherd women and who auspiciously was marked with cow dung and cow urine out of affection.**

**Комментарий:**

He crushed all the groves of Kamsa, situated six krosas around outside of his house using her body which became as big as a mountain. And he played on her breast.

Sukadeva says:

*patamāno'pi taddehastrigavyūtyantaradrumān \|*  
*cūrṇayāmāsa rājendra mahadāsīt tad adbhutam \|\|*

**О King Pariksit, when the gigantic body of Putana fell to the ground, it smashed all the trees within a limit of twelve miles. Appearing in a gigantic body, she was certainly extraordinary. (SB 10.6.14)**

*bālaṁ ca tasyā urasi krīḍantamakutobhayam \|*  
*gopyastūrṇaṁ samabhyetya jagṛhurjāta-saṁbhramāḥ \|\|*

**Without fear, the child Krsna was playing on the upper portion of Putana Raksasi’s breast, and when the gopis saw the child’s wonderful activities, they immediately came forward with great jubilation and picked him up. (SB 10.6.18)**

Satisfied because she dressed as a nurse, he gave her liberation. He cut the tangle of samsara of the demoness who killed many children, who was the enemy of the boy.

Uddhava says:

*aho vakīyaṁ stanakālakūṭaṁ jighāṁsayā pāyayadapy asādhvī \|*  
*lebhe gatiṁ dhātryucitāṁ tato'nyaṁ kaṁ vā dayāluṁ śaraṇaṁ vrajema \|\|*

**Oh! Evil Putana, who offered her poisonous breast to Krsna to drink with the intention of killing him, attained the position of a nurse in the spiritual world. Who else is so merciful? I surrender to him! (SB 3.2.23)**

By the killing of Putana and destruction of his garden, an auspicious prayer for Kamsa’s killing is suggested. He was protected by the group of cowherd women who were expert in scriptural rules. How did they do this? They affectionately marked his limbs with cow dung and cow urine. Sukadeva says:

**yaśodārohiṇībhyāṁ tāḥ samaṁ bālasya sarvaśaḥ \|**  
**rakṣāṁ vidadhire samyaggopucchabhramaṇādibhiḥ \|\|**

**Thereafter, mother Yasoda and Rohini, along with the other elderly gopis, waved about the switch of a cow to give full protection to the child Sri Krsna. (SB 10.6.19)**

*gomūtreṇa snāpayitvā punargorajasārbhakama rakṣāṁ ca cakruḥ śakṛtā dvādaśāṅgeṣu nāmabhiḥ \|\|*

The child was thoroughly washed with cow urine and then smeared with the dust raised by the movements of the cows. Then different names of the Lord were applied with cow dung on twelve different parts of his body, beginning with the forehead, as done in applying tilaka. In this way, the child was given protection. (SB 10.6.20)

### 6

*sphuṭa-nikhila-ballavī-hṛdaya-nava-candanaṁ*  
*bhaja capala-mānasa vraja-nṛpati-nandanam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О fickle mind! Worship the son of Nanda, a fresh moon blossoming in the hearts of all the cowherd women.**

### Text 5

*tava jayati nandanandana padāravindoru-bhakti-makarandaḥ \|*  
*ja(ya)n mādhurī-lavāgre mukti-sukhaṁ śuktitām eti \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О son of Nanda! May the honey of great bhakti to your lotus feet, which makes liberation as insignificant as a seashell, remain with all excellence.**

guccha kākhyam idaṁ chandaḥ \|

*The meter is called gucchaka.*

nagaṇasagaṇāṅkito janajagurusaṁyuto bhavati kila gucchako vasuyativibhūṣitaḥ \|

*sss ssl sis sss sis 1 (na, sa,ja, na,ja, gu.) with caesura after the eighth syllable is called gucchaka.*

## atha sakata-trnavarta-bhangadi

**Killing Sakata, Trnavarta and others**

### Text 6

*mama matir uccala-caraṇe bhagavati paryaṅki-kāśayite \|*  
*kapaṭa-krandita-kuśale śakaṭa-vighaṭṭini parisphuratu \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May my mind shine in the Lord who, lying under the cart, lifting his feet, while skillfully but falsely crying, kicked the cart away.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of him his mother was busy with the festival of the child turning over in bed (autthanika). His mother was busying taking care of all the women of Vraja who had come to the festival. He was lying on a soft, colorful bed beneath a cart. He was bathed while music played with song and brahmana’s chanting. The brahmanas were worshipped with attractive food, clothing and ornaments. His mother lay him to rest on a bed beneath the cart, understanding that he had fallen asleep. He cried, thirsty for her breast milk while his mother was busy receiving the people of Vraja. Sukadeva says:

### 1

*autthānika-maha-saṅkulitāmbaka*  
*śakaṭādhastana-śayanālambaka \|*  
*kuca-rasa-tṛṣṇā-viracita-rodana*  
*cañcala-pada-kṛta-śakaṭa-vinodana \|*

**Перевод:**

**The liberal mother Yasoda, absorbed in celebrating the utthana ceremony, was busy receiving guests, worshiping them with all respect and offering them clothing, cows, garlands and grains. Thus she could not hear the child crying for his mother. At that time, the child Krsna, demanding to drink the milk of His mother’s breast, angrily threw his legs upward. (SB 10.7.6)**

**Комментарий:**

He broke the cart heavy with many pots using his moving soft bud-like feet.

Sukadeva says:

*adhaḥśayānasya śiśorakalpakapravāla mṛdvaṅghrihataṁ vyavartata*

**Lord Srl Krsna was lying down underneath the handcart in one corner of the courtyard, and although his little legs were as soft as leaves, when he struck the cart with his legs, it turned over violently and collapsed. (SB 10.7.7)**

### 2

*vismita-paśupa-sudurgama-ceṣṭita*  
*kathita-nijehita-śāvaka-veṣṭita \|*  
*kātara-janakī-janaka-gatāntika*  
*māntrika-dharaṇī-sura-kṛta-śāntika \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who surprised the cowherds, unable to understand your activities! О Krsna, surrounded by young children who said he had kicked the cart! О Krsna, approached by his mother and father who were worried! О Krsna, whose obstacles were removed by chanting brahmanas!**

**Комментарий:**

The cowherds were surprised, unable to understand his activities. “How did this happen?” Pasupa means gopis like Yasoda and gopas like Nanda. He was surrounded by young children who said that Krsna had kicked the cart. He was approached by his mother and father who were worried, not believing the story told by the boys, but fearing some ghost. He had obstacles removed by brahmanas (.dharani-sura') who chanted mantras. She then fed him milk, after the rituals were done by the brahmanas. Inspired by the Lord, the chief cowherds fixed the cart and pacified the planets and then Krsna was blessed by brahmanas who offered yogurt and rice. This concludes the story of Sakatasura’s killing.

### 3

*jananī-durvaha-gaurava-vigraha sapadi vidhitsita-danuja-vinigraha \|*  
*danu-tanayena kṣaṇam apavāhita kaṇṭha-taṭī-graha-nirmathitāhita \|*  
*viklava-jananī-nirbhara-śocita virudad-gopī-kula-parilocita \|*  
*nirmita-jananī-bandhu-mahodaya mām api gokula-maṅgala modaya \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, whose heavy body form became difficult to carry by your mother! О Krsna, wanting to destroy the demon quickly! О Krsna, suddenly taken up in the air by the demon! О Krsna, who grabbing the demon by the throat and crushed him on a stone slab! О Krsna, who troubled Yasoda who lamented greatly! О Krsna, seen by all the surrounding gopis who were weeping! О Krsna, giving great joy to the friends of his mother! Give joy to me, О auspiciousness of Gokula!**

**Комментарий:**

Next killing the demon Trnavarta is described. His powerful form became difficult to carry, like a mountain, by his mother. He manifested his power in order to separate himself from her. He thought, “My mother should not suffer because of the demon.” Why did he do this? He wanted (vidhitsita) to quickly destroy (vinigraha) the demon.

He was suddenly taken up in the air by the demon, while Krsna thought, “I will accomplish my purpose by this.” Krsna went up in the air to see his pastime place.

Seeing the place, he then killed (ahita) the enemy, grabbing by the throat and throwing him on a stone slab. Disturbed on not seeing her son, the mother lamented greatly. “Where has he gone? Who took my baby? What will I do?” she lamented.

He was' seen playing fearlessly on the demon’s chest by all the surrounding gopis who were weeping. He causes great joy to the friends of his mother, being taken and given to her after he had killed the demon for everyone’s auspiciousness. O auspiciousness of Gokula! Give pleasure to me as you gave to his mother and others. The killing of Trnavarta has been described.

### 4

*nava-śiśu-līlā-laṅghita-hāyana gargāviṣkṛta-nāma-rasāyana \|*  
*riṅgana-maṇḍita-nanda-niketana madhurima-tarpita-gokula-cetana \|*  
*calatara-tarṇaka-puccha-vikarṣaṇa vismṛta-gṛha-kṛti-ramaṇī-harṣaṇa \|*  
*kutukinna-samaya-vatsa-vimocana caurya-viśaṅkita-cañcala-locana \|*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, who passed one year as a new baby! O Krsna, given a name by Garga! O Krsna, decorating Nanda’s house by crawling! O Krsna, satisfying the people of Vraja by your sweetness! O Krsna, who pulled the tails of the moving calves! О Krsna, giving joy to the gopis who forgot their duties! О Krsna, who released the calves at the time of milking! О Krsna, with eyes showing fear when stealing yogurt!**

**Комментарий:**

Another pastime is related. You passed one year as a new baby. Then you were given a name by Garga, after coming from Mathura and being worshipped by Nanda. You decorated Nanda’s house by crawling on your knees and hands. Niketana means house according to Amara-kosa. You satisfied the people (cetane) of Vraja by your sweetness.

Then his fickle na ture of walking rather than crawling is described. You pulled tails of the calves who were moving, being pulled away by them. The women laughed by such actions and forgot to do their household duties, seeing your fickleness and beauty. Understanding the cows’ affection for their calves (kutukin), you released the calves at the time of milking (asamaya). The great affection of the gopis when he stole the yogurt and butter is described. Your eyes showed fear and unsteadiness fearing someone would know and catch you stealing the yogurt.

### 5

*ākrośana-kṛta-hasitāḍambara mukha-pāṭava-kṛta-luñcana-saṁvara \|*  
*racitolūkhala-pṛṣṭha-virājana randhrita-śikya-sthita-vara-bhājana \|*  
*gavya-vinirmita-kapi-kula-rañjana kalpita-nava-dadhi-haṇḍī-bhañjana \|*  
*jananī-vīkṣita-sabhaya-vilocana jaya jaya gokula-padma-virocana \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who smiled when the gopis shouted! О Krsna, who covered the theft by the splendid facial expression! О Krsna, who stood on the mortar! О Krsna, who put a hole in the hanging pot! О Krsna, who attracted the monkeys with the milk products! О Krsna, who broke the pot of fresh butter! О Krsna, who showed fearful eyes on being seen by Yasoda! O sun for the lotuses of Vraja! Manifest your excellence!**

**Комментарий:**

“O moon-faced Krsna! Why are you so fickle?” When the gopis shouted in this way, he would show a smile and say, “Are you accusing me of being a thief? I am the best of the well behaved.” How should the fault of stealing be removed? He covered his theft by the splendid expression on his face (mukha-patava).

He stood on the pestle to take the pots which were tied above by the gopis who were engaged in household duties, so that he could not steal the yogurt. He put a hole in the hanging pot. The next two items are clear in meaning. Sukadeva says:

*vatsānmuñcankvacidasamaye krośasaṁjātahāsaḥ steyaṁ svādvattyatha dadhipayaḥ kalpitaiḥ steyayogaiḥ \|*  
*markānbhokṣyanvibhajati sa cennātti bhāṇḍaṁ bhinatti dravyālābhe sagṛhakupito yātyupakrośya tokān \|\|*

**Our dear friend Yasoda, your son sometimes comes to our houses before the milking of the cows and releases the calves, and when the master of the house becomes angry, your son merely smiles. Sometimes he devises some process by which he steals palatable curd, butter and milk, which he then eats and drinks. When the monkeys assemble, he divides it with them, and when the monkeys have their bellies so full that they won’t take more, he breaks the pots. Sometimes, if he gets no opportunity to steal butter or milk from a house, he will be angry at the householders, and for his revenge he will agitate the small children by pinching them. Then, when the children begin crying, Krsna will go away. (SB 10.8.29)**

Returning home after playing, he showed fearful eyes because of his acts, seeing Yasoda who was not able to scold him when the gopis came with a desire to see him reprimanded for his fickle acts and informed her. О sun who makes the lotuses of Vraja blossom! May you manifest excellence.

### 6

*rāma-prakaṭīkṛta-mṛd-bhakṣaṇa jananī-saṁmukha-dhṛta-bhaya-lakṣaṇa \|*  
*mukha-puṭa-darśita-nikhila-carācara gopeśvara-suta mayi mudam ācara \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who showed his powers when eating dirt! О Krsna, who showed fear in front of his mother! О Krsna, who showed all moving and non-moving in his mouth! О son of Nanda! Give bliss to me!**

**Комментарий:**

Though knowing in truth, when my mother sees my supreme power, she should not have fear. He showed his powers when eating dirt. That he ate dirt was revealed by Balarama, his chief friend. He showed fear in front of his mother who was lamenting, “O uncontrolled boy! Why do you eat dirt, giving up butter and sugar?” His eyes contracted and he trembled. I have not eaten dirt. “Look.” He showed all moving and non-moving beings situated in his mouth. His mother understood his powers. “This is the power of my son.” Sukadeva says:

*kiṁ svapna etaduta devamāyā kiṁ vā madīyo bata buddhimohaḥ \|*  
*atho amuṣyaiva mamārbhakasya yaḥ kaścanotpattika ātmayogaḥ \|\|*

**Is this a dream, or is it an illusory creation by the external energy? Has this been manifested by my own intelligence, or is it some mystic power of my child? (SB 10.8.40)**

### Text 7

*gṛhaṁ sakhi karālike praviśati sma nīlaḥ śiśur*  
*dṛḍhīkuru kavāṭikāṁ dadhi-haraṁ dadhāmy uddhuram \|*  
*iti prakaṭam īrite mukharayā mahā-śaṅkaṭaṁ*  
*vilokya tanu-kaṅkaṭīkṛtatamā hariḥ pātu vaḥ \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“O my friend Karalika! The dark boy has entered the house. Lock the door. I will catch the impudent stealer of yogurt.” When Mukhara said this aloud, Krsna looked around in great fear. May Krsna, who made his body merge in the darkness, protect you.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of its charm, the author again describes stealing yogurt.

Mukhara is Radha’s maternal grandmother. Karala is Candravali’s maternal grandmother. In the first part of the verse, when Mukhara spoke, Krsna looked around with great worry. “How can I exit from this locked house?” Not seeing any other method, he used darkness as his protection (kankatt) for his body. He became invisible in the darkness of the room. She did not see him. “I came here for fun.” Smiling, having had his fun, he then ate butter.

**korakākhyam idam chandaḥ \|**

The meter is koraka. It is described in this way:

*ṣoḍaśakalacaraṇaṁ bhuvi saṁprati modavivardhakamakhilajanaṁ prati \| śeṣaya makalaghuyugalamano hara matir ucikorakasaṁjñam udāhara \|\|*

**Each line with sixteen matras increased enjoyment of all people immediately on earth. At the end of the line are attractive rhyming words with two short syllables. Declare this as the definition of koraka.**

According to this definition, the work has been written. This definition is applied elsewhere also.

## atha yamal-ārjuna bhañjanam

**Breaking the Yamalarjuna trees**

### Text 8

*indranīla-madhura-prabhaṁ janaṁ*  
*hāsayantam anasaḥ prabhañjanam \|*  
*bibhrataṁ puraṭa-piṅgalaṁ paṭaṁ*  
*dhehi citta navanīta-lampaṭam \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О heart! Meditate on the butter thief, whose effulgence is sweet like a sapphire, who makes the people of Vraja laugh, who broke the cart and who wears golden cloth.**

**Комментарий:**

To describe stealing butter, getting tied up, and fickle actions towards his mother, the author writes this verse as an indication. О heart! Hold Krsna, the butter thief, to yourself (meditate on him). You will attain the butter. Butter is the essence of yogurt according to Halayudha. Krsna is described. He has the sweet effulgence of a sapphire. He makes the people of Vraja (janam) laugh by his various pastimes. He broke the cart. He wears golden cloth. There is yamdka (rhyme) at the end.

### 1

*dhṛta-dadhi-manthana-daṇḍa jananī-cumbita-gaṇḍa*  
*pīta-savitrī-dugdha kala-bhāṣita-kula-mugdha \|*  
*jananī-payasā-tṛpta bhājana-bhañjana-dṛpta*  
*kṛta-haiyaṅgava-moṣa mātṛ-vinirmita-roṣa \|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, grabbing the churning rod and kissed by your mother! О Krsna, who drank your mother’s milk and uttered many pleasing words! О Krsna, who, not satisfied with drinking, out of anger broke the pot! О Krsna, who, stealing the butter, made your mother angry!**

**Комментарий:**

О Madhava! Please protect me! О root of auspiciousness! Manifest your excellence (jaya jaya). The words are connected with these verbs. You grabbed the churning rod, since you desired breast milk.

*tāṁ tanyakāma āsādya mathnatī jananīṁ hariḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā dadhimanthānaṁ nyaṣedhatprītimāvahan \|\|*

**While mother Yasoda was churning butter, Lord Krsna, desiring to drink the milk of her breast, appeared before her, and in order to increase her transcendental pleasure, he caught hold of the churning rod and began to prevent her from churning. (SB 10.9.4)**

Placing you on her lap, your mother kissed you on the cheek. You drank your mother’s (savitri) milk. Savitri means mother according to Dhananjaya. You were enchanting with many soft words. You spoke to her sweetly. You were not satisfied with your mother’s milk since she left to take care of overboiling milk meant for her son to drink. “You gave me up and went away. 1 will destroy the objects in your house.” With anger he broke the yogurt pot. You stole (mosd) the butter to give to the monkeys after you finished eating it. You made your mother angry. Sukadeva says:

*tamaṅkamārūḍhamapāyayatstanaṁ snehastu(sru)taṁ sasmitamīkṣatī mukham \|*  
*atṛptamutsṛjya ya(ja)vena sā yayāvutsicyamāne payasi tvadhiśrite \|\|*

**Mother Yasoda then embraced Krsna, allowed him to sit down on her lap, and began to look upon the face of the Lord with great love and affection. Because of her intense affection, milk was flowing from her breast. But when she saw that the milk pan on the oven was boiling over, she immediately left her son to take care of the overflowing milk, although the child was not yet fully satisfied with drinking the milk of his mother’s breast. (SB 10.9.5)**

*sa jātakopaḥ sphuritāruṇādharaṁ saṁdaśya dadbhirdadhimaṇḍamājanam \|*  
*bhittvā mṛṣāśu dṛṣadaśmanā raho jaghāsa haiyaṁgavamantaraṁ gataḥ \|\|*

**Being very angry and biting his reddish lips with his teeth, Krsna, with false tears in his eyes, broke the container of yogurt with a piece of stone. Then he entered a room and began to eat the freshly churned butter in a solitary place. (SB 10.9.6)**

### 2

*janayitrī-kṛta-dhāva muni-gaṇa-durlabha-bhāva*  
*vidita-savitrī-pīla parihṛta-dhāvana-līla \|*  
*dhṛta-haiyaṅgava-gandha kalitolūkhala-bandha*  
*dṛṣṭārjuna-taru-mūla sura-muni-vāg-anukūla \|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who ran away from Yasoda, having a mood rare for sages! О Krsna, who, knowing your mother’s fatigue, stopped running! О Krsna, fragrant with butter, who was tied to the mortar! О Krsna, who, seeing the roots of the two arjuna trees, fulfilled the curse of Narada!**

**Комментарий:**

You were chased by your mother who saw everything destroyed, in order to catch you, running behind you as you fled. Your mother’s mood with you running in fear could not be attained by sages even mentally. How were you caught? You made your mother tired. You then gave up running. Understanding your mother was tired you gave up running. You smelled like butter. Your mother tied you to the mortar. Sukadeva says:

*svamātuḥ khinnagātrāyā visrastakavarasrajaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā pariśramaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛpayāsītsvabandhane \|\|*

**Because of mother Yasoda’s hard labor, her whole body became covered with perspiration, and the flowers and comb were falling from her hair. When child Krsna saw his mother thus fatigued, he became merciful to her and agreed to be bound. (SB 10.9.18)**

When your mother went elsewhere, thinking, “Bound up for a moment, he will give up his restlessness,” you saw the root of two arjuna trees. The purpose is explained. You fulfilled the words of Narada, liberating the two from his curse.

### 3

*kṛta-yamalārjuna-bhaṅga guhyaka-nuti-dhṛta-raṅga*  
*nija-bhaktīkṛta-yakṣa mādhava mām api rakṣa \|*  
*vismita-ballava-dṛṣṭa susmita-mukha-puṭa hṛṣṭa*  
*nanda-vimocita-bandha jaya jaya maṅgala-kanda \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, who broke the two arjuna trees and was pleased by the Guhyakas’ prayers! O Krsna, who made them into devotees! O Madhava! Protect me also. O Krsna, who with smiling face, joyful were seen by the cowherds! O Krsna, freed of your bondage by Nanda! O root of auspiciousness! Manifest your excellence!**

**Комментарий:**

You then broke the two arjuna trees by going between the trees dragging the mortar at right angles. You were pleased by the prayers of the two Guhyakas, Kuvera’s sons. You made them into your devotees. You were seen by the cowherds who thought, “How did the two trees fall?” when they came because of the loud sound. O Krsna, with smiling face? O overjoyed Krsna! You had your bonds untied by laughing Nanda, who asked, “O child! How have you become bound up?”

### Text 9

*bṛhad-vipina-maṇḍane kaluṣa-maṇḍalī-khaṇḍane*  
*vraja-praṇaya-śaṁsane danuja-vṛddhi-vidhvaṁsane \|*  
*muhur dharaṇi-rocane mahita-ballavī-locane*  
*parisphuratu kaiśave ratir atīva naḥ śaiśave \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May we manifest intense rati for Kesava, performing his childhood pastimes, who decorates Mahavana, who destroys piles of sins, who praises the affection of Vraja, who destroys many demons, who is attractive to the earth always, who give joy to the gopis’ eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of the attractiveness of Mahavana, the author again speaks. May we manifest intense rati for Kesava, performing his childhood pastimes! He destroyed piles of sins (kalusa). He pleases the earth (dharani). He gives bliss (mahita) to the gopis’ eyes. The rest is clear.

**anukūlākhyam idaṁ chandaḥ \|**

The meter is anukiila. It is described as follows.

*ekādaśa kala dhāri budha jana māna sahāri \|*  
*idam anukūlam avehi laghukam antam anudhehi \|\|*

**Understand this anukiila. It has eleven matras that attract people’s minds with a weak syllable at the end.**

According to this definition it has been written. It is also called abhira, with sis at the end.

## atha vṛndāvane vatsacāraṇādi

**Herding calves in Vrndavana, etc.**

### Text 10

*kadā vṛndāraṇye mihira-duhituḥ saṅga-mahite*  
*muhur bhrāmaṁ bhrāmaṁ carita-laharīr gokula-pateḥ \|*  
*lapann uccair uccair nayana-payasāṁ veṇibhir ahaṁ*  
*kariṣye sotkaṇṭho niviḍam avasekaṁ viṭapinām \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When will I, with longing, loudly reciting the pastimes of Krsna while wandering always in Vrndavana on the bank of the Yamuna, thoroughly water the trees with rivers of my tears?**

**Комментарий:**

The pastime of coming to Vrndavana from Mahavana should be described. That is expressed in this prayer. The meaning is clear. Veni means a stream according to Haima. May I cry at the base of every tree out of prema.

### 1

*vrajendur upanandāntarīṇam atinodī*  
*manojñatara-vṛndāvanāntar-anumodī \|*  
*antaḥstha-janayitryā nijāṅkam upanītaḥ*  
*kuraṅga-nayanābhiḥ saharṣam anugītaḥ \|*

**Перевод:**

**May the moon of Vraja, who inspired Upananda’s mind, who favored going to attractive Vrndavana, who was held on the lap of Yasoda who mounted the cart, who was joyfully glorified by other women, be pleased with me.**

**Комментарий:**

May the moon of Vraja (vrajenduh) wearing a forest garland be satisfied with me. May he be pleased by the singing of pastimes. (This is placed at the end of the composition). He is described. He inspires the mind of Upananda, his uncle and advisor to Nanda. He inspires him to give permission to go to Vrndavana. He internally permitted Vrndavana, more attractive than Brhad-vana. When Upananda gave permission, the journey is described. He sat on Yasoda’s lap when she mounted the cart with Rohini. Anah means cart or chariot according to Halayudha. He was praised by other gopis who had mounted the car.

### 2

*praphulla-pṛthu-vṛndāvanopahṛta-raṅgaḥ*  
*kalinda-giri-putrī-taṭānta-dhṛta-saṅgaḥ \|*  
*girīndra-kaṭakāṅgīkṛtoru-paritoṣaḥ*  
*samasta-sakhi-rājī-vilāsa-maṇi-koṣaḥ \|*

**Перевод:**

**May the moon of Vraja, joyful on attaining vast, blossoming Vrndavana, who came near the Yamuna, who was joyful in coming to the side of Govardhana, who was a treasure house of gem-like pastimes in the groves, be pleased with me.**

**Комментарий:**

He became joyful at attaining broad Vrndavana, blossoming with trees and creepers. The meaning of the next line is clear. Sukadeva says:

*gopavṛddhā mahotpātānanubhūya bṛhadvane \|*  
*nandādayaḥ samāgamya vraja-kāryam amantrayan \|\|*

**Then one time, having seen the great disturbances in Brhadvana, all the elderly persons among the cowherd men, headed by Nanda Maharaja, assembled and began to consider what to do to stop the continuous disturbing situations in Vraja. (SB 10.11.21)**

*tatropanandanāmāha gopo jñānavayodhikaḥ \|*  
*deśakālārthatattvajñaḥ priyakṛdrāmakṛṣṇayoḥ \|\|*

**At this meeting of all the inhabitants of Gokula, a cowherd man named Upananda, who was the most mature in age and knowledge and was very experienced according to time, circumstances and country, made this .suggestion for the benefit of Rama and Krsna. (SB 10.11.22)**

*utthātavyamito'smābhirgokulasya hitaiṣibhiḥ  \|*  
*vanaṁ vṛndāvanaṁ nāma paśavyaṁ navakānanam \|*

**He said: My dear friends the cowherd men, in order to do good to this place, Gokula, we should leave it, because so many disturbances are always occurring here, just for the purpose of killing Rama and Krsna. (SB 10.11.23)**

*vanaṁ vṛndāvanaṁ nāma paśavyaṁ navakānanam \|*  
*gopagopīgavāṁ sevyaṁ puṇyāditṛṇavīrudham \|\|*

**Between Nandesvara and Mahavana is a place named Vrndavana. This place is very suitable because it is lush with grass, plants and creepers for the cows and other animals. It has nice gardens and tall mountains and is full of facilities for the happiness of all the gopas and gopis and our animals. (SB 10.11.28)**

*tattatraivādya yāsyāmaḥ śakaṭānyuṅkta māciram \|*  
*godhanānyagrato yāntu bhavatāṁ yadi rocate \|\|*

**Therefore, let us immediately go today. There is no need to wait any further. If you agree to my proposal, let us prepare all the bullock carts and put the cows in front of us, and let us go there. (SB 10.11.29)**

*tacchrutvaikadhiyo gopāḥ sādhu sādhviti vādinaḥ \|*  
*vrajānsvānsvān samādāya yayū rūḍhaparicchadāḥ \|\|*

**Upon hearing this advice from Upananda, the cowherd men unanimously agreed. “Very nice,” they said, “Very nice.” Thus they sorted out their household affairs, placed their clothing and other paraphernalia on the carts, and immediately started for Vrndavana. (SB 10.11.30)**

*gopyo rūḍharathā nūtnakucakuṅkumakāntayaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇalīlāṁ jaguḥ prītā niṣkakaṇṭhyaḥ muvāsasaḥ \|\|*

**The cowherd women, riding on the bullock carts, were dressed very nicely with excellent garments, and their bodies, especially their breasts, were decorated with fresh kunkuma powder. As they rode, they began to chant with great pleasure the pastimes of Krsna. (SB 10.11.33)**

*tathā yaśodārohiṇyāvekaṁ śakaṭamāsthite \|*  
*rejatuḥ kṛṣṇarāmābhyāṁ tatkathāśravaṇotsuke \|\|*

**Thus hearing about the pastimes of Krsna and Balarama with great pleasure, mother Yasoda and Rohinidevi, so as not to be separated from Krsna and Balarama for even a moment, got up with Them on one bullock cart. In this situation, they all looked very beautiful. (SB 10.11.34)**

*vṛndāvanaṁ govardhanaṁ yamunāpulināni ca \|*  
*vīkṣyāsīduttamā prītī rāmamādhavayor nṛpa \|\|*

**O King Pariksit, when Rama and Krsna saw Vrndavana, Govardhana and the banks of the River Yamuna, They both enjoyed great pleasure. (SB 10.11.36)**

He was joyful in coming to the side of Govardhana. Uruparitosa means joy. Synonyms are given by Dhananjaya. He was a chest of shining gems for all his friends.

### 3

*samīpa-bhuvi vatsa-pracāra-dhṛta-tarṣaḥ*  
*suhṛtsu guru-khelā-bhareṇa kṛta-harṣaḥ \|*  
*taraṅgad-uru-geṇḍu-praviṣṭa-cala-dṛṣṭiḥ*  
*praṇīta-vara-vaṁśī-nināda nava-sṛṣṭiḥ \|*

**Перевод:**

**May the moon of Vraja, who desired to pasture the calves in the neighboring land, who became joyful with intent while playing with friends, whose eyes moved as the ball rose and fell, who made fresh tunes on an excellent flute, be pleased with me.**

**Комментарий:**

You had the desire to pasture the calves in the land beside the house. You were joyful with friends with the strong intention of playing. His playing is described. Your moving eyes followed the ball as it rose and fell. You made fresh tunes on your excellent flute.

### 4

*tarakṣu-nakha-lakṣmī-parīta-mṛdu-kaṇṭhaḥ*  
*kaṭīra-taṭa-kūjad-vicitra-laghu-ghaṇṭaḥ \|*  
*samūḍha-śikhi-cūḍā-praṇīta-vara-cūḍaḥ*  
*sumañjutara-guñjāvalībhir upagūḍhaḥ \|*

**Перевод:**

**May the moon of Vraja, whose tender throat was decorated with beautiful tiger claws, who had small jeweled bells on the waist, whose excellent hair was topped with a peacock feather, who was embraced by charming gunja berries, be pleased with me.**

**Комментарий:**

Your tender throat was endowed with the beauty by tiger claws embedded in gold. Taraksu means a tiger according to Halayudha. You had small bells embedded with gems that jingled on your waist. You fine hair was decorated with a peacock feather on top. The next line is clear.

### 5

*suhṛdbhir api sārdhaṁ prapanna-vṛṣa-veṣaḥ*  
*kaṭhoratara-vatsāsurebhaharir eṣaḥ \|*  
*sthaviṣṭha-baka-tuṇḍa-praveśa-kṛta-līlas*  
*tad-aṅga-giri-kūṭa-prabheda-paviśīlaḥ \|*

**Перевод:**

**May the moon of Vraja who dressed up like a bull along with friends, who became a lion against the elephant-like Vatsasura, who performed the pastimes of entering the beak of huge Baka, who was like a thunderbolt in bifurcating his mountainous body, be pleased with me.**

**Комментарий:**

You dressed up like a bull along with your friends. You were a lion with the elephant-like Vatsasura. You killed him. Sukadeva says:

*avidūre vrajabhuvaḥ saha gopāladārakaiḥ \| cārayāmāsaturvatsānnānākrīḍāparicchadau \|\|*

**Not far away from their residential quarters, both Krsna and Balarama, equipped with all kinds of playthings, played with other cowherd boys and began to tend the small calves. (SB 10.11.38)**

*kvacidvādayato veṇuṁ kṣepaṇaiḥ kṣipataḥ kvacit \|*  
*kvacitpādaiḥ kiṅkiṇībhiḥ kvacitkṛtrimagovṛṣaiḥ \|\|*

*anukṛtya rutairjantūśceratuḥ prākṛtau yathā \|\|*

**Sometimes Krsna and Balarama would play on their flutes, sometimes they would throw ropes and stones devised for getting fruits from the trees, sometimes they would throw only stones, and sometimes, their ankle bells tinkling, they would play football with fruits like bael and amalaki. Sometimes they would cover themselves with blankets and imitate cows and bulls and fight with one another, roaring loudly, and sometimes they would imitate the voices of the animals. In this way they enjoyed sporting, exactly like two ordinary human children. (SB 10.11.39-40)**

*kadācidyamunātīre vatsāṁścārayatoḥ svakhaiḥ \|*

**One day while Rama and Krsna, along with their playmates, were tending the calves on the bank of the River Yamuna, another demon arrived there, desiring to kill them.**

*taṁ vatsarūpiṇaṁ vīkṣya vatsayūthagataṁ hariḥ \|*  
*darśayanbaladevāya śanairmugdha ivāsadat \|\|*

**When the Supreme Lord saw that the demon had assumed the form of a calf and entered among the groups of other calves, he pointed out to Baladeva, “Here is another demon.” Then he very slowly approached the demon, as if he did not understand the demon’s intentions. (SB 10.11.42)**

*gṛhītvāpara-pādābhyāṁ saha-lāṅgūlamacyutaḥ*  
*bhrāmayitvā kapitvāgre prāhiṇodgatajīvitam*  
*sa kapitthair mahd-kdyah patyamanaih papata ha*

**Thereafter, Sri Krsna caught the demon by the hind legs and tail, twirled the demon’s whole body very strongly until the demon was dead, and threw him into the top of a kapittha tree, which then fell down, along with the body of the demon, who had assumed a great form. (SB 10.11.43)**

*taṁ vākṣya vismitā bālāḥ śaśaṁsuḥ sādhusādhviti \|*

**Upon seeing the dead body of the demon, all the cowherd boys exclaimed, “Well done, Krsna! Very good, very good! Thank you.” In the upper planetary system, all the demigods were pleased, and therefore they showered flowers on the Supreme Lord. (SB 10.11.44)**

Now the killing of Bakasura is described. You entered the beak of Baka, Putana’s brother, and in that way killed him. Like a thunderbolt, you divided his body (ahga) like a mountain peak (kuta). Ahga means body according to Halayudha. Kuta means peak according to Amara-kosa.

### 6

*suhṛdbhir api tuṣṭair bhujābhir abhimṛṣṭaḥ*

You were embraced by the arms of your friends after you killed Bakasura. You were then sprinkled with jasmine flowers (sumand) by the devatas. Sumana means jasmine according to Amara-kosa. The next two lines are clear. Sukadeva says.

*gatvā jalāśayābhyāsaṁ pāyayitvā papurjalam \|\|*

*te tatra dadṛśurт bālā mahā-sattvam avasthitam \|*

*kṛṣṇaṁ mahābakagrastaṁ dṛṣṭvā rāmādayo'rbhakāḥ \|*

**When Balarama and the other boys saw that Krsna had been devoured by the gigantic duck, they became almost unconscious, like senses without life. (SB 10.11.49)**

*taṁ tālumūlaṁ pradahantamagnivad gopāla sūnuṁ pitaraṁ jagadguroḥ \| caccharda sadyo'tiruṣākṣataṁ bakastuṇḍena hantuṁ punarabhyapadyata \|\|*

**Krsna, who was the father of Lord Brahma but who was acting as the son of a cowherd man, became like fire, burning the root of the demon’s throat, and the demon Bakasura immediately disgorged him. *tam āpatantaṁ sa nigṛhya tuṇḍayordorbhyāṁ bakaṁ kaṁsasakhaṁ satāṁ gatiḥ \|*

By thus killing the demon, Krsna very much pleased the denizens of heaven. (SB 10.11.51)**

### Text 11

*api sphārāmode pratipada-sudhākoṭi-madhure*

*kṛpā-yaṣṭyā tūrṇaṁ damaya tam amuṁ tarṇaka-pate \|\|11\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O master of the calves! The sweet river of your pastimes, sweet at every moment with abundant nectar, flows in the ancient village but my mind enters to drink from the pit of material poison. Quickly tame, with the stick of mercy, my mind which is like Vatsasura!**

**Комментарий:**

The author prays to Krsna, protector of calves, to control his mind, like Vatsasura, which wanders on the wrong path. O master of the calves! The sweet river of your pastimes flows in the village of Purdnas (ancient village), but my mind enters to drink from the hole of material poison. Quickly tame with the stick of mercy my mind which is like Vatsasura so that it does not drink the poison. The river is fragrant, with your qualities and form. The ancient village is the collection (grama) of Puranas headed by Bhdgavatam.

**praphulla-kusumālī-nāmedaṁ chandaḥ \|**

The meter is praphulla-kusumali. It is described as follows.

*praphullakusumālī satīyamatimodā \|*  
*jasau ragaṇanau cettato guruka yugmam \|\|*

**Praphulla-kusumali is most charming with the following meter: sis ssl Isl sss 11 (ja, sa, ra, na, gu, gu)**

According to this the poem was written.

## atha vatsa-cāraṇādi caritam

**Pastime of herding calves**

### Text 12

*ābhāso’pi śruti-parisaraṁ tāvakīnasya nāmnaḥ*  
*sarpann alpaṁ laghutaram agha-sto\[ma\]-mokṣaṁ karoti \|*  
*naitac citraṁ sakhibhir akhilair antarālaṁ praviṣṭo*  
*yad govinda svayam ayam aghaṁ mokṣayasy ekam eva \|\|12\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Govinda! The abhasa of your name, going just a little to the ear, quickly causes liberation from piles of sin. This is not astonishing because you liberated Agha, entering within him with all your friends.**

**Комментарий:**

Before describing Brahma’s bewilderment, the author summarizes the liberation of Agha. О Govinda! The abhasa of your name, going just a little to the ear, quickly (laghutaram) causes liberation from piles of sin. This is not astonishing. Why is that? You, the Supreme lord (svayam ay am), entering the body with all your friends, liberate one’s sin (agha). Agha means sin and Aghasura.

### 1

*kānanānta-bhukti-kamam ucca-nāda-pūra-dhāma-*  
*śṛṅga-buddhavatsa-pāla-valgu-bāla-cakravāla-*  
*saṅga-labdhatoṣa-jālam agra-nunna-vatsa-pālam*  
*adbhutāti-bhūri-khela-mitra-saṅga-nītavelam*

**Перевод:**

**О lotus-eyed Lord! I take shelter of you who had a desire to picnic in the forest, who become blissful in the company of many charming cowherd boys who had understood your intentions from the horn, the abode of loud sound, who sent off many of the boys to herd the calves in front, who passed time with friends in many astonishing pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

О lotus-eyed Lord! I take shelter (asrayami) of you (bhavantam). The phrases before this are all connected to this statement. The Lord is described.

You had a desire to picnic in the forest. You become blissful (tosa-jalam) in the company of many charming cowherd boys who wanted to play in the forest and eat, who understood from the horn, the house of loud sound. He was most happy with his cowherd friends who had similar desires and had similar qualities and age. He sent off (nunna) many of them to herd the calves. What did he do himself? He passed time (yelam) with friends in many astonishing pastimes. Because of absorption in playing with boys skillful at many types of play, the time to eat passed.

### 2

*aṅga-ruddha-kānanasya śārvarāñcitānanasya*  
*dāvatulya-locanasya pūti-gandhi-mocanasya*  
*megha-bhāga-tānavasya sarpa-rūpa-dānavasya*  
*vīkṣayātivismitena tasya kukṣim āśritena*  
*vatsapāla-maṇḍalena nīta-khedam uccalena*

**Перевод:**

**I take shelter of you who felt pain because of the group of fickle cowherd boys who in astonishment entered the stomach of the demon disguised as a snake which blocked the forest with his body, whose mouth was filled with great darkness, whose eyes were like forest fires, who emitted a putrid smell, who towered as high as a cloud.**

**Комментарий:**

He is further described. He felt pain because of the group of cowherd boys. How did they give him pain? This is described with modifying phrases. They took shelter of (entered) the stomach of the demon disguised as a snake. Why did they enter? They were astonished (ativismitena) on seeing him. Looking at his mouth which was like a cave of an unprecedented mountain, out of astonishment and fickleness of childhood, they entered. Krsna lamented when they entered. The snake is described. He blocked the forest with his body. This means he was very broad. His mouth was filled with great darkness. His eyes were like forest fires. He emitted a putrid smell. They were bewildered by the smell, thinking some animal had been burned by a forest fire. He was not small (atanavasya). He was like a cloud. He was towering.

### 3

*tatra maṅkṣu saṁpraviṣṭam uddhūta-sva-bhakta-riṣṭa-*  
*medhitāṅga-ruddha-vāta-marditāhi-janma-jātam*  
*īkṣayābhījīvitena ḍimbha-sañcayena tena*  
*sārdham etya sat-taḍāga-tīram āpta-bhukti-rāgam*

**Перевод:**

**I take shelter of you who quickly entered the snake and destroyed the boys’ misery, who by expanding your body, stopped its life air, who killed the demon bom as a snake, who desired to eat on the edge of the pond with the boys who were brought to a normal state by your glance.**

**Комментарий:**

Thinking he could not remain outside, giving up his distressed friends, meeting them, he destroyed (uddhuta) his friends’ misery (ristam). Rista means misfortune according to Halayudha. How could he destroy their misfortune without destroying them as well? By expanding his body (edhita) in the snake’s throat, he stopped its life air. Thus, the demon born as a snake was killed, his life air leaving through his split head. Coming to the bank of a clear pond with all the boys, he desired to eat (bhukta-ragam). How could he enjoy eating with the boys who had been afflicted by the touch of the snake’s poison? They were brought to good health by his glance which showered sweetness.

### 4

*eṣu bhoktum udyateṣu bhūri-rāji-santateṣu*  
*madhyasīmni rājamānam arpitebha-ḍimbha-mānam*  
*atra sarva-saṁmukhāsyam ujjihāna-manda-hāsyam*  
*adhvaropapanna-bhakṣam arbhakopabhoga-dakṣam*

**Перевод:**

**I take shelter of you who sat in the center of the many groups of boys eager to eat, who were respected by the friends who were like baby elephants, who faced everyone while gently smiling, whose food was suitable for sacrifices, who were skillful at eating with the boys.**

**Комментарий:**

The eating is described. You were sitting in the center of the many groups of boys eager to eat, like the center of a lotus surrounded by thousands of petals. You were respected by the friends who were like baby elephants. Another version has ardita. Then the meaning is “You defeated the beauty of a baby elephant.” You faced everyone by your acintya-sakti in the gathering of friends. Sukadeva says:

*kṛṣṇasya viśvak pururājimaṇḍalai  ramyānanāḥ phulladṛśo vrajārbhakāḥ \|*  
*sahopaviṣṭā vipine virejuśchadā yathāmbhoruha karṇikāyāḥ*

**Like the whorl of a lotus flower surrounded by its petals and leaves, Krsna sat in the center, encircled by lines of His friends, who all looked very beautiful. Every one of them was trying to look forward toward Krsna, thinking that Krsna might look toward him. In this way they all enjoyed their lunch in the forest. (SB 10.13.8)**

You gently smiled at the boys who were praising the food supplied by their mothers. Indra and others came to see the gathering. Your food was suitable for sacrifices (adhvara). You were skillful at eating (upabhoga) yogurt and rice with the boys.

### 5

*indramukhya-deva-varga-vīkṣamāṇa-keli-sargam*  
*eṣu vatsapālakeṣu bhakṣayatsu bālakeṣu*  
*dūragāmi-vatsa-puñja-saṅgamāya labdha-kuñjam*

**Перевод:**

**I take shelter of you, observed by the host of devatas as you played, who went to a mountain bower to herd all the calves, who had wandered off to an inaccessible place, while the boys continued eating. Being observed by the host of devatas, the cowherd, though invoked by mantras by priests at sacrifices, was present here and hungrily ate the food with the boys.**

**Комментарий:**

His eating pastimes were observed by the astonished devatas.'

He went to a mountain bower to herd all the calves, who had wandered off out of greed for grass while the boys ate. “Do not break your lines. Please eat. I will see the calves and come.”

### 6

*ambujanma-yoninā tad-utsukena vatsa-jātam*  
*arbha-maṇḍalaṁ ca nītam abhram ābhisaṁparīta-*  
*dhītayādhigatya hāsam udvamantam indubhāsam*  
*āśu tat-tad-ātma-rūpa-sanniveśita-svarūpam*

**Перевод:**

**I take shelter of you who became the calves and boys because Brahma was curious to see your powers, who smiled softly like moonlight in full knowledge like the midday sun and who quickly assumed all the forms of the calves and boys.**

**Комментарий:**

You did not see the boys on the bank of the pond or the calves in the bowers. They were taken by Brahma who came because of the drums sounded of the devatas when Agha was liberated, who was astonished by the liberation, and who was curious to see other charming powers. You showed a moon-like smile, understanding by perfect wisdom, clear Jike the midday sun. You smiled, thinking, “He will not understand my powers today, though he is the most knowledgeable of all the meanings of the Vedas.”

“Though the Lord is omniscient, how could he play a joke on Brahma and resolve the issue of the boys stolen by Brahma with all the mothers?” He immediately established himself as the forms of all the calves and boys. Sukadeva says:

*yāvadvatsapavatsakālpakavapuryāvatkarāṅghryādikaṁ yāvadyaṣṭiviṣāṇaveṇudalaśig yāvadvibhūṣāmbaram \| yāvacchīlaguṇābhidhākṛtivayo yāvadvihārādikaṁ sarvaṁ  viṣṇumayaṁ giro'ṅgavadajaḥ sarvasvarūpo babhau*

**By his Vasudeva feature, Krsna simultaneously expanded himself into the exact number of missing cowherd boys and calves, with their exact bodily features, their particular types of hands, legs and other limbs, their sticks, bugles and flutes, their lunch bags, their particular types of dress and ornaments placed in various ways, their names, ages and forms, and their special activities and characteristics. By expanding himself in this way, beautiful Krsna proved the statement samagra-jagad visnumayam: “Lord Visnu is all-pervading.” (SB 10.13.19)**

### 7

*etadīya-mātṛ-toṣa-hetu-śīla-ratna-koṣam*  
*ullasantam atra varṣam edhitānurāga-tarṣam*  
*abjayoni-dṛṣṭa-tattvam adbhutāti-śuddha-sattva-*  
*rūpa-vīkṣaṇāti-matta-gokulānuvṛtt-yatta-*  
*padmaja-stutānubhāvam āhṛtātma-goṣṭha-śāvam*

**Перевод:**

**I take shelter of you, a treasury to make the mothers happy, lasting a whole year, who increased the thirst of the people of Vraja, who made Brahma see the truth, who was then praised by Brahma, favorable to Gokula and intoxicated on seeing the astonishing form of pure sattva, and who continued to eat your meal with your friends.**

**Комментарий:**

What was the purpose in this? You were a treasury to make their mothers happy. Not seeing their sons, they would lament. You made them happy. He also fulfilled their desire to be his mother. How long did this last? He played (ullasantam) for a year in the forests of Vraja (atra). Sukadeva says:

*itthamātmātmanātmānaṁ vatsapālamiṣeṇa saḥ \|*  
*pālayanvatsapo varṣaṁ cikrīḍe vanagoṣṭhayoḥ*

**In this way, Lord Sri Krsna, having himself become the cowherd boys and groups of calves, maintained himself by himself. Thus he continued his pastimes, both in Vrndavana and in the forest, for one year. (SB 10.13.27)**

You increased the thirst of the people of Vraja. Sukadeva says:

*vrajaukasāṁ svatokeṣu snehavallyābdamanvaham \|*  
*śanairniḥsīma vavṛdhe yathā kṛṣṇe tvapūrvavat \|\|*

**Although the inhabitants of Vrajabhumi, the cowherd men and cowherd women, previously had more affection for Krsna than for their own children, now, for one year, their affection for their own sons continuously increased, for Krsna had now become their sons. There was no limit to the increment of their affection for their sons, who were now Krsna. Every day they found new inspiration for loving their children as much as they loved Krsna. (SB 10.13.26)**

You showed Brahma your real form. He was shown the powerful form and the form searching for the boys and calves.

*eko'pi san bahudhā yo vibhāti*

**Though one he manifests as many. (Gopala-tapanl Upanisad)**

Sukadeva says:

*tāvatsarve vatsapālāḥ paśyato'jasya tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*vyadṛśyanta ghanaśyāmāḥ pītakauśeyavāsasaḥ \|\|*

**Then, while Lord Brahma looked on, all the calves and the boys tending them immediately appeared to have complexions the color of bluish rainclouds and to be dressed in yellow silken garments. (SB 10.13.46)**

*satya-jñānānantānanda-mātraika-rasa-mūrtayaḥ*  
*asprsta-bhuri-mahatmya api hy upanisad-drsam*

**The visnu-miirtis all had eternal, unlimited forms, full of knowledge and bliss and existing beyond the influence of time. Their great glory was not even to be touched by the jnanis engaged in studying the Upanisads. (SB 10.13.54)**

*vatsān sakhīniva purā parito vicinvadekaṁ sa pāṇikavalaṁ parameṣṭhy acaṣṭa*

**Lord Brahma saw the child in a family of cowherd men and standing all alone, just as before, with a morsel of food in his hand, searching everywhere for the calves and his cowherd friends. (SB 10.13.61)**

Otherwise, feelings of friendship would slacken. His greatness was then praised by Brahma, who made efforts to be favorable to Gokula and was extremely agitated on seeing your astonishing form surpassing pure knowledge and bliss. Brahma said:

*tad bhūri-bhāgyamiha janma kimapyaṭavyāṁ yadgokule'pi katamāṅdhirajo'bhiṣekam*

**My greatest possible good fortune would be to take any birth whatever in this forest of Gokula and have my head bathed by the dust falling from the lotus feet of any of its residents. (SB 10.14.34)**

He recited prayers starting with (SB 10.14.1. When Brahma returned to his planet, he ate along with the friends who were returned. Sukadeva says:

*tato'nujñāpya bhagavān svabhuvaṁ prāgavasthitān \|*  
*vatsān pulinamāninye yathā pūrvasakhi svakam \|\|*

**After granting his son Brahma permission to leave, the Supreme Personality of Godhead took the calves, who were still where they had been a year earlier, and brought them to the riverbank, where he had been taking his meal and where his cowherd boyfriends remained just as before. (SB 10.14.42)**

*ūcuśca suhṛdaḥ kṛṣṇaṁ svāgataṁ te'tiraṁhasā \|*  
*naiko'pyabhoji kavala ehītaḥ sādhu bhujyatām \|\|*

**The cowherd boyfriends said to Lord Krsna: You have returned so quickly! We have not eaten even one morsel in your absence. Please come here and take your meal without distraction. (SB 10.14.45)**

*tato hasanhṛṣīkeśo'bhyavahṛtya sahārbhakaiḥ \|*  
*darśayaṁścarmājagaraṁ nyavartata vanādbrajam \|\|*

**Then Lord Hrsikesa, smiling, finished his lunch in the company of his cowherd friends. While they were returning from the forest to their homes in Vraja, Lord Krsna showed the cowherd boys the skin of the dead serpent Aghasura. (SB 10.14.46)**

### 8

*ambujākṣa bho bhavantam āśrayāmi kunda-danta*  
*nanda-goṣṭha-bhūri-bhāga cāru-kuntalāgra-bhāga-*  
*śoka-puṣpa-mañjarīka gandha-lubdha-cañcarīka*

**Перевод:**

**О lotus-eyed Krsna, with jasmine teeth! I take shelter of you. О good fortune of Nanda’s village! О Krsna, decorated with asoka buds at the front of your attractive locks! О Krsna with bees greedy for your fragrance!**

О Krsna with teeth like jasmines! О good fortune to Nanda’s village! I offer respects to you always. Describing the beauty of Krsna who plays in the forest, kills enemies and returns to Vraja, the author calls out to him. You are decorated with asoka flowers at the front of your attractive locks of hair. You are surrounded by bees greedy for your fragrance.

### 9

*pīta-keli-puṇḍarīka vaśya-vatsa-maṇḍalīka*  
*bāhu-rājad-aṅgadāya mitra-saṅgha-raṅgadāya*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna with yellow tilaka! О Krsna controlling the calves! О Krsna with shining armlets on your arms! I offer respects to you, with beautiful earrings, whose feet are decorated with anklets, who give joy to all your friends, who tends the attractive calves, who is decorated with mineral pigments.**

**Комментарий:**

You are anointed with yellow tilaka. The meaning is clear for the other two items. Your feet are beautiful with harhsaka ornaments. Hamsaka means foot bracelets according to Amara-kosa. You protect (gupta) the calves. You wear ointments made of minerals.

### 10

*gopa-gotra-vallabhāya yogi-varga-durlabhāya*  
*karṇa-saṅgi-campakāya durgatānukampakāya*  
*tubhyam iddha-kīrti-gātha sarvadā namo’stu nātha*  
*dehi dehi bhakti-leśam apy aśeṣa-pūru-śeṣa \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects continually to you, dear to all the cowherd families, but rare for all yogis, who have campaka flowers in your ears, who gives mercy to persons in difficulty. О Krsna, shining with verses of your fame! О master! О Supreme Lord! Give me a particle of bhakti.**

**Комментарий:**

You are dear to the cowherd families (gotra). Gotra means a group according to Amara-kosa. Sukadeva says:

*barhaprasūnavanadhātuvicitritāṅgaḥ proddāmaveṇudalaśṛṅgaravotsavāḍhyaḥ \|*  
*vatsān gṛṇannanugagītapavitrakīrtirgopīdṛg utsavadṛśiḥ praviveśa goṣṭham \|\|*

**Lord Krsna’s transcendental body was decorated with peacock feathers and flowers and painted with forest minerals, and his bamboo flute loudly and festively resounded. As he called out to his calves by name, his cowherd boyfriends purified the whole world by chanting his glories. Thus Lord Krsna entered the cow pasture of his father, Nanda Maharaja, and the sight of his beauty at once produced a great festival for the eyes of all the cowherd women. (SB 10.14.47)**

Verses of your fame are shining. О master! О Supreme Lord (asesa-purusa)! Give me a particle of bhakti. You gave the bliss of liberation to Agha though he was a demon. Thus, the kaumara pastimes of Krsna have been described.

### Text 13

*yāṁ nirvaktum abhūt prabhur nahi catur-vaktro’pi te mādhurīṁ*  
*tām udghāṭayatādya yadyapi satāṁ hāso mayā svīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*vaiyarthyāya tathāpi deva bhavitā nāyaṁ mamopākramaḥ*  
*sarvānartha-haras tvadīya-bhajanābhāso’pi yad viśrutaḥ \|\|13\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Lord! Even though the wise laugh at me, having only one mouth, who describe your sweetness which even Brahma, with four heads cannot describe, may my attempts to describe your sweetness not be useless, since even a shadow of worshipping you destroys all anarthas at their roots.**

**Комментарий:**

Since you are the subject, my lack of learning is not useless. О lord! Even though the wise laugh at me, having only one mouth, who describe (udghatayata) your sweetness which even Brahma, with four heads (catur-vaktrah) cannot describe, may my attempts to describe your sweetness (иракгатаК) not be useless. Why? It is said that even a shadow of worshipping you destroys all anarthas, all ignorance at its root.

*sāṁkelyaṁ pārihāsyaṁ vā stobham helanam eva va*  
*vaikuntha-nama-grahanam asesagha-haram viduh*

**Chanting the name of the Lord while indicating someone else or while joking in a friendly manner, or chanting the Lord’s name in order to fill up space while chanting verses or chanting with neglect destroys unlimited sins and desires. (SB 6.2.14)**

**aśoka-puṣpa-mañjarī-chandaḥ \|**

The meter is asoka-puspa-manjari. It is a type of dandaka.

*yatra dṛśyate guroḥ paro laghuḥ kramātsa kabhyate budhair aśoka-puṣpa-mañjarī*

## atha tālavana-caritam

**Pastime at Talavana**

### Text 14

*sa pātu māṁ yas tṛṇa-rāja-rājī-*  
*phalair virājan vraja-rāja-putraḥ \|*  
*sukhāni cakrāṅka-karaḥ sakhīnāṁ*  
*cakrīvatāṁ cakram udasya cakre \|\|14\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the shining son of Nanda, who holds a cakra in his hand, who made his friends happy with the fruit from the tala tree, who killed a group of donkey demons, protect me.**

**Комментарий:**

Pauganda pastimes should be described. This verse suggests the killing of Dhenuka which should be described. May the son of Nanda protect me. He is described.

He gave happiness to his friends by the fruits of the grove of tala trees. Trna-raja means tala tree according to Amara-kosa. Though at first his friends did not eat the fruit, later on, they got great happiness by playing there and eating the fruit. He had a cakra in his hand. What did he do? He killed (udasya) the group of donkeys like Dhenuka (cakrivatam). Cakrivat means a donkey according to Amara-kosa.

### 1

*jaya dhenu-lakṣa-śata-gupti-dakṣavana-maṇḍalāntam anusṛtya kāntam*  
*upalabdha-harṣa kṛta-keli-varṣa baladeva-gīta-ghana-śākhi-śīta-*  
*vanarāji-rūpa paśupāla-bhūpa kṛta-pakṣi-vāra-cariktānukāra-*  
*dhṛta-mitra-raṅga rasa-valgad-aṅga*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, expert at protecting millions of cows! Manifest your excellence. О Krsna, joyful at the edge of the beautiful forest! О Krsna, performer of a shower of pastimes! О Krsna, who praised the cool, dense forest to please Balarama! О king of the cowherds! О Krsna, blissful with friends by imitating the actions of birds! О Krsna, whose limbs became attractive with the bliss of rasa!**

**Комментарий:**

О lord! May you manifest excellence (jaya). You are expert at protecting millions of cows. You become joyful at the edge of the beautiful forest. You performed a shower of pastimes. You have a form in forests cool with dense trees, which you praise to please Balarama. The Lord says:

*aho amī devavarāmarārcitaṁ pādāmbujaṁ te sumanaḥphalārhaṇam \| namantyupādāya śikhābhirātmanastamopahatyai tarujanma yatkṛtam \|\|*

**О greatest of Lords, just see how these trees are bowing their heads at your lotus feet, which are worshipable by the immortal demigods. The trees are offering you their fruits and flowers to eradicate the dark ignorance that has caused their birth as trees. (SB 10.15.5)**

О king of the cowherds! You became blissful with friends by imitating the actions of birds such as swans, peacocks, parrots and cranes. Your limbs became attractive with the bliss of rasa.

### 2

*puru-malla-yuddha paṭu-bāhu-ruddha-bala-durdurūḍha-nija-mitra-kūṭa yamunopakūla-taru-rāji-mūla-*  
*pada-bhadra-sena-kṛta-dugdha-phena-paṭalānukalpa-nava-puṣpa-talpa-*  
*vara-madhya-supta suhṛdāli-gupta*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who defeated your friends of unrestricted strength by your two arms expert at intense wrestling! О Krsna, who took rest on a fresh flower bed, white as foam, made by Bhadrasena, under the trees on the bank of the Yamuna! О Krsna, protected there by your friends!**

**Комментарий:**

You defeated your group of friends unrestricted in strength by your two arms expert at intense wrestling. Durduriidha means very strong. You took rest on a fresh flower bed, white as foam, made by Bhadrasena under the trees on the bank of the Yamuna. You were protected there by your friends.

### 3

*vṛṣabhānu-baddha-mṛdu-rāga-naddha-kala-gīta-hṛṣṭa subalābhimṛṣṭa kṛta-padmaninda-caraṇāravinda*  
*viṭapāvatāna-parivījyamāna*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, joyful on hearing the delicate song with a gentle raga concerning your pastimes produced by Vrsabha! О Krsna, whose lotus feet which deride the lotus were massaged by Subala! О Krsna, fanned by small branches of flowering asoka trees!**

**Комментарий:**

You became joyful on hearing the delicate song concerning your pastimes produced by Vrsabha with a gentle raga. Your lotus feet which deride the lotus were massaged by Subala. You were fanned by small branches of flowering asoka trees. Sukadeva says:

*kvacicca kalahaṁsānāmanukūjati kūjitam \|*  
*abhinṛtyati nṛtyantaṁ barhiṇaṁ hāsayankvacit \|\|*

**Sometimes Lord Krsna would imitate the cooing of swans. Sometimes he vigorously imitated the dancing of a peacock, making his cowherd boyfriends laugh. (SB 10.15.11)**

*cakorakrauñcacakrāhvabhāradvājāṁśca barhiṇaḥ \|*  
*anurauti sma sattvānāṁ bhītabahyāghrasiṁhayoḥ \|\|*

**Sometimes he would cry out in imitation of birds such as the cakoras, krauncas, cakrahvas, bharadvajas and peacocks, and sometimes He would run away with the smaller animals in mock fear of lions and tigers. (SB 10.15.13)**

*nṛtyato gāyataḥ kvāpi valgato yuddhyato mithaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītahastau gopālānhasantau praśaśaṁsatuḥ \|\|*

**Sometimes, as the cowherd boys danced, sang, moved about and playfully fought with each other, Krsna and Balarama, standing nearby hand in hand, would glorify their friends’ activities and laugh. (SB 10.15.15)**

*kvacitpallavatalpeṣu niyuddhaśramakarśitaḥ \|*  
*vṛkṣamūlāśrayaḥ śete gopotsaṅgopabarhaṇaḥ \|\|*

**Sometimes Lord Krsna grew tired from fighting and lay down at the base of a tree, resting upon a bed made of soft twigs and buds and using the lap of a cowherd friend as his pillow. (SB 10.15.16)**

*pādasaṁvāhanaṁ cakruḥ kecittasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*apare hatapāpmāno vyajanaiḥ samabījayan \|\|*

**Some of the cowherd boys, who were all great souls, would then massage his lotus feet, and others, qualified by being free of all sin, would expertly fan the Supreme Lord. (SB 10.15.17)**

*anye tadanurūpāṇi manojñāni mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*gāyanti sma mahārāja snehaklinnadhiyaḥ śanaiḥ \|\|*

**My dear King, other boys would sing enchanting songs appropriate to the occasion, and their hearts would melt out of love for the Lord. (SB 10.15.18)**

### 4

*paripakva-tāla-phala-lubdha-bāla-*  
*kala-vākya-rūḍha-hasitopagūḍha-mukhatārakeśa dhṛta-vīra-veśa*  
*ghana-tuṅga-tāla-vipināntarālam upalabdha-rāma-sahitātma-dhāma-*  
*dhuta-ghūrṇad-agra-tṛṇa-rāṭ-samagra-phala-vṛnda-pāta-kṛta-harṣa-jāta*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, whose face was embraced by a smile because of the soft words of the boys greedy for the ripe tala fruit! О Krsna, who assumed the stance of a warrior! О Krsna who approached the center of the forest dense with huge tala trees! О Krsna, happy when the fruits of the tala trees all fell after you shook them with strength, along with Balarama!**

**Комментарий:**

After describing various types of play the author describes the tala forest.

Your face was embraced by a smile which appeared because of the soft words of the boys greedy for the ripe tala fruit. He smiled to hint, “O friend! Today these fruits are not tasty. But the rasa of fighting will be tasty!” He assumed the stance of a warrior to kill the demon. You came to the center of the forest dense with huge tala trees. You were happy when the fruits of the tala trees all fell after you shook the first ones with strength along with Balarama.

### 5

*phala-śabda-ruṣṭa-khara-rūpa-duṣṭa-hara-kāma-pāla-kṛta-harṣa-māla*  
*turagāri-kāla khara-cakravāla-tṛṇa-vīti-hotra ramitātma-gotra*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who made Balarama happy by allowing him to kill the demon having a donkey form, who was angry on hearing the sound of the fruit fall! О Krsna, killer of the horse demon! О Krsna, fire for the host of grass-like donkeys! О Krsna, pleasing to your friends!**

**Комментарий:**

You made Balarama (kamapdla) happy by allowing him to kill the demon with donkey form who was angry on hearing the sound of the fruit fall. О killer of the horse demon (turagdri)! It is not astonishing that you kill the donkey demon since you killed the horse demon. You are fire (viti-hotra) for the host of donkeys, who rushed there angrily when their friend had been killed. You pleased your friends (gotra) by killing Dhenuka.

Sukadeva says:

*śrīdāmā nāma gopālo rāmakeśavayoḥ sakhā \|*  
*subalastokakṛṣṇādyā gopāḥ premṇedama bruvan \|\|*

**Once, some of the cowherd boys—Sridama, the very close friend of Rama and Krsna, along with Subala, Stokakrsna and others—lovingly spoke the following words. (SB 10.15.20)**

*rāma rāma mahābāho kṛṣṇa duṣṭanibarhaṇa \|*  
*ito'vidūre sumahadvanaṁ tālālisaṁkulam \|\|*

**\[The cowherd boys said:\] O Rama, Rama, mighty-armed one! O Krsna, destroyer of the miscreants! Not far from here is a very great forest filled with rows of palm trees. (SB 10.15.21)**

*phalāni tatra bhūrīṇi patanti patitāni ca \|*  
*santi kiṁtvavaruddhāni dhenukena durātmanā \|\|*

**In that Talavana forest many fruits are falling from the trees, and many are already lying on the ground. But all the fruits are being guarded by the evil Dhenuka. (SB 10.15.22)**

*prayaccha tāni naḥ kṛṣṇa gandhalobhitacetasām \|*  
*vāñchāsti mahatī rāma gamyatāṁ yadi rocate \|\|*

**O Krsna! Please get those fruits for us. Our minds are so attracted by their aroma! Dear Balarama, our desire to have those fruits is very great. If you think it’s a good idea, let’s go to that Tala forest. (SB 10.15.26)**

*balaḥ praviśya bāhubhyāṁ tālānsaṁparikampayan \|*  
*phalāni pātayāmāsa mataṅgaja ivaujasā \|\|*

**Lord Balarama entered the Tala forest first. Then with his two arms He began forcefully shaking the trees with the power of a maddened elephant, causing the tala fruits to fall to the ground. (SB 10.15.28)**

*phalānāṁ patatāṁ śabdaṁ niśamyāsurarāsabhaḥ \|*  
*abhyadhāvatkṣititalaṁ sanagaṁ parikampayan \|\|*

**Hearing the sound of the falling fruits, the ass demon Dhenuka ran forward to attack, making the earth and trees tremble. (SB 10.15.29)**

*sametya tarasā pratyagdvābhyāṁ padbhyāṁ balaṁ balī \|*  
*nihatyorasi kāśabdaṁ muñcanparyasaratkhalaḥ \|\|*

**The powerful demon rushed up to Lord Baladeva and sharply struck the Lord’s chest with the hooves of his hind legs. Then Dhenuka began to run about, braying loudly. (SB 10.15.30)**

*sa taṁ gṛhītvā prapadorghrāmayitvaikapāṇinā \|*  
*cikṣepa tṛṇarājāgre bhrāmaṇatyakta jīvitam \|\|*

**Lord Balarama seized Dhenuka by his hooves, whirled him about with one hand and threw him into the top of a palm tree. The violent wheeling motion killed the demon. (SB 10.15.32)**

*tataḥ kṛṣṇaṁ ca rāmaṁ ca jñātayo dhenukasya ye \|*
