*koṣṭāro'bhyadravansarve saṁrabdhā hata-bāndhavāḥ \|\|*

**The other ass demons, close friends of Dhenukasura, were enraged upon seeing his death, and thus they all immediately ran to attack Krsna and Balarama. (SB 10.15.36)**

*evaṁ  cāpatataḥ kṛṣṇo rāmaśca nṛpalīlayā \| gṛhītapaścācaraṇānprāhiṇottṛṇarājiṣu \|\|*

**О King, as the demons attacked, Krsna and Balarama easily seized them one after another by their hind legs and threw them all into the tops of the palm trees. (SB 10.15.37)**

*tayostadadbhutaṁ karma niśamya vibudhādayaḥ \|*  
*mumucuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi cakrurvādyāni tuṣṭuvuḥ \|\|*

**Hearing of this magnificent feat of the two brothers, the demigods and other elevated living beings rained down flowers and offered music and prayers in glorification. (SB 10.15.39)**

### 6

*hata-dhenukādya vibudhābhivādya tṛṇa-rāja-bhaṅga-bhara-jāta-raṅga*  
*ripu-varga-bhīda mayi saṁprasīda \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О killer of Dhenuka! О Krsna, praised by the devatas! О Krsna, producing great joy by breaking the tala trees! О killer of many enemies! Be merciful to me.**

**Комментарий:**

О killer of Dhenuka! О killer (bhida) of many enemies! Kamsa became terrified with the killing of Dhenuka. Be merciful to me.

### Text 15

*pīnāpīna-bharodgatair anudinaṁ yāḥ kṣīra-pūrair balād*  
*ambhojākṣa viḍambayanti niviḍaṁ kṣīrāmbudhair vaibhavam \|*  
*tāsāṁ rājata-gaṇḍa-śaila-paṭalī-pāṇḍu-tviṣāṁ maṇḍalaṁ*  
*dhenūnāṁ paripālayantam aṭavī-kuñje bhavantaṁ bhaje \|\|15\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О lotus-eyed Krsna! I worship you, who play in the forest bowers, who herd the groups of cows, which deride the wealth of milk ocean by the mass of milk coming from their full udders and which are as white as a host of silver Ganda-saila mountains.**

**Комментарий:**

The author describes Krsna herding the cows with his friends after killing Dhenuka and his followers. О lotus-eyed Krsna! I worship you, playing in the forest bowers. Krsna is described. You herd the groups of cows very white like a host of silver Ganda-saila mountains. The cows are further described. They at all times (anudinam) deride the wealth of milk ocean by the mass of milk coming from their full udders. Apina means udder according to Amara-kosa. Brahma samhita says:

*sa yatra kṣīrābdhiḥ sarati surabhībhyaśca sumahān*

**I worship Goloka, pure and uncontaminated, where extensive oceans of milk flow from the cows. (Brahma-samhita 5.56)**

**kala-gīta-nāma chandaḥ \|**

The meter is kala-gita. It is described as follows.

*sagaṇaṁ nidhāya jagaṇaṁ vidhāya \|*  
*kavisaukhyadhāma kalagītanāma \|\|*

**The combination of sa and ja (ssl sis) the abode of happiness for poets is called kala-gita.**

According to this definition the poem has been written. Another name for the meter is madhubhara.

## atha kāliya-damanam

**Subduing Kaliya**

### Text 16

*kāliyasya phaṇa-ratna-kuṭṭimaṁ*  
*kuṭṭayan pada-saroja-ghaṭṭanaiḥ \|*  
*maṅgalāni vitanotu tāṇḍave*  
*paṇḍitas tava śikhaṇḍa-śekharaḥ \|\|16\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Wearing a peacock feather on his head, skilled at the art of southern dancing, pounding Kaliya’s jeweled hood with blows from his lotus feet, may he spread auspiciousness to you.**

**Комментарий:**

He presents this verse to introduce the subduing of Kaliya. An alternative is Kaliya. His hood was an arena of jewels. Kuttimam means earth according to Amara-kosa. Krsna pained (kuttayan) his hood with blows from his lotus feet. Krsna had a peacock feather on his head. May he spread auspiciousness to you. He was skilled at southern style of dancing (.tandave).

### 1

*jagad-vināśi saṅgamaṁ garutmatā gajaṅgamaṁ*  
*bhujaṅga-maṇḍalī-padaṁ pataṅga-nandinī-hradaṁ*  
*viṣāgni-dagdha-nīrajaṁ nirīkṣya tasya tīrajaṁ*  
*mudādhiruhya darpataḥ kadambam ugra-sarpataḥ*  
*kṣaṇādaśaṅkitastataḥ patanguruḥ samantataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the lake of the Yamuna, the abode of many snakes, with lotuses burned by poison, where Garuda could not come for fish, the supporter of the universe, joyfully climbed a tree with confidence, and, unafraid of Kaliya, jumped from the tree.**

**Комментарий:**

О master! О ocean of mercy! О ocean of jewels of pastimes! О destroyer of suffering to the surrendered, drying up the rivers of suffering of the devotee! О eternal one! May you manifest your excellence (jaya). Be merciful to me! The words previously to this are connected to these words in the last line of the poem.

Seeing the lake of the Yamuna, its lotuses burned by poison, he proudly and joyfully climbed a kadamba which grew on the bank of the lake but was unburned because of the sprinkling of drops of nectar brought by Garuda. Without fear of the fierce snake, supporting the universe (guruh) he jumped from the kadamba (tatah). The lake was a confluence for destroying the universe, since it was filled with snakes. Garuda, being cursed by Saubhari, could not go there for fish. It was the abode of many snakes.

### 2

*payo vikīrṇavān alaṁ parijvalad-viṣānalaṁ*  
*dhanuḥ-śate satāṁ gatir bhujoddhatāmbu-saṁhatiḥ*  
*karāla-dṛṣṭi-dāruṇaiḥ phaṇair maṇi-prabhāruṇair*  
*yutena loka-dāhinā vinadya kāliyāhinā*  
*ruṣodbhaṭena veṣṭitaḥ prapanna-bāla-cesṭitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**The goal of the devotees, Krsna, splashed water which was burning with the fire of poison, onto the bank, and disturbed the water with his powerful arms. Shouting, appearing like an innocent child, he was surrounded by the angry snake which burned the worlds, with hoods red with effulgent gems and cruel, gaping eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

He splashed water everywhere on the bank (dhanuh-sate). The water was burning with the fire of poison. He was the goal of the devotes. He produced waves with the force of his arms. Shouting, he was surrounded by Kaliya, with hoods, red from effulgent gems and cruel, gaping eyes. Karala means wide open according to Halayudha. He burned the worlds by his fiery poison. He was full of intense anger. Krsna appeared like an innocent child.

*taṁ caṇḍavegaviṣavīryamavekṣya tena duṣṭāṁ nadīṁ ca khalasaṁyamanāvatāraḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇaḥ kadambam adhiruhya tato'tituṅgamāsphoṭya gāḍharaśano nyapatad viṣode \|\|*

**Lord Krsna saw how the Kaliya serpent had polluted the Yamuna River with his terribly powerful poison. Since Krsna had descended from the spiritual world specifically to subdue envious demons, the Lord immediately climbed to the top of a very high kadamba tree and prepared himself for battle. He tightened his belt, slapped his arms and then jumped into the poisonous water. (SB 10.16.6)**

*sarpahradaḥ puruṣasāranipātavegasaṁkṣobhitoragaviṣocchvasitāmburāśiḥ \| paryakpluto viṣakaṣāyavibhīṣaṇormirdhāvandhanuḥśatamanantavalasya kiṁ tat \|\|*

**When the Supreme Personality of Godhead landed in the serpent’s lake, the snakes there became extremely agitated and began breathing heavily, further polluting it with volumes of poison. The force of the Lord’s entrance into the lake caused it to overflow on all sides, and poisonous, fearsome waves flooded the surrounding lands up to a distance of one hundred bow-lengths. This is not at all amazing, however, for the Supreme Lord possesses infinite strength. (SB 10.16.7)**

*tasya hṛde viharato bhujadaṇḍaghūrṇavārghoṣamaṅga varavāraṇavikramasya \|*  
*āśrutya tatvasadanābhibhavaṁ nirīkṣya cakṣuḥśravāḥ samasarat tad amṛṣyamāṇaḥ \|\|*

**Krsna began sporting in Kaliya’s lake like a lordly elephant—swirling his mighty arms and making the water resound in various ways. When Kaliya heard these sounds, he understood that someone was trespassing in his lake. The serpent could not tolerate this and immediately came forward. (SB 10.16.8)**

### 3

*tato’dbhutāvalokataḥ sametya tīvra-śokatas*  
*tanu-skhalat-paṭālibhir mahārta-nāda-śālibhir*  
*balopadeśa-sāratas tadā hradāvatārataḥ*  
*śanair nivṛtta-lālasair muhur vyathā-kulālasaiḥ*  
*sadāra-vṛddha-bālakaiḥ samasta-dhenu-pālakair*  
*vilokitaḥ smitānanaḥ kṛtoragāvamānanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You were seen with intense lamentation by all the cowherd people, young and old with their wives, who had arrived there on seeing the unusual omens, stumbling and wailing in great pain, withering because of mental anguish. They gave up entering the pond on hearing Balarama’s advice. You smiled and showed contempt for the snake.**

**Комментарий:**

You were seen (vilokya) with intense lamentation by all the cowherds old and young with their wives, who had arrived (sametya') at the shore of the lake, because of seeing the omens like earthquakes and comets, and left eyes quivering, indicating a fearful event (adbhutavlokatah). They saw you bound by Kaliya and having no movement. They stumbled with their bodies (tanu-skhalat-patdlibhir). This means they ran forward. They shouted in great pain. “Since Krsna was their very life, why did they not enter the lake?” They gradually gave up the idea (nivrtta-lalasaih) of going into the lake (hradavataratah) on attaining strength when Balarama spoke (balopadesa-saratah). “Krsna will tame the snake and quickly come out.” They lost their effulgence because of their suffering (vyathd-kulalasaih). Sukadeva says:

*kṛṣṇa-prāṇānnirviśato nandādīnvīkṣya taṁ hradam \|*  
*pratyaṣedhatsa bhagavānrāmaḥ kṛṣṇānubhāvavit \|\|*

**Lord Balarama then saw that Nanda Maharaja and the other cowherd men, who had dedicated their very lives to Krsna, were beginning to enter the serpent’s lake. As the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Balarama fully knew Lord Krsna’s actual power, and therefore he restrained them. (SB 10.16.22)**

Tasting the supreme prema of his dear Vraja devotees he smiled to give them bliss (smitananah). And he disrespected the snake.

### 4

*praṇunna-bhoga-rodhanaḥ suhṛd-gaṇādhiśodhanaḥ*  
*śritāṇḍajendra-vibhramaḥ sphurat-karāla-vikramaḥ*  
*sva-mūrdha-ratna-piñjaraṁ nirasya nāga-kuñjaraṁ*  
*plutena tasya raṅgataḥ phaṇāṅgaṇeṣu saṅgataḥ*  
*praṇīta-divya-nartanaḥ kṛtotsavānuvartanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You released yourself from the snake’s coils and gave relief to your friends. Beautiful as Garuda, you manifested ferocious valor. Deriding the chief snake, whose heads glowed with jewels, you jumped upon his hood in glee and began dancing, giving joy to all again.**

**Комментарий:**

You released yourself from his coils by shaking your body (pranunnd). You relieved your friends of their mental anguish (adhi-sodhanah). Adhi means mental pain according to Amara-kosa. “That would not be enough to relieve them of pain.” He displayed the beauty (vibhramah) of Garuda. He displayed great valor. He derided (nirasya) the chief snake, yellowish (pinjard) with jewels on his head. You attained (sangatah) the hoods of the chief snake by jumping in joy (plutena rangatah) and danced on them.

*evaṁ paribhramahataujasamunnatāṁsamānamy tatpṛthuśiraḥsvadhirūḍha ādyaḥ \|*  
*tanmūrdharatnanikaraspa rśatitāmrapādāmbujo'khilakalādi gurur nanarta \|\|*

**Having severely depleted the serpent’s strength with his relentless circling, Sri Krsna, the origin of everything, pushed down Kaliya’s raised shoulders and mounted his broad serpentine heads. Thus Lord Sri Krsna, the original master of all fine arts, began to dance, his lotus feet deeply reddened by the touch of the numerous jewels upon the serpent’s heads. (SB 10.16.26)**

He again gave everyone bliss as previously (anuvartanah).

### 5

*prasūna-vṛnda-varṣibhiḥ khalārdanena harṣibhiḥ*  
*sapadma-bhū-pinākibhir nabhasy analpa-nākibhiḥ*  
*stuto vicitra-bālakaḥ sulāsyataś ca lālakaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You were praised by devatas, Laksmi, Brahma and Siva who were overjoyed at the affliction of the demon. They showered clouds of flowers. You were an amazing child, with locks swaying from the fine dancing.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna is further described. He was praised by many devatas (nakibhih) situated in the sky, along with Laksmi, Brahma and Siva, who showered many flowers, who were joyful at his afflicting the wicked snake. You were an amazing child. Your hair was moving about because of the fine dancing (sulasyatah). Aidka means locks according to Amara-kosa.

### 6

*sakhi svabālya-cañcalaṁ paribhramad-dṛg-añcalaṁ*  
*suśobhanāṅga-hārakaṁ bhujaṅga-darpa-dārakaṁ*  
*praṇīta-divya-hastakaṁ vilāsa-kampi-mastakaṁ*  
*vikāsi-hāsya-korakaṁ vilola-kaṇṭha-ḍorakaṁ*  
*rasād amuṁ samagrataḥ sphuṭaṁ naṭantam agrataḥ*  
*sutaṁ vilokayādhunā tvam īkṣaṇena sādhunā*  
*vrajeśvarīti yoṣitāṁ giraṁ pramoda-ghoṣitāṁ*  
*niśamya labdha-modayā vilokito yaśodayā*

**Перевод:**

**The women shouted in joy, “O Yasoda! Look with affection intently at your son, who displays fickleness of childhood, who glances around with the edge of his eye, whose limbs are attractive with fine dancing, who curbs the snake’s pride, who moves his hands gracefully, who shakes his head playfully, who smiles like a blossoming flower, who wears a cord around his neck, who clearly dances with all his limbs in front of us.” Yasoda gazed upon you with bliss.**

**Комментарий:**

He is further described. “O my friend Yasoda! Out of affection, look at your son intently (sadhuna iksanena) with fine gaze.” Hearing the words of the cowherds’ wives, shouted with joy, you were seen by Yasoda, who became joyful. Her son is described by ten phrases with clear meaning. Of these, his limbs by movements of dancing became beautiful (atiga-harah). He moves his hands attractively when dancing (hastakam). Doraka is a cord for a pendant. Samagratah means all his limbs.

### 7

*khala-pramardane kharaḥ śriyā hy anaṅga-śekharaḥ*  
*phaṇa-vraje muhuḥ plutaḥ phaṇāvatī-gaṇaiḥ stutas*  
*tadāti-dakṣiṇāśayaḥ phaṇīśvare kṛtābhayaḥ*  
*kṣaṇād amūbhir arcitaḥ parārdhya-gandha-carcitaḥ*  
*śruti-prasakta-kairavaḥ phaṇi-vrajeṣv abhairavaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You sharply punished the rascal. You were the crest jewel of Cupid by your beauty. Continuously you jumped on Kaliya’s many hoods. You were praised by Kaliya’s wives. Then with sincere heart, you dissipated Kaliya’s fear and were worshipped joyfully by his wives. They anointed you with fine scents and put lotuses on your ears. You became pleased with the snakes.**

**Комментарий:**

He is further described. Ten items are clear in meaning. Kharah means sharp. By your beauty you are the head ornament of Cupid. You constantly jumped from one hood to another. You were praised by Kaliya’s wives (phanavati-ganaih)

“O master! О Supreme Lord! Supreme creator! Let go of the snake. Give to your servants our husband’s good fortune.” You were very sincere in heart (daksinasayah). You were worshipped joyfully (ksanat) by the wives (amiibhih). You were anointed with fine scents by them. You became pleased (abhairavah) with the snakes. Bhairava means fierce according to Halayudha. Sukadeva says:

*itthaṁ sa nāgapatnībhirbhagavānsamabhiṣṭutaḥ \|*  
*mūrcchitaṁ bhagnaśirasaṁ visasarjāṅghrikuṭṭanaiḥ \|\|*

**Thus praised by the Naga-patnis, the Supreme Personality of Godhead released the serpent Kaliya, who had fallen unconscious, his heads battered by the striking of the Lord’s lotus feet. (SB 10.16.54)**

*mukto bhagavata rajan krsnenadbhuta-karmanataṁ pūjayāmāsa tadā nāgapatnyaśca sādaram \|\|*

**My dear King, having been released by Lord Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose activities are wonderful, Kaliya joined his wives in worshiping him with great joy and reverence. (SB 10.16.64)**

*divyāmbarasradmaṇibhiḥ parārdhyairapi bhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*divyagandhānulepaiśca mahatyotpalamālayā \|\|*

**Kaliya worshiped the Lord of the universe by offering him fine garments, along with necklaces, jewels and other valuable ornaments, wonderful scents and ointments, and a large garland of lotus flowers. (SB 10.16.65)**

*tataḥ prīto'bhyanujñātaḥ parikramyābhivandya tam \|*  
*sakalatrasuhṛtputro dvīpamabdherjagāma ha \|\|*

**Receiving the Lord’s permission to leave, Kaliya circumambulated him and offered him obeisances. Then, taking his wives, friends and children, he went to his island in the sea. (SB 10.16.66)**

*tadaiva sāmṛtajalā yamunā nirviṣābhavat*

**The very moment Kaliya left, the Yamuna was immediately restored to her original condition, free from poison and full of nectarean water. (SB 10.16.67)**

### 8

*sva-bandhu-vṛnda-nandanaḥ kṛtārya-pāda-vandanaḥ*  
*praharṣato’vilambayā vicumbitas tvam ambayā*  
*jaya prabho kṛpā-nidhe vilāsa-ratna-vāridhe*  
*natārti-pūra-śātana prasīda me sanātana \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You gave joy to your friends and offered respects to the feet of the elders. You were immediately kissed by your mother in joy. О master! О ocean of mercy! О ocean of jewels of pastimes! О destroyer of suffering to the surrendered, drying up the rivers of suffering of the devotee! О eternal one! May you manifest your excellence!**

**Комментарий:**

You offered respects to the feet of Nanda and Balarama and others when they offered blessings. Yasoda immediately placed you on her lap in joy and kissed you. May you manifest your excellence (jaya)!

### Text 17

*kāmaṁ dāmodara mama manaḥ-pannagaḥ pīna-bhogo*  
*duṣṭāśībhiḥ kuṭila-valanaiḥ kṣobhayaty eṣa lokam \|*  
*tad-vikrāntas tvam udita-pada-dvandva-paṅkeruhāṅkaṁ*  
*kurvan darvīkara-damana he tāṇḍavair daṇḍayāmum \|\|17\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Damodara! О subduer of Kaliya! The snake of my mind, fat with enjoyment, with poisonous fangs, and crooked movements, disturbs the world. Therefore, you who are very strong, imprint my mind with your lotus feet and subdue it by dancing.**

**Комментарий:**

The author prays to Krsna, subduer of the snake, that the snake in his heart be subdued. О Damodara! О subduer of Kaliya (darvikara)\\ The snake of my mind disturbs the world. The snake is described. It has a fat body (pina-bhogah), enjoying form, taste, etc., fit for kings. It disturbs the world by poison (dusta) fangs (asibhih) of desires for material enjoyment and crooked movements (kutila-valanaih)- This is rUpaka alankara with succession of angas of rupaka. Therefore (tat), you who are very strong (vikrantah), imprint my mind with your lotus feet and subdue it by dancing.

Since you subdued Kaliya, will you subdue my mind, like an uncontrollable snake? Show your feet to my heart today and remove first the wicked desires.

**anaṅga-śekhara-cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is ananga-sekhara.

*laghu gurur nijecchayā yadā niveśyate tadeṣa daṇḍako bhavaty anaṅga-śekharaḥ*

**The dandaka becomes ananga-sekhara when short and long syllables are places according to one’s desire, (slslslsl slslslsl) (Vrrta-ratnakara)**

## atha bhāṇḍīra-krīḍanādi

**Playing at Bhandira etc.**

### Text 18

*bhāṇḍīrasya taṭānte tarukhaṇḍā-khaṇḍalasya raṇa-śauṇḍa \|*  
*sakhi-maṇḍalāni bāḍhaṁ vikrīḍaya puṇḍarīkākṣa \|\|18\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Krsna, skillful at fighting! Make your friends play intensely at the Bhandira banyan tree, king of trees.**

**Комментарий:**

Playing at Bhandira should be described. The word adi indicates killing Pralamba and swallowing the forest fire. O Krsna, skillful at fighting (rana-saunda)!

Make your friends play intensely at the Bhandira banyan tree. It is the king of all trees. It is very broad, thick with leaves, touches the sky and has gems at its base. Alliteration of ta-varga indicates courage.

### 1

*suhṛd-āvali-parivītaḥ śruti-hara-muralī-gītaḥ*  
*surabhī-vīthy-anusārī vara-pītāmbara-dhārī*  
*pīnojjvala-bhuja-daṇḍaḥ śirasi sphurita-śikhaṇḍaḥ*  
*śaśi-khaṇḍābha-lalāṭaḥ pīvara-hṛdaya-kapāṭaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You are surrounded by friends. Your flute song attracts the ears. You follow the path of the cows. You wear excellent yellow cloth. You have thick, shining arms. You have a peacock feather trembling on your head. Your forehead is like the crescent moon. Your broad chest is like a door panel.**

**Комментарий:**

The pastime is now described. O ocean of rasa of the people of Gokula! O friend of the miserable! You (tvam), please manifest your excellence (jaya). The words are related to the last line of the poem, modifying tvam. The first eight phrases are clear in meaning.

### 2

*khara-mihirātapa-vāse prasaraty api śuci-māse*  
*dhṛta-madhu-lakṣmī-bhāraṁ parihṛta-dāva-vikāraṁ*  
*dhenu-manohara-śādaṁ pika-kṛta-pañcama-nādaṁ*  
*ṣaḍ-jodgāri-mayūraṁ visṛmara-saurabha-pūraṁ*  
*vikasita-cāru-śirīṣaṁ sphuṭa-mallī-nibirīṣaṁ*  
*vṛndāvanam atihṛṣṭaḥ sabalaḥ svayam abhiviṣṭaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With Balarama, you joyfully enter Vrndavana which is filled with spring during Jyestha month with harsh rays of the sun, which is devoid of forest fires, filled with green grass attractive to cows, filled with the fifth note sung by the cuckoo and the first note sung by the peacock, which is filled with unfading fragrance of attractive blossoming sirisa flowers and thickets of blossoming jasmines.**

**Комментарий:**

You joyfully enter Vrndavana with Balarama. Vrndavana is described in the preceding lines. It has the qualities of spring (madhu) when Jyestha month (suci-mase) starts with harsh rays of the sun (mihiratapa).

*grīṣmo nāmartur abhavan nāti-preyāñ śarīriṇām \|*

**This season is not very pleasing to embodied souls. (SB 10.18.2)**

*sa ca vṛndāvana-guṇair vasanta iva lakṣitaḥ*  
*yatraste bhagavan saksad ramena saha kesavah*

**Nevertheless, because the Supreme Personality of Godhead was personally staying in Vrndavana along with Balarama, summer manifested the qualities of spring. (SB 10.18.3)**

*vanaṁ kusumitaṁ śrīmannadaccitramṛgadvijam \|*  
*gāyanmayūrabhramaraṁ kūjat-kokila-sārasam \|\|*

**Flowers beautifully decorated the forest of Vrndavana, and many varieties of animals and birds filled it with sound. The peacocks and bees sang, and the cuckoos and cranes cooed. (SB 10.18.7)**

It is without forest fires (dava-vikaram). It is attractive to the cows with green grass (sadam) always. Sada means grass according to Haima. The next two phrases are clear. It is filled with fragrance which does not dissipate (yisrmard). The fullness of fragrance is described. It has blossoming sirtsa flowers and is thick with blossoming jasmine. Nibirisam means condensed according to Halayudha.

### 3

*kalpita-bhuja-saṅgrāmaḥ kvacid īhita-viśrāmaḥ*  
*kutracid abhinava-tumbaiḥ kvacid atikomala-kumbhaiḥ*  
*kva ca paripākima-guñjaiḥ kva ca bilvāmala-puñjaiḥ*  
*krīḍann adbhuta-caryaḥ keliṣu paṇḍita-varyaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You engage in wrestling and sometimes take rest. In some places, you play with fresh gourds, with soft kumbha fruits, with ripe gunja berries, or with bilva and amalaki fruits. You play in an amazing way. You are most expert in playing.**

**Комментарий:**

You engage in wrestling. Sometimes your rest in the shade of a tree. In some places your play with fresh bottle gourds or soft kumbha tree fruits, or with piles of bilva or amalaki fruits. You have astonishing types of play. You are most expert in playing. Sukadeva says:

*kvacid bilvaiḥ kvacitkumbhaiḥ kvacitkamalamuṣṭibhiḥ \| aspṛśya-netra-bandhādyaiḥ kvacitkhaga mṛgehayā \|\|*

**Sometimes the cowherd boys would play with bilva or kumbha fruits, and sometimes with handfuls of amalaka fruits. At other times they would play the games of trying to touch one another or of trying to identify somebody while one is blindfolded, and sometimes they would imitate animals and birds. (SB 10.18.14)**

### 4

*pībara-kutukādhāre dvandvībhāva-vihāre*  
*kalpita-nirbhara-rāgaḥ kṛta-sakhi-varga-vibhāgaḥ*  
*śītala-marud-anukūle bhāṇḍīra-druma-mūle*  
*kṛtvā ballava-veśaṁ praviśantaṁ danujeśaṁ*  
*jānann eva vilāsī svīkṛtavān khala-śāsī*

**Перевод:**

**You became eager to make two teams and experience great pleasure. You divided your friends into groups under the Bhandira tree with cool breezes. You understood that a demon dressed as a cowherd had entered the group. Fond of pastimes, the punisher of demons, you accepted him.**

**Комментарий:**

You became enthusiastic to play with two teams, which would give great pleasure (pibara-kutuka). The playing is described. You put some friends on Balarama’s team, and some on your team (krta-sakhi-varga-vibhagah). Where did the game take place? That is described: at the base of the Bhandira tree, with cool breezes. Some amazing event took place. You understood that a demon had entered, taking the dress of a cowherd (ballava-vesam), but you accepted him as a friend. Why? You liked pastimes and were the chastiser of the wicked (khala-sasi). You did this to kill him in a proper way.

### 5

*jaitrī-kṛta-bala-pakṣaḥ sudurūha-krama-dakṣaḥ*  
*śrīdāma-priya-kāmaḥ sura-ripu-vāhita-rāmaḥ*  
*kṣapayan pralamba-kāyaṁ halinā nirmita-māyaṁ*  
*daivata-pariṇuta-līlaḥ suhṛd-ānanda-śīlaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You made Balarama win. You were expert at arranging things most difficult to understand. You desired the affection of Sridama. You had Pralamba carry Balarama. You had Pralamba destroyed by Balarama. Your pastimes are praised by the devatas. You give bliss to your friends.**

**Комментарий:**

How this took place is described. You made Balarama win. You were expert at arranging actions most difficult to understand (suduruha). “Since Balarama’s group won, Pralamba on my side is the loser. He must carry Balarama and his true identity will be revealed.” This was Krsna’s understanding. He should not be killed by me. You desired the affection of Sridama. Krsna would carry Sridama, on Balarama’s side, since he had been defeated. He had Pralamba carry Balarama. He had Pralamba destroyed by Balarama (halind). The next two lines are clear. Sukadeva says:

*paśuśvārayato gopaistadvane rāmakṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*goparūpī pralambo'gādasurastajjihīrṣayā \|\|*

**While Rama, Krsna and their cowherd friends were thus tending the cows in that Vrndavana forest, the demon Pralamba entered their midst. He had assumed the form of a cowherd boy with the intention of kidnapping Krsna and Balarama. (SB 10.18.17)**

*taṁ jānannapi dāśārho bhagavānsarvadarśanaḥ \|*  
*anvamodata tatsakhyaṁ vadhaṁ tasya vicintayan \|\|*

**Since the Supreme Lord Krsna, who had appeared in the Dasarha dynasty, sees everything, he understood who the demon was. Still, the Lord pretended to accept the demon as a friend, while at the same time seriously considering how to kill him. (SB 10.18.18)**

*tatropāhūya gopālānkṛṣṇaḥ prāha vihāravit \|*  
*he gopā vihariṣyāmo dvandvībhūya yathāyatham \|\|*

**Krsna, who knows all sports and games, then called together the cowherd boys and spoke as follows: “Hey cowherd boys! Let’s play now! We’ll divide ourselves into two even teams.” (SB 10.18.19)**

*tatra cakruh parivrdhau gopd rama-janardanau*  
*kṛṣṇasaṁghaṭṭinaḥ kecidāsan rāmasya cāpare*

**The cowherd boys chose Krsna and Balarama as the leaders of the two parties. Some of the boys were on Krsna’s side, and others joined Balarama. (SB 10.18.20)**

*acerur vividhah krida vahya-vahaka-laksanahyatrārohanti jetāro vahanti ca parājitāḥ*

**The boys played various games involving carriers and passengers. In these games the winners would climb up on the backs of the losers, who would have to carry them. (SB 10.18.21)**

*vahanto vāhyamānāśca cārayantaśca godhanam \|*  
*bhāṇḍīrakaṁ nāma vaṭaṁ jagmuḥ kṛṣṇa purogamāḥ \|\|*

**Thus carrying and being carried by one another, and at the same time tending the cows, the boys followed Krsna to a banyan tree known as Bhandiraka. (SB 10.18.22)**

*uvāha kṛṣṇo bhagavāñśrīdāmānaṁ parājitaḥ \|*  
*vṛṣabhaṁ bhadrasenastu pralambo rohiṇīsutam \|*

**Defeated, the Supreme Lord Krsna carried Sridama. Bhadrasena carried Vrsabha, and Pralamba carried Balarama, the son of Rohini. (SB 10.18.24)**

*avisahyam manyamanah krsnarn danava-pungavahvahandrutataraṁ prāgādavarohaṇataḥ param*

**Considering Lord Krsna invincible, that foremost demon \[Pralamba\] quickly carried Balarama far beyond the spot where he was supposed to put his passenger down. (SB 10.18.25)**

*athāgata-smṛtir abhayo ripuṁ balo vihāya sārtham iva harantamātmanaḥ \| ruṣāhanac chirasi dṛḍhena muṣṭinā surādhipo girimiva vajraraṁhasā \|\|*

**Remembering the actual situation, the fearless Balarama understood that the demon was trying to kidnap him and take him away from his companions. The Lord then became furious and struck the demon’s head with his hard fist, just as Indra, the king of the demigods, strikes a mountain with his thunderbolt weapon. (SB 10.18.28)**

*dṛṣṭvā pralambaṁ nihataṁ balena balaśālinā \|*  
*gopāḥ suvismitā āsansādhu sādhvitivādinaḥ \|\|*

**The cowherd boys were most astonished to see how the powerful Balarama had killed the demon Pralamba, and they exclaimed, “Excellent! Excellent!” (SB 10.18.30)**

*pāpe pralambe nihate devāḥ paramanirvṛtāḥ \|*  
*abhyavarṣanbalaṁ mālyaiḥ śaśaṁsuḥ sādhu sādhviti \|\| iti \|*

**The sinful Pralamba having been killed, the demigods felt extremely happy, and they showered flower garlands upon Lord Balarama and praised the excellence of his deed. (SB 10.18.32)**

### 6

*tatra vidūraṁ yātāḥ surabhīr laghu-pada-pātāḥ*  
*samam anviṣyan gopaiḥ śaṅkita-nija-dhana-lopair*  
*muñjāvali-vikarāle vipine kvacana viśāle*  
*labdhākhila-dhavalākas tuṅgita-sukha-paripākaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**With the boys in anxiety because of losing their wealth, you searched for the cows which had quickly wandered far off in the forest and found them all in huge tangled thicket of reeds. You showered everyone with happiness.**

**Комментарий:**

After describing the killing of Pralamba, the destruction of the forest fire is described. Along with the boys he searched for the cows which had quickly wandered far away, greedy for grass in the forest. The boys were worried about the loss of the cows, their wealth. They were overwhelmed with anxiety. Then what happened? You found the cows in a huge forest tangled with reeds. You showered everyone with bliss on attaining the wealth of cows. Sukadeva says:

*krīḍāsakteṣu gopeṣu tadgāvo dūracāriṇīḥ \|*  
*svairaṁ carantyo viviśustṛṇalobhena gahvaram \|\|*

**While the cowherd boys were completely absorbed in playing, their cows wandered far away. They hungered for more grass, and with no one to watch them they entered a dense forest. (SB 10.19.1)**

*te'paśyantaḥ paśūngopāḥ kṛṣṇarāmādayastadā \|*  
*jātānutāpā na vidurvicinvanto gavāṁ gatim \|\|*

**Not seeing the cows before them, Krsna, Rama and their cowherd friends suddenly felt repentant for having neglected them. The boys searched all around, but could not discover where they had gone. (SB 10.19.3)**

*muñjāṭavyāṁ bhraṣṭamārgaṁ krandamānaṁ svagodhanam \|*  
*saṁprāpyaṁ tṛṣitāḥ śrāntāstataste saṁnyavartayan \|\|*

**Within the Munja forest the cowherd boys finally found their valuable cows, who had lost their way and were crying. Then the boys, thirsty and tired, herded the cows onto the path back home. (SB 10.19.5)**

### 7

*pīta-bhayaṅkara-dāvaḥ prakaṭollasad-anubhāvaḥ*  
*praṇata-janotsava-kārī tvaṁ bhāṇḍīra-vihārī*  
*gokula-jana-rasa-sindho jaya jaya durvidha-bandho \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You swallowed the fearful forest fire, and experienced great joy. You gave bliss to the surrendered cowherds, as you wandered near Bhandira. О ocean of rasa of the people of Gokula! О friend of the miserable! Please manifest your excellence!**

**Комментарий:**

Later at the reed forest, suddenly a forest fire arose. You made the boys close their eyes and you extinguished the fire. You made them all happy. Again, with the boys endowed with wide smiles, you play at Bhandira.

Sukadeva says:

*tataḥ samantād dava-dhūmaketur*  
*yadṛcchayābhūt kṣaya kṛd vanaukasām \|*  
*samiritah sarathinolbanolmukair*  
*vilelihanah sthira-jangaman mahan*

**Suddenly a great forest fire appeared on all sides, threatening to destroy all the forest creatures. Like a chariot driver, the wind swept the fire onward, and terrible sparks shot in all directions. Indeed, the great fire extended its tongues of flame toward all moving and nonmoving creatures. (SB 10.19.7)**

*tamāpatantaṁ parito davāgniṁ*  
*gopāśca gāvaḥ asamīkṣya bhītāḥ*  
*ucus ca krsnam sa-balam prapanna*  
*yatha harim mrtyu-bhayardita janah*

**As the cows and cowherd boys stared at the forest fire attacking them on all sides, they became fearful. The boys then approached Krsna and Balarama for shelter, just as those who are disturbed by fear of death approach the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The boys addressed them as follows. (SB 10.19.8)**

*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahābāho he rāmāmitavikrama \|*  
*dāvāgninā dahyamānān prapannāṁstrātumarhathaḥ \|\|*

**\[The cowherd boys said:\] O Krsna! Krsna! Most powerful one! O Rama! You whose prowess never fails! Please save your devotees, who are about to be burned by this forest fire and have come to take shelter of You! (SB 10.19.9)**

*vaco niśamya kṛpaṇaṁ bandhūnāṁ bhagavān hariḥ*  
*nimilayata ma bhaista locananily abhasata*

**Hearing these pitiful words from his friends, the Supreme Lord Krsna told them, “Just close your eyes and do not be afraid.” (SB 10.19.11)**

### Text 19

*kalita-śrīdāmānaṁ śrīdāmānandi-keli-tundilitam \|*  
*vande rāmāvarajaṁ rāmāvarajaṅgama-dyutarum \|\|19\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Krsna, younger brother of Balarama, who wore Radha’s garland on his chest, who gave bliss to Sridama by carrying him, who is an excellent, moving desire tree for the gopis.**

**Комментарий:**

The author offers respects to Krsna, who performed the pastimes. I offer respects to Krsna, the younger brother of Balarama. He wears on his chest Radha’s (sri) garland (dama). He is nourished by the pastime of carrying Sridama which gives bliss to Sridama. He is an excellent, moving (jarigama) desire tree (dyutaram) for the gopis.

**dvipadikā cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is dvipadika. It is described as follows.

*dvipadī parigaditā sā dvādaśa-kala-yuktā*

**Dvipadl is endowed with twelve kalas (matras).**

According to this the poem has been written.

## atha varṣā-śarad-vihā-racaritam

**Pastimes in monsoon and autumn**

### Text 20

*premollāsana-śīlā ballava-mallasya vijayate līlā \|*  
*yan mādhurīṁ vipañcī viriñci-sūnoḥ prapañcayati \|\|20\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna’s pastimes of monsoon and autumn, binding the devotee to prema, whose sweetness is broadcast by Narada’s vina, remain excellent.**

**Комментарий:**

The author indicates the pastimes of autumn, etc., which will be described in the poem. The pastimes of Krsna during monsoon and autumn manifest excellence (vijayate). They bind the devotee to bhava (premollasana). The glory of the pastimes is described. Narada’s (virinci-stinoh) vina (vipancl) broadcasts (prapancayati) their sweetness.

### 1

*megha-samaya-pūtir acita-vṛṣṭiṣu taru-kanda-racita*  
*nīpakakubha-puṣpa-valita sāndra-vipina-labdha-lalita-*  
*bhakta-pariṣad-iṣṭa-varada hāri-vibhava-dhāri-śarad-*  
*alaṅkṛta-bahu-pakṣi-bharita-kānana-kṛta-divya-carita*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, enjoying herding the cows in the rain! О Krsna, taking shelter of the trees and caves during the showers! О Krsna, decorated with kadamba and asoka flowers! О Krsna, giving gifts to the devotees attractive in the dense groves! О Krsna, performing attractive pastimes in the forests filled with various birds and ornamented with autumn holding attractive wealth!**

**Комментарий:**

О lord! Protect persons like me (mad-vidha-jana—at end of poem). All phrases are related to this sentence at the end. You enjoy herding the cows during the rainy season.

You go to the shelters under the trees when the rains pour. You do not want your red turban to get wet. You make costumes from kadamba and arjuna flowers. You give desired gifts such as food to your devotee friends attractive in the dense groves. Thus, the monsoon pastimes have been described. Sukadeva says:

*kvacidvanaspatikoḍe guhāyāṁ cābhivarṣati \|*  
*nirviśan bhagavānneme kandamūlaphalāśanaḥ \|\|*

**When it rained, the Lord would sometimes enter a cave or the hollow of a tree to play and to eat roots and fruits. (SB 10.20.28)**

*dadhyodanamupānītaṁ śilāyāṁ salilāntike \|*  
*saṁbhojanī yairbubhuje gopaiḥ saṁkarṣaṇānvitaḥ \|\|*

**Lord Krsna would take his meal of boiled rice and yogurt, sent from home, in the company of Lord Sahkarsana and the cowherd boys who regularly ate with him. They would all sit down to eat on a large stone. (SB 10.20.29)**

Or he gives desirable objects to the group of sages he meets in the forest. Autumn is then described. He performs attractive pastimes in the groves filled with many types of birds like swans, which are ornamented with autumn which possesses attractive wealth such as lotuses. Sukadeva says:

*itthaṁ śaratkhacchajalaṁ padmākarasugandhinā \|*  
*nyaviśadvāyunā vātaṁ sagogopālako'cyutaḥ \|\|*

**Thus the Vrndavana forest was filled with transparent autumnal waters and cooled by breezes perfumed with the fragrance of lotus flowers growing in the clear lakes. The infallible Lord, accompanied by his cows and cowherd boyfriends, entered that Vrndavana forest. (SB 10.21.1)**

*kusumita-vanarāji-śuṣmi-bhṛṅga dvija-kula-ghuṣṭa-saraḥ-śaran-mahidhram*  
*madhupatir avagdhya carayan gah*  
*saha-pasu-pdla-balas cukiija venum*

**The lakes, rivers and hills of Vrndavana resounded with the sounds of maddened bees and flocks of birds moving about the flowering trees. In the company of the cowherd boys and Balarama, Madhupati \[Sri Krsna\] entered that forest, and while herding the cows he began to vibrate his flute. (SB 10.21.2)**

### 2

*veśa-tulita-nartaka-vara candraka-cita-cāru-kabara*  
*gopa-yuvati-dhairya-mathana-rūpa tad-abhinīta-kathana*  
*locana-phala venu-valana-valgad-adhara-vaktra-kalana*  
*sarva-sukṛta-vaibhava-dhara-veṇu-rasita-rajyad-adhara*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, dressing like the best dancer! О Krsna, whose attractive hair is ornamented with a peacock feather! О Krsna, whose beauty disturbs the gopis’ composure! О Krsna, subject of their conversations! О Krsna, the fruit for their eyes! О Krsna, showing a face with pursed lips playing the flute! О Krsna, whose lips are tasted by the flute which has accrued all pious acts!**

**Комментарий:**

The next two phrases are clear. It is said: barhapldam nata-vara-vapuh: he is dressed as the best dancer with a peacock feather. (SB 10.21.5) Your beauty disturbs the composure of the gopis. They talk about you.

*tad varṇayitum ārabdhāḥ smarantyaḥ kṛṣṇaceṣṭitam \|*  
*nāśakansmāravegena vikṣiptamanaso nṛpaḥ \|\|*

**The cowherd girls began to speak about Krsna, but when they remembered his activities, О King, the power of Cupid disturbed their minds, and thus they could not speak. (SB 10.21.4)**

О fruit for the eyes! Your show a face with pursed lips when you play the flute.

The gopis describe this.

*akṣaṇvatāṁ phalamidaṁ na paraṁ vidāmaḥ sakhyaḥ prasūnanuniveśayatorvayasyaiḥ \|*  
*vaktraṁ vrajeśasutayoranuveṇujuṣṭaṁ yairvā nipītam anuraktakayakṣa--mokṣam \|\|*

**The cowherd girls said: О friends, those eyes that see the beautiful faces of the sons of Maharaja Nanda are certainly fortunate. As these two sons enter the forest, surrounded by their friends, driving the cows before them, they hold their flutes to their mouths and glance lovingly upon the residents of Vrndavana. For those who have eyes, we think there is no greater object of vision. (SB 10.21.7)**

Your shining red lips are tasted by the flute which possesses a wealth of all pious acts. The flute performed pious acts. The gopis say:

*gopyaḥ kimācaradayaṁ kuśalaṁ sma veṇurdāmodarādharasudhāmapi gopikānām*

**My dear gopis, what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of Krsna’s lips independently and leave only a taste for us gopis, for whom that nectar is actually meant! (SB 10.21.9)**

### 3

*veṇu-madhura-nāda-naṭita-keki-nivaha megha-ghaṭita-*  
*seva janita-mukta-yavasa-dhenu-nicaya-citta-rabhasa-*  
*rūpa-vilasad-aṅga-valana-mohita-sura-vṛnda-lalana*  
*bhilla-yuvati-toṣi-masṛṇa-śaspa-milita-pāda-ghusṛṇa*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, making the peacocks dance by the sweet sound of your flute! О Krsna, served by the clouds which give shade! О Krsna, making the cows’ hearts joyful so they stop chewing grass! О Krsna, bewildering the wives of the devatas by the movements of your limbs shining with beauty! О Krsna, satisfying the Pulinda women by the kunkuma from your feet mixed with the soft grass!**

**Комментарий:**

You make the flocks of peacocks dance by the sweet sound of your flute. Mentioning the flute three times in proximity is not a fault since different details are given each time. The gopis say:

*govindaveṇumanu mattamayūra nṛtyam*  
*preksyadri-sanv-avaratanya-samasta-sattvam*

**The peacocks dance madly when they hear Govinda’s flute, and when other creatures see them from the hilltops, they all become stunned. (SB 10.21.10)**

You have the clouds serve by forming an umbrella above. Worried about the rays of the autumn sun, the clouds produce shade.

*sakhyur vyadhāt sva-vapuṣāmbuda ātapaktram*

**With its multitude of flower-like droplets of water, the cloud became an umbrella for the sake of his friend. (SB 10.21.16)**

The cows with joyful (rabhasa) hearts stop chewing their grass on experiencing the flute. You make the wives of the devatas bewildered by the movements (valana) of your limbs which shine with beauty. The gopis say:

*kṛṣṇaṁ nirīkṣya vanitotsavacāraveśaṁ śrutvā ca tatkvaṇitaveṇuvicitragītam \|*  
*devyo vimānagatayaḥ smaranunnasārā dṛśyatprasūnakavarā mumuhur vinīvyaḥ \|\|*

**Krsna’s beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods’ wives flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of him and hear his resonant flute-song, their hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair and their belts loosen. (SB 10.21.12)**

The kunkuma from your feet mixed with the tender grass gives pleasure to the Pulinda girls. The Pulinda girls smear the kunkuma stuck to the green grass, which came from your feet which were touched by Radha’s breasts, upon their faces and relieve themselves of the fire of desire. The gopis say:

*pūrṇāḥ pulindya urugāya padābjarāgaśrīkuṅkumena dayitāstanamaṇḍitena \|*  
*taddarśanasmararujastṛṇarūṣitena limpantya ānanakuceṣu jahustadādhim \|\|*

**The aborigine women of the Vrndavana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass marked with reddish kunkuma powder. Endowed with the color of Krsna’s lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts of his beloved, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they feel fully satisfied and give up all their anxiety. (SB 10.21.17)**

### 4

*hāri-hariṇa-yoṣid-amala-netra-sukhada-vaktra-kamala*  
*dāsya-nirata-śaila-racita-sevana paśu-pāśa-khacita*  
*pāhi karuṇa mad-vidha-janam īśvara duravāpa-bhañjana \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, whose lotus face gives joy to the pure eyes of the attractive wives of the deer! O Krsna, giving service to your servant Govardhana! О Krsna, holding a rope for restraining the cows! О merciful Krsna! Protect this person. О Lord! Destroyer of the impossible!**

**Комментарий:**

Your lotus face gives happiness to the pure eyes of the attractive wives of the deer. The gopis say:

*dhanyāḥ sma mūḍhamatayo'pi hariṇya etā yā nandanandanamupāttavicitraveṣam \|*  
*ākarṇya veṇuraṇitaṁ saha kṛṣṇasārāḥ pūjāṁ dadhurviracitā praṇayāvalokaiḥ \|\|*

**Blessed are all these foolish deer because they have approached Maharaja Nanda’s son, who is gorgeously dressed and is playing on his flute. Indeed, both the doe and the bucks worship the Lord with looks of love and affection. (SB 10.21.11)**

You are served by the mountain with dasya mood. The gopis say:

*hantāyam adrir avalā haridāsavaryo yad rāma-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa-sparśa-pramodaḥ \|*  
*mānaṁ tanoti saha go-gaṇayos tayor yat pānīya-sūyavasa-kandara-kandamūlaiḥ \|\|*

**Of all the devotees, this Govardhana Hill is the best! О my friends, this hill supplies Krsna and Balarama, along with their calves, cows and cowherd friends, with all kinds of necessities—water for drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respects to the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Krsna and Balarama, Govardhana Hill appears very jubilant. (SB 10.21.18)**

You have ropes for tying the legs of the cows to control them. О best of the cowherds!

*niyoga-pāśalakṣaṇayoḥ*

**They carry ropes to bind the cows’ rear legs at the time of milking. (SB 10.21.19)**

О merciful Krsna!

### Text 21

*ghana-praṇaya-ghaṭṭanodghurita-ghoṣa-sīmantinī-*  
*prapañcita-jagat-trayī-śruti-viṭaṅka-vikrīḍite \|*  
*śarad-vihasitāṭavī-kuhara-bhū-vihāra-priye*  
*ratis tvayi tarasvinī mama salīlam unmīlatu \|\|21\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May I easily manifest rati for you, fond of pastimes in the caves of Vrndavana in autumn, whose pastimes, ear ornaments for women of the three worlds, spread to the limits of the village which is unsteady with intense affection.**

**Комментарий:**

The author prays for affection for the Lord who plays in Vrndavana.

О Krsna! May I develop rati for you. The rati is described. It is bold. Krsna is described. Your pastimes are the ear ornament for the women of the three worlds and spread to the edge of the village unsteady with fickleness produced by intense affection. You are fond of pastimes in the caves of Vrndavana, manifesting autumn.

**hāri-hariṇa-cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is hari-harina. It is described as follows.

*hāri-hariṇam etad amalam asti bhasanalena saruciḥ \|*

**Pure hari-harina is attractive with Iss ssl sss s (bha, sa, na, la).**

According to that, this poem is written.

## atha vastra-haraṇam

**Stealing the gopis’ clothing**

### Text 22

*smerābhiḥ salile kalinda-duhitur magnābhir ākandharaṁ*  
*skandha-nyasta-samasta-paṭṭa-vasano narmokti-bhaṅgī-paṭuḥ \|*  
*nirvyājaṁ vraja-kanyakābhir asakṛd bhavyābhir abhyarthitaḥ*  
*pāyāt tuṅga-kadamba-śākhi-śikharārūḍhas trilokīṁ hariḥ \|\|22\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, placing the girls’ clothing on his shoulder and climbing to the top of a tall kadamba tree, implored innocently by the auspicious young girls of Vraja who smiled and submerged themselves up to the neck in Yamuna’s water, while he skillfully joked, protect the three worlds.**

**Комментарий:**

The stealing of the gopis’ clothing is told in summary first.

May Krsna protect the three worlds. He is described. He placed the clothing of all the girls on his shoulders (skandha). He climbed to the top of a towering kadamba tree. He was requested sincerely (nirvyajam) many times by the girls of Vraja to obtain their cloths. They were forms of auspiciousness (bhavyabhih). They were not bold in appearance. They submerged themselves up to the neck (akandharam) in the Yamuna’s water. Out of shyness they could not come out. Kandhara means the neck according to Halayudha. He was skillful at joking. By describing Krsna as a great thief and the protector of the three worlds virodhabhasa is indicated. This suggests the intense bhakti of his pure devotees.

### 1

*nija-guṇodayollāsa-lobhitā giri-sutā-vratārambha-śobhitāḥ*  
*paśupa-kanyakāḥ sūrajāvane racita-majjanāḥ prekṣya pāvane*  
*tvaritam āgato luñcitāmbaraḥ priyakam āśrito raṅgiṇāṁ varaḥ*  
*sapadi lokayan goṣṭha-bālikā bhrū-kuṭi-vallarī-bhaṅgurālakāḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the young cowherd girls, who were lured by the joy of the manifestation of your qualities, who were beautiful on performing the Katyayani vrata, who had submerged themselves to the neck in Yamuna’s water, you came there and quickly stole their clothing. Expert at pastimes, you climbed a kadamba tree and gazed upon them, with locks of hair falling on their frowning brows.**

**Комментарий:**

О Lord! О lord of all! О shelter of Laksmi! О king of Vraja! Protect me. This line at the end is connected with the previous phrases. Seeing the young cowherd girls, you were immediately attracted by their love and came there (agatah). They are described. They were lured by joy manifested by the appearance of your extraordinary qualities like being the best man and being controlled by prema. They were beautiful with the start of the vrata of Katyayani with bathing in Margaslrsa month along with worship. They bathed in the water of Yamuna (surajavane) to conclude the vrata of worshipping Katyayani in order to have Krsna as their husband.

Arriving there, what did he do? He grabbed their clothing. Taking the cloth, he climbed a kadamba tree (priyakam). He gazed at the group of gopis and smiled. “Today they have come under my control. 1 will test their prema." Their locks were touching their frowning eyebrows.

### 2

*smita-parisphurad-vaktra-maṇḍalaḥ sphuṭita-mālatī-kḷpta-kuṇḍalaḥ*  
*sarabhasaṁ tataḥ śīta-vepitaiḥ praṇaya-kopibhiḥ suṣṭhu-hrepitair*  
*vadana-visphurat-kāku-jalpanair vihita-sāmabhir bheda-kalpanaiḥ*  
*sicaya-sañcayaṁ saṁbhramākulair jhaṭiti-yācitaḥ kanyakākulaiḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Your face shows a smile. You wore earrings the blossoming jasmines. You were joyfully requested the clothing by the all the respectful girls, who were shivering from the cold, who were filled with affectionate anger, who were drowning in an ocean of shame, who spoke softly, making polite requests and threats.**

**Комментарий:**

At once you were joyfully (sarabhasam) requested for the piles of cloth (sicaya-sancayam) by the girls. Sicaya means cloth according to Haima. They were trembling from the cold. They showed affectionate anger. “Is this proper conduct for the beloved king’s son?” They drowned in an ocean of shame (hrepitaih). Soft words came from their mouths. “We are your servants.” They spoke affectionate words (samabhih). “O Krsna, praised in Gokula! О knower of dharma!” They made threats. “If you do not give us our clothing, we will tell Kamsa.”

*mānayaṁ bhoḥ kathāstvāṁ tu nandagopasutaṁ priyam \|*  
*jānīmo'ṅga vrajaślāghyaṁ dehi vāsāṁsi vepitāḥ \|\|*

**Dear Krsna, don’t be unfair! We know that you are the respectable son of Nanda and that you are honored by everyone in Vraja. You are also very dear to us. Please give us back our clothes. We are shivering in the cold water. (SB 10.22.14)**

*śyāmasundara te dāsyaḥ karavāma tavoditam \|*  
*dehi vāsāṁsi dharmajña no cedrājñe bruvāmahe*

**О Syamasundara, we are your maidservants and must do whatever you say. But give us back our clothing. You know what the religious principles are, and if you don’t give us our clothes we will have to tell the king. Please! (SB 10.22.15)**

Still they had respect for him as their Lord (sambhramakulaih).

### 3

*pṛthutarāṁsayor arpitāṁśukaḥ sitaradollasan-mañjulāṁśukaḥ*  
*prakaṭitāgrahair bhūpa-helibhiḥ sakhi-kulādṛtair jalpa-kelibhis*  
*taru-puras taṭe tās tadā balād aciram ānayan gokulābalāḥ*  
*mudita-mugdha-dhīḥ keli-narmadaḥ sakala-ballavī-vṛnda-śarmadaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Placing the cloth on your thick shoulders, with white teeth emanating attractive rays, you quickly brought the girls of Gokula by force to the base of the tree by your playful words, full of insistence, denigrating the king and approved by your young friends. You showed your joyful, innocent mind and your joking play. You gave good fortune to all the cowherd girls.**

**Комментарий:**

You placed the cloth on your thick shoulders. Attractive rays emanated from your white teeth. You forcibly brought the girls of Gokula in front of the base of the kadamba tree using playful words (jala-kelibhih). They were very insistent words. “If you are my servants, then come here and take your garments.” He disrespected Kamsa (bhilpa-helibhih). “You are proud of taking shelter of Kamsa. What can he do to me?” The words were respected by his friends, five years old who could not stay home. “O Krsna! This is right.” The next three phrases are clear in meaning.

### 4

*prakaṭam ambarī-bhūta-hastakāḥ savidham āgatā namra-mastakāḥ*  
*sa paṭur ātmano vākya-kārikā-dhṛta-mahotsavaḥ prekṣya dārikāḥ*  
*salila-majjane vyajya nagnatāṁ vrata-vidher vadan suṣṭhu bhagnatāṁ*  
*śirasi kārayann asya pūrtaye prasabham ātmane kṣema-mūrtaye*  
*madhuram añjaliṁ mañju-locanaḥ praṇayinī-manas-tāpa-mocanaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Skillful at testing their love, seeing the girls obey your words, using their hands as cloth and approaching near with lowered heads, you became joyful. Saying, “You have broken the rules of the vrata by bathing naked in the water,” you made them place their sweet hands on their heads to fulfill the vow, giving respect to the form of forgiveness. Your eyes opened wide to see them. You freed them from mental anguish because they had true love for you.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna is further described. You are skillful (patuh) at testing pure bhava. Seeing the girls (darikah) obeying your words you were joyful. They used their hands as cloth (ambari). They covered their private parts with their hands and approached near in that manner, with heads lowered in shame. You said that they broke the rules of the vrata by bathing naked in the water. The purpose of the vrata will not appear since you have offended the deity of the water. “How can we restore the vrata?” Understanding their anxiety, he then tested their love. “To fulfill the vow, fold your sweet hands on your heads in front of me, the form of forgiveness. By offering respects to me, the form of auspiciousness, the form of all results, the vrata will bear results with its arigas” They did as he said. His attractive eyes opened to see their limbs. He understood that they had love for him (pranayini). He freed them from all mental pain.

### 5

*kim api kanyakālībhir ānataḥ praṇaya-saṅkulād āśu mānataḥ*  
*sukha-bharād amūr atra tarpayan vasana-sañcayaṁ tūrṇam arpayan*  
*kṛta-kumārikā-citta-dohadaḥ sakala-sundarī-prema-mohadaḥ*  
*praṇata-maṇḍalābhīṣṭa-kāma-dhuk kamana-ballavī-mallikā-madhuḥ*  
*tvam akhileśa mām indirālaya vraja-mahendra he deva pālaya \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You were immediately offered respects by the young girls, because of their great affection and love. You satisfied them by awarding their desires. Quickly you returned their clothing. You satisfied the desire in their hearts and bewildered them all with prema. You grant the desires of the devotees. You are spring for the jasmines, the beautiful gopis. О lord of all! О abode of Laksmi! О king of Vraja! О shining lord! Please protect me.**

**Комментарий:**

You were quickly offered respects by the pleased girls, who had great affection, and the mood of a lover (manatah). Since they became blissful that they would be accepted by you (sukha-bharat), you satisfied them. “I approve of your vow. It will bear fruit.” Quickly you gave them the clothing. You fulfilled the desire in their hearts (dohadah). Dohada means desire according to Amara-kosa. He made the object of their vrata manifest. You gave bewilderment in prema to all the beautiful girls. You are satisfied with the devotees. You fulfill the desires (kama-dhuk) of those surrendered to you. You are spring (madhu) from the jasmines of the beautiful (катана) gopis since you give your devotees bliss. You fulfill their desires.

### Text 23

*vidadhīnayāpi dhavalaṁ tava jagad evādya kīrti-candrikayā \|*  
*keśava paśupālīnāṁ citraṁ dviguṇīkṛto rāgaḥ \|\|23\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Kesava! The prema (redness) of the gopis has doubled by the moonlight of your fame, which turns the world white.**

**Комментарий:**

He became famous for giving mercy to the girls of Vraja.

О Kesava! Today the attraction of the gopis has doubled by the moonlight of your fame, which turns the world white. Dhavala means white and sinless. Raga means red and prema. This is the alankara of visama where cause and effect are reversed. Pun is its anga.

**indirā cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is indira.

*nagaṇato rarāvindirā lagau*

**Indira consists of sss Isl Isl si (na, ra, ra, la, gd).**

According to this the poem has been written.

## atha yajña-patnī-prasādaḥ

**Mercy to the Wives of the Brahmanas**

### Text 24

*paritoṣayituṁ na yāyajūkais*  
*tvam anūcāna-janaiś ca nāsi śakyaḥ \|*  
*rati-hārya ratiṁ dadasva vande*  
*tava govinda sadā padāravindam \|\|24\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You cannot be satisfied by learned brahmanas performing sacrifices. О Krsna controlled by rati! О best of the cowherds! Please give rati. I offer respects to your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

The author presents the pastime of mercy to the brahmanas' wives which will be described in detail.

О Krsna, able to be controlled by rati (rati-harya)! О Govinda, master of the cowherds! You cannot be satisfied by the learned (апйсапа) brahmanas performing sacrifice (yayajtikaih). Yayajuka means someone performing sacrifice. Апйсапа means study or wisdom according to Amara-kosa. Thus, bestow bhava (rati). I offer respects always to your lotus feet for that purpose.

Though the brahmanas, engaged in karmas like upanayana, etc., were devoid of your mercy, their wives attained the Lord’s mercy. By stating the effects of performing (brahmanas) and not performing karmas (their wives), karma is rejected as a cause of the Lord’s mercy. Association of devotees is the cause. The brahmanas said concerning this:

*dhigjanma nastrividvidyāṁ dhigvrataṁ dhigbahujñatām \|*  
*dhikkulaṁ dhikkṛyādākṣyaṁ vimukhā ye tvadhokṣaje \|\|*

**To hell with our threefold birth, our vow of celibacy and our extensive learning! To hell with our aristocratic background and our expertise in the rituals of sacrifice! These are all condemned because we were inimical to the transcendental Personality of Godhead. (SB 10.23.40)**

*nāsāṁ dvijātisaṁskāro na śaucaṁ na kriyāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*athāpi hyuttamaśloke kṛṣṇe yogeśvareśvare \|*  
*bhatirdṛḍhā na cāsmākaṁ saṁskārādimatāmapi \|\|*

**These women have never undergone the purificatory rites of the twice-born classes, nor have they lived as brahmacarls in the asrama of a spiritual master, nor have they executed austerities, speculated on the nature of the self, followed the formalities of cleanliness or engaged in pious rituals. Nevertheless, they have firm devotion for Lord Krsna, whose glories are chanted by the exalted hymns of the Vedas and who is the supreme master of all masters of mystic power. We, on the other hand, have no such devotion for the Lord, although we have executed all these processes. (SB 10.23.44)**

It is understood that the wives were able to attain devotee association.

### 1

*raṅgatas toṣita-jñātinā saṅgato dhenukārātinā*  
*karṇa-pālī-sphurat-pallavair veṣṭitaḥ sarvato ballavair*  
*gopa-sīmantinī-kāmukaḥ kānanotsaṅga-saṁgāmukaḥ*  
*kḷpta-vṛndāṭavī-mānanaḥ prekṣita-smera-gopānanaḥ*  
*saṁstuvan bhūruhāṁ sampadaḥ ślāghayan vyājataḥ śaṁpadaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Accompanied by Balarama, who satisfied your relatives by giving them knowledge of your pastimes, surrounded by gopis decorated with petal earrings, beloved of the gopis, desiring to associate with them in the forest, praising Vrndavana, glancing at a friend with a smile, you glorified the wealth of trees. Praising the trees, you gave them joy.**

**Комментарий:**

О Govinda! May you play in Gokula (khelatat—this comes at the end of the poem)! Protect me, of bad character (uddhatam), always assailed by severe calamity (daruna apad dhatam). The phrases are all connected to these last lines of the poem. Krsna is described. You are accompanied by Balarama (dhenuka-aratina) who satisfies relatives with knowledge of Krsna’s surprising pastimes. You are the lover (kamukah) of the gopis. You like to associate (sangamukah) with them in the depth of the forest. You praise (mananah) Vrndavana. You praise the wealth of Vrndavana trees (.bhuruham). Though praising them, you gave them happiness. Sukadeva says:

*nidāghārkātape tigme chāyābhiḥ svābhirātmanaḥ \|*  
*ātapaktrāyitānvīkṣya drumānāha vrajaukasaḥ \|\|*

**Then the sun’s heat became intense, Lord Krsna saw that the trees were acting as umbrellas by shading him, and thus he spoke as follows to his boyfriends. (SB 10.22.30)**

*paśyataitānmahābhāgānparārthaikāntajīvitān \|*  
*vātavarṣātapahimānsahato vārayanti naḥ \|\|*

**See these greatly fortunate trees, whose lives are completely dedicated to the benefit of others. Even while tolerating the wind, rain, heat and snow, they protect us from these elements. (SB 10.22.32)**

### 2

*svān sakhīn kṣud-bharottāpitān premabhiḥ prārthanām āpitān*  
*preṣayann adhvare’dūrataḥ khyāpita-brāhmaṇa-krūrataḥ*  
*kalpita-brāhmaṇāvajñayā preṣṭha-saṁkrāmita-prajñayā*  
*laṅghita-kṣema-bhāk-satrayā pūrikāpūritāmatrayā*

**Перевод:**

**You sent your friends, afflicted with hunger, who begged out of affection, to the nearby sacrifice and learned from them that the brahmanas were cruel. You were gazed upon by the brahmanas’ wives who disobeyed their husbands, who left the auspicious sacrifice, because of intelligence directed to you, bringing plates full of sweets.**

**Комментарий:**

He sent his friends who were afflicted with great hunger to a sacrifice nearby. They requested for Krsna, out of affection for him, thinking that they should relieve Krsna of hunger. “Since Krsna and his friends are eternally satisfied, it is impossible to relieve them of hunger. He should come to us at some time. The friend of the suffering people should beg food from us.” Thus, it was by the desire of the devotees, the wives that their hunger appeared.

He learned from them, who returned without any food, that the brahmanas’ were cruel. The friends said, “The brahmanas did not give food to us your servants. They did not receive us with kind words.”

He was gazed upon (preksitah) by the brahamanas’ wives, who quickly came when requested by the boys who had been sent by Krsna. He had said, “Go to the wives who are my devotees.” (five lines later) They had disobeyed their husbands (avajnaya). Their intelligence was directed to Krsna, object of the highest prema (prestha). They ignored the great sacrifice (satram), the abode of auspiciousness (ksema-bhak). What did they bring to the Lord? They carried plates filled with sweets (amatrayd.).

### 3

*sthālikā-nyasta-sad-bhaktayā sneha-sampattito’bhyaktayā*  
*ratna-pātrī-dhṛta-kṣīrayā kānanopakrame dhīrayā*  
*bhājananyasta-saṁyāvayā kautukottuṅga-saṁrāvayā*  
*gauravān nirbharottālayā prekṣito brāhmaṇī-mālayā*

**Перевод:**

**They brought cooked rice sprinkled profusely with ghee, milk in gem studded plates, and cakes made with devotion. They diligently approached the forest while speaking loudly in joy, coming quickly with reverence.**

**Комментарий:**

They made loud noises (samravaya) out of joy on going to Krsna. They came very quickly (uttalaya) out of respect for Krsna (gauravat). Uttala means quickly and bhajana means a dish according to Halayudha.

### 4

*spardhamānaṁ rucā hāṭakaṁ dhārayann ujjvalaṁ śāṭakaṁ*  
*sakhyur aṁse karaṁ dakṣiṇaṁ nyasya lokotrayī-rakṣiṇaṁ*  
*visphuran-nartakālaṅkṛtiḥ sañcarat-kiñkiṇī-jhaṅkṛtiḥ*  
*kāntibhir ninditendīvaraḥ sundaroras taṭe pīvaraḥ*  
*sañcaran-mañjarī-kuṇḍalaḥ ślāghita-brāhmaṇī-maṇḍalaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**You wore a bright cloth that rivaled the beauty of gold. Placing your right hand, protector of the three worlds, on a friend’s shoulder, you shone. You were dressed like a dancer, with bells moving and jingling. You derided the blue lotus by your beauty. You had a broad beautiful chest. Your flower earrings swayed. You praised the wives of the brahmanas.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna is described. You wore bright cloth (satakam) which competed with gold in beauty. You shone (visphuran), placing your right hand, protector of the three worlds on the shoulder of a friend. You were dressed like a dancer (nartakalankrtih). The next five items are clear in meaning. He praised the brahmanas’ wives. “O most fortunate ones! O my unalloyed devotees!”

Sukadeva says:

*śyāma hiraṇyaparidhiṁ vanamālyabarhadhātupravālanaṭaveṣamanuvratāṁse \|*  
*vinyastahastamitareṇa dhunānamabjaṁ karṇotpalālakakapolamukhābjahāsam \|\|*

**His complexion was dark blue and his garment golden. Wearing a peacock feather, colored minerals, sprigs of flower buds, and a garland of forest flowers and leaves, he was dressed just like a dramatic dancer. He rested one hand upon the shoulder of a friend and with the other twirled a lotus. Lilies graced his ears, his hair hung down over his cheeks, and his lotus-like face was smiling. (SB 10.23.22)**

### 5

*kṛṣṇa he sundara-kuṇṭhayā preritās tūrṇam utkaṇṭhayā*  
*rakṣa naḥ saṅgatā dūrataḥ svāntike tvaṁ yataḥ sūrataḥ*  
*kṣmāsurī-kākum ity agrataḥ śīlayan vyañjita-vyagrataḥ*  
*sarvathā datta-tad-vāñchitaḥ kīrti-viñcholi-kālāñchitaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**He heard the wives plead in front of him, “O beautiful Krsna! Impelled by intense longing, quickly we came from far off to you since you are merciful. Do not reject us.” Visibly disturbed, he told them that their desire would be fulfilled, and he designated them with great fame.**

**Комментарий:**

He listened (silayan) to the pleas of the wives (ksamdsuri) in front of him. “O beautiful Krsna! Impelled by strong longing we have come quickly from far off. Do not reject us since you are merciful (suratah).” The words are out of order because of metrical needs and should be correctly ordered.

“How can I the prince of Nanda satisfy the wives of the brahmanas whose minds are absorbed in madhurya-bhava? How could I continue respond to it?” He hinted at his confusion in this way. What did he do? He said, “This cannot be given completely, but after this life, you will meet with me. In this way I can fulfill your desires.” He designated them with heaps of fame (kirti-vincholika)— possessing bhavas as a devotee while preserving the rules.

He said to them:

*na prītaye'nurāgāya hyaṅgasako nṛṇāmiha \|*  
*tanmano mayi yuñjānā acirānmāmavāpsyatha \|\|*

**For you to remain in my bodily association would certainly not please people in this world, nor would it be the best way for you to increase your love for me. Rather, you should fix your minds on me, and very soon you will achieve me. (SB 10.23.32)**

### 6

*proṣita-brāhmaṇī-ko’malaḥ pallavād apy alaṁ komalaḥ*  
*sad-guṇair indriyāmodanaṁ bhuktavān bhojayan nodanaṁ*  
*matta-mātaṅga-līlā-karaḥ kiṅkarānandi-śīlākaraḥ*  
*sarvadā vibhramārambhavān khelatād gokule’laṁ bhavān*  
*santataṁ dāruṇāpaddhataṁ pāhi govinda mām uddhatam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You sent the wives of the brahmanas home and remained pure. But internally you were more tender than a new leaf. You fed your friends the food, pleasurable to the senses and with good qualities and you ate as well. Performing pastimes like an intoxicated elephant, a mine of actions which give bliss to your servants, always performing pastimes, may you play in Gokula. O Govinda! Protect me, a wicked soul, always afflicted by terrible calamity!**

**Комментарий:**

He sent the wives of the brahmanas home (presita-brdhmanikah).

He remained pure (amalah). He was more tender than a new mango leaf. Knowing their pain, he felt pain. What did he do? He fed his friends the food pleasing to the senses and with good qualities like softness, brightness and fragrance and ate the food himself. He performed this pastime like an intoxicated elephant. This is nidarsana alankara. You are a mine (akarah) of activities (sila) which give joy to your servants. Sila means action according to Halayudha. Such actions occurred continually. You always commence pastimes (vibhrama).

### Text 25

*duḥkhocchittiḥ parama-madhurānanda-pūrānubhūtiḥ*  
*seyaṁ dāmodara tad-ucitā sādhanānuṣṭhitir vā \|*  
*sattāṁ dhatte na kamala-bhuvo’py antareṇārta-bandho*  
*kāruṇyaṁ te muhur aham ataḥ prārthaye tasya bindum \|\|25\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Damodara! Without your mercy even Brahma cannot destroy ignorance and experience the full, highest sweet bliss and even perform sadhana for liberation. O friend of the suffering souls! Therefore, I constantly pray for a drop of that mercy.**

**Комментарий:**

The wives by the Lord’s mercy attained the goal of life but their husbands, devoid of that mercy, did not. O friend of the suffering souls! O Krsna! Without your mercy even Brahma cannot destroy ignorance (duhkha ucchittih'). He cannot attain realization of full sweet bliss. Liberation characterized by destruction of suffering and attainment of the highest bliss can be attained only by your mercy.

“It is said that liberation is attained by practice of jnana and vairagya.” Without your mercy, performance of sadhanas suitable for liberation do not occur. By your mercy alone Brahma performed sadhanas for liberation. It is not otherwise. If that is so what to speak of other sadhanas? Thus, 1 pray always for a drop of your mercy. The alankara is tulya-yogita. Brahma says:

*tatte'nukampāṁ susamīkṣyamāṇo bhuñjāna evātmakṛtaṁ vipākam \| hṛdvāgvapurbhirvidadhannamaste jīveta yo muktipade sa dāyabhāk \|\|*

**My dear Lord, one who earnestly waits for you to bestow your causeless mercy upon him, all the while patiently suffering the reactions of his past misdeeds and offering you respectful obeisances with his heart, words and body, is surely eligible for liberation, for it has become his rightful claim. (SB 10.14.8)**

*ajavalepandha-tamo-’ndha-caksusaeṣo'nukampyo mayi nāthavāniti*

**My eyes are blinded by the darkness of ignorance, which causes me to think of myself as the unborn creator of the universe. But please consider that I am your servant and therefore worthy of your compassion. (SB 10.14.10)**

*athapi te deva padambuja-dvaya-*  
*prasada-lesdnugrhita eva hi*  
*janati tattvam bhagavan-mahimno*  
*na canya eko ’pi ciram vicinvan*

**My Lord, if one is favored by even a slight trace of the mercy of your lotus feet, he can understand the greatness of your personality. But those who speculate to understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead are unable to know you, even though they continue to study the Vedas for many years. (SB 10.14.29)**

**matta-mātaṅga-līlā-kara-cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is matta-mdtanga-lila-kara. It is described as follows:

*yatra rephaḥ paraṁ svecchayā gumphitaḥ sa smṛto daṇḍako mattamātaṅgalīlākaraḥ*

**Dandaka with Isl (ra) repeated at will is matta-matahga-Itla-kara. (Vrtta-ratnakara)**

## atha govardhanoddhāraṇam

**Lifting Govardhana**

### Text 26

*amanda-mada-maṇḍalair alam akhaṇḍam ākhaṇḍalaṁ*  
*nyaruddha rabhasena yaḥ pṛthu-mudasya govardhanam \|*  
*acaṇḍakara-mādhurī-paṭala-daṇḍi-tuṇḍa-śriyaṁ*  
*tam ātta-vara-maṇḍanaṁ makara-kuṇḍala tvāṁ bhaje \|\|26\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I worship you, wearing makara earrings and fine ornaments, whose face of intense beauty derides the moon, who, lifting heavy Govardhana in joy, completely destroyed Indra, full of great pride.**

**Комментарий:**

The story of lifting Govardhana which will be described is summarized.

I worship you, wearing makara earrings. The intense beauty of your face derides the sweetness of the moon (acandakara). You wear excellent ornaments like armbands and bracelets. Joyfully (rabhasena') lifting heavy (prthu) Govardhana you completely (alam) destroyed Indra (akhandalam), full of strong pride (amanda-mada-mandalaih).

### 1

*hetu-vādaja-jalpita-vraja-vāsavādhvara-mardane*  
*bhūsurotkara-go-mahīdhara-pūjanotsava-vardhane*  
*parvatārcana-sampad-arjana-hetutā-paribodhake*  
*kalpitātula-sūpa-saṅkula-śaṣkulīdadhi-modake*

**Перевод:**

**May this fickle minded bee remain facing you, who destroyed Indra’s sacrifice by harsh words using logic, who increased the worship of brahmanas, cows and Govardhana, who explained the reason for increasing wealth by worshipping the mountain, who had the people make various sweets and many incomparable soups.**

**Комментарий:**

The story is told in detail, (last line) O Madhava! This also means spring. O supreme person! May the fickle minded bee (sillmukhl) remain facing you. Destroy aversion to you, as you destroyed Indra. Siltmukha is a bee according to Halayudha. Krsna is described. You destroyed Indra’s sacrifice by many strong words arising from logic.

“It is seen that sacrifices like kariri, putresti, and jyotistoma give results by positive and negative logic. The devata is an ahga of karma like ghee. Without karma, the devata does not give results, (negative) Prakrti, induced by the actions of a living being, produces clouds as a result by movement of rajas, and showers rain. (Positive) The nature of the moon is to shower water from the cloud, just as it showers snow. What is the use of Indra in all this?” To speak using dry logic is called hetuvada.

Using others ideas, Krsna made them disrespect Indra. That was his desire. He made them worship the brahmanas, etc., as Vedic worship. He exalted the worship of cows, and many (utkara) brahmanas (bhusura) and Govardhana, the best of devotees. He informed them of the reason for gaining wealth by worship of Govardhana.

*tasmādgavāṁ brāhmaṇānāmadreścārabhyatāṁ makhaḥ \|*  
*ya indrayāgasaṁbhārāstairayaṁ sādhyatāṁ makhaḥ \|\|*

**Therefore may a sacrifice for the pleasure of the cows, the brahmanas and Govardhana Hill begin! With all the paraphernalia collected for worshiping Indra, let this sacrifice be performed instead. (SB 10.24.25)**

*hūyantāmagnayaḥ samyagbrāhmaṇairbrahmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*annaṁ bahuguṇaṁ tebhyo deyaṁ vo dhenudakṣiṇāḥ \|\|*

**The brahmanas who are learned in the Vedic mantras must properly invoke the sacrificial fires. Then you should feed the priests with nicely prepared food and reward them with cows and other gifts. (SB 10.24.27)**

The mountain nourishes the cows with grass and water. We maintain our lives by the cows. He had them make sweets and soups for the worship of the brahmanas. The list of preparations also include rice, etc.

### 2

*puṣpa-vandana-dhātu-canadan-maṇḍitākhila-godhane*  
*gopa-maṇḍala-kalpitācala-sānukandara-śodhane*  
*udbhaṭārava-bhū-dharotsava-sañjitākhila-bandhute*  
*tat-parikrama-pūjana-krama-bhūri-sambhrama-sandhute*

**Перевод:**

**May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, who had them decorate the cows with flowers, sandalwood, red dye and minerals, who had the cowherds clean the caves and plateaus of Govardhana, who made your relatives attached to the festival of the mountain while they shouted loudly, who quickly had them perform the worship and circumambulate the hill.**

**Комментарий:**

He had them decorate the cows with flowers, sandalwood, red power (vandana) and minerals. He had all the cowherds clean the caves and plateaus of the mountain. He made all his relatives become attached to the festival of the mountain while shouting. He had them quickly perform the worship and circumambulate the hill.

### 3

*kṣmādharopama-vigrahottama-bhukta-visphurad-odane*  
*maṅgalākara-visphurad-vara-vṛnda-ballava-modane*  
*ruṣṭa-vāsava-vṛṣṭi-saṁplava-khinna-gokula-veṣṭite*  
*trāsa-saṅkula-bandhu-maṇḍala-śarmadādbhuta-cesṭite*

**Перевод:**

**May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, who took the form of a mountain and ate the resplendent food, who gave joy to all the excellent cowherds shining like auspicious mines, who was surrounded by Gokula which suffered the deluge from angry Indra’s rain, who performed astonishing acts to give happiness to all your relatives afflicted by fear of Indra.**

**Комментарий:**

Taking the form of the mountain he ate the resplendent food (odane). it is said:

*kṛṣṇastvanyatamaṁ rūpaṁ gopaviśrambhaṇaṁ gataḥ \|*  
*śailo'smīti vadanbhūri balimādadbṛhadvapuḥ \|\|*

**Krsna then assumed an unprecedented, huge form to instill faith in the cowherd men. Declaring, “I am Govardhana Mountain!” he ate the abundant offerings. (SB 10.24.35)**

You gave joy to the excellent cowherds who shone like auspicious mines.

You were surrounded by Gokula which suffered from the deluge caused by showers produced by angry Indra. You performed astonishing actions to give happiness to the group of friends disturbed by fear of Indra.

### 4

*dakṣiṇetara-pāṇi-puṣkara-śīlitātula-parvate*  
*vibhramāṅkura-nirdhūtoddhura-jambha-mardana-garvite*  
*gotra-gahvara-vāsitāb-bhara-vihvalātma-suhṛj-jane*  
*kāritodbhavadadbhūtārṇava-bāndhava-vraja-majjane*

**Перевод:**

**May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, who lifted the incomparable mountain in your left hand, who destroyed the pride of arrogant Indra by a sprout of your pastimes, who had your friends dwell in a hole in the mountain, who made your relatives drown in an ocean of astonishment.**

**Комментарий:**

His actions are described. You lifted the incomparable mountain by your left lotus hand. You destroyed the pride of arrogant (uddhura) Indra (jambha-mardana) by a sprout of your pastimes. You had your friends afflicted by rain (ambhara) live in the wide hole in the mountain. You made all your relatives sink in an ocean of astonishment.

### 5

*nanditāśaya-mitra-sañcaya-vīkṣita-sphurad-ānane*  
*medura-smita-kaumudī-kṛta-rakta-yauvata-mānane*  
*bhīta-nandita-vismayānvita mātṛ-pāṇy-upalālite*  
*cāru-cañcala-locanāñcala-rādhayāpi nibhālite*

**Перевод:**

**May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, whose shining face was seen by rejoicing friends, who responded to the attracted gopis with a soft moon-like smile, who was caressed by the hand of Yasoda who was astonishing, joyful and fearful, who was seen by Radha with her attractive, restless eyes.**

**Комментарий:**

Your shining face was seen by all your friends who rejoiced when free of fear of the rain. You acknowledged the attracted gopis by a soft moon-like smile. You were caressed by the hands of your mother who was astonished by your act, joyful on seeing your face and fearful of the mountain above. “How can this child, soft as butter, lift the mountain?” This was her astonishment.

You were gazed upon by Radha with her attractive restless eyes. Her crooked gaze indicated, “In this crowd Krsna looks at me and holds up the mountain. I will smile at him sweetly. By that may he be nourished to lift the mountain.” By that, both parties would be showered with rasa.

### 6

*mārutonmada-caṇḍa-nīrada-maṇḍalāśani-vāraṇe*  
*sampad-andhita-śakra-sañcita-garva-carvaṇa-kāraṇe*  
*sapta-vāsara-hasta-saṁstara-śāyitātula-parvate*  
*nirmadīkṛta-śakra-saṁvṛta-nīradekṣaṇa-nirvṛte*

**Перевод:**

**May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, who stopped the thunderbolts coming from masses of fierce clouds agitated by wind, who crushed the great pride of Indra, blinded by wealth, who kept the mountain sleeping in the bed of your hand for seven days, who by your glance cleared the clouds produced by Indra who gave up his pride.**

**Комментарий:**

You thwarted the thunderbolts released by Indra with fierce clouds agitated by wind. You were the cause of crushing the pride of Indra, blinded by wealth. How long did you hold up the mountain? For seven days you kept the mountain sleeping in the bed of your hand. By your glance you stopped the clouds furnished by Indra, who had been humbled (nirmadikrta). The howling wind stopped, and the sky became clear. The wind blew gently with fragrance. It would be good to leave the hole in the mountain.

### 7

*mañju-bhāṣita-mudrayā kṛta-bāndhavāvali-niṣkrame*  
*kautukoccala-mitra-maṇḍala-gīta-maṅgala-vikrame*  
*pādayojjvala-tan-nija-sthala-yojita-pravarācale*  
*sarvadā vraja-bāndhava-vraja-rakṣaṇa-vrata-niścale*

**Перевод:**

**May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, who with charming words had your relatives leave the hole, whose auspicious heroism was praised by all your friends overcome with joy, who placed the mountain in its previous place, shining with trees, who had firmly vowed to protect your Vraja relatives always.**

**Комментарий:**

Using charming words, you made all your relatives leave the hole. Your auspicious prowess was praised by all your friends who were intensely joyous. You placed the incomparable mountain in its place shining with trees. Why did you agree to do such great acts? You had made a firm vow to protect your Vraja friends always. Krsna himself says:

*tasmānmaccharaṇaṁ goṣṭhaṁ mannāthaṁ matparigraham \|*  
*gopāye  svātmayogena so'yaṁ me vrata āhitaḥ \|\|*
