**I must therefore protect the cowherd community by my transcendental potency, for I am their shelter, I am their master, and indeed they are my own family. After all, I have taken a vow to protect my devotees. (SB 10.25.18)**

### 8

*phulla-ballava-nāthayor nava-harṣa-vīkṣaṇa-sakṣaṇe*  
*kuṅkumākṣata-pallavākṣata-ballavī-kṛta-rakṣaṇe*  
*channa-bhānuni śaila-sânuni pīṭhita-pravarāṁśuke*  
*bhīta-lajjita-śakra-vandita-pāda-paṅkaja-pāṁśuke*

**Перевод:**

**May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, who became joyful on seeing the fresh joy of your parents with hairs standing on end, who were offered protection by the women who held kunkuma, rice, and leaves in their hands, who was enthroned by Indra on an excellently draped throne on a plateau of Govardhana, which eclipsed the sun, and who inspired Indra to bow to the dust of your lotus feet with fear and shame.**

**Комментарий:**

You became joyful on seeing the fresh joy of your parents (ballava-ndthayoh) whose hairs stood on end (phulla) because of joy at the heroic act of their son. “1 am happy having served my parents.” The women offered you protection, chanting svasti-vacana, etc., their hands full of (aksata) kutikuma, rice, leaves, and mango buds. Indra then came to victorious Krsna to surrender.

You were seated by Indra on a throne on a plateau of the high mountain, which covered the sun. Sdnu means an excellent cloth covered platform according to Amara-kosa. Indra established you on a jeweled throne beautiful with soft back pillow, spread with colorful silk cloth. The dust from your lotus feet was worshipped by Indra who was frightened and ashamed. “The Supreme Lord will be angry with me because of my great offense.” That was his fear. “Since I am his servant, this action was not proper for me.” That was his shame. Indra offered respects, saying “O Lord! Forgive my offense since I am your ignorant servant.”

### 9

*smera-saṁmukha-visphuran-mukha-lupta-vāsava-bhī-bhrame*  
*tan-manohara-varṇa-nirbhara-bhāratī-bhara-vibhrame*  
*go-śiva-pradam indratā-padam etya nirbhara-nandite*  
*gāyad-ambara-lambi-tumburu-rāga-ḍambara-vandite*

**Перевод:**

**May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, who dispelled Indra’s fear by your face shining in front of him with a smile, who attracted Indra with your charming, skillful words, who became overjoyed on attaining the position of Indra who gives auspiciousness to the cows, who was glorified loudly with ragas by Tumburu in the sky.**

**Комментарий:**

You smiled. “You have understood that I am the Supreme Lord.” Facing Indra, he said, “My desire has been fulfilled by your committing offense.” By his smiling face he dispelled Indra’s (vdsava) fear (bhi-bhrame). You were charming with skillful words full of syllables attractive to Indra.

*gamyatāṁ śakra bhadraṁ vaḥ kriyatāṁ me'nuśāsanam \|*  
*sthīyatāṁ svādhikāreṣu bhavadbhirdambhavarjitaiḥ \|\|*

**Indra, you may now go. Execute my order and remain in your appointed position as King of heaven. But be sober, without false pride. (SB 10.27.17)**

He pacified Indra, who had been frightened and ashamed, with his affectionate words. You were very pleased, attaining the position of Indra (indrata-padam) who gives auspiciousness to the cows (go-siva-pradam)

*ahaṁ kilendro devānāṁ tvaṁ gavāmindratāṁ gataḥ \|*  
*govinda iti lokāstvāṁ gāsyanti bhuvi śāśvatam \|\|*

**I am Indra of the devatas. You have become Indra for the cows. The world will glorify you as Govinda in this world eternally. (Hari-vamsa)**

You were praised with many ragas sung by Tumburu along with Narada in the sky.

### 10

*mugdha-saurabha-digdha-saurabha-dugdha-pūra-kṛtokṣaṇe*  
*kalpitākhila-piṣṭa-pātulatāpa-maṇḍala-mokṣaṇe*  
*matta-kokila-vibhrame kila mādhava tvayi sammukhī*  
*vartatāṁ mama puruṣottama lola-buddhi-śilīsukhī \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Madhava! O Supreme Lord! May the fickle minded bee remain facing you, who was bathed by Surabhi’s fragrant milk, who freed the devatas from incomparable suffering.**

**Комментарий:**

You were bathed (uksane) with Surabhi’s abundant milk, which was full of attractive fragrance. You freed the devatas (pistapanam) of incomparable suffering.

Your words enchant the intoxicated cuckoo. You speak with great charm.

### Text 27

*śyāmottuṅga-bhujārgale vinihitaḥ kṛṣṇena vṛṣṭi-cchaṭā-*  
*dhaitair dhātubhir eṣa tālakunaṭī-mukhyair girir gaur itaḥ \|*  
*śuddhāṣṭāpada-kalpitasya vipula-cchatrasya lakṣmī-bharaṁ*  
*bibhrad-gāruḍa-ratna-nirmita-mahā-daṇḍasya vibhrājate \|\|27\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**This mountain which is colored yellow by the minerals loosened by the massive rain and established by Krsna on top of his huge door-bolt, black arm, possessing the great beauty of an umbrella of pure gold with a huge sapphire handle, shines.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of its great beauty the author describes Govardhana held on the tip of Krsna’s left hand. This mountain established by Krsna on top of his huge door bolt black arm shines. It is made yellow by minerals such as tala and kunatl washed by the massive rains. An image is presented. It shines with a wealth of beauty of huge umbrella of pure gold with a huge stick made of sapphire (garuda-ratna). This is nidarSana alankara, because of similarity.

**mugdha-saurabhaṁ cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is mugdha-saurabha. It is described as follows:

*mugdha-saurabha-nāma dhehi rasau jajau ca bharau yadā*

**When there is Isl ssl sis sis Iss Isl (ra, sa, ja, ja, bha, ra) give it the name mugdha-saurabha.**

The poem has been written according to this. It is also called carcari.

## atha nandāpaharaṇam

**Abduction of Nanda**

### Text 28

*nandāpahāra-cakitasya kirīṭa-śṛṅga*  
*bhṛṅgāvalī-paricitaṁ salileśvarasya \|*  
*hṛdyaṁ sanandana-durāpa-parāga-gandhaṁ*  
*vande mukunda tava deva padāravindam \|\|28\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Mukunda! I offer respects to your lotus feet, whose charming fragrance is hard to attain by Sanandana, which were surrounded by the bee-like tips of the crown of Varuna who was fearful because of stealing Nanda.**

**Комментарий:**

Bringing Nanda from Varuna’s abode is described in summary.

О Mukunda! О lord! I offer respects to your lotus feet. The feet are described. They are surrounded by the bee-like tips of the crown of Varuna. Their fragrance is hard to attain for Sanandana and others. Varuna became afraid because he had taken Nanda. Cakita means fearful according to Halayudha.

### 1

*nīrādhipa-bhṛtyāhṛta-gopeśvara-mārgāśrita*  
*labdhāmbudhi-nāthālaya pāśīḍita-līlā-caya*  
*śuddhojjvala-vāṇī-sudha dāsāyita-pāśāyudha*  
*mantu-klama-saṁmārjana tan-nirmita-harṣārjana*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who followed Nanda, stolen by the servants of Varuna! О Krsna, who came to Varuna’s abode! О Krsna, who was worshipped by Varuna! О Krsna, who gave Varuna sweet, clear, pure instructions! О Krsna, who made Varuna his servant! О Krsna, who purified him of his offense! О Krsna, who was content with Varuna’s praise!**

**Комментарий:**

Everything is connected with the last phrase: О Damodara! Please protect me.

*kalārdhāṁ dvādaśīṁ dṛṣṭvā niśīthādūrdhvameva hi \|*  
*ā madhyāhnāt kriyāḥ sarvāḥ kartavyāḥ śaṁbhuśāsanāt \|\|*

**Seeing one half of a kala of dvadasl remaining, before night ends, one should perform all the rituals to be performed up to noontime, by the order of Siva.**

He followed the path of his father, who had entered the water to accomplish his Vedic rituals such as bathing before the sunrise, on the strength of scriptures. He was respecting the parana time of Dvadasi, where only a kala remained after fasting for Ekadasi. Nanda had been taken to Varuna’s planet by his servants, because they did not know the scriptural rules. He began to search for Nanda on being informed by his father’s servants. He arrived at the abode of the controller of water. He enacted a pastime of being worshipped by Varuna (разг). Pasi means Varuna according to Amara-kosa.

He gave sweet instructions, pure and clear to Varuna. He made Varuna his servant. He purified him of the sickness of his aparadha (mantu). He was satisfied (harsarjand) with actions of Varuna who had dasya-bhakti.

### 2

*bhakty-arpita-nandekṣaṇa labdhātula-citta-kṣaṇa*  
*pitrā saha gehaṁ gata-mātṛ-klama-hāri-vrata*  
*sarvādbhuta-sandarśana-cittānvita-nandānana*  
*saṅkarṇita-lokottara-tat-tan-nija-caryābhara-*  
*sambhāvita-sarveśvara-bhāvotsuka-gopotkara-*  
*hṛdyeṅgita-saṁvedana-saṅkalpita-tat-sādhana*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who glanced at Nanda with affection! О Krsna, who then experienced great bliss! О Krsna, who returned home with Nanda! О Krsna, who revived Yasoda from her lamentation! О Krsna, who decided to fulfill the affectionate request of the cowherds eager to experience your lordly powers after they heard from Nanda of the astonishing acts at Varuna’s abode.**

**Комментарий:**

You glanced at Nanda with affection. You experienced an incomparably happy heart on seeing him. The next two items are clear in meaning. Because of Krsna, Nanda became astonished (cittanvita) by seeing Varuna welcome his son (sarvadbhuta-samdarsanaih). He fulfilled the request that Krsna would show the cowherds his own abode, when the cowherds became eager to see Krsna’s lordly powers on hearing from Nanda Krsna’s remarkable worship and praise by Varuna.

### 3

*divya-hrada-madhyārpita-godhug-gaṇa-sandarśita-*  
*sac-cin-maya-lokottama niṣkāsita-gopa-bhrama*  
*sandhukṣita-bandhu-vraja sañcārita-kīrti-dhvaja*  
*gopī-gaṇa-śarmākara māṁ pālaya dāmodara \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who showed your spiritual abode to the cowherds after submerging them in Akrura-tirtha! О Krsna, who dissipated the illusion of the cowherds! О Krsna, who gave joy to your friends in Vraja! О Krsna, who fulfils the desires of the devotee! О Krsna, mine of joy for the gopis! О Damodara! Please protect me.**

**Комментарий:**

The method is explained. You showed the most astonishing place made of sac-cit to the cowherds after submerging them in attractive Akrura-tirtha. This was a special manifestation of Vraja. Sukadeva says:

*iti sañcintya bhagavān*  
*mahā-kāruṇiko hariḥ*  
*darśayām āsa lokaṁ svaṁ*  
*gopānāṁ tamasaḥ param*

**Thus deeply considering the situation, the all-merciful Supreme Personality of Godhead Hari revealed to the cowherd men his abode, which is beyond material darkness. (SB 10.28.14)**

*satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ yad*  
*brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam*  
*yad dhi paśyanti munayo*  
*guṇāpāye samāhitāḥ*

**Lord Krsna revealed the indestructible spiritual effulgence, which is unlimited, conscious and eternal. Sages see that spiritual existence in trance, when their consciousness is free of the modes of material nature. (SB 10.28.15)**

*te tu brahmahradaṁ nītā magnāḥ kṛṣṇena coddhṛtāḥ \|*  
*dadṛśurbrahmaṇo lokaṁ yatrākrūro'dhyagātpurā \|\|*

**The cowherd men were brought by Lord Krsna to the Brahma-hrada, made to submerge in the water, and then lifted up. From the same vantage point that Akrura saw the spiritual world, the cowherd men saw the planet of the Absolute Truth. (SB 10.28.16)**

He dispelled the cowherds’ illusion that there was a superior place to Vraja that they were seeing at present. He gave great joy to his friends in Vraja (samdhuksita).

Sukadeva says:

*nindādayastu taṁ dṛṣṭvā paramānandanirvṛtāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṁ ca tatra cchandobhiḥ stūyamānaṁ suvismitāḥ \|\|*

**Nanda Maharaja and the other cowherd men felt the greatest happiness when they saw that transcendental abode. They were especially amazed to see Krsna himself there, surrounded by the personified Vedas, who were offering him prayers. (SB 10.28.17)**

You satisfied the desires of the devotees (klrti-dhvaja). You are a mine of happiness for the gopis. О Damodara!

### Text 29

*loko ramyaḥ ko’pi vṛndāṭavīto*  
*nāsti kvāpīty añjasā bandhu-vargam \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhaṁ yaḥ suṣṭhu saṁdarśya bhūyo*  
*goṣṭhaṁ ninye pātu sa tvāṁ mukundaḥ \|\|29\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Mukunda, who, showing his friends Vaikuntha, made them realize that there was no more attractive place than Vrndavana, and again brought them to Vraja, protect you.**

**Комментарий:**

The author extracts the meaning of the episode.

There is no place as attractive as Vrndavana which you see. Showing Goloka included in Vraja, famous in scriptures for being situated above Vaikuntha to his friends, to make them understand that point, he removed their illusion and again brought them to present Vraja. May Mukunda protect you. If Vraja is a spiritual manifestation, why does it appear the opposite? One should accept that Krsna himself appears like a human child.

**saṁphulla-cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is samphulla. It is described as follows:

*chandas tād yato lau yadi saṁphullakanāmāñcati*

**Starting with Ils sll 11 (ta, ya, la, la) is called samphulla.**

The poem has been written according to this.

## atha rāsakrīḍā

**The Rasa dance**

### Text 30

*parisphuratu sundaraṁ caritam atra lakṣmī-pates*  
*tathā bhuvana-nandinas tad-avatāra-vṛndasya ca \|*  
*harer api camatkṛti-prakara-vardhanaḥ kintu me*  
*bibharti hṛdi vismayaṁ kam api rāsa-līlā-rasaḥ \|\|30\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the beautiful pastimes of the lord of Laksmi manifest in this world. May the pastimes of all avataras, giving joy to the world manifest. But the rasa of the rasa dance, increasing the astonishment of Krsna himself, cause indescribable astonishment in my heart.**

**Комментарий:**

The author describes how the rasa dance to be discussed is supreme among all pastimes. May all the pastimes of power concerning Visnu with Laksmi as described in the scriptures, manifest in this world. May the pastimes of all his avataras such as Narasimha manifest in this world. These are not astonishing to me. But the rasa of the rasa dance causes indescribable astonishment in my heart. That pastime increases the astonishment of the Lord himself, Krsna.

*santi yadyapi me prājyā līlāstāstā manoharāḥ \|*  
*na hi jāne smṛte rāse mano me kīdṛśaṁ bhavet \|\|*

**Though all my major pastimes in Vraja are attractive, 1 do not know what will happen to my mind when I think of the rasa dance. (Brhad-vamana Purana**

### 1

*śārada-vidhu-vīkṣaṇa-madhu-vardhita-mada-pūra*  
*iṣṭa-bhajana-vallabha-jana-citta-kamala-sūra*  
*gopa-yuvati-maṇḍala-mati-mohana-kala-gīta*  
*mukta-sakala-kṛtya-vikala-yauvata-parivīta*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, intoxicated by the honey of seeing the autumn moon! О Krsna, sun for the lotus hearts of the gopis dedicated to you! О Krsna, bewildering the gopis by the sound of your flute! О Krsna, surrounded by helpless gopis who gave up household duties!**

**Комментарий:**

You became more intoxicated by the liquor of seeing the autumn moon. You are the sun for the lotus hearts of the gopis who were dedicated to you. You make their minds blossom. The next line is clear. You enchant the gopis by the sound of your flute. You are surrounded by gopis who came, made helpless by the flute sound (yikala), giving up their household duties.

### 2

*yoṣid-amala-netra-kamala-lobhi-daśana-māla*  
*kautuka-bhara-nirmita-khara-narma-vacana-jāla*  
*tan-niśamana-sāśru-nayana-bhīrubhir abhinīta*  
*vallabha-jana-kheda-śamana-vibhrama-bhara-vīta*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, showing your teeth as you smiled out of greed for the pure lotus eyes of the gopis! О Krsna, who joked profusely with rough words out of joy! О Krsna, who lured the gopis who, hearing your words, wept! О Krsna, who skillfully pacified the lamentation of the gopis!**

**Комментарий:**

You showed your teeth in a smile expressing your desire for the pure lotus eyes of the gopis. You spoke intolerable, rough, joking words filled with crooked words expressing your joy. “Why have you chaste women come to the forest at night? This is condemned. If you say you came to see the forest in the autumn moon, that has been achieved. If you came to see me, everyone is attracted to me, not just you. Therefore, it is best to go home quickly.”

You brought the gopis who hearing your words began to weep. Bhlru means a woman according to Dhananjaya. They entreated him, “You should not speak to us in this way since we, surrendered to you, were called by you in the night.” With charm you pacified the gopis’ lamentation.

### 3

*śyāma-vimala-kānti-paṭala-dhūta-madana-lakṣa*  
*raktima-dhara-yoṣid-adhara-cumba-nasvana-dakṣa*  
*vigraha-pada-yauvata-mada-vīkṣaṇa-parilīna*  
*caṇḍima-dhara-bhakta-nikara-māna-bhuja-gavīna*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, causing hundreds of thousands of Cupids to tremble by your dark, pure beauty! O Krsna, expert at kissing the gopis’ coral-red lips! O Krsna, who disappeared on seeing the pride of the gopis, which was contrary to the dance! O Krsna, Garuda for the snake of pride in the angry gopis!**

**Комментарий:**

You make a hundred thousand Cupids tremble by your pure, dark beauty. With your gopi associates your beauty bewilders Cupid. You are expert at kissing the gopis’ lips, red like coral. Sukadeva says:

*iti viklavitaṁ tāsāṁ śrutvā yogeśvareśvaraḥ \|*  
*prasahya sadayaṁ gopīrātmārāmo'pyarīramat \|\|*

**Smiling upon hearing these despondent words from the gopis, Lord Krsna, the supreme master of all masters of mystic yoga, mercifully enjoyed with them, although he is self-satisfied. (SB 10.29.42)**

*tābhiḥ sametābhir udāra-ceṣṭitaḥ*  
*priyekṣaṇotphulla-mukhībhir acyutaḥ*  
*udāra-hāsa-dvija-kunda-dīdhatir*  
*vyarocataiṇāṅka ivoḍubhir vṛtaḥ*

**Among the assembled gopis, the infallible Lord Krsna appeared just like the moon surrounded by stars. He whose activities are so magnanimous made their faces blossom with his affectionate glances, and his broad smiles revealed the effulgence of his jasmine-bud-like teeth. (SB 10.29.43)**

*bāhu-prasāra-parirambha-karālakoru*  
*nīvī-stanālabhana-narma-nakhāgra-pātaiḥ*  
*kṣvelyāvaloka-hasitair vraja-sundarīṇām*  
*uttambhayan rati-patiṁ ramayāṁ cakāra*

**Sri Krsna went with the gopis to the bank of the Yamuna, where the sand was cooling and the wind, enlivened by the river’s waves, bore the fragrance of lotuses. There Krsna threw his arms around the gopis and embraced them. He aroused Cupid in the beautiful young ladies of Vraja by touching their hands, hair, thighs, belts and breasts, by playfully scratching them with his fingernails, and also by joking with them, glancing at them and laughing with them. In this way the Lord enjoyed his pastimes. (SB 10.29.46)**

You disappeared on seeing the gopis’ pride in their good fortune, who took shelter of a position which was contrary to the rasa dance. Vigraha means conflict according to Visvalocana. You were Garuda (yina) for the snake of pride in all the angry gopis, who thought “I am the best.”

“The rasa dance with unity can only take place when their pride is destroyed by separation from me.” Thus he disappeared.

Sukadeva says:

*evaṁ bhagavataḥ kṛṣṇāllabdhamānā mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṁ menire strīṇāṁ māninyo'bhyadhikaṁ bhuvi \|\|*

**The gopis became proud of themselves for having received such special attention from Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and each of them thought herself the best woman on earth. (SB 10.29.47)**

*tāsāṁ tarasaubhagamadaṁ vīkṣya mānaṁ ca keśavaḥ \|*  
*praśamāya prasādāya tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\|*

**Lord Kesava, seeing the gopis too proud of their good fortune, wanted to relieve them of this pride and show them further mercy. Thus he immediately disappeared. (SB 10.29.48)**

### 4

*lola-gatibhir ārta-matibhir ābhiranabhidṛṣṭa*  
*puṣpa-guruṣu valli-taruṣu bhūriṣu paripṛṣṭa*  
*labdha-nalina-gandha-pulina-gopy-anukṛta-līla*  
*śaśvad-amita-raṅga-ramita-rādhika vara-śīla*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, unseen by the gopis, full of pain, and trembling as they walked! O Krsna, about whom they asked the many creepers and trees laden with flowers! O Krsna, whose pastimes were imitated by the gopis on the bank laden with lotus fragrance! O Krsna, who enjoyed constantly unlimited pastimes with Radha! O Krsna, whose nature is most excellent!**

**Комментарий:**

You could not be seen by the gopis, in pain and trembling as they walked. They inquired about you from the flowering trees. Sukadeva says:

*antarhite bhagavati sahasaiva vrajāṅganāḥ \|*  
*atapyaṁstamacakṣāṇāḥ kariṇya iva yūthapam \|\|*

**When Lord Krsna disappeared so suddenly, the gopis felt great sorrow at losing sight of him, like a group of female elephants who have lost their mate. (SB 10.30.1)**

*gāyantya uccair amum eva saṁhatā*  
*vicikyur unmattaka-vad vanād vanam*  
*papracchur ākāśa-vad antaraṁ bahir*  
*bhūteṣu santaṁ puruṣaṁ vanaspatīn*

**Singing loudly of Krsna, they searched for him throughout the Vrndavana forest like a band of madwomen. They even asked the trees about him, who as the Supersoul is present inside and outside of all created things, just like the sky. (SB 10.30.4)**

Your pastimes of killing Putana, breaking the cart, etc., were imitated by the gopis on the bank fragrant with lotuses. Sukadeva says:

*ityunmattavaco gopyaḥ kṛṣṇānveṣaṇakātarāḥ \|*  
*līlā bhagavatastāstā hyanucakrustad-ātmikā \|\|*

**Having spoken these words, the gopis, distraught from searching for Krsna, began to act out his various pastimes, fully absorbed in thoughts of him. (SB 10.30.14)**

When he disappeared he took Radha with him. You constantly enjoyed unlimited pastimes with Radha. You had an excellent nature, responding to Radha, who had the most excellence.

### 5

*phulla-suṣama-vanya-kusuma-maṇḍita-dayitāṅga*  
*keli-talina-vaktra-nalina-bhṛṅgita-tad-apāṅga*  
*nirbhara-rati-vardhana-mati-nihnuta-nija-deha*  
*prema-śaraṇa-vallabha-gaṇa-mānasa-kuśa-leha*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who decorated Radha’s limb with beautiful, blossoming forest flowers! О Krsna, whose lotus face, the bed of pastimes, made Radha’s glance into a bee! О Krsna, who disappeared from her, thinking of increasing the rasa dance to the extreme! О Krsna, whose actions made the minds of the surrendered gopis auspicious!**

**Комментарий:**

You decorated her limbs with beautiful blossoming forest flowers. You transformed her glance into a bee for your lotus face, the abode of pastimes. Talina means bed according to Halayudha.

*tais taiḥ padais tat-padavīm*  
*anvicchantyo ’grato ’balāḥ*  
*vadhvāḥ padaiḥ su-pṛktāni*  
*vilokyārtāḥ samabruvan*

**The gopis began following Krsna’s path, as shown by his many footprints, but when they saw that these prints were thoroughly intermixed with those of his dearmost consort, they became perturbed and spoke as follows. (SB 10.30.26)**

*kasyāḥ padāni caitāni*  
*yātāyā nanda-sūnunā*  
*aṁsa-nyasta-prakoṣṭhāyāḥ*  
*kareṇoḥ kariṇā yathā*

**\[The gopis said:\] Here we see the footprints of some gopi who must have been walking along with the son of Nanda Maharaja. He must have put his arm on her shoulder, just as an elephant rests his trunk on the shoulder of an accompanying she-elephant. (SB 10.30.27)**

*anayārādhito nūnaṁ*  
*bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ*  
*yan no vihāya govindaḥ*  
*prīto yām anayad rahaḥ*

**Certainly this particular gopi has perfectly worshiped the all-powerful Personality of Godhead, Govinda, since he was so pleased with her that he abandoned the rest of us and brought her to a secluded place. (SB 10.30.28)**

Thus, the supreme position of Radha is proved. Without their minds being one, the rasa dance could not take place. He began to accomplish this. You disappeared thinking of increasing the rasa dance with their minds being one. You thought that you should disappear from Radha also to make their minds one. You acted in this way to make the minds of the gopis who were dependent on affection, auspicious. You acted for giving auspiciousness to all the gopis. To make their mind one for happiness in the rasa dance, you disappeared from all of them.

### 6

*dṛṣṭa-vikala-rādha-nikhila-yauvata-parihūta*  
*bhūri-rudita-tat-tad-udita-vīthibhir abhibhūta*  
*viklava-tanu-gopa-sutanu-locana-padavīta*  
*cāru-hasana pīta-vasana kuṅkuma-bhara-pīta*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, beckoned by all the gopis when they saw Radha suffering! O Krsna, conquered by the gopis as they wept intensely! O Krsna, who appeared to the disturbed gopis! O Krsna, with attractive smile, with yellow cloth! O Krsna, yellowed by abundant kuhkuma!**

**Комментарий:**

All the gopis called out to you on seeing Radha in distress. Sukadeva says:

*ity evaṁ darśayantyas tāś*  
*cerur gopyo vicetasaḥ*  
*yāṁ gopīm anayat kṛṣṇo*  
*vihāyānyāḥ striyo vane*  
*sā ca mene tadātmānaṁ*  
*variṣṭhaṁ sarva-yoṣitām*  
*hitvā gopīḥ kāma-yānā*  
*mām asau bhajate priyaḥ*

**As the gopis wandered about, their minds completely bewildered, they pointed out various signs of Krsna’s pastimes. The particular gopi whom Krsna had led into a secluded forest when he had abandoned all the other young girls began to think herself the best of women. “My beloved has rejected all the other gopis,” She thought, “even though they are driven by Cupid himself. He has chosen to reciprocate with me alone.” (SB 10.30.35-36)**

*tato gatvā vanoddeśaṁ dṛptā keśavamabravīt \|*  
*na pāraye'haṁ calituṁ naya māṁ yatra te manaḥ \|\|*

**As the two lovers passed through one part of the Vrndavana forest, the special gopi began feeling proud of herself. She told Lord Kesava, “I cannot walk any further. Please carry me wherever you want to go.” (SB 10.30.37)**

*evam uktaḥ priyām āha*  
*skandha āruhyatām iti*  
*tataś cāntardadhe kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*sā vadhūr anvatapyata*

**Thus addressed, Lord Krsna replied, “Just climb on my shoulder.” But as soon as he said this, he disappeared. His beloved consort then immediately felt great remorse. (SB 10.30.38)**

*anvicchantyo bhagavato māgaṁ gopyo vidūrataḥ \|*  
*dadṛśuḥ priyaviśleṣamohitāṁ duḥkhitāṁ sakhīm \|\|*

**While continuing to search out Krsna’s path, the gopis discovered their unhappy friend close by. She was bewildered by separation from her lover. (SB 10.30.40)**

Seeing Radha’s prema, the others gave up envy of her and thought with one mind. In this way Krsna, desiring the rasa dance, accomplished his wish. Without envy, they all called out, “O gem of rasas! Show yourself!” Radha acted in order to show the other gopis her auspiciousness. Krsna acted for producing happiness of the rasa dance by making their minds one. He fell under the control of the gopis who wept profusely.

*ayati te ’dhikaṁ janmanā vrajaḥ*  
*śrayata indirā śaśvad atra hi*  
*dayita dṛśyatāṁ dikṣu tāvakās*  
*tvayi dhṛtāsavas tvāṁ vicinvate*

**fortune, always resides here. It is only for your sake that we, your devoted servants, maintain our lives. We have been searching everywhere for you, so please show yourself to us. (SB 10.31.1)**

You appeared to the eyes of the gopis who suffered from separation. О Krsna, with attractive smile! О Krsna wearing yellow cloth! О Krsna, yellowed by excessive kunkuma! Sukadeva says:

*iti gopyaḥ pragāyanyaḥ pralapatyaśca citradhā \|*  
*ruruduḥ sukharaṁ rājan kṛṣṇadarśanalālasāḥ \|\|*

**О King, having thus sung and spoken their hearts out in various charming ways, the gopis began to weep loudly. They were very eager to see Lord Krsna. (SB 10.32.1)**

*tāsāmāvirabhūcchauriḥ smayamānamukhāmbujaḥ \|*  
*pītāmbaradharaḥ sragvī sākṣānmanmathamanmathaḥ \|\|*

**Then Lord Krsna, a smile on his lotus face, appeared before the gopis. Wearing a garland and a yellow garment, he directly appeared as one who can bewilder the mind of Cupid, who himself bewilders the minds of ordinary people. (SB 10.32.2)**

### 7

*nandita-mati-ghoṣa-yuvati-vāsasi viniviṣṭa*  
*tuṣṭi-racana-cāru-vacana-dhūta-hṛdaya-riṣṭa*  
*saṁmada-caya-phulla-hṛdaya-yauvata-tata-rāsa*  
*kunda-radanacāru-vadana-śobhita-mṛdu-hāsa*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, made to sit on the cloth of the joyous gopis! О Krsna, who destroyed the wounds in their hearts by your attractive, satisfying words! О Krsna, who began the rasa dance with the gopis whose hearts blossomed with great bliss! О Krsna, whose tender smile decorated a face attractive with jasmine teeth!**

**Комментарий:**

You were made to sit as the acarya upon the upper cloths of the gopis who were joyous on seeing you, to teach them the conclusions of prema.

*tad-darśanāhlāda-vidhūta-hṛd-rujo*  
*manorathāntaṁ śrutayo yathā yayuḥ*  
*svair uttarīyaiḥ kuca-kuṅkumāṅkitair*  
*acīkḷpann āsanam ātma-bandhave*

**Their heartache vanquished by the ecstasy of seeing Krsna, the gopis, like the personified Vedas before them, felt their desires completely fulfilled. For their dear friend Krsna they arranged a seat with their shawls which were smeared with the kunkuma powder from their breasts. (SB 10.32.13)**

You destroyed (dhuta) the injury (rista) in their hearts by attractive words which satisfied them. The son of Nanda is rough. When asked, “Why in the night have you abandoned us young girls who worship you,” you answered, “Since you gave up the authority of worldly opinion, of the Vedas and of your relatives for me, I for only a moment gave you up to increase your attachment for me.” They thought, “He still has not accepted our love, though we desire his benefit alone.” Seeing their dissatisfaction, he said, “I am indebted always to you, my pure devotees.”

*na pāraye ’haṁ niravadya-saṁyujāṁ*  
*sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṁ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ*  
*yā mābhajan durjara-geha-śṛṅkhalāḥ*  
*saṁvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā*

**I am not able to repay my debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahma. Your connection with me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped me, cutting off all domestic ties, which are difficult to break. Therefore, please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation. (SB 10.32.22)**

You gave them a spiritual answer. By that they were pleased. “You gave up the chains of household duties difficult to break and worshipped me. I cannot respond by giving up the same chains. Since I cannot fulfil the promise to respond as my devotees worship me, I am a debtor.”

He then performed the rasa dance with the gopis who were all of one mind, their hearts blossoming with heaps of bliss (sammada-caya) by his words which showed he was controlled by their prema. You smiled softly with a face, attractive with teeth like jasmines.

### 8

*dvi-dvi-yuvati-madhya-vasati-vardhita-ruci-kāmya*  
*labdha-lalitabhṛṅga-valita-campaka-tati-sāmya*  
*sva-sva-savidha-bodhi-vividha-veśa-yuvati-hṛdya*  
*śaṅkara-mukha-daivata-sukha-vardhi-naṭana-vidya*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, who attracted the gopis by your beauty, as you stayed between each pair! O Krsna, like a graceful bee among masses of campaka flowers! O Krsna, pleasing to the gopis dressed in various ways, who thought that you were with them individually! O Krsna, whose art of dancing increased the happiness of Siva and others!**

**Комментарий:**

You were most desirable because of your beauty which increased by being situated between pairs of gopis.

*rāsotsavaḥ sampravṛtto*  
*gopī-maṇḍala-maṇḍitaḥ*  
*yogeśvareṇa kṛṣṇena*  
*tāsāṁ madhye dvayor dvayoḥ*  
*praviṣṭena gṛhītānāṁ*  
*kaṇṭhe sva-nikaṭaṁ striyaḥ*

**The festive rasa dance commenced, with the gopis arrayed in a circle. Lord Krsna expanded himself and entered between each pair of gopis, and as that master of mystic power placed his arms around their necks, each girl thought he was standing next to her alone. (SB 10.33.2-3)**

It is explained that because of his swift movements he was simultaneously with each of them. You were like graceful bees on masses of campaka flowers.

*tatrātiśuśubhe tābhir*  
*bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ*  
*madhye maṇīnāṁ haimānāṁ*  
*mahā-marakato yathā*

**In the midst of the dancing gopis, Lord Krsna appeared most brilliant, like an exquisite sapphire in the midst of golden ornaments. (SB 10.33.6)**

You were attractive (hrdya) to the gopis dressed in various ways, who thought that you were with them personally. Your knowledge of dancing increased the happiness of Siva and other devatas. Your art of dancing astonished Siva and others.

### 9

*mohita-śaśi-maṇḍala vaśi-khecara-muni-yoṣa*  
*kiṅkiṇi-yuta-nūpura-ruta-lambhita-paritoṣa*  
*saurabha-pura-miṣṭa-khapura-rañjita-madhurāsya*  
*suṣṭhu-mahita-gīta-sahita-yauvata-tata-lāsya*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who enchanted the moon! О Krsna, who satisfied the Gandharvas and sages’ wives by the sound of your ankle bells! О Krsna, whose sweet face was tinged with betel nut full of fragrance! О Krsna, who danced with the gopis who sang praiseworthy songs!**

**Комментарий:**

You enchanted the moon by your dancing. You satisfied the Gandharvas and others living and moving in the sky, the wives of sages, by the sound of your ankle bells. To see the rasa dance, Lord Siva and others came, and enchanted by the bliss of the rasa festival, saw a portion of the pastime according to their qualification.

His servant Yogamaya covered the confidential portions. Sukadeva says:

*yaṁ manyerannabhastāvadvimānaśatasaṁkulam \|*  
*divaukasāṁ sadārāṇāmautsukyanibhṛtātmanām \|*

**The demigods and their wives were overwhelmed with eagerness to witness the rasa dance, and they soon crowded the sky with their hundreds of celestial airplanes. (SB 10.33.3)**

*tato dundubhayo nedurnipetuḥ puṣpavṛṣṭayaḥ \|*  
*jagurgandharvapatayaḥ sastrīkāstadyaśo'malam \|\|*

**Kettledrums then resounded in the sky while flowers rained down and the chief Gandharvas and their wives sang Lord Krsna’s spotless glories. (SB 10.33.4)**

*valayānāṁ nūpurāṇāṁ kiṅkiṇīnāṁ ca yoṣitām \|*  
*sa priyāṇāmabhūcchabdastumulo rāsamaṇḍale \|\|*

**A tumultuous sound arose from the armlets, ankle bells and waist bells of the gopis as they sported with their beloved Krsna in the circle of the rasa dance. (SB 10.33.5)**

*kṛṣṇavikrīḍitaṁ vīkṣya mumuhuḥ khecarastriyaḥ \|*  
*kāmārditāḥ śaśāṅkaśca sagaṇo vismito'bhavat \|\|*

**The wives of the demigods, observing Krsna’s playful activities from their airplanes, were entranced and became agitated with lust. Indeed, even the moon and his entourage, the stars, became astonished. (SB 10.33.18)**

Your sweet face was colored by betel nut mixed with cloves, laden with fragrance. Khapura means betel nut. You were made to dance by the gopis along with their most praiseworthy singing. Sukadeva says:

*uccairjagurnṛtyamānā raktakaṇṭhyo ratipriyāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇābhimarśamuditā yadgītenedamāvṛtam \|\|*

**Eager to enjoy conjugal love, their throats colored with various pigments, the gopis sang loudly and danced. They were overjoyed by Krsna’s touch, and they sang songs that filled the entire universe. (SB 10.33.8)**

*kācitsamaṁ mukundena svarajātīramiśritāḥ \|*  
*unninye pūjitā tena prīyatāṁ sādhu sādhviti \|\|*

**One gopi, joining Lord Mukunda in his singing, sang pure melodious tones that rose harmoniously above his. Krsna was pleased and showed great appreciation for her performance, saying “Excellent! Excellent!” (SB 10.33.9)**

### 10

*viśva-karaṇa-dhairya-haraṇa-kāraṇa-kala-gāna*  
*raktibhir uparuddha-paśupa-bhīru-kalitamāna*  
*kūji-valaya-tāṇḍava-laya-ghūrṇita-sura-rāji*  
*komala-raṇa-ṣaṭpada-gaṇa-guñjita-bhara-bhāji*  
*tatra rahasi rāsa-mahasi saṁbhṛta-vara-śobha*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, whose soft songs made the devatas lose control of their senses! О Krsna, honored by the gopis controlled by prema! О Krsna, displaying fine beauty in the dancing festival which was devoid of unqualified people, which stupefied Indra with its graceful dancing and jingling ankle bells, which was filled with the soft humming of bees!**

**Комментарий:**

Your soft singing caused the ears, eyes and minds of the devatas to lose control.

You were honored by the gopis who were controlled by anuraga. Sukadeva says:

*gopyaḥ sphurat-puraṭa-kuṇḍala-kuntala-tviḍ-*  
*gaṇḍa-śriyā sudhita-hāsa-nirīkṣaṇena*  
*mānaṁ dadhatya ṛṣabhasya jaguḥ kṛtāni*  
*puṇyāni tat-kara-ruha-sparśa-pramodāḥ*

**The gopis honored their hero with smiling glances sweetened by the beauty of their cheeks and the effulgence of their curly locks and glittering golden earrings. Overjoyed from the touch of his fingernails, they chanted the glories of his all-auspicious transcendental pastimes. (SB 10.33.21)**

He had fine beauty in the dancing festival which was devoid of unqualified people. (This line comes later in the text).

*trailokya-lakṣmy-eka-padaṁ vapurdadhat*

**His transcendental body, the exclusive abode of beauty and opulence within the three worlds, shone brilliantly as the gopis worshiped him. (SB 10.32.14)**

How was the rasa dance? It defeated Indra by the dancing with jingling ankle bells. It was filled with the soft buzzing of bees. It was filled with humming of bees attracted by the fragrance.

### 11

*mauktika-śuci-susmita-ruci-sṛṣṭa-yuvati-lobha*  
*mārjita-rati-khinna-yuvati-maṇḍala-mṛdu-gaṇḍa*  
*prema-lalaha-kāma-kalaha-paṇḍita-bhuja-daṇḍa*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, who incited the gopis’ desire by the beauty of your smile, bright like pearls! О Krsna, who wiped the cheeks of the gopis fatigued by amorous pastimes! О Krsna, whose arms were expert at amorous embraces desired in prema!**

**Комментарий:**

You incited the gopis’ desire for you by your beautiful smile shining like pearls.

You wiped the soft cheeks of the gopis who were fatigued by the enjoyment.

Your arms were expert at amorous embracing, which was desired in prema.

Sukadeva says:

*kṛtvā tāvantamātmānaṁ yāvatīrvrajayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*reme sa bhagavāṁstābhirātmārāmo'pi līlayā \|\|*

**Expanding himself as many times as there were cowherd women to associate with, the Supreme Lord, though selfsatisfied, playfully enjoyed their company (SB 10.33.19)**

*tāsāmativihāreṇa śrāntānāṁ vadanāni saḥ \|*  
*prāmṛjatkaruṇaḥ premṇā śaṁtamenāṅga pāṇinā \|\|*

**Seeing that the gopis were fatigued from conjugal enjoyment, my dear King, merciful Krsna lovingly wiped their faces with his comforting hand. (SB 10.33.20)**

### 12

*vibhrama-para-valgu-nakhara-cihnita-nava-vāma*  
*sauṣṭhava-yuta-kāntibhir uta kāma-manasi-kāma*  
*śīta-salila-keli-kalila-citta-yuvati-sikta*  
*dīvyad-acira-jāta-rucira-dīptibhir atirikta*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, who marked the young gopis with your charming nails inclined to amorous actions! O Krsna, who was praised by the excellent beautiful women! O Krsna, who was Cupid in Cupid’s mind! O Krsna, splashed by the gopis whose hearts were absorbed in playing in the cool water! O Krsna, becoming more beautiful by shining splendor of long-lasting charm! You marked the breasts of the young gopis with your charming nails attached to amorous acts. Bahu-prasara-parirambha: Krsna threw his arms around the gopis and embraced them. (SB 10.29.46) You are known (uta) by your excellent beloveds. The root is uh. You are the Cupid in Cupid’s mind (kama-manasi-kama). This means that you are more beautiful than Cupid.**

**Комментарий:**

*saksan manmatha-manmathah*

**He directly appeared as one who can bewilder the mind of Cupid. (SB 10.32.2)**

The water pastimes are described. You were splashed by the gopis whose hearts were absorbed in playing in the cool water. You became even more beautiful by the shining splendor with long-lasting charm.

### 13

*deva-vicita-puṣpa-racita-vṛṣṭibhir abhivṛṣṭa*  
*prema-sarala-keli-tarala-goṣṭha-sutanu-dṛṣṭa*  
*visphurad-ibha-nāyaka-nibha mañjula-jala-khela*  
*cañcala-kara-puṣkara-vara-kṛṣṭa-yuvati-cela*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, showered with flowers by the devatas! O Krsna, gazed upon by the gopis fickle in pastimes and sincere in love! O Krsna, shining like the king of the elephants! O Krsna, charming at playing in the water! O Krsna, who pulled the gopis’ clothing with your excellent, fickle lotus hand!**

**Комментарий:**

You were showered with a rain of flowers from the devatas. You were gazed upon by the gopis fickle in the pastimes and sincere in their prema. Yow were like a brilliant king of elephants. You performed charming pastimes in the water. You pulled the clothing of the gopis by your excellent fickle lotus hand. It was like an elephant trunk (puskara). Puskara means a lotus and the tip of the trunk of an elephant according to Halayudha.

### 14

*ratna-bhavana-sannibha-vana-kuñja-vihita-raṅga*  
*rāga-nirata-yauvata-rati-cihna-vilasad-aṅga*  
*sandhṛta-naya nanda-tanaya sundara jaya vīra*  
*yāmuna-taṭa-maṇḍala-naṭa rāsa-racana-dhīra*  
*pāpāni mayi durgati-jayi-pāda-bhajana-leśa*  
*dhehi karuṇa dṛṣṭim aruṇa-locana nikhileśa \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, performing pastimes in forest bowers resembling jeweled palaces! O Krsna, radiant with marks made by gopis absorbed in love! O Krsna, whose conduct is governed by prema! O son of Nanda! O beautiful Krsna! O valiant Krsna! May you manifest all excellence! O Krsna, dancing in a circle on the bank of the Yamuna! O Krsna, skillful at making the rasa dance! O Krsna, a particle of whose worship destroys ignorance! Glance upon this sinful person! Ocean of mercy! O red-eyed Krsna! O lord of all beings!**

**Комментарий:**

You have pastimes in the forest bowers similar to jeweled palaces. Your limbs shine with the marks made by the gopis absorbed in love. Sukadeva says:

*so ’mbhasy alaṁ yuvatibhiḥ pariṣicyamānaḥ*  
*premṇekṣitaḥ prahasatībhir itas tato ’ṅga*  
*vaimānikaiḥ kusuma-varṣibhir īdyamāno*  
*reme svayaṁ sva-ratir atra gajendra-līlaḥ*

**My dear King, in the water Krsna found himself being splashed on all sides by the laughing gopis, who looked at him with love. As the demigods worshiped him by showering flowers from their airplanes, the self-satisfied Lord took pleasure in playing like the king of the elephants. (SB 10.33.23)**

*tataś ca kṛṣṇopavane jala-sthala*  
*prasūna-gandhānila-juṣṭa-dik-taṭe*  
*cacāra bhṛṅga-pramadā-gaṇāvṛto*  
*yathā mada-cyud dviradaḥ kareṇubhiḥ*

**Then the Lord strolled through a small forest on the bank of the Yamuna. This forest was filled to its limits with breezes carrying the fragrances of all the flowers growing on the land and in the water. Followed by his entourage of bees and beautiful women, Lord Krsna appeared like an intoxicated elephant with his she-elephants. (SB 10.33.24)**

Your conduct is governed by the principle of complete love as exemplified in na paraye’harn niravadya sarhyujam: I can never repay my debt to you. (SB 10.32.22) May you manifest your excellence (jaya). О Krsna dancing in the circle on the bank of the Yamuna. О Krsna, intelligent at making the rasa dance. A fragment of worship of your feet, following madhurya-rasa, destroys ignorance (durgati). Sukadeva says:

*vikrīḍitaṁ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṁ ca viṣṇoḥ*  
*śraddhānvito ’nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ*  
*bhaktiṁ parāṁ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṁ*  
*hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ*

**Anyone who faithfully hears or describes the Lord’s playful affairs with the young gopis of Vrndavana will attain the Lord’s pure devotional service. Thus he will quickly become sober and conquer lust, the disease of the heart. (SB 10.33.39)**

О ocean of mercy! Give a glance of mercy to me, most sinful. О Krsna with red eyes! О Lord of all!

### Text 31

*rambhorū-nikuramba-nirbhara-parīrambheṇa labdha-dyuter*  
*bibhrāṇasya taḍit-kadamba-vilasat-kādambinī-vibhramam \|*  
*krīḍāḍambara-dhūta-jambha-mathana-stamberamoru-śriyo*  
*rāsārambha-rasārthinas tava vibho vande padāmbhoruham \|\|31\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Lord! I offer respects to the lotus feet of you who desire bliss through the performance of the rasa dance, who attain beauty by embracing tightly all the gopis, who is mistaken for a mass of clouds playing with flashes of lightning, who derides the great beauty of Indra’s elephant by your many pastimes.**

**Комментарий:**

The author remembers what was stated.

O Lord! I offer respects to your lotus feet. The Lord is described. He desires always the greatest bliss caused by the rasa dance (rasarambha). How is that?

He attains beauty by strongly embracing all the gopis (rambhoru). Metaphor is given. One could mistake you for a mass of clouds playing with many lightning flashes.

*gāyantyas taṁ taḍita iva tā megha-cakre virejuḥ*

**Lord Krsna’s young consorts shone like streaks of lightning in a mass of clouds. (SB 10.33.7)**

You deride the great beauty of Indra’s elephant Airavata by your great pastimes.

**lalita-bhṛṅga-cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is lalita-bhrnga. It is described as follows.

**Know that lalita-bhrnga, attractive to the hearts of all poets, has the following pattern: Iss ssl sss sis sss Is (bha, sa, na,ja, na, ga, la)**

According to this the poem has been written.

## atha sudarśanādi-mocanam sankhacuda-nidhanam

**Liberation of Sudarsana and killing of Sankhacuda etc.**

### Text 33

*bibhrataṁ śravaṇa-sīmni śāradaṁ*  
*padmam ujjvala-kalā-viśāradam \|*  
*ballavī-hṛdaya-hāra-nāyakaṁ*  
*hanta citta bhaja goṣṭha-nāyakam \|\|33\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О mind! Worship Krsna, the prince of Vraja, wearing a lotus in his ear, skillful in the arts of madhurya-rasa, the center jewel on the hearts of the gopis!**

**Комментарий:**

The author describes freeing Sudarsana, which will then be described in more detail. Hanta indicates joy! О mind! Worship Krsna, the prince of Vraja (gostha-nayakam)\\ He wears a lotus on his ear. He is skillful in arts of madhurya-rasa (ujjvala-kala). The rest is clear.

### 1

*bhūruhollasad-ambikā-vana-maṇḍalāntara-bhūmi-pāvanam*  
*abja-sambhava-kanyakodaka-nirmitāplavam akṣi-modaka-*  
*vāridojjvala-kānti-ḍambaram āpta-kāñcana-bhāsva-dambaram*  
*ātta-ballava-rāḍ-bhujaṅgama-mūrti-kalpita-pāda-saṅgamam*

**Перевод:**

**I take shelter of you, who purified the land of Ambika forest beautiful with trees, who bathed in the water of the Sarasvatl River, whose beauty gave more pleasure to the eye than a cloud, who wore cloth shining like gold, who touched the snake that was swallowing Nanda’s foot.**

**Комментарий:**

I take shelter of you, О Syamasundara, conquering collyrium by your shining beauty! The phrases are related to this sentence in the seventh line. You purify the land in the forest of Ambika at the edge of Mathura, beautiful with trees, by your feet when you walk there. You bathed (plavam) in the water of the Sarasvatl which flowed there. You talked to the gopis who also bathed there. You spread dazzling beauty which gave more bliss to the eyes than a cloud (yarida). When all people gazed at your beauty like a mass of clouds, you touched the gopis. The cloth you wore shone like gold. Your foot touched the body of the snake which had swallowed (dtta) Nanda’s (ballava-rad) foot. You touched the snake with your foot.

### 2

*ugra-saṅkaṭa-bhāk-sudarśana-śāpa-mocanam iṣṭa-darśanam*  
*ātma-vallabha-nanda-mocanam uddhṛtākhila-bandhu-śocanam*  
*āśrayāmi bhavantam ujjvala-kānti-kandala-dhūta-kajjalam*

**Перевод:**

**I take shelter of you, who freed Sudarsana from Angira’s curse of being a snake, who showed your pleasing form to him, who freed Nanda from the snake, who delivered your relatives from lamentation, whose shining beauty defeats collyrium.**

**Комментарий:**

Then what happened? You freed Sudarsana from the curse which caused great problems for him. He had obtained birth as a snake because of the curse of ferocious Ahgira (ugra). He was relieved of his snake body given by Angira and became the Vidyadhara named Sudarsana. He was able to see your pleasing form (ista-dasanam). You freed Nanda (dtma-vallabha) from the snake. You delivered all the relatives from lamenting for Nanda’s suffering. Thus, freeing Sudarsana has been described. Sukadeva says:

*ekadā devayātrāyāṁ gopālā jātakautukāḥ \|*  
*anobhiranaḍuḍyuktaiḥ prayayuste'mbikāvanam \|\|*

**One day the cowherd men, eager to take a trip to worship Lord Siva, traveled by bullock carts to the Ambika forest. (SB 10.34.1)**

*tatra snātvā sarasvatyāṁ devaṁ paśupatiṁ vibhum \|*  
*ānarcurahaṇairbhaktyā devī ca nṛpate'mbikām \|\|*

**О King, after arriving there, they bathed in the Sarasvati and then devotedly worshiped with various paraphernalia the powerful Lord Pasupati and his consort, goddess Ambika. (SB 10.34.2)**

*gāvo hiraṇyaṁ vāsāṁsi madhumadhvannamādṛtāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyo daduḥ prītā devo naḥ prīyatāmiti \|\|*

**The cowherd men gave the brahmanas gifts of cows, gold, clothing and cooked grains mixed with honey. Then the cowherds prayed, “May the lord be pleased with us.” (SB 10.34.3)**

*ūṣuḥ sarasvatītīre jalaṁ prāśya dhṛtavratāḥ \|*  
*rajanīṁ tāṁ mahābhāgā nandasannandakādayaḥ \|\|*

**Nanda, Sunanda and the other greatly fortunate cowherds spent that night on the bank of the Sarasvati, strictly observing their vows. They fasted, taking only water. (SB 10.34.4)**

*kaścinmahānahistasminvipine'tibubhukṣitaḥ \|*  
*yadṛcchayāgato nandaṁ śayānamurago'grasīta \|\|*

**During the night a huge and extremely hungry snake appeared in that thicket. Slithering on his belly up to the sleeping Nanda Maharaja, the snake began swallowing him. (SB 10.34.5)**

*sa cukrośāhinā grastaḥ kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahānayam \|*  
*sarpo māṁ grasate tāta prapannaṁ parimocaya \|\|*

**In the clutches of the snake, Nanda Maharaja cried out, “Krsna, Krsna, my dear boy! This huge serpent is swallowing me! Please save me, who am surrendered to you!” (SB 10.34.6)**

*tasya cākranditaṁ śrutvā gopālāḥ sahasotthitāḥ \|*  
*grastaṁ ca dṛṣṭvā vibhrāntāḥ sarve vivyadhurulmukaiḥ \|\|*

**When the cowherd men heard the cries of Nanda, they immediately rose up and saw that he was being swallowed. Distraught, they beat the serpent with blazing torches. (SB 10.34.7)**

*alātairhanyamāno'pi nāmuñcattamuraṁgamaḥ \|*  
*tamaspṛśatpadābhyetya bhagavānsātvatāṁ patiḥ \|\|*

**But even though the firebrands were burning him, the serpent would not release Nanda Maharaja. Then the Supreme Lord Krsna, master of his devotees, came to the spot and touched the snake with his foot. (SB 10.34.8)**

*sa vai bhagavataḥ śrīmatpādasparśahatāśubhaḥ \|*  
*bheje sarpavapurhitvā rūpaṁ vidyādharārcitam \|\|*

**The snake had all his sinful reactions destroyed by the touch of the Supreme Lord’s divine foot, and thus he gave up his serpent body and appeared in the form of a worshipable Vidyadhara. (SB 10.34.9)**

*tamapṛcchaddhṛṣīkeśaḥ praṇata samavasthitam \|*  
*dīpyamānena vapuṣā puruṣaṁ hemamālinam \|\|*

**The Supreme Lord Hrsikesa then questioned this personality, who was standing before him with his head bowed, his brilliantly effulgent body bedecked with golden necklaces. (SB 10.34.10)**

*ko bhavānparayā lakṣmyā rocate'dbhutadarśanaḥ \|*  
*kathaṁ jugupsitāmetāṁ gatiṁ vā prāpito'vaśaḥ \|\|*

**\[Lord Krsna said:\] My dear sir, you appear so wonderful, glowing with such great beauty. Who are you? And who forced you to assume this terrible body of a snake? (SB 10.34.11)**

*śāpo me'nugrahāyaivakṛtastaiḥ karuṇātmabhiḥ \|*  
*yadahaṁ lokaguruṇā padā spṛṣṭo hatāśubhaḥ \|\|*

**It was actually for my benefit that those merciful sages cursed me, since now I have been touched by the foot of the supreme spiritual master of all the worlds and have thus been relieved of all inauspiciousness. (SB 10.34.14)**

*ityanujñāpya dāśārhaṁ parikramyābhivandya ca \|*  
*sudarśano divaṁ yātaḥ kṛcchrānnandaśca mocitaḥ \|\|*

**Thus receiving the permission of Lord Krsna, the demigod Sudarsana circumambulated him, bowed down to offer him homage and then returned to his heavenly planet. Nanda Maharaja was thus delivered from peril. (SB 10.34.18)**

### 3

*mānitojjvala-śarvarī-mukham āpta-pūrvaja-saṅgam unmukha-*  
*ballavākhila-vallabhātula-netra-khañjana-vibhramākulam*  
*adbhutāmala-gīta-mohita-ballavī-kulam ātta-lohita-*  
*candanaṁ khala-yakṣa-nāyaka-bhīti-yauvata-śānti-dāyakam*

**Перевод:**

**I praise you, whose face was worshipped by the night, who was accompanied by Balarama, who became agitated by the khanjana bird eyes of all the gopis facing you, who enchanted the gopis with an astonishing pure song, who wore kunkuma and who pacified the gopis fearful of the wicked leader of the Yaksas.**

**Комментарий:**

The author describes the killing of Sankhacuda. The words are all connected to the sentence in the last line of the poem. О Krsna whose lotus feet are worshipped kings of the universe! О Krsna, giving benefit to the gopis! О Madhava! О lord of the universe! I praise you. Protect me, most miserable (durgatam).

Krsna is described. Your face is worshipped by the splendorous night. You had gone with the gopis for Horika festival pastimes at the edge of Govardhana in the evening of spring full moon. You were accompanied by Balarama as well as the gopis. You became bewildered by the playing of the khanjana bird eyes of the gopis facing you. Your heart was pierced by their glances. You bewildered the gopis by an astonishing pure song. You sung a song suitable for Horika. You wore kunkuma. Saying “Do not fear,” you pacified the gopis who were fearful of the wicked Yaksa Sankhacuda who came among them.

### 4

*ugra-vigraha-yakṣa-mardanam aṅganā-gaṇa-raṅga-vardhanam*  
*āpta-guhyaka-ratna-nandita-pūrvajaṁ bhuvanendra-vandita-*  
*pāda-padma bhavantam āhita-gokulotsavam aṅganāhita*  
*naumi mādhava māṁ kṛpālaya durgataṁ jagadīśa pālaya \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I praise you, who killed the huge Yaksa, who increased the joy of the gopis, who gave joy to Balarama by giving him the Yaksa’s gem, who gave joy to Gokula. О Krsna whose lotus feet are worshipped by kings of the universe! О Krsna, giving benefit to the gopis! О Madhava! О lord of the universe! О abode of mercy! I praise you. Protect me, most miserable!**

**Комментарий:**

How did you pacify them? You killed the huge Yaksa (ugra-vigrahd). You increased the joy of the gopis. You gave joy to Balarama by offering him Sankhacuda’s jewel. You gave Balarama the Syamantaka jewel. Sukadeva says:

*kadācidatha govindo rāmaścādbhutavikramaḥ \|*  
*vijahnaturvane rājyāṁ madhyagau vrajayoṣitām \|\|*

**Once Lord Govinda and Lord Rama, the performers of wonderful feats, were playing in the forest at night with the young girls of Vraja. (SB 10.34.20)**

*niśā-mukhaṁ mānayantāv*  
*uditoḍupa-tārakam*  
*mallikā-gandha-mattāli-*  
*juṣṭaṁ kumuda-vāyunā*

**The two Lords praised the nightfall, signaled by the rising of the moon and the appearance of stars, a lotus-scented breeze and bees intoxicated by the fragrance of jasmine flowers. (SB 10.34.22)**

*evaṁ vikrīḍatoḥ khairaṁ gāyatoḥ saṁpramattavat \|*  
*śaṅkhacūḍa iti khyāto dhanā dānucaro'bhyagāt \|\|*

**While Lord Krsna and Lord Balarama thus played according to their own sweet will and sang to the point of apparent intoxication, a servant of Kuvera named Sankhactida came upon the scene. (SB 10.34.25)**

*tayonirīkṣato rājaṁstannāthaṁ pramadājanam \|*  
*kośantaṁ kālayāmāsa diśyudīcyāmaśaṅkitaḥ \|\|*

**О King, even as the two Lords looked on, Sankhactida brazenly began driving the women off toward the north. The women, who had accepted Krsna and Balarama as their Lords, began to cry out to them. (SB 10.34.26)**

*tamanvadhāvadgovindo yatra yatra sa dhāvati \|*  
*jihīrṣustacchiroratnaṁ tasthau rakṣanstriyo balaḥ \|\|*

**Lord Govinda chased the demon wherever he ran, eager to take his crest jewel. Meanwhile Lord Balarama stayed with the women to protect them. (SB 10.34.30)**

*avidūra ivābhyetya śirastasya durātmanaḥ \|*  
*jahāra muṣṭinaivāṅga saha cūḍāmāṇiṁ vibhuḥ \|\|*

**The mighty Lord overtook Sankhacuda from a great distance as if from nearby, my dear King, and then with his fist the Lord removed the wicked demon’s head, together with his crest jewel. (SB 10.34.31)**

*śaṅkhacūḍaṁ nihatyaivaṁ maṇimādāya bhāsvaram \|*

**Having thus killed the demon Sankhacuda and taken away his shining jewel, Lord Krsna gave it to his elder brother with great satisfaction as the gopis watched. (SB 10.34.32)**

You create auspiciousness for the gopis (anganahita). This suggests that the jewel should be given to the most excellent person as a prize. It should be given to Radha.

### Text 34

*jayati mahotsava-vidyā vidyādhara-śāpa-mardinī mūrtiḥ \|*  
*paribhūta-śaṅkhacūḍa-cūḍāmanṇir akhila-lokasya \|\|34\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The form of samvit possessing eternal bliss, the form who destroyed the snake form of the Vidyadhara, who killed Sankhacuda, who is the crest jewel of the whole world, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

The author remembers both pastimes. The meaning is clear.

Mahotsava-vidya means the form of samvit, having eternal bliss.

**kānti-ḍambara-cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is hanti-dambara. It is described as follows:

*kāntiḍambaram antato laghu pūrvato rasajaiśca vaibhavi*

## atha gopikā-gītam

**Song of the Gopis**

### Text 35

*niryāsaḥ śyāmalimnāṁ pariṇatir amala-prema-lakṣmī-bharāṇāṁ*  
*sākṣātkāraḥ kṛpāṇām akhila-madhuratā-saṁpadāṁ sampradāyaḥ \|*  
*gāmbhīryaṁ bibhramāṇām upacitir amitaś cāturīṇāṁ ciraṁ vo*  
*bhūyād ābhīra-nārī-kuca-kalasa-taṭālaṅkṛtir maṅgalāya \|\|35\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the glorious form, the ornament on the pot-like breasts of the gopis, who is the essence of black beauty, the bestower of unconditional love, the manifestor of mercy, the inaugurator of the path of all sweetness, the cause of inscrutable pastimes and unlimited expansion of cleverness, grant you auspiciousness always.**

**Комментарий:**

In describing the song of the gopis, the author describes Krsna, the subject of their song. May the glorious form, the ornament on the pot-like breasts of the gopis, Krsna, grant you auspiciousness. He is the essence (niryasah) of dark beauty. He manifests a dark form sparkling like a sapphire. He is the giver (parinatih) of causeless affection. He is the revealer of mercy. This means he is most merciful. He is the initiator (sampradayah) of the path of all types of sweetness. He is the cause of various pastimes (vibhratnanam) difficult to understand because of their various parts. He is an unlimited expansion of cleverness. He increases his cleverness in every pastime. The alarikdra is mala-rupaka (series of metaphors). Hetu alankdra is included in the statement. Krsna is the subject described with many unusual descriptive elements. He is like the sun, which rises and unlocks the lotuses.

### 1

*divasa-virahārta-yuvati-kṛta-vārta*  
*pṛthulatara-vāma-bhuja-śikhara-dhāma*  
*vilasad-avataṁsa vadana-dhṛta-vaṁśa*  
*sura-nagara-yoṣid-akhila-mati-moṣi-*  
*madhuratara-gīta paśu-nivaha-vīta*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, the object of discussion of the gopis pained by separation during the day! O Krsna, whose earrings shine about your broad shoulders! O Krsna, holding a flute in your mouth! O Krsna, whose sweet song steals the minds of all devata women! O Krsna, surrounded by herds of cows!**

**Комментарий:**

The gopis sing about Krsna alone. You are made the topic of discussion by the gopis pained by separation during the day. Your earrings shine on your broad shoulders. You have a flute in your mouth. Your sweet song steals the intelligence of all heavenly women. You are surrounded by herds of cows.

### 2

*sarid-udaka-pūra-virati-vidhi-śūra*  
*kamala-bhava-bharga-mukha-vibudha-varga*  
*mati-duranumāna-rasada-kala-gāna*  
*madayad-avaloka muṣita-nata-śoka*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, able to stop the flow of the rivers! O Krsna, whose soft, enlivening song cannot be understood by the devatas headed by Brahma and Siva! O Krsna, destroyer of the devotees’ suffering by your joyful glance!**

**Комментарий:**

You can stop the flow of the rivers like Yamuna. Your delicate song, giving rasa, is hard to interpret by the devatas headed by Brahma and Siva (bharga).

You destroy the suffering of your devotees by your joyful glance.

### 3

*hṛta-hariṇa-jāta kalita-sukha-vāta*  
*giriśa-mukha-deva kṛta-caraṇa-seva*  
*mada-janita-ghūrṇa-nayana rasa-pūrṇa*  
*gati-vijita-nāga dhṛta-ghusṛṇa-rāga*  
*yuvati-dina-tāpa-hara-madhura-lāpa*  
*caṭula naṭaveśa kṛpaya mathureśa \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, attracting the deer by your flute! O Krsna, standing in the pleasant, fragrant breeze! O Krsna, whose eyes roll from the intoxication of youth! O Krsna, full of rasa! O Krsna, whose gait defeats that of an elephant! O Krsna, colored by kunkuma! O Krsna, whose sweet talks destroy the suffering of the gopis during the day! O clever Krsna! O Krsna wearing a dancers dress! O lord of Mathura! Be merciful to me.**

**Комментарий:**

You attract the deer by the sound of your flute. You are fond of the breeze, cool, fragrant and gentle. The devatas headed by Siva bow to your feet. Your eyes roll with the intoxication of youth. You are full of rasa. Your gait defeats the elephant. You are anointed with kunkuma. Your sweet talks destroy the suffering of the gopis. O clever one! O lord of Mathura! Be merciful to me.

Sukadeva says:

*krsna-lilah pragayantyo ninyur duhkhena vasaran*

**Whenever Krsna went to the forest, the minds of the gopis would run after him, and thus the young girls sadly spent their days singing of his pastimes. (SB 10.35.1)**

*vāmabāhukṛtavāmakapolo valgitabhruradharārpitaveṇum \| komalāṅgulibhirāśritamārgaṁ gopya īrayati yatra mukundaḥ \|\|*  
*vyomayānavanitāḥ saha siddhairvismitāstadupadhārya salajjāḥ \|*  
*kāmamārgaṇasamarpitacittāḥ kaśmalaṁ yayurapasmṛtanīvyaḥ \|\|*

**The gopis said: When Mukunda vibrates the flute he has placed to his lips, stopping its holes with his tender fingers, he rests his left cheek on his left arm and makes his eyebrows dance. At that time the demigoddesses traveling in the sky with their husbands, the Siddhas, become amazed. As those ladies listen, they are embarrassed to find their minds yielding to the pursuit of lusty desires, and in their distress they are unaware that the belts of their garments are loosening. (SB 10.35.2-3)**

*vṛndaśo vrajavṛṣā mṛgagāvo veṇuvādyahṛtacetasa ārāt \|*  
*dantadaṣṭakavalā dhṛtakarṇā nidritā likhitacitramivāsan \|\|*

**He vibrates his flute, Vraja’s bulls, deer and cows, standing in groups at a great distance, are all captivated by the sound, and they stop chewing the food in their mouths and cock their ears. Stunned, they appear as if asleep, or like figures in a painting. (SB 10.35.5)**

*tarhi bhagnagatayaḥ sarito vai tatpadāmbujarajo'nilanītam \| spṛhayatīvaiyamivābahupuṇyāḥ premavepitabhujāḥ stimitāpaḥ \|\|*

**At that time the rivers stop flowing, their water stunned by the ecstasy they feel as they eagerly wait for the wind to bring them the dust of his lotus feet. But like us, the rivers are not very pious, and thus they merely wait with their arms trembling out of love. (SB 10.35.7)**

*savanasastadupadhārya sureśāḥ śakraśarvaparameṣṭhipurogāḥ \|*  
*kavaya ānatakandharacittāḥ kaśmalaṁ yayuraniścitatattvāḥ \|\|*

**Brahma, Siva, Indra and other chief demigods become confused upon hearing the sound. Although they are the most learned authorities, they cannot ascertain the essence of that music, and thus they bow down their heads and hearts. (SB 10.35.15)**

*kvaṇitaveṇuravavañcitacittāḥ kṛṣṇamanvasata kṛṣṇagṛhiṇyaḥ \|*  
*guṇagaṇārṇamanugatya hariṇyo gopikā iva vimuktagṛhāśāḥ \|\|*

**As Krsna plays his flute and sings, the music attracts the black deer’s wives, who approach that ocean of transcendental qualities and sit down beside him. Just like us cowherd girls, they have given up all hope for happiness in family life. (SB 10.35.19)**

*mandavāyurupavātyanukūlaṁ mānayanmalayajasparśena \|*  
*bandinastamupadevagaṇā ye gītavādyabalibhiḥ parivavruḥ \|\|*

**The gentle breeze honors him with its soothing fragrance of sandalwood, while the various Upadevas, standing on all sides like panegyrists, offer their music, singing and gifts of tribute. (SB 10.35.21)**

*vatsalo vrajagavāṁ yadagadhro vandyamānacaraṇaḥ pathi vṛddhaiḥ \|*  
*kṛtsnagodhanamupohya dinānte \|*  
*gītaveṇuranugeḍitakīrtiḥ \|\|*

**Out of great affection for the cows of Vraja, Krsna became the lifter of Govardhana Hill. At the end of the day, having rounded up all his own cows, he plays a song on his flute, while exalted demigods standing along the path worship his lotus feet and the cowherd boys accompanying him chant his glories. (SB 10.35.22)**

*madavighūrṇitalocana īrṣanmānadaḥ svasuhṛdāṁ vanamālī \|*  
*badarapāṇḍuvadano mṛdugaṇḍaṁ maṇḍayankanakakuṇḍalalakṣmyā \|\|*  
*yadupatirdviradarājavihāro yāminīpatirivaiṣa dinānte \|*  
*muditavaktra upayāti durantaṁ mocayanvrajagavāṁ dinatāpam \|\|*

**As Krsna respectfully greets his well-wishing friends, his eyes roll slightly as if from intoxication. He wears a flower garland, and the beauty of his soft cheeks is accentuated by the brilliance of his golden earrings and the whiteness of his face, which has the color of a badara berry. With his cheerful face resembling the moon, lord of the night, the Lord of the Yadus moves with the grace of a regal elephant. Thus he returns in the evening, delivering the cows of Vraja from the heat of the day. (SB 10.35.24-25)**

## atha ariṣṭa-vadhādi

**Killing of Arista**

### Text 37

*turaga-danu-sutāṅga-grāva-bhede dadhānaḥ*  
*kuliśa-ghaṭita-taṭaṅkoddaṇḍa-visphūrjitāni \|*  
*tad-uru-vikaṭa-daṁṣṭronmṛṣṭa-keyūra-mudraḥ*  
*prathayatu kuśalaṁ vaḥ kaiśavo vāma-bāhuḥ \|\|37\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna’s left arm, which manifested as a thunderbolt chisel to break the stone-like limbs of the horse demon, whose arm bands were polished by the demon’s vicious bites, bestow auspiciousness to you.**

**Комментарий:**

In describing the killing of Vrsa, Kesi and Vyoma, the killing of Kesi is described in summary in this verse since he was the most powerful among them. This was described in Virudavali. Because of being included in that work, it is not repeated in detail here. Uru-vikata, etc., in the third line is anukula alankara

since by using his teeth to bite Krsna’s arm he polished Krsna’s arm bands. It is said in Kavya-kaustubha:

*anukūlaṁ prātikūlyādyadi syādanukūlatā*

**If something which is unfavorable becomes favorable it is called anukula alankara.**

### 1

*vṛṣa-danuja-janita-ruja-paśupa-kula-toṣaṇaṁ*  
*svakaratala-ninada-khala-vṛṣabha-pariroṣaṇaṁ*  
*dayita-vara-bhuja-śikhara-nihita-bhuja-daṇḍakaṁ*  
*jagad-asukha-vikaṭa-mukha-danuja-mada-khaṇḍakaṁ*

**Перевод:**

**Worship the Lord who satisfied the cowherd people afflicted by the bull demon, who angered the wicked bull by the sounds of his hands slapping his arms, who placed his arm on the shoulder of his dear friend Subala, who demolished the pride of the demon whose gaping mouth distressed the whole world.**

**Комментарий:**

O heart! Worship the lotus-eyed Lord, (last line) The Lord is described.

He satisfied the cowherd families who were afflicted by the bull demon. What was the satisfaction? He angered the wicked bull by the sounds of his hands clapping his arms. He placed his arm on the shoulder of his very dear friend Subala.

He destroyed the pride of the demon whose gaping mouth caused sorrow to the world, by disregarding him.

### 2

*niviḍa-bala-caṭula-milad-anaḍud-apanodanaṁ*  
*gagana-tala-milad-akhila-sura-nikara-modanaṁ*  
*bhuja-vibhava-mahima-lava-dalita-vṛṣa-śṛṅgakaṁ*  
*tad-abhihati-dalita-diti-tanuja-tanu-bhaṅgakaṁ*

**Перевод:**

**Worship the Lord, who with skillful strength threw the bull far away, who pleased all the devatas who had gathered in the sky, who uprooted the bull’s horns with a particle of the great strength of his arms, who crushed the demon’s wasp-like body by beating him with the horns.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna, skillful with great strength, threw the bull (anadud) far away when he faced him. Krsna pleased the devatas who had gathered in the sky, by killing the bull. He uprooted the bull’s horns with a particle of the greatness of his strong arms.

The wasp-like body of the bull was destroyed by beating him with his two horns. He was destroyed like destroying an insect. Sukadeva says:

*atha tarhyāgato goṣṭamariṣṭo vṛṣabhāsuraḥ \|*  
*mahīṁ mahākakutkāyaḥ kampayankhuravikṣatām \|\|*

**The demon Arista then came to the cowherd village. Appearing in the form of a bull with a large hump, he made the earth tremble as he tore it apart with his hooves. (SB 10.36.1)**

*yasya nihrāditenāṅga niṣṭureṇa gavāṁ nṛṇām \|*  
*patantyakālato garbhāḥ sravanti sma bhayena vai \|\|*

**My dear King, clouds hovered about sharp-homed Aristasura’s hump, mistaking it for a mountain, and when the cowherd men and ladies caught sight of the demon, they were struck with terror. (SB 10.36.3)**

*nirviśanti ghanā yasya kakudy acala-śaṅkayā*  
*taṁ tīkṣṇa-śṛṅgam udvīkṣya gopyo gopāś ca tatrasuḥ*

**Indeed, the strident reverberation of his roar so frightened the pregnant cows and women that they lost their fetuses in miscarriages. (SB 10.36.4)**

*kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti te sarve govindaṁ śaraṇaṁ yayuḥ \|*

**The domestic animals fled the pasture in fear, O King, and all the inhabitants rushed to Lord Govinda for shelter, crying, “Krsna, Krsna!” (SB 10.36.5)**

*bhagavānapi taṁ vīkṣya gokulaṁ bhayavidrutam \|\|*  
*mā bhaiṣṭeti girāśvāsya vṛṣāsuramupāhvayat \|*

**When the Supreme Lord saw the cowherd community distraught and fleeing in fear, he calmed them, saying, “Don’t be afraid.” Then he called out to the bull demon as follows. (SB 10.36.6)**

*ityāsphoṭyācyuto'riṣṭaṁ talaśabdena kopayan \|\|*  
*sakhyuraṁse bhujābhogaṁ prasāryāvasthito hariḥ \|*

**Having spoken these words, the infallible Lord Hari slapped his arms with his palms, further angering Arista with the loud sound. The Lord then casually threw his mighty, serpentine arm over the shoulder of a friend and stood facing the demon. (SB 10.36.8)**

*so'pyevaṁ kopito'riṣṭaḥ khureṇāvanimullikhan \|\|*  
*udyatpucchabhramanmeghaḥ kruddhaḥ kṛṣṇamupādravat \|\|*

**Thus provoked, Arista pawed the ground with one of his hooves and then, with the clouds hovering around his upraised tail, furiously charged Krsna. (SB 10.38.9)**

*gṛhītvā śṛṅgayostaṁ vā aṣṭādaśapadāni saḥ \|*  
*pratyapovāha bhagavān gajaṁ pratigajo yathā \|\|*

**The Supreme Lord Krsna seized Aristasura by the horns and threw him back eighteen steps, just as an elephant might do when fighting a rival elephant. (SB 10.36.11)**

*so'paviddho bhagavatā punarutthāya satkharaḥ \|*  
*āpatatsvinnasarvāṅgo niḥśvasan krodhamūrchitaḥ \|\|*

**Thus repulsed by the Supreme Lord, the bull demon got up and, breathing hard and sweating all over his body, again charged him in a mindless rage. (SB 10.36.12)**

*tamāpatantaṁ sa nigṛhya śṛṅgayoḥ padā samākramya nipātya bhūtale \|*  
*nipīḍayāmāsa yathārdramambaraṁ kṛtvā viṣāṇena jaghāna so'patat \|\|*

**As Arista attacked, Lord Krsna seized him by the horns and knocked him to the ground with his foot. The Lord then thrashed him as if he were a wet cloth, and finally he yanked out one of the demon’s horns and struck him with it until he lay prostrate. (SB 10.36.13)**

### 3

*nija-nikaṭa-gati-vikaṭa-haya-danuja-locitaṁ*  
*praṇaya-bhara-mṛdulatara-yuvati-gaṇa-śocitaṁ*  
*avagaṇita-guru-raṇitaturaga-khura-ghaṭṭanaṁ*  
*nija-lalita-gati-kalita-tad-uru-mada-kuṭṭanaṁ*

**Перевод:**

**Worship the Lord who was seen by the fearful horse demon, for whom the gopis, tender with affection, lamented, who ignored the horse’s hoof blows and loud neighing, who crushed his pride by skillfully avoiding him.**

He describes the killing of Kesi. Krsna was seen by the horse demon Kesi, fearful to the devatas (vikata), who came towards Krsna. He was the cause of lamentation for the gopis, very soft with affection. Krsna ignored his stomping hooves and raucous neighing. He avoided his blows. He crushed his pride by skillfully avoiding him.

### 4

*dhanur-ayuta-parigamita-haya-danuja-vigrahaṁ*
