*tad-upacaya-vihita-haya-danuja-tanu-dāraṇaṁ*

**Перевод:**

**Worship the Lord, who threw the horse demon a bow’s length away, who punished the demon by putting his arm in the horse’s gaping mouth, who knocked out the teeth of the horse demon by his snake-like arms, who split the horse demon by expanding his arm in his mouth.**

**Комментарий:**

He threw the demon’s body a bow’s length away. He punished his life by putting his arm, like hot iron, in the horse’s gaping mouth. He knocked out Kesi’s teeth by putting his snake-like arms in his mouth. He split the horse demon’s body by expanding his arm.

### 5

*nija-lalita-lava-dalita-jagad-avaśa-keśinaṁ*  
*pramada-kula-rasa-caṭula-paśupa-sabha-veśinaṁ*  
*dara-hasita-ruci-ramita-nuti-catura-nāradaṁ*  
*giriśa-vara-nikhila-sura-nikara-sukha-bhāradaṁ*

**Перевод:**

**Worship the Lord, who destroyed Kesi, uncontrollable in this world, by a particle of his grace, who sat among all the cowherds who were trembling with the taste of joy and heroism, whom Narada, pleased with a slight smile, skillfully praised, who gave great joy to all the devatas including Siva.**

**Комментарий:**

He vanquished the horse, uncontrolled in the world, by a particle of his charming pastimes. He sat with all the cowherds who were sweet with the taste of joy and heroism. Sabha means all according to the sutra, asala ca: a tat-purusha compound ending with the word sabha, when it does not mean a house, but means concourse, is neuter. (Panini Sutras 2.4.24)After killing Kesi he met with his friends. He was skillfully praised by Narada, who was happy with the beauty of a slight smile. He was praised by joyful Narada. He gave great happiness to all the devatas among whom was excellent Siva. He made the devatas happy by killing Kesi who was very strong and a friend of Kamsa. Thus, the killing of Kesi has been described. Sukadeva says:

*keśī tu kaṁsa-prahitaḥ khurair mahīṁ*  
*mahā-hayo nirjarayan mano-javaḥ*  
*saṭāvadhūtābhra-vimāna-saṅkulaṁ*  
*kurvan nabho heṣita-bhīṣitākhilaḥ*

*taṁ trāsayantaṁ bhagavān sva-gokulaṁ*  
*tad-dheṣitair vāla-vighūrṇitāmbudam*  
*ātmānam ājau mṛgayantam agra-ṇīr*  
*upāhvayat sa vyanadan mṛgendra-vat*

**The demon Kesi, sent by Kamsa, appeared in Vraja as a great horse. Running with the speed of the mind, he tore up the earth with his hooves. The hairs of his mane scattered the clouds and the demigods’ airplanes throughout the sky, and he terrified everyone present with his loud neighing.**

**When the Supreme Personality of Godhead saw how the demon was frightening his village of Gokula by neighing terribly and shaking the clouds with his tail, the Lord came forward to meet him. Kesi was searching for Krsna to fight, so when the Lord stood before him and challenged him to approach, the horse responded by roaring like a lion. (SB 10.37.1-2)**

*sa taṁ niśāmyābhimukho mukhena khaṁ pibannivābhyadravadatyamarṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*jaghāna padbhyāmaravindalocanaṁ durāsadaścaṇḍajavo duratyayaḥ \|\|*

**Seeing the Lord standing before him, Kesi ran toward him in extreme rage, his mouth gaping as if to swallow up the sky. Rushing with furious speed, the unconquerable and unapproachable horse demon tried to strike the lotuseyed Lord with his two front legs. (SB 10.37.3)**

*tadvañcayitvā tamadhokṣajo ruṣā pragṛhya dorbhyāṁ parividhya pādayoḥ \|*  
*sāvajñamutsṛjya dhanuḥśatāntare yathoragaṁ tārkṣyasuto vyavasthitaḥ \|\|*

**But the transcendental Lord dodged Kesi’s blow and then with his arms angrily seized the demon by the legs, whirled him around in the air and contemptuously threw him the distance of one hundred bow-lengths, just as Garuda might throw a snake. Lord Krsna then stood there. (SB 10.37.4)**

*sa labdhasaṁjñaḥ punarutthito ruṣā vyādāya keśī tarasāpataddharim \| so'pyasya vaktre bhujamuttaraṁ smayan praveśayāmāsa yathoragaṁ bile \|\|*

**Upon regaining consciousness Kesl angrily got up, opened his mouth wide and again rushed to attack Lord Krsna. But the Lord just smiled and thrust his left arm into the horse’s mouth as easily as one would make a snake enter a hole in the ground. (SB 10.37.5)**

*dantā nipeturbhagavadbhujaspṛśaste keśinastaptamayaspṛśo yathā \|*  
*bāhuśca taddehagato mahātmano yathāmayaḥ saṁvavṛdhe upekṣitaḥ \|\|*

**Kesi’s teeth immediately fell out when they touched the Supreme Lord’s arm, which to the demon felt as hot as molten iron. Within Kesi’s body the Supreme Personality’s arm then expanded greatly, like a diseased stomach swelling because of neglect. (SB 10.37.6)**

*samedhamānena sa kṛṣṇabāhunā niruddhavāyuścaraṇāvudakṣipan \|*  
*prabhinnagātraḥ parivṛttalocanaḥ papāta leṇḍaṁ visṛjankṣitau vyasuḥ \|\|*

**As Lord Krsna’s expanding arm completely blocked Kesi’s breathing, his legs kicked convulsively, his body became covered with sweat, and his eyes rolled around. The demon then passed stool and fell on the ground, dead. (SB 10.37.7)**

*taddehataḥ karkaṭikāphalopamāhyasorapākṛṣya bhujaṁ mahābhujaḥ \|*  
*avismito'yatnahatārirutsmayaḥ prasūnavarṣairdiviṣadbhirīḍitaḥ \|\|*

**The mighty-armed Krsna withdrew his arm from Kesi’s body, which now appeared like a long karkatika fruit. Without the least display of pride at having so effortlessly killed his enemy, the Lord accepted the demigods’ worship in the form of flowers rained down from above. (SB 10.37.8)**

### 6

*uraṇa-datica-pala-mati-suhṛda-vana-khelanaṁ*  
*tad-apahṛti-milad-amati-danuja-kṛta-melanaṁ*  
*sva-sahacara-nikara-hara-danuja-kṛti-vedinaṁ*  
*jagad-abhaya-valad-anaya-maya-tanaya-bhedinaṁ*  
*sakṛd-amala-padakamala-vinata-bhaya-mocanaṁ*  
*bhaja sadaya-mayi hṛdaya sarasiruha-locanam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Worship the Lord who played with his fickle minded friends acting as sheep, who met the foolish demon who mixed with the boys, thinking of stealing them, who knew the demon’s intention to steal all his friends, who destroyed Vyomasura, unrighteous and fearless of the world, and who destroys ignorance of those who bow to his pure lotus feet. О heart! Worship the merciful lotus-eyed Lord!**

**Комментарий:**

Now the killing of Vyoma is described. Krsna played with his friends of fickle minds, who played at being sheep. Urana means sheep according to Halayudha. The foolish demon mingled with the group with the aim of stealing the boys. Krsna understood the intention of the demon to harm the boys (krti)—taking them away and sealing them in a cave in the mountain. He killed the son of Maya who was devoid of a particle of good conduct (valad-anaya), who was without fear of the world. He destroys ignorance of those who bow once to pure his lotus feet. Sukadeva says:

*ekadā te paśūnpālāścārayanto'drisānuṣu \| cakrurnilāyanakrīḍāścora pālāpadeśataḥ \|\|*

**One day the cowherd boys, while grazing their animals on the mountain slopes, played the game of stealing and hiding, acting out the roles of rival thieves and herders. (SB 10.37.26)**

*tatrāsan katicit pālāś caurāśca katicinnṛpa \|*  
*meṣāyitāśca tatraike vijahnur akutobhayāḥ \|\|*

**In that game, О King, some acted as thieves, others as shepherds and others as sheep. They played their game happily, without fear of danger. (SB 10.37.27)**

*mayaputro mahāmāyo vyomo gopālarūpadhṛk \|*  
*meṣāyitānapovāha prāyaścaurāyito bahun \|\|*

**A powerful magician named Vyoma, son of the demon Maya, then appeared on the scene in the guise of a cowherd boy. Pretending to join the game as a thief, he proceeded to steal most of the cowherd boys who were acting as sheep. (SB 10.37.28)**

*giridaryāṁ vinikṣipya nītaṁ nītaṁ mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*śilayā pidadhe dvāraṁ catuḥpañcāvaśeṣitāḥ \|\|*

**Gradually the great demon abducted more and more of the cowherd boys and cast them into a mountain cave, which he sealed shut with a boulder. Finally only four or five boys acting as sheep remained in the game. (SB 10.37.29)**

*tasya tatkarma vijñāya kṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇadaḥ satām \|*  
*gopānnayantaṁ jagrāha vṛkaṁ haririvaujasā \|\|*

**Lord Krsna, who shelters all saintly devotees, understood perfectly well what Vyomasura was doing. Just as a lion grabs a wolf, Krsna forcefully seized the demon as he was taking away more cowherd boys. (SB 10.37.30)**

*sa nijaṁ rūpam āsthāya*  
*girīndra-sadṛśaṁ balī*  
*icchan vimoktum ātmānaṁ*  
*nāśaknod grahaṇāturaḥ*

**The demon changed into his original form, as big and powerful as a great mountain. But try as he might to free himself, he could not do so, having lost his strength from being held in the Lord’s tight grip. (SB 10.37.31)**

*taṁ nigṛhyācyuto dorbhyāṁ pātayitvā mahītale \|*  
*paśyatāṁ divi devānāṁ paśumāramamārayat \|\|*

**Lord Acyuta clutched Vyomasura between his arms and threw him to the ground. Then, while the demigods in heaven looked on, Krsna killed him in the same way that one kills a sacrificial animal. (SB 10.37.32)**

*guhāpidhānaṁ nirbhidya gopānniḥsārya kṛcchrataḥ \|*  
*stūyamānaḥ surairgopaiḥ praviveśa svagokulam \|\|*

**Krsna then smashed the boulder blocking the cave’s entrance and led the trapped cowherd boys to safety. Thereafter, as the demigods and cowherd boys sang his glories, he returned to his cowherd village, Gokula. (SB 10.37.33)**

### Text 38

*yenāriṣṭaḥ prāpito’bhūd ariṣṭaṁ*  
*cakre keśī līlayaivāvakeśī \|*  
*vyomo’lambhi vyoma-sāmyaṁ sa kaṣṭād*  
*goṣṭhādhīśaḥ suṣṭhu gopāyatān naḥ \|\|38\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the leader of Gokula, by whom Arista met death, by whom Kesi’s plans became fruitless, by whom Vyomasura became void, easily protect us from danger.**

**Комментарий:**

Remembering these three pastimes in order, the author speaks.

May the leader of Gokula, Krsna, protect (gopayatat) us nicely. He is described. By him Arista met death. By him Kesi got scattered hair (avakesi) or had his plans made fruitless. Avakesi means barren or fruit according to Amara-kosa. By him Vyomasura became equal to the void (vyoma-samyam). All this was done as a pastime, easily (lllaya). This is the alankara of dipaka, in which three actions are related to one subject.

### Text 39

*apavarga-sukha-spṛhoru-vallī-*  
*sthala-kulaṅkaṣa-vīcir ambujākṣa \|*  
*tava keli-sudhā-nadī madīyaṁ*  
*śiśirāṅgī-gala-jāṅgalaṁ gatāstu \|\|39\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Krsna! May the sweet river of your pastimes, cooling to the limbs, whose waves demolish the assemblies having huge vines of desire for the happiness of liberation, arrive at the desert of my throat.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the pastimes of Vraja, the author prays with a desire to attain them.

O lotus-eyed Krsna! May the sweet river of your pastimes come (gata astu) to the desert of my throat. Jarigala means a desert according to Visvalocana. The river is described. It has waves which cut away assembly places with great creepers of desire for the bliss of liberation with predominance of one’s own powers. It cools the limbs, making one lose the desire for liberation.

**gucchakabheda chandaḥ \|**

The meter is gucchdka. It is described as follows.

*nikhila-kavi-kalita-ruci-śucitagaṇapañcakaṁ yadi tadanu ragaṇamanubhavati kila gucchakam*

**If there are five groups of na, shining with taste by all poets, followed by ra it becomes gucchaka. (sss sss sss sss sss Isl)**

According to this the poem has been written.

### Text 40

*puruṣottamasya parito*  
*gokula-caritāmṛtena kṛta-sekaḥ \|*  
*prema-maranda-syandaṁ*  
*tanotu mama citta-mākandaḥ \|\|40\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the mango tree of my heart, sprinkled with the sweet Gokula pastimes of Krsna, spread a river of sweet prema everywhere.**

**Комментарий:**

The author indicates steadiness in the pastimes of Vraja. May the mango tree of my heart distribute the river of honey of prema. Makanda means mango according to Visvalocana. The tree is described. It is sprinkled with the sweet Gokula pastimes of Nanda’s son.

## atha raṅga-sthala-krīḍanam

**Pastimes at the wrestling arena**

### Text 41

*kriyād vaḥ kalyāṇaṁ bhuja-samara-śauṭīrya-kaṇikā-*  
*vikāsenodbhūya prakaṭa-bala-malla-pratibhaṭān \|*  
*bhajan svairī raṅge mada-kala-mṛgendrasya lalitaṁ*  
*kacākṛṣṭi-krīḍā-mathita-mathurārir madhuripuḥ \|\|41\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May the killer of Madhu, who, after killing the very strong wrestling opponents with a particle of his valor in close combat and playing independently like an intoxicated lion in the arena, killed Kamsa and dragged him by his hair, grant you auspiciousness.**

**Комментарий:**

The author describes the pastimes at the wrestling arena in brief.

May the killer of Madhu grant you auspiciousness. He is described. Killing the very strong (prakatd) wrestling opponents like Canura by displaying a particle of his valor in close combat (bhuja-samard) he played like a furiously intoxicated lion. He jumped around like a lion, because he was independent (svan). By him, pulling Kamsa by the hair in play, Kamsa was killed.

### 1

*yaḥ paura-lokāravindāvalī-heli-raṅgī-kṛtottuṅga-raṅga-sthalī-kelir*  
*āpīta-kauśeya-śobhollasan-mūrtir āvartitāśeṣa-lokotsava-sphūrtir*  
*utphullalāvaṇyakallolinīsindhurādhijvarādhīnadīnāvalī-bandhur*  
*akṣīṇa-kaṇṭhīr-avākuṇṭha-vikrāntir ugraṁ mamardoru-dantīndram aśrānti*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord, a sun for the lotus-like people of Mathura, who accepted pastimes in the raised arena, whose form shone beautifully with yellow silk, who gave joy to unlimited people who returned, who was an ocean with swelling rivers of beauty, who was the friend of the miserable filled with mental anguish, who had the unlimited prowess of a strong lion, killed without fatigue the huge, fierce elephant.**

**Комментарий:**

He describes the pastimes in the arena using the seven vibhaktis, ending with the vocative. The seven phrases are related to the statement: without being tired (asranti) he killed (mamarda) the huge, fierce elephant named Kuvalayaplda at the gate of the arena. He is described. He was the sun for the people of Mathura, who were like a group of lotuses. Like the sun for lotuses he made the people of Mathura blossom. Heli means sun according to Haima. The next two phrases are clear. Ranga means the fighting arena. It is said that ranga means a place for dancing or fighting. He caused joy for unlimited people who returned. He was an ocean of swelling rivers of beauty. He was the friend of the wretched who experiences the fever of mental anguish. He destroyed the fever. He had the unlimited prowess of a powerful (aksina) lion (kanthirava). This is the first vibhakti (nominative).

### 2

*yaṁ nirmitottuṅga-mātaṅga-nirvāṇam urvī-mahānanda-vṛndāni kurvāṇam*  
*udbhāsi-dānāsra-bindūrmi-varmāṇam ānamra-santoṣa-nirmāṇa-karmāṇam*  
*unmīlitāstoka-vistāra-tāruṇyam antas tamastoma-vidhvaṁsi-kāruṇyam*  
*ālokayāmāsa bhinnāri-marmāṇam agre jana-śreṇir-uddāma-śarmāṇam*

**Перевод:**

**The crowd saw the Lord who liberated the huge elephant, who gave great joy to earth, who shone with a shield of the elephant’s blood and ichor, who gave satisfaction to the devotees, who manifested full youth, who by mercy destroyed inner darkness of ignorance, who broke the joints of the elephant, who gave unrestricted happiness to the citizens.**

**Комментарий:**

The crowd of people saw Krsna, who had liberated (nirvdnam) the huge elephant. The next phrase is clear. He had armor made of ichor and blood.

*aṁsanyastaviṣāṇo'sṛṅmada bindubhir aṅkitaḥ*

**With the elephant’s tusk perched on his shoulder (arhsa-nyasta-visano), fine particles of perspiration like drops of dew on his lotus face, and the drops of blood and ichor from the elephant. (SB 10.43.15)**

He gave satisfaction to the devotees. He shone with highly developed youth. He had mercy which destroyed inner dense darkness of ignorance. He had broken the joints of the elephant.

He gave unimpeded happiness to the citizens by killing the elephant. This is the second vibhakti (accusative).

### 3

*uddaṇḍa-dor-daṇḍa-darpānuviddhena vismāpitāmanda-gandharva-siddhena*  
*pīnāṁsa-piṇḍollasad-danta-daṇḍena vidyeti-gharmāmbu-saṁvīta-gaṇḍena*  
*dīptendra-nīlāvalī-rājad-aṅgena labdha-pralambāri-gopāla-saṅgena*  
*mallāvalī yena raṅga-praveśena vikṣobhitā maṅkṣu vīrendra-veśena*

**Перевод:**

**They saw him, by whom, with strong arms defeating Cupid’s pride, astonishing all the Gandharvas, the elephant’s tusk shining on his broad shoulder, his cheeks shining with drops of perspiration, his limbs shining like glittering sapphires, accompanied by his cowherd friends, wearing the dress of a hero, all the wrestlers developed terror as he entered the arena.**

**Комментарий:**

By him all the wrestlers became immediately terrified (viksobhita) when he entered the arena. By his arms he conquered the pride of Cupid. The next three items are clear. His limbs shone like sparkling sapphires. He was in the association of his cowherd friends. He wore the cloth of a hero. This is the third vibhakti (instrumental).

### 4

*manda-smitārabdha-kundāli-nindāya vṛndārakānandi-pādāravindāya*  
*cañcan-nakha-śreṇi-bhā-cakra-bālāya vakṣas-taṭī-lakṣya-nakṣatra-mālāya*  
*phullī-bhavac-cilli-cāpa-prasarpāya nirvāhitāpūrva-kandarpa-darpāya*  
*nāryo muhur dṛṣṭa-mādhurya-caryāya yasmai spṛhāṁ cakrur ābhīra-varyāya*  
*yasmād vilāsena raṅga-sthale rantur ānamra-lokātiśokāpadāhantur*

**Перевод:**

**They saw the Lord to whom the women constantly developed attraction, whose soft smile derided jasmines, whose lotus feet gave bliss to crowd, whose toenails trembled with great beauty, who wore a pearl necklace on his chest, whose expanding eyebrows quivered, who possessed the pride of Cupid previously unexperienced by his beloveds, who was seen to have human-like activities, who was the prince of the cowherds.**

**Комментарий:**

To him the women became attracted (sprham cakruh). He is described. The first two phrases are clear. He had trembling beauty in his toenails. He had an attractive necklace of twentyseven pearls on his chest. Naksatra-mala means a necklace of twenty-seven pearls according to Amara-kosa. He moved his expanding bow-like brows. He had the pride of Cupid previously unexperienced by his beloveds. He had sweet, human-like activities seen by the wise.

*kāmināṁ darśayandainyaṁ strīṇāṁ caiva durātmatām*

**He showed the wretchedness of ordinary lusty men and hardhearted women. (SB 10.30.34)**

He showed the wicked nature of women who agitate a man by anger and showed the miserable nature of the male lover dependent on a young woman, for purposes of increasing rasa. He was the young son of the king of cowherds (abhira-varyaya). This is the fourth vibhakti (dative).

### 5

*yasmād vilāsena raṅga-sthale rantur ānamra-lokātiśokāpadāhantur*  
*indrādi-vṛndārakānanda-nirmātur akṣṇor vinodena vṛṣṇy-andhakān pātur*  
*āryāṅganā-tīvra-sādhvī-vrata-cchettur avyagra-mallāṅganā-tuṣṭir-nirbhettur*  
*āvalgataḥ kṣauṇi-bhartāpi sa trāsam āsādya vibhrāntadhī-vṛttiratrāsa*

**Перевод:**

**From him, who destroyed the devotees’ unfortunate lamentation by his pastimes, who enjoyed in the arena, who gave bliss to Indra and other devatas, who protected the Vrsns and Andhakas, who broke the firm chastity vows of the cultured women by his playful glance, who destroyed the happiness of the wrestlers’ confident wives with his boldness, Kamsa developed fear and shone with erring intelligence.**

**Комментарий:**

From whom Kamsa being terrified, blazed (asa) with illusioned intelligence.

Asa means to shine. Endowed with fickle intelligence because of fear, Kamsa shone. The next four items are clear. By his play he destroyed (ahantuh) the misfortune and suffering of the obedient people. He broke the firm chastity of the innocent women. This may be connected to the phrase aksnor vinodena (giving pleasure to their eyes). He destroyed the happiness of the wrestlers’ wives who thought their husbands were courageous (avyagrd). He was bold (avalgatah) or fickle in fighting. This is the fifth vibhakti (ablative).

### 6

*yasyārditoddaṇḍa-duṣṭābhimānasya kaṣṭaṁ pitṛbhyāṁ tu saṁdṛśyamānasya*  
*raṅgasthalī-valgapādapravālasya bhālāntaviśrāntakāntāgravālasya*  
*padmāvatī-putra-hṛnmarma-kīlasya sarvātmanābhīṣṭa-yoryuddha-līlasya*  
*yuddhaṁ parisphāra-śauṭīrya-ghorasya cānūra-mallena vṛttaṁ kiśorasya*

**Перевод:**

**The crowd saw the young boy whose fight with the wrestler Canura began, who assaulted the pride of wicked Kamsa, who was observed by Nanda and Vasudeva, who jumped around the arena with his bud-like feet, whose locks rested attractively on his forehead, who was spike in the heart of Kamsa, who played at wrestling to his full content, who was ferocious in his towering pride.**

**Комментарий:**

The crowd saw the Lord whose fight started with the wrestler Canura. The meaning is clear. Dusta means Kamsa. He afflicted the pride of greatly wicked Kamsa. He was seen by Nanda and Vasudeva (pitrbhyam). He jumped around the arena with his bud-like feet (pada-pravalasya). Pravala means a fresh sprout according to Visvalocana. His front locks of hair were attractive (hanta), resting on his forehead. He was a spike in the heart of Padmavati’s son Kamsa. He terrified Kamsa and others with the ferocity (ghorasya) of his great pride (sautirya). This is the sixth vibhakti (genitive).

### 7

*yasmin muni-śreṇi-vaktra-sphuran-nāmni vistīrṇa-vakṣaḥ-sthalī-vibhramad-dāmni*  
*navyollasad-vāri-vāhāvalī-dhāmni niḥśeṣa-vīrotkarollaṅghana-sthāmni*  
*prodyat-pada-dyota-nirdhūta-pañceṣu saundarya-darpodgame ramya-mañceṣu*

**Комментарий:**

The many members of the Bhoja and Dasarha clans, astonished (vilaksani) by his beauty, etc., ascending to the large, pleasant stands, showed devotion to Krsna. Situated in the stands on Kamsa’s order they offered Krsna respect. Vilaksa means astonished according to Amara-kosa. The first three items are clear. By his strength (.sthamni) he destroyed unlimited groups of warriors. By the beauty of his feet manifesting strongly (prodyat) for playing in the arena, he conquered the manifestation of Cupid’s pride in his beauty. He was an unequalled ocean of beauty. This the seventh vibhakti (locative).

О Krsna, joyfully dancing with your lotus feet without fear! О Krsna, attracting chaste women by the beauty of your attractive gestures! О Krsna, having them reverentially smell the honey of your bodily fragrance!**

О lion for the elephant-like wrestlers headed by Canura! Being of this nature (sasn), please protect me (patu main). О master of the gopis (gopa-narindra)\\ You were Balarama (talanka), attacking Mustika by twirling him around with your left hand. О Krsna who killed Mustika through your brother. You were a cowherd beautiful with abundant decorations of gems, flute, etc. You defeated a series of powerful wrestlers.

*cāṇūre muṣṭike kūṭe śale tośalake hate \|*

With your lotus (nallka) feet you joyfully danced without fear. Nailka means lotus according to Haima. You attracted chaste women by the beauty of your attractive gestures (anga-hara). You had them drink or reverentially smell the honey of your bodily fragrance.

*jighranta iva nāsābhyām*

**The kings relished his fragrance with their nostrils. (SB 10.73.6)**

О Krsna, anointed with perfumes by Kubja! Please protect me!**

**Комментарий:**

You were a cup of sweet nectar for the eyes of the gopis.

*gopyas tapaḥ kim acaran yad amuṣya rūpaṁ*

Your whole body was decorated with many garlands by Sudama.

**Beautifully adorned with these garlands, Krsna and Balarama were delighted, and so were their companions. The two Lords then offered the surrendered Sudama, who was bowing down before them, whatever benedictions he desired. (SB 10.41.50)**

You displayed great amounts of fine sweetness. You were sweetly dressed in colorful, fragrant garlands. You pulled him off the dais and killed him. You liberated Kamsa by doing that. О killer of Kamsa!

*tam āviśantam ālokya mṛtyumātmana āsanāt \|*  
*manasvī tarasotthāya jagṛhe so'sicarmaṇī \|\|*

**Seeing Lord Krsna approaching like death personified, the quick-witted Kamsa instantly rose from his seat and took up his sword and shield. (SB 10.44.35)**

*taṁ saṁparetaṁ vicakarṣa bhūmau hariyathebhaṁ jagato vipaśyataḥ \|\|*

The next two items are clear. It is said:

*mātaraṁ pitaraṁ caiva mocayitvātha bandhanāt \|*

He offered the thriving seven divisions of the kingdom to the devotee Ugrasena. The seven limbs are king, ministers, friends, treasury, state, fort, and army according to Amara-kosa.

*āha cāsmānmahārāja prajāścājñaptum arhasi \|\|*

**О mighty King, We are your subjects, so please command us. (SB 10.45.13)**

Your limbs were anointed with fragrance by Kubja.

*rūpapeśalamādhuryahasitālāpavīkṣitaiḥ \|*  
*dharṣitātmā dadau sāndramubhayoranulepanam \|\|*

**Her mind overwhelmed by Krsna’s beauty, charm, sweetness, smiles, words and glances, Trivakra gave both Krsna and Balarama generous amounts of ointment. (SB 10.42.4)**

*tatas tāv aṅga-rāgeṇa sva-varṇetara-śobhinā*

**Anointed with these most excellent cosmetics, which adorned them with hues that contrasted with their complexions, the two Lords appeared extremely beautiful. (SB 10.42.5)**

This is the vocative section. Taking sections of the original text I have explained the meaning. May the wise be pleased with the abbreviated work.

### Text 42

*mallān ullaṅghya raṅge kara-vicalad-asir yena mañca-prapañce*  
*keśeṣv ākṛṣya kaṁso vighaṭita-mukuṭaṁ vighna-hetur nijaghne \|*  
*sa tvaṁ sattvādhirāja sphurad-uru-karuṇāḍambarālambi-cetāḥ*  
*pātād duḥkhābdhipātād yadu-kula-kamaloddaṇḍa-caṇḍa-dyutir mām \|\|42\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О controller of all existence! May the Lord, powerful son for the lotus of the Yadu dynasty, inflictor of suffering, whose heart is filled with great, resplendent mercy, who, with sword in hand, vanquishing all the wrestlers in the arena, dragging Kamsa by the hair from his throne, throwing his crown far away, killed him, protect me, since I have fallen in the ocean of suffering.**

**Комментарий:**

Because of the attractiveness of indicating the Lord’s powers, the author repeats what he has described previously. О controller of everything, in the form of the protector Visnu (sattvadhiraja)'. Protect me (patat), because I have fallen in the ocean of misery. The third person is used (sa patat instead of tvam patu) since it is perceived first in the statement (sa tvam). Kamsa, sitting on his dais was pulled by the hair and killed, by he who killed the wrestlers in the arena. He waved a sword in his hand. He inflicted suffering (vighna-hetuh). He threw Kamsa’s crown far away. His heart manifested great shining mercy. He showed great mercy to the cows, brahmanas and devotees.

### Text 43

*manasija-phaṇi-juṣṭe labdha-pāto’smi duṣṭe*  
*timira-gahana-rūpe hanta saṁsāra-kūpe \|*  
*ajita nikhila-rakṣā-hetum uddhāra-dakṣām*  
*upanaya mama haste bhakti-rajjuṁ namas te \|\|43\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O unconquered Lord! I have fallen into the evil well of samsara, filled with intense darkness, furnished with the snake of lust. Bring the rope of bhakti, the cause of all protection, skillful at delivering, to my hand. I offer respects to you.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the Lord’s mercy by describing his pastimes, the author prays for his deliverance. O unconquered Lord! I have fallen into the well of samsara, which is dense darkness, devoid of discrimination. “What should 1 do?” Supply to my hand the rope of bhakti.

### Text 44

*samasta-puruṣārthataḥ pṛthutayādya bhaktiṁ vidan*  
*vadann api na yad bhajet tvad-akṛpātra hetur vibho \|*  
*prasīda yamunā-taṭe luṭhita-mūrtir abhyarthaye*  
*kṛpāṁ kṛpaṇa-nātha he kuru mukunda mande mayi \|\|44\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Though knowing bhakti to be greater than all other purusarthas, though speaking of it, one does not practice it. O Lord! The cause is lack of your mercy. Be pleased with me. Rolling on the bank of the Yamuna, I pray. O Mukunda! O protector of the miserable! Show mercy to me, a fool.**

“Why don’t you perform bhakti, since you know scriptures?” The meaning is clear. Without your mercy, I can do nothing.

**bhṛṅgāra-cchandaḥ \|**

The meter is bhrngara. It is described as follows:

*bhṛṅgāram etac caturbhiś ca tairviddhi*

**Know that bhrngara is Ils (td) four times. (Ils Ils Ils Ils)**

According to that the poem has been written. It is also called saranga.

*yadvidyābhūṣaṇo'yaṁ haricaritabhṛtāṁ bhāṣyamaṣṭādaśānāṁ*  
*dīvyadhyaṅgyaṁ vyatānītphaṇipatigaṇināṁ chandasāṁ sapramāṇam \| tenāsminkṛṣṇadevaḥ svakṛtarucidharo rūpadevaśca bhūyāt-*  
*sadvargaścāpi tīvraśramaguṇanapaṭustuṣṭipāteva sadyaḥ \|\|*

**Vidyabhusana has presented this commentary on eighteen attractive poems describing Krsna’s pastimes, with proofs for the meters calculated by Panini’s students. May Krsna and Rupa accept it. May the devotees, skillful at multiple, intense endeavor, be satisfied.**

*ityaṣṭādaśa chandāṁsi vyākhyātāni \|*  
*iti kaṁsavadhāntāḥ śrīkṛṣṇalīlāḥ samāptāḥ \|*

**Thus eighteen poems in various meters concerning Krsna’s pastimes have been explained ending with the killing of Kamsa.**

## līlāntara-varṇanam

**Description of other pastimes**

atha tatra visesatah kascit—

Something else with particulars on this topic—

## atha govardhanoddharanam

**Lifting of Govardhana**

*śrī-govardhanoddharāya namaḥ \|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the lifter of Govardhana.**

### Text 1

*jhamajjham iti varṣati stanita-cakra-vikrīḍayā*  
*vimuṣṭa-ravi-maṇḍale ghana-ghaṭābhir ākhaṇḍale \|*  
*rarakṣa dharaṇī-dharoddhṛti-paṭuḥ kuṭumbāni yaḥ*  
*sa dārayatu dāruṇaṁ vraja-purandaras te daram \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When Indra showers rain with cloud masses thundering, covering the sun with movement of clouds, may the skillful lifter of Govardhana, the prince of Vraja, who protected his family, destroy their intense fear.**

**Комментарий:**

Some pastime should be discussed in detail. Atha indicates “The pastimes which were described in general should be discussed in detail.” When Indra (akhandale) showered with cruel thundering cloud “jhamajhama,” he who is skillful at lifting the mountain protected his family. May that prince of Vraja destroy their fear (daram). The rest is clear. Jhama-jhama imitates the sound of the falling rain.

### Text 2

*mahā-hetu-vādair vidīrṇendra-yāgaṁ*  
*giri-brāhmaṇopāsti-vistīrṇa-rāgam \|*  
*sapady eka-yuktīkṛtābhīra-vargaṁ*  
*puro-datta-govardhana-kṣmābhṛd argham \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you who stopped Indra’s sacrifice using Sahkhya argument, who became absorbed in worship of the mountain and brahmanas, who immediately brought the cowherds together, who first worshipped the mountain Govardhana.**

**Комментарий:**

The author describes using bhujariga-prayata meter. The verses are connected to the statement in verse twenty-seven he govinda, vayam bhavantam namas kurmahe: O Govinda! We offer respects to you. Krsna is described. He destroyed Indra’s sacrifice by using Sarikhya logic (maha-hetu-vadaih). Then he explained Vedic conclusions in the next line. The rest is clear. How was this done? That is explained. He immediately gathered the cowherds together. First, he gave respect to the mountain (hsmabhrt) Govardhana.

### Text 3

*priyā-śaṁsinībhir dalottaṁsinībhir*  
*virājat-paṭābhiḥ kumārī-ghaṭābhiḥ \|*  
*stuvadbhiḥ kumārair api sphāra-tāraiḥ*  
*saha vyākirantaṁ prasūnair dharaṁ tam \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, who sprinkled the mountain with flowers along with the gopis who praised the mountain with affection and cowherds who praised the mountain with loud voices.**

**Комментарий:**

You along with the gopis and cowherds showered the mountain with flowers. The gopis are described. They praised, “O Govardhana! Be pleased with us.” They wore attractive, colorful cloth. The cowherds are described. They praised, “O Giriraja! You are the Lord. Fulfill our desires.” They did this with loud notes (sphara-taraih). “O Giriraja! May you prosper! May you remain victorious!” or they opened their eyes wide, astonished by the beauty of the mountain (sphara-taraih)

### Text 4

*giri-sthūla-dehena bhutkopahāraṁ*  
*vara-śreṇi-santoṣitābhīra-dāram \|*  
*samuttuṅga-śṛṅgāvalī-baddha-cailaṁ*  
*kramāt prīyamāṇaṁ parikramya śailam \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you who, expanding yourself as a huge mountain, ate the offerings, who pleased the cowherd women with fine gifts, who placed flags on the summit of the mountain, who affectionately circumambulated the mountain.**

**Комментарий:**

You consumed the offerings through the form of a huge mountain.

*kṛṣṇas tvanyatamaṁ rūpaṁ gopaviśrambhaṇaṁ gataḥ \|*  
*śailo'smīti bruvan bhūri balimādadbṛhad vapuḥ \|\|*

**Krsna then assumed an unprecedented, huge form to instill faith in the cowherd men. Declaring “I am Govardhana Mountain!” He ate the abundant offerings. (SB 10.24.35)**

You satisfied the women by desirable gifts. You placed colorful flags on top of the mountain. You expressed your affection by circumambulating the mountain. This was worship of Govardhana. It includes worship of the brahmanas.

### Text 6

*makha-dhvaṁsa-saṁrambhataḥ svarga-nāthe*  
*samantāt kilārabdha-goṣṭha-pramāthe \|*  
*muhur varṣati cchanna-dik-cakravāle*  
*sad-ambholi-nirghoṣam ambhoda-jāle \|\|5\|\|*

*muhur vṛṣṭi-khinnāṁ paritrāsābhinnāṁ*  
*vrajeśa-pradhānāṁ tatiṁ ballavānām \|*  
*vilokyāpta-śītāṁ gavālīṁ ca bhītāṁ*  
*kṛpābhiḥ samunnaṁ suhṛt-prema-nunnam \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, who, seeing the cowherds headed by Nanda, suffering from constant rain, seeing the fearful cows, became soft with mercy, inspired by your love for the people of Vraja, when Indra, angry at destruction of his sacrifice, constantly showered rain with clouds covering the directions and rumbling thunder, which tormented the cowherds.**

**Комментарий:**

Angry at destruction of the sacrifice, Indra (svarga-nathe), giving trouble to the cowherds, showered rain with masses of clouds covering the directions, along with loud thunder. Seeing the cowherds suffering from the constant rain, seeing the fear in the cows, you became soft (samunnam) with mercy for them, inspired by (nunnam) your love for the inhabitants of Vraja. The two verse are together.

### Text 7

*tataḥ savya-hastena hastīndra-khelaṁ*  
*samuddhṛtya govardhanaṁ sāvahelam \|*  
*adabhraṁ tam abhraṁlihaṁ śaila-rājaṁ*  
*mudā bibhrataṁ vibhramaj-jantu-bhājam \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We worship you who, lifting in your left hand without effort huge Govardhana, upon which animals wandered, and which touched the sky, like the king of the elephants playing, held it up joyfully.**

**Комментарий:**

Without effort lifting Govardhana, like play of the king of the elephants, he held it joyfully (muda). Govardhana was huge (adabhram). It touched the sky (abhramliham). It had animals like monkeys and parrots wandering on it. By the power of the Lord, the animals did not suffer at all, despite the heavy rain.

### Text 8

*praviṣṭāsi mātaḥ kathaṁ śoka-bhāre*  
*paribhrājamāne sute mayy udāre \|*  
*abhuvan bhavanto vinaṣṭopasargā*  
*na citte vidhatta bhramaṁ bandhu-vargāḥ \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О mother! Why do you lament when I, your son, full of good qualities, am present? О friends! Your calamity has been destroyed. Do not think otherwise.**

**Комментарий:**

О mother! Why do you lament, thinking how to escape Indra’s anger, when your son full of all good qualities is present? О my friends! The calamity caused by Indra has been destroyed. Do not be bewildered thinking, “Indra will kill us.”

### Text 9

*hatā tāvadītir vidheyā na bhītiḥ*  
*kṛteyaṁ viśālā mayā śaila-śālā \|*  
*tad asyāṁ praharṣād avajñāta-varṣā*  
*vihasyāmareśaṁ kurudhvaṁ praveśam \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“The extreme conditions have been overcome. Do not fear. I have created this huge room in the mountain. Without concern for the rain, enter it while laughing at Indra.”**

**Комментарий:**

The extreme conditions have been overcome. You should not fear. “Why should we not fear?” I have created this huge room in the mountain that you should all enter. Therefore, without concern for the rain (avajnata-varsa), joyfully enter into it, mocking Indra (amaresam). Smile, thinking, “Indra will not be able to do anything.”

### Text 10

*iti svairam āśvāsitair gopa-vṛndaiḥ*  
*parānanda-sandīpitāsyāravindaiḥ \|*  
*girer gartam āsādya harmyopamānaṁ*  
*cireṇātihṛṣṭaiḥ pariṣṭūyamānam \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, who were praised by the cowherds, easily pacified by your words, whose faces lit up in great bliss, joyful that the hole was made in the mountain, like a palace.**

**Комментарий:**

You were praised by the cowherds who were pacified by your words expressed in the previous two verses (8-9). Their faces lit up with intense bliss because of the Lord’s words. They were overjoyed by the making of the hole in the mountain, which became like a palace. Three phrases describe them.

### Text 11

*girīndraṁ guruṁ komale pañca-śākhe*  
*kathaṁ hanta dhatte sakhā te viśākhe \|*  
*purastād amuṁ prekṣya hā cintayedaṁ*  
*muhur māmakīnaṁ mano yāti bhedam \|\|11\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“O Visakha! How does your friend hold up the king of mountains with his soft hand? Seeing him holding up the mountain in front, my mind is in constant worry.”**

**Комментарий:**

The next five verses (11-15) are Radha’s words. O Visakha! Hanta expresses lamentation. How did your friend lift the king of mountains in his soft hand (panca-sakhe)? Seeing him holding up the mountain in front, my mind splits from constant worry.

### Text 12

*stanadbhiḥ kaṭhore ghanair dhvānta-ghore*  
*bhramad-vāta-māle hatāśe’tra kāle \|*  
*ghana-sparśi-kūṭaṁ vahann anna-kūṭaṁ*  
*kathaṁ syān na kāntaḥ sarojākṣi tāntaḥ \|\|12\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed friend! Carrying Govardhana whose peaks touch the clouds, who ate a pile of food when thunder pierced the ears, thick darkness spread everywhere and the directions could not be discerned, how can my lover not be tired?**

**Комментарий:**

O lotus-eyed friend! Carrying Govardhana who ate a pile of food at that time, how can my lover not be tired? He must be tired. The mountain is described. Its peaks touch the clouds. The time is described. The time was noisy, painful to the ears (kathore) with intense thunder. It was terrifying (ghore), painful for the eyes, with darkness. At that time there were winds blowing and the directions could not be discerned (hatase).

### Text 13

*na tiṣṭhanti goṣṭhe kaṭhorāṅga-daṇḍāḥ*  
*kiyanto’tra gopāḥ samantāt pracaṇḍāḥ \|*  
*śirīṣa-prasūnāvalī-saukumārye*  
*dhṛtā dhūr iyaṁ bhūrir asmin kim ārye \|\|13\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Yasoda! There are not a few cowherds who are firm bodied and strong in this village. Why is the burden given to this young boy decorated with sirisa flowers?**

**Комментарий:**

O Yasoda (arye)! In this village there are not a few cowherds of firm body (kathoranga) who are strong. There are many. How has this heavy burden been given to Krsna, your young boy decorated with sirisa flowers. Speak to the cowherds, saying, “Hold up the mountain for a moment. Let him rest.”

### Text 14

*gire tāta govardhana prārthaneyaṁ*  
*vapuḥ sthūla-nālī-laghiṣṭhaṁ vidheyam \|*  
*bhavantaṁ yathā dhārayann eṣa haste*  
*na dhatte śramaṁ maṅgalātman namas te \|\|14\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O mountain! O Govardhana! I pray to you that your body becomes as light as a morning glory leaf so that Krsna, holding you up with his hand, does not become tired. O auspicious one! I offer respects to you.**

**Комментарий:**

She prays to Govardhana. O mountain! O Govardhana! I pray to you in this way. Make your body very light like a morning glory leaf. Nall means kalamba flower according to Haima. Thus, Krsna will not become tired, holding you up with his hand. O auspicious one! I offer respects to you. You should do this.

### Text 15

*bhramat-kuntalāntaṁ smita-dyotakāntaṁ*  
*lasad-gaṇḍa-śobhaṁ kṛtāśeṣa-lobham \|*  
*sphuran-netra-lāsyaṁ murāres tvam āsyaṁ*  
*varākūṭa-śāli sphuṭaṁ lokayāli \|\|15\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O friend! Look at Krsna’s face, causing us unlimited greed, with swaying locks of hair, with a soft smile, with shining beautiful cheeks, with glittering, dancing eyes, revealing his deep love.**

**Комментарий:**

Getting Visakha’s attention, she speaks to her again.

O my friend, Visakha! Look at Murari’s face. His face is described. It makes everyone develop great greed. We are all attracted to it. It expresses his inner love (varakuta-sali) through his glance. The rest is clear. By my prayer the mountain has become light as cotton. No one can estimate the greatness of his inconceivable will by which his wish comes true.

### Text 16

*nipīyeti rādhā-latā-vāṅ-marandaṁ*  
*vara-prema-saurabhya-pūrād amandam \|*  
*dadhānaṁ madaṁ bhṛṅgavat-tuṅga-kūjaṁ*  
*varāṅgī-calāpāṅga-bhaṅgāpta-pūjam \|\|16\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you who, drinking the honey of Radha’s words which was the best because of its full fragrance of excellent prema, became intoxicated like a bee, humming loudly, worshipped by the gopis’ fickle glances.**

**Комментарий:**

Drinking the honey of the words just spoken by Radha, like a creeper, you became intoxicated like a bee (bhrnga-vat). The honey is described. It is the best (amandam) because of its fragrance of the best prema. Krsna is described. He buzzes loudly (tunga-kujam). He is worshipped by the waves of fickle glances from Radha and others. He is worshipped by their glances. These six verses make a kulaka.

### Text 17

*kathaṁ nāma dadhyāt kṣudhākṣāma-tundaḥ*  
*śiśur me gariṣṭhaṁ girīndraṁ mukundaḥ \|*  
*tad etasya tuṇḍe haṭhād arpayāraṁ*  
*vrajādhīśa dadhnācitaṁ khaṇḍa-sāram \|\|17\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Nanda! How can my child whose mouth cannot tolerate hunger, hold up the heavy mountain? Quickly offer to his mouth some sugar with yogurt.**

**Комментарий:**

О master of Vraja, Nanda! How can the child, Mukunda, very hungry, hold up the king of mountains? Therefore (tat) offer to his mouth (tunde) quickly some sugar with yogurt.

### Text 18

*mahā-bhāra-niṣṭhe sthite te kaniṣṭhe*  
*labhe vatsa nīlāmbaroddāma-pīḍām \|*  
*avaṣṭabhya sattvaṁ tadasmai bala tvaṁ*  
*dadasvāvilambaṁ sva-hastāvalambam \|\|18\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Balarama! I am in great pain because your younger brother is supporting this heavy load. Therefore, using your strength, quickly assist him with your hand.**

**Комментарий:**

О dear Balarama! With your younger brother lifting the huge load, I am in great pain. Therefore, take support of your power (sattvam). Sattvam means strength according to Visva. О Balarama (bala)! Quickly assist your younger brother (asmai) with your hand.

### Text 19

*iti snigdha-varṇāṁ samākarṇayantaṁ*  
*giraṁ mātur enāṁ ca nirvarṇayantam \|*  
*kaniṣṭhāṅgulī-śṛṅga-vinyasta-gotraṁ*  
*pariprīṇita-vyagra-gopāla-gotram \|\|19\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, who heard your mother’s words and looked at her with affection, who placed the mountain on the tip of your little finger, and who pleased the suffering cowherd families.**

**Комментарий:**

You heard the words of your mother expressed in the two verses (17-18) above. You looked upon your mother with affection. The mountain was placed on the tip of your little finger. You satisfied the cowherd families (gotra) afflicted by the rain. Gotra means family according to Visvalocana. Krsna is described by these three phrases.

### Text 20

*amībhiḥ prabhāvaiḥ kuto’bhūd akuṇṭhaḥ*  
*śiśur-dhūli-kelī-paṭuḥ kṣīra-kaṇṭhaḥ \|*  
*bibharty adya sāptābdiko bhūri-bhāraṁ*  
*giriṁ yac cirād eṣa kailāsa-sāram \|\|20\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**How has this child fond of playing in the dust and eager to drink milk developed such excellences with these powers? The seven-year-old child holds up the heavy mountain, big as Kailasa for a long time today.**

**Комментарий:**

How has this child, fond of playing in the dust and drinking milk, become excellent with these powers—taking Indra as his servant and holding up the mountain like a mushroom? One should conclude that he has all powers and all the power to fulfill his will as his very nature since the seven-year-old child holds up the mountain big as Kailasa today for a long time.

### Text 21

*na śaṅkā dhara-bhraṁśane’smākam asmān*  
*nakhāgre sahelaṁ vahaty eṣa yasmāt \|*  
*girir-dik-karīndrāgrahaste dharāvad*  
*bhuje paśyaty āsya sphuraty adya tāvat \|\|21\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We have no fear that the mountain will fall from his hand since he carries it easily on the tip of his nail. Look! The mountain today shines on his arm like the elephant of the directions holding the earth on the tip of its trunk.**

**Комментарий:**

His ability to make his desire true is described. We have no fear that the mountain will fall from our child since he holds it up easily on the tip of his fingernail. The mountain now looks beautiful in the child’s left hand, as if on the tip of the trunk of the elephant of the directions. Look! The sons of Sagara looking for the sacrificial horse, dug up the earth and saw in Rasatala the four elephants of the directions, as big as mountains, standing there, holding up the earth on their heads. This is famous in Bala-kanda, Ramayana. In Fifth Canto of Bhdgavatam it is described that the similar four elephants of the directions stand on Manasottara Mountain, stepping on the earth. Therefore, there is no fear the mountain will fall from his hand.

### Text 22

*iti sphāra-tārekṣaṇair mukta-bhogair*  
*vrajendreṇa sārdhaṁ dhṛta-prīti-yogaiḥ \|*  
*muhur ballavair vīkṣyamānāsya-candraṁ*  
*puraḥ sapta-rātrāntara-tyakta-tandram \|\|22\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, tireless for seven nights, whose moon-like face was gazed upon by the cowherd men with Nanda, wide-eyed with astonishment, filled with affection, free of material enjoyment.**

**Комментарий:**

Your moon-like face was seen constantly by the cowherd men who spoke the above two verses (20-21). They are described. Their eyes were wide with astonishment. Krsna is described. You had no fatigue for seven nights. The rest is clear in meaning. There are three descriptive phrases for the cowherds.

### Text 24

*taḍid-dāma-kīrṇān samīrair udīrṇān*  
*visṛṣṭāmbu-dhārān dhanur yaṣṭi-hārān \|*  
*tṛṇīkṛtya ghorān sahasrāṁśu-caurān*  
*durantoru-śabdān kṛtāvajñam abdān \|\|23\|\|*

*ahaṅkāra-paṅkāvalī-lupta-dṛṣṭer*  
*vraje ṣāvad iṣṭaṁ praṇītoru-vṛṣṭeḥ \|*  
*balāreś ca durmānitāṁ visphurantaṁ*  
*nirākṛtya duṣṭāli-daṇḍe durantam \|\|24\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you, who always punish the wicked, and who shone, destroying the pride of Indra, showering torrents of rain on Vraja, who made insignificant as grass the clouds which flashed with lightning, which were driven by the wind, which showered streams of water, which were decorated with Indra’s bow, which covered the sun and roared intolerably.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna is described in two verses. You shone, making the clouds insignificant like grass and destroyed the pride of Indra. Krtavajnam (disrespectfully) acts as an adverb. The clouds are described. They were full of lightning. They were impelled by the wind. They released showers of rain like water from an elephant’s trunk. They were decorated with Indra’s bow as a jeweled necklace. They were decorated by Indra. They were fearsome (ghoran). They covered the sun (sahasrdmsu). They roared intolerably. Indra is described. His intelligence of being a servant was lost by the mud of pride, thinking, “I am master of the three worlds.” The rest is clear.

### Text 25

*visṛṣṭoru-nīrāḥ sa-jhañjhā-samīrās*  
*taḍidbhiḥ karālā yayur megha-mālāḥ \|*  
*raviś cāmbarāntar vibhāty eṣa śāntaḥ*  
*kṛtānanda-pūrā bahir yāta śūrāḥ \|\|25\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The mass of clouds, pouring rain, with fierce lightning and roaring wind, has gone. The sun shines in the sky. It is peaceful. О brave cowherds! Go outside.**

**Комментарий:**

О brave cowherds (surah)! Leave the hole in the mountain. “How can we leave when it is raining heavily?” The rest of the verse answers.

### Text 26

*iti procya niḥsārita-jñāti-vāraṁ*  
*yathā-pūrva-vinyasta-śailendra-bhāram \|*  
*dadhi-kṣīra-lājāṅkurair bhāvinībhir*  
*mudā kīryamāṇaṁ yaśa-stāvinībhiḥ \|\|26\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**We offer respects to you who, saying this, had your relatives leave the hole, who placed the mountain in its original position, and who were sprinkled with yogurt, milk and laja by the women who uttered your glories.**

**Комментарий:**

Saying the previous verse, he had his relatives leave the hole. He was showered by the women uttering praises.

### Text 27

*vayaṁ hanta govinda saundaryavantaṁ*  
*namaskurmahe śarma-hetor bhavantam \|*  
*tvayi spaṣṭa-niṣṭhyūta bhūyaś cid-induṁ*  
*mudā naḥ prasādīkuru prema-bindum \|\|27\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Govinda! We offer respects to you, most beautiful, for attaining bliss. Joyfully bestow to us drop of prema for you, which derides completely the moon of jnana.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the pastime, the author prays. O Govinda! We, your servants, offer respects to you, for attaining you, the cause of bliss (sarma-hetoh). Sasthl hetu-prayoge’pi: the sixth case-affix is employed after a noun implying the cause of an action, when the word hetu is used along with such a word. (Panini Sutras 2.3.26) Give us a drop of prema for you. The drop of prema makes us clearly spit upon the moon of jnana. The method of jnana of the santas is derided. They worship the Lord with knowledge of Paramatma, full of bliss, an ocean devoid of waves of variegated pastimes.

### Text 28

*kṣubhyad-dambholi-jṛmbhottarala-ghana-ghaṭārambha-gambhīra-karmā*  
*nistambho jambha-vairī giri-dhṛti-caṭulād vikramād yena cakre \|*  
*tanvā nindantam indīvara-dala-valabhī-nandad-indindirābhāṁ*  
*taṁ govindādya nandālaya-śaśi-vadanānanda vandemahi tvām \|\|28\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Govinda, giving bliss to Yasoda in Nanda’s house! We offer respects to you, whose body derides the beauty of a bee enjoying in pavilion of blue lotus petals, by whom Indra, relentless in sending masses of clouds agitated by disturbing thunderbolts, was deflated in pride by your valorous act of lifting the mountain.**

**Комментарий:**

O Govinda! You give bliss to Yasoda and other mothers with moon-like faces in Nanda’s house by your qualities like defeating demons, in response to affection for your parents. We offer respects to you today. By your body you deride the beauty of a bee (indindira) enjoying in the watchtower made of blue lotus petals. Your beauty derides that of a bee which has turned even blacker from drinking honey of a blue lotus. The beauty defeats the luster of collyrium. By you, Indra (jambha-vain) was made devoid of pride (nistambhah) by your valorous act of holding up the mountain.

Indra is described. He performed acts, unstoppable by others (gambhira), of inciting clouds agitated (uttarala) with appearance (jrmbha) of lightning which moved about because of being thrown with great strength (ksubhyat). Thus, lifting of Govardhana has been explained.

## atha vastra-haraṇam

**Stealing the gopis’ clothing**

*śrī ballavendrāya namaḥ \|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the king of the cowherds.**

### Text 1

*vanyāśritā murāriḥ kanyāḥ sanyāyam unmadayan \|*  
*anyābhilāṣitāṁ te dhanyārpita-sauhṛdo hanyāt \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Murari, who gave joy to the young girls bathing in the Yamuna, who showed most affection to the gopi Dhanya among them, remove other desires.**

**Комментарий:**

Wanting to describe stealing of the clothing, the author prays for his desired goal from Krsna, performer of the pastime.

Please remove desires other than desires for you. You give joy to the young gopis bathing in the flow of the Yamuna (vanyasrita). You give joy to them in a righteous way (sa-nyayam). What was unlawful, having them show their limbs by stealing the clothing, when they desired Krsna as their lover, became proper (sa-nyayam). He offered friendship to Dhanya. He was most affectionate to her.

### 1

*sahasi vratinīrabhitaḥ kṛtinīr girijāstavane salilāplavane*  
*kalitollasanāḥ kila dig-vasanās taṭa-bhāk-paṭikā rasa-lampaṭikāḥ*  
*sphuṭa-bālya-yutāḥ paśupāla-sutāḥ kutukī kalayan matim ullalayann*  
*upagatya manobhavavat-kamano hṛtavān sicayān suhṛdāṁ nicaya*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the young gopis who were performing a vrata in the winter month, who were very skillful at praising Katyayani, who were eager to bathe in the water, taking their clothes off and putting them on the bank, desiring Krsna as their husband, acting childish in the water, you, fun-loving, attractive as Cupid, developing desire for them, approached them and stole their garments.**

**Комментарий:**

O killer of Kesi! May you manifest your excellence (jaya)\\ With generous heart (pra-mana-comes later in the verse), manifesting great affection for your devotees, play (vihara)! O Lord! O redlipped Krsna! Be (kalayeh) merciful to me, wicked in heart, (last line of poem). Fun-loving (kutuki), seeing the cowherd girls, approaching them, you stole their clothing (sicayan). They are described. They had made a vow in Margasirsa month (sahasi). Saha means Margasirsa month according to Amara-kosa. They were skillful (krtinih) at praising Parvati. They were eager to bath in the water. The next two items are clear. They were greedy to have Krsna as their husband (rasa-lamapatikah). They were fickle when playing in the water (sphuta-balya). Krsna is described. You were desirous of them (matim ullalayan). You were beautiful like Cupid (manobhava-vat).

### 2

*antaragaṁ tarasā priyakaṁ svarasād adhiruhya nagaṁ taṭa-kānana-gaṁ*  
*kṛpayā snapayann atha tās trapayan pṛthulāṁ sa-raṭī-dhṛta-dhauta-paṭī-*  
*paṭalo hasita-prabhayollasitaḥ śṛṇuta pramadā giram aśramadām*  
*upagatya hitām abhitaḥ sahitā yadi vā kramataḥ sphuṭa-vibhramataḥ*

**Перевод:**

**In the middle of young boys, quickly you climbed a kadamba tree in a grove on the bank, and, showering the girls with mercy, embarrassed them, and, with their clean cloths on your broad shoulder, joyful with a beautiful smile, you said, “O girls! Hear my beneficial words which will relieve your fatigue. Come near me either together or one by one, manifesting your beauty, and take your clothing.”**

**Комментарий:**

You were in the middle (antaragah) of a group of small children for four or five years, who were devoted to you (suhrdam). Quickly you climbed by your desire (svarasdt) a kadamba (priyakam) tree in a forest on the Yamuna’s bank. You bathed the girls in mercy and embarrassed them. You placed all their clean (dhauta) clothing on your broad shoulder. You blossomed with beautiful smiles. You spoke to them. О girls (pramada)'. Listen (srnuta) to my beneficial (hitam) words which will relieve you of fatigue (asramadam)!  Come near (abhitah) me one by one (kramatah) or together (yadi va sahita). In a charming manner (vibramatah) take your clothing.

### 3

*sicayān nayata cchalanaṁ na yataḥ kathitaṁ na mayā januṣaḥ samayād*  
*anṛtaṁ lalitā yaśasojjvalitā vidur indu-hṛdas tad amī suhṛdas*  
*tanavai na hasād uditaṁ sahasā bata yūyam itā vratataḥ śramitā*  
*iti saṅkathayan paṭutāṁ pratahyann aticañcala he viśa mā kalahe*

**Перевод:**

**“I am not a cheater, since from birth I have not told a lie. О charming girls, shining with fame, endowed with moon-like minds! My friends know this. I do not say this boldly as a joke. You are fatigued from the vow, having bathed.” Saying this, he showed his skill to his friends. “O most fickle boy! Do not argue with us!”**

**Комментарий:**

I am not a cheater since I have not told a lie (anrtam) from the time of my birth (janusah). О girls with charming limbs (lalita), shining with fame! My friends know this.

*na mayoditapūrvaṁ vā anṛtaṁ tadime viduḥ*

**I have never before spoken a lie, and these boys know it. (SB 10.22.11)**

I will not say this as a joke (hasat) rashly (sahasa). Oh! You are tired from the vow. In this way he spoke, showing his cleverness (patutam) to his friends. The girls then spoke. О most fickle boy! Do not enter an argument.

### 4

*vitarādya paṭaṁ kuru mā kapaṭaṁ karavāma sadā vacanaṁ rasadās*  
*tava dāsya-parā na vayaṁ tv aparā na hi cet tvaritaṁ nikhilaṁ caritaṁ*  
*khalu rājñi tava prabale kitava pragadāma madoddhata-ghora-mado*  
*vacanaṁ ca ruṣā prasarat-puruṣākṣaram ity uditaṁ saruṣā ruditaṁ*  
*jaḍatā-kalile yamunā-salile vilasad-vapuṣāṁ guru-kampa-juṣāṁ*  
*cala-cāru-dṛśāṁ bahudhā sudṛśāṁ niśamayya tataḥ praṇayī satata-*

**Перевод:**

**“Immediately give us our clothing. Do not trick us. We always obey your words. We give you milk. We are your servants and not others’ servants. If you do not agree, we will immediately tell the powerful king of your character. О cheater! О boy infatuated with pride!” He heard their rough words brimming with anger, as they stood in the cold water of the Yamuna, shivering intensely, with shining bodies. They wept in anger, while their attractive eyes glanced about.**

**Комментарий:**

Immediately offer us our clothing. Do not be deceptive. We, who give milk (rasadah) to you, obey your words always. Rasadah also means giving amorous pleasure. We are your servants and do not belong to anyone else. If you do not respect our words, we will inform the strong king Kamsa of your cheating character. О cheater! О child intoxicated with pride! He heard their words revealing their fear, filled with rough words indicating anger, as they wept in anger, while their shining bodies shivered in the cold water of the Yamuna.

### 5

*smita-candrikayā sphurito’dhikayā yadi yūyam ṛte mama vāg-amṛte*  
*bhavatha grahilā niyataṁ mahilā upasṛtya tataḥ priyakāt patataḥ*  
*svapaṭī-padakān sva-paricchadakān urarīkuruta pramadād gurutas*  
*tyajatānucitaṁ hṛdi saṅkucitaṁ na hi cen nitarāṁ na paṭān vitarāmy*  
*uru-vīrya-caye mayi kiṁ racayen nṛpatiḥ paritaḥ sa ruṣā bharitaḥ*  
*sphuṭam ity amalaṁ nigadan kamalaṁ bhramayann uditaḥ śaśivan muditaḥ*

**Перевод:**

**More than ever he showed his constant moon-like smile. “O women! If you really favor my sweet, true words, approach me and in great joy take your clothing and ornaments which have fallen from the kadamba tree. Give up reserve in your hearts. It is inappropriate. If you do not agree to my words, then I will not give you your clothing. What can the king filled with great anger do to me, endowed with great valor?” Saying these spotless words, he twirled a lotus and smiled like the moon, oveijoyed at the sight.**

**Комментарий:**

He manifested a constant moon-like smile more than previously. He was overjoyed because he was their friend (pranaya). He spoke (nigadan) pure words which were clear. О women! If you are receptive to my sweet words which are true, come near. With great joy (pramadat) take your clothing and ornaments which have fallen from the hadamba tree. Give up reserve in your heart, which is not proper. If you do not respect my word, saying,

“How can we approach you without clothing?” Then I will not give you the clothing at all. If you do not obey me and show the king’s power, it is useless. What can the king filled with anger do to me, since I have great prowess (uruvirya-caye). His servants have all been killed. Thus, he will also be killed. Twirling a lotus, he appeared like the moon. He was fearless. Seeing them, he was joyful (muditah).

### 6

*svakarāmbariṇīr atha tā hariṇī-nayanāḥ  kalayan sva-śiraś calayan*  
*bata nagnatayā spṛhayonnatayā jala-majjanataḥ kṛta-varjanataḥ*  
*ku(ka)pater janitā laghutā vanitās tad alaṁ durita-kṣataye sphurita-*  
*dyuti-sundarayor yugalaṁ karayoḥ śirasi prayatā drutam arpayatā-*  
*ruṇam ity adhunā nija-vāṅ-madhunā parilabhya madaṁ hṛdi vibhra-madaṁ*  
*kiratībhir alaṁ nayanaṁ viralaṁ racitāñjalibhiḥ pramadāvalibhiḥ*  
*praṇato madhuraḥ kṛtakā-madhuraḥ subhagaṅkaraṇaṁ vasanābharaṇaṁ*

**Перевод:**

**With their clothing in your hands you looked at the girls and shook your head. “O women! You have committed offense to Varuna by bathing naked out of intense desire, ignoring scriptures. To remove the sin, you must place your red hands, beautiful with quivering luster, upon your heads and quickly come to me.” You were offered respects by the girls, each with folded hands, who gazed upon you after attaining passion with bewilderment by hearing your sweet words. You were attractive, having fulfilled your desire.**

**Комментарий:**

He was offered (pranatah) respects by the girls. He was attractive (madhurah). They are described. They gazed upon him (.nayanam kirattbhih), having developed passion which produced bewilderment in their hearts by the sweetness of his words. They each folded their hands. This means they offered respects to their dear Lord. О women (vanitah')! Because of bathing naked out of uncontrolled desire, which is forbidden in scriptures (krta-varjanatah), you have offended Varuna, lord of the water. Placing the phrases out of order is not a fault since it is required for alliteration. To destroy the sin of offending Varuna (durita-ksataye), quickly approach me, the form of auspiciousness, with your red hands, beautiful with shining luster on your heads. His desire was fulfilled (krta-kama-dhurah).

### 7

*vihitānataye lālanā-tataye dadad-aṅkurita-praṇaya-cchuritaḥ*  
*parito hṛṣite madanottṛṣite trapayā namite priya-saṅgamite*  
*nava-rāga-dhare dyuti-bhāga-dhare hasitāṅkurataḥ sphurite purataḥ*  
*sthagite raśanā-vilasad-vasanā-kulite pṛthunā sphuṭa-vepathunā*  
*calad-agra-kare pramadā-prakare vihiteṣṭa-varaḥ praṇayi-pravaraḥ*

**Перевод:**

**Attracted to their budding affection, you gave the auspicious clothing to the girls with bowed heads. You promised to fulfil desire of the girls who were oveijoyed, thirsty for love, humbled by shyness on meeting their lover, tinged with fresh beauty, effulgent, slightly smiling, hiding themselves in front of him, collecting their clothing and belts, shivering intensely, fingers trembling. You were the best of the affectionate.**

**Комментарий:**

You gave the auspicious cloth to the girls, their heads bowed. You developed attraction for them, because of their manifesting affection. You granted the desire (vihitesta-varah) of the cowherd girls (pramadd-prakare).

*yātāvalā*  
*vrajaṁ siddhā mayemā raṁsyati kṣapā*

**Go now, girls, and return to Vraja. Your desire is fulfilled, for in my company you will enjoy the coming nights. (SB 10.22.27)**

He promised to give what they desired. The girls are described. Ten phrases describe them. They are clear in meaning. He was the chief of the affectionate (pranaya-pravarah).

### Text 2

*sutarāṁ sukhibhir valitaḥ sakhibhir bahudhākhuralī-vilasan-muralī-*  
*nava-kākali-kālibhir utkalikā-kulabhiḥ kulam unnamayan sudṛśāṁ ramayan*  
*dhiyam unmadanaḥ kṛpayā sadana-prahita-pramadaḥ kalita-pramadaḥ*  
*kusuma-stavakaṁ śravaṇe navakaṁ dadhad-ābharaṇaṁ jagatāṁ śaraṇaṁ*  
*jaya keśi-hara pramaṇā vihara tvam atipraṇayaṁ svajane praṇayan*  
*mayi durhṛdaye bhagavan vidaye kalayer aruṇādhara he karuṇām \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Surrounded by happy friends, increasing the longing of the gopis by the sweet, fresh sounds from your flute, displaying various musical exercises, giving pleasure to the gopis, creating madness in their minds, mercifully sending them home, becoming joyful yourself, wearing fresh flower cluster ornaments in your ears, О killer of Kesi, may you, the shelter of all beings, manifest your excellence. With generous heart, manifesting great affection for your devotees, play! О Lord! О red-lipped Krsna! Be merciful to me, wicked in heart.**

**Комментарий:**

You were surrounded by happy friends. You increased the longing (utkalika) of the women by the fresh sweet sounds of your flute which manifested a variety of exercises. You gave pleasure (ramayan) to their minds. You produced madness in them (unmadanab.). By your mercy you sent them home. You became joyful by these pastimes (kalita-pramadah). You wore fresh ornaments of flower clusters (kusuma-stavaka) in your ears. You were the shelter of all beings in the universe. Kusuma-stavaka is the name of the dandaka.

### Text 3

*yasya sphūrti-lavāṅkureṇa laghunāpy antar munīnāṁ manaḥ*  
*spṛṣṭaṁ mokṣa-sukhād virajyati jhaṭity āsvādyamānād api \|*  
*premṇas tasya mukunda sāhasitayā śaknotu kaḥ prārthane*  
*bhūyāj janmani janmani pracayinī kintu spṛhāpy atra me \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Mukunda! Who can boldly pray for that prema, a tiny, temporary sprout of which makes the minds of sages, touched by that experience, immediately give up the happiness of liberation? But may I have increasing desire for prema birth after birth.**

**Комментарий:**

O Mukunda! By a slight small particle of prema, the minds of the sages performing austerities, etc., touched by the experience of prema, quickly become detached from the happiness of liberation—an experience of Paramatma devoid of pastimes, like an ocean without waves. Their minds desire the svariipa of the Lord with various pastimes. Sukadeva says:

*pariniṣṭhito'pi nairguṇye uttamaślokalīlayā \|*  
*gṛhītacetā rājarṣe ākhyānaṁ yadadhītavān \|\|*

**Though I was fixed in Brahman and beyond the gunas, my mind became attracted to the pastimes of the Lord. I thus learned about his pastimes. (SB 2.1.9)**

Nairgunya means Paramatma devoid of quality of pastimes.

Who can boldly pray, “Give me prema”? No one can. But may I have the increasing (pracayini) desire for prema, birth after birth. If one has the desire, at some time prema will manifest. The stealing of the gopis clothing has again been explained.

## atha rasa krida

**The Rasa dance (in pajjhatika meter)**

*namaḥ śrī-rāsa-rasikāya \|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the taster of the rasa dance.**

### Text 1

*śārada-śaśadhara-vīkṣaṇa-hṛṣṭaḥ*  
*parama-vilāsādibhir abhimṛṣṭaḥ \|*  
*ballava-ramaṇī-maṇḍala-bhāvaḥ*  
*prollāsaka-kala-muralī-rāvaḥ \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who was joyful on seeing the autumn moon, who was permeated with the highest pleasure, thinking of the circle of gopis, playing his sweet flute to cause great joy, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

I offer respects to the taster of the rasa dance. Because of its beauty, the rasa dance is again described using pajjahatika meter. Fifteen verses constitute one sentence.

Krsna is described. He was joyful by seeing the autumn moon. He was saturated (abhimrstah) with the highest joy.

### Text 2

*atha sakalābhir mada-vikalābhir*  
*niśi paribhūya svajanān bhūyaḥ \|*  
*aviruvatībhir nava-yuvatībhir*  
*vihitoddeśaḥ sundara-veśaḥ \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, sought by the young gopis who had come to the forest, completely bypassing their elders and wounded by the passion of youth, who went silently, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

He was sought (yihita uddesah) by the young gopis who had come to the forest, completely bypassing their elders (sva-janan). They were rendered helpless by passion arising from youth (mada-vikalabhih). They were silent (aviruvatibhih).

### Text 3

*milita-mṛgākṣī-vāñchita-sākṣī-*  
*kṛta-parihāsaḥ sphīta-vilāsaḥ \|*  
*tad amala-vāṇī-niśita-kṛpāṇī-*  
*dalita-nikāraḥ kalita-vikāraḥ \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, pretending to be indifferent to the desire of the assembled gopis, bursting with charm, whose deception was destroyed by the sharp knife of their pure words, pierced by their glances, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

He joked with them, being neutral (saksl-krta) to the desires of the women who had come to him. This means he showed indifference to them as a joke. They destroyed your deception by the sharp knife of their pure words (yam). Nikrti (nikarah in the verse) means deception according to Amara-kosa. Your heart was pierced by their glances (kalita-vikarah).

### Text 4

*pramadottaralita-ballava-nārī-*  
*mukha-cumbana-parirambhaṇa-kārī \|*  
*unnata-manasāṁ sudṛśāṁ māna-*  
*prekṣaṇataḥ kalitāntardhānaḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who embraced the gopis, trembling in bliss, and kissed their mouths, who disappeared on seeing the pride of the gopis, who felt themselves privileged, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing the pride of the bold hearted gopis, caused by thinking themselves most fortunate as a lover, he disappeared to destroy their pride as this was necessary for the rasa dance, which need a common mind.

### Text 5

*anukṛta-caritaḥ puline paritas*  
*taruṣu ca pṛṣṭaḥ kvāpi na dṛṣṭaḥ \|*  
*yuvati-camūbhis tvaritam amūbhir*  
*muhur anugītaḥ kutuka-parītaḥ \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, whose pastimes were immediately imitated by the army of gopis everywhere on the bank of the Yamuna, whose whereabouts they asked from the trees, who was not seen anywhere, who was the subject of their songs, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

His pastimes were imitated by the army (camubhih) of gopis on the bank of the Yamuna. The meaning is clear.

### Text 6

*kākubhir ābhiḥ prārthita-saṅgaḥ*  
*prakaṭita-mūrtir dhṛta-rati-raṅgaḥ \|*  
*kim api nigūḍha-ruṣā paripṛṣṭaḥ*  
*kalitottara-vidhir alam upaviṣṭaḥ \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, to whom they prayed for association in choked voices, who then manifested himself, who was placed on a seat and interrogated by them because of their deep anger, who answered skillfully, who performed amorous pastimes with them, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

His association was requested by them in choked voices. He manifested himself to them. He was then placed on a seat made of their upper cloths (upavistah). He was interrogated by them, who held deep anger.

“Why did you abandon us, devoted to you, in the night?” He answered them. “I gave you up to increase your prema for me.” But they were not pleased. Then he answered, “I am indebted to you.” He then had amorous pastimes with them (dhrta-rati-rangah), as they were satisfied.

### Text 7

*karuṇā-śīlaḥ khaṇḍita-pīlaḥ*  
*stavakita-līlaḥ kuvalaya-nīlaḥ \|*  
*dhṛta-mṛdu-hāsaḥ prema-vilāsas*  
*tata-tanu-vāsaḥ kalpita-rāsaḥ \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, full of mercy, having abandoned the gopis, blossoming with pastimes, dark like a blue lotus, smiling softly, joyful with prema, emanating great fragrance from his body, performing the rasa dance, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

He was merciful. His limbs were dark like a blue lotus (kuvalaya). He had great (tata) fragrance (vasa) emanating from his body. Or his body was a great abode (vosa) for enjoying. Vasa means a house or place according to Haima. He performed the rasa dance (kalpita-rasah).

### Text 8

*atha parikalpita-maṇḍala-bandhaḥ*  
*kusuma-śarāsana-vibhrama-kandaḥ \|*  
*yuvatī-yuga-yuga-subhaga-skandha-*  
*nyasta-lasad-bhuja-daṇḍa-dvandvaḥ \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, the cause of Cupid’s pastimes, making a closed circle, placing his two beautiful arms on the shoulders of each pair of gopis, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

He is the cause (kandah) of pastimes of Cupid (kusama-sarasana'). He placed his two beautiful arms on the shoulders of pairs of gopis.

### Text 10

*aliparivīte māruta-śīte*  
*vara-saṅgīte bhuvanātīte \|*  
*bhūṣaṇatāra-dhvani-parisāra-*  
*krānta-vanānte śaśi-ruci-kānte \|\|9\|\|*

*madhyaga-madhyaga-madhupa-virāji-*  
*sphuṭa-campaka-tati-vibhrama-bhāji \|*  
*rāse kṛta-rucir anta-sthāyī*  
*veṇu-mukhādhara-pallava-dāyī \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, tasting the rasa dance, pervaded by bees, cooled by the breeze, with fine music, transcending this world, beautiful with the light of the moon, whose loud sounds of ornaments reached the edge of the forest, which appeared like many bees placed between pairs of campaka trees, when he stood in the middle with Radha, with the flute on his bud-like lips, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses are connected. He is further described. He desired the rasa dance (rase krta-rucih). The dance is described. It was pervaded by bees. The meaning is clear.

The loud (tara) jingling of their ornaments reached the edge of the forest.

It appeared like bees situated between pairs of campaha trees. He was situated in the center with Radha. He placed his bud-like lips to the mouth of the flute.

### Text 11

*stambhita-rākā-patir avikārān*  
*api sura-dārān madayann ārāt \|*  
*kutukākṛṣṭaś ciram abhivṛṣṭaḥ*  
*sapadi vilūnaiḥ sura-taru-sūnaiḥ \|\|11\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, stunning the moon, agitating the sober heavenly women in the sky, attracted by the pleasure of the dance, continuously showered with flowers from heavenly desire trees at that time, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

He is further described. He stunned the moon. He agitated the heavenly women who cannot be disturbed, who were far away (arat), in the sky. He was attracted to the pleasure of the rasa dance (kutuka). He at that moment was showered with flowers cut from the heavenly desire trees.

### Text 12

*atha kalpīkṛta-rajani-vihārī*  
*khastha-surāsura-vismaya-kārī \|*  
*nija-nija-nikaṭa-sthiti-vijñāna-*  
*pramudita-ramaṇī-kṛta-saṁmānaḥ \|\|12\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, making the night into Brahma’s night, astonishing all the devatas in the sky, respected by the gopis who were overjoyed on realizing he was at the side of each of them, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

He played, making the night into Brahma’s night. The night of three yamas, he made into Brahma’s night. They mutually desired to experience each other’s qualities to perfection. This is explained by the wise in the following:

*brahmarātra upāvṛtte vasudevanumoditah*

**After an entire night of Brahma had passed, Lord Krsna advised the gopis to return to their homes. (SB 10.33.38)**

He astonished the devatas in the sky. He was respected by the gopis who were overjoyed on experiencing him situated beside each of them.

### Text 13

*nija-dṛg-bhaṅgī-kṣubhita-kuraṅgī-*  
*nayanāmaṇḍala-guru-kuca-saṅgī \|*  
*keli-vilolaḥ pracala-nicolaḥ*  
*sveda-jalāṅkura-cāru-kapolaḥ \|\|13\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who embraced the group of heavy-breasted doe-eyed gopis agitated by his glance, who moved about while playing, whose garments became loose, whose forehead was decorated with drops or perspiration, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

He associated in the form of embracing the heavy-breasted gopis agitated by his glance. The rest is clear.

### Text 14

*kumuda-yutāyāṁ taraṇi-sutāyāṁ*  
*salila-vinoda-pravalita-modaḥ \|*  
*yuvati-nikāya-prokṣita-kāyaḥ*  
*śithilita-mālaḥ pulaka-karālaḥ \|\|14\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, who took pleasure in water sports in the Yamuna filled with lotuses, whose body was splashed by all the gopis, whose garland became loose, whose hairs stood on end, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

He was blissful in water play. His body was splashed (proksita) by the groups of gopis. His hairs stood on end intensely.

### Text 15

*atha vanamālī vara-vipinālī-*  
*kuñja-niketana-vīkṣaṇa-śālī \|*  
*jayati vihāri niśi maṇi-hārī*  
*vraja-taruṇī-gaṇa-mānasa-hārī \|\|15\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, wearing a forest garland, searching for a bower house in the forest, playing at night, wearing a jewel necklace, attracting the minds of the gopis, manifests his excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

Playing in the forest is described. The meaning is clear.

### Text 16

*nata-jana-bandho jaya rasa-sindho*  
*vadanollasita-śrama-jala-bindo \|*  
*tvam akhila-devāvali-kṛta-sevā-*  
*santatir adhamā vayam iha ke vā \|\|16\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О friend of the surrendered! О ocean of rasa! May you manifest excellence. О Krsna, whose face shines with perspiration! You are served by all the devatas. Who are we, devoid of good qualities, to engage in serving you?**

**Комментарий:**

Having described the rasa dance, the poet hopes for victory.

May you be victorious or display excellence. Manifest your excellence by such pastimes in Vraja. Krsna may say, “You should serve me in these pastimes.” You are served by all the devatas. Who are we humans, without good qualities (adhama), for serving you (iha)? We are no one. How can we be considered for serving you? If you are merciful, since you are the friend of the surrendered, then we become qualified. We take shelter of that.

### Text 17

*jaya jaya kuṇḍala-yuga-ruci-maṇḍala-*  
*vṛta-gaṇḍa-sthala damitākhaṇḍala \|*  
*dhṛta-govardhana gokula-vardhana*  
*dehi ratiṁ me tvayi mura-mardana \|\|17\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna whose cheeks are covered with the glow of your earrings! О conqueror of Indra! О lifter of Govardhana! О prosperity of Gokula! О killer of Mura! Give me rati for you.**

**Комментарий:**

Fortune of service may be beyond reach. Give a particle of rati. This is his hope.

Your cheeks are covered by the glitter of your earrings. The earrings are attracted to his cheeks. The rest is clear. Thus, the rasa pastime has been explained.

## atha svayum utprekṣita-līlā

*śrī-rādhā-vallabhāya namaḥ \|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to Radha-vallabha.**

### Text 1

*śyāmala-sundara-sauhṛda-baddhā kāmita-tat-pada-saṅgatir addhā \|*  
*dhairyam asau smara-vardhita-bādhā prāpa na mandira-karmaṇi rādhā \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Radha could not remain steady in her household duties, since she was bound by friendship to Syama-sundara, had increased her love, and desired the association of his lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

May Rupa, who condenses all the pastimes of the couple, by whose words people, on tasting them, develop concentrated bliss in sweet streams, grant our desires.

The pastime accomplished by the svayam-duti (words in this case) is called the svayam utpreksita pastime. Radha cannot stay settled in her household duties (mandira-karmani). She is described. She is bound by friendship to Syama-sundara. Thus, she is bound by Cupid. And thus, she desires his association.

### Text 2

*taṁ kamalekṣaṇam īkṣitukāmā sā cchalataḥ savyam ujjhita-dhāmā \|*  
*yāmuna-rodhasi cāru carantī dūram avindata sundara-dantī \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Desiring to see lotus-eyed Krsna, Radha with beautiful teeth, deciding to leave the house on a pretext, went far away to the bank of the Yamuna.**

**Комментарий:**

On the pretext of picking flowers for worship of the sun, Radha went far away, so that there would be no worry of people seeing her. This is in dodhaka meter.

*dodhakamicchati bhatritayā gau*

**Dodhdkam is composed of Iss Iss Iss 11. (bha, bha, bha, gu, gu).**

### Text 3

*prāpyodārāṁ parimala-dhārāṁ kaṁsārāter udayati vāte \|*  
*seyaṁ dattā diśi diśi yattā dṛṣṭiṁ kamrām akirad anamrā \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**When the wind rose, she smelled his intense fragrance. Intoxicated, she cast her attractive glance in all directions, peering with effort, with raised head.**

**Комментарий:**

When the wind rose, she obtained many (udaram) streams of fragrance from Krsna. She became intoxicated and cast her attractive (hamram) glance in all directions. She made efforts to look (yatta), with raised head (anamra).

### Text 4

*bhṛṅgīveyaṁ tam aparimeyaṁ mugdhā gandhaṁ hṛdi kṛta-bandham \|*  
*vyagra-prāyā pulakita-kāyā premodbhrāntā drutam abhiyātā \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Like a bee, disturbed, hairs standing on end, agitated by prema, bewildered Radha quickly went towards the immeasurable fragrance, intent on seeing him.**

**Комментарий:**

Bewildered Radha, like a bee, went quickly towards his unlimited fragrance, intent on seeing him (hrdi krt-bandham). She was quite disturbed (vyatra-praya). The rest is clear. The meter is matta.

*jñeyā mattā mabhasagasṛṣṭā*

**Matta is understood to be 111 Iss ssl 1. (ma, bha, sa, gu).**

### Text 5

*kṛṣṇam avekṣya tataḥ parituṣṭā puṣpa-gaṇāhṛti-kaitava-juṣṭā \|*  
*manthara-pāda-saroruha-pātā kuñja-kuṭīra-taṭīm upayātā \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**
