**Seeing Krsna at that place, satisfied, she went near a bower cottage on the pretext of picking flowers, stepping slowly with her lotus feet.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Krsna there, Radha was satisfied and went near a bower cottage. What was her pretext? She went on the pretext of picking flowers. She was not able to go properly because of her absorption in prema. She stepped slowly with her lotus feet.

### Text 6

*sā pṛthu-vepathu-dolita-hastā prema-samutthita-bhāva-vihastā \|*  
*phulla-mahīruha-maṇḍala-kānte tatra puraḥ prasasāra vanānte \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**With violently quivering hands, disturbed by bhavas arising from prema, she went to the edge of the forest beautiful with many blossoming trees.**

**Комментарий:**

This is in dodhaka meter. She went to the edge of the forest. She is described.

Her hands moved while violently trembling. She was agitated by choked voice, etc., indicating joy, arising from prema. Vihasta means disturbed according to Amara-kosa. The edge of the forest is described. It was beautiful with many blossoming trees. A bhava called vilasa arising from sattva is described. It is described as follows:

*viśeṣo dayitāloke mukhanetrādikarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*yānasthānāsanādeśca vilāsaḥ kathyate budhaiḥ \|\|*

**The wise say that vilasa means particular actions of the mouth, eyes, etc., when moving, standing or sitting, on seeing the beloved. (Kavya-kaustubha)**

This can be applied elsewhere also.

### Text 7

*mādhavas tāṁ tad ālokayan rādhikāṁ*  
*ballavī-vargataḥ sad-guṇenādhikām \|*  
*keyam udbādhate mad-vanaṁ rāgatas*  
*tūrṇam ity ullapan phulla-dhīrāgataḥ \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Madhava, seeing Radha, surpassing all the gopis in good qualities, said, “Who is quickly coming to my forest with attraction?” With joyful mind he approached her.**

**Комментарий:**

Madhava, seeing Radha, approached (agatah). He said, “Who comes to my forest out of attraction?” The rest is clear.

### Text 8

*bhāla-vidyotita-sphīta-gorocanaṁ*  
*pārśvataḥ prekṣya taṁ vibhramal-locanam \|*  
*sā paṭenāvṛtā kaitavād bhāminī*  
*vakrita-bhrūr abhūd dūra-bhū-gāminī \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing Krsna, his forehead bright with gorocana tilaka, his eyes wandering about, Radha, covering herself with her cloth, frowning, went to a distant place on the pretext of picking flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

Seeing Krsna at her side, Radha (bhamini) covered with a cloth, on the pretext of picking some fine flowers (kaitavat) went to a far-off place (dura-bhii-ganiini). She is described. She was frowning. She showed false anger. “Why are you harassing me when I am going to pick flowers for worshipping the sun?” He is described. The meaning is clear. The meter is sragvini. It was explained previously.

### Text 9

*līlodbhrāntaṁ muhur atha nudatī*  
*netra-dvandvaṁ diśi diśi sudatī \|*  
*vīkṣāṁcakre dala-bharāvikaṭāṁ*  
*mallī-vallīṁ taṭa-bhuvi nikaṭām \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Looking with eyes wandering playfully in all directions, she saw a jasmine creeper thick with leaves near the bank of the Yamuna.**

**Комментарий:**

Radha (sudati) saw a jasmine creeper near the bank of the Yamuna. She looked with eyes wandering playfully in all directions. The creeper was full of leaves.

### Text 10

*tām unmīlad-bhramara-vilasitāṁ*  
*labdhā puṣpair upari kila sitām \|*  
*līnevābhūd vikasita-madanā*  
*tasyāḥ prānte sarasija-vadanā \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Lotus faced Radha, manifesting love, came to the creeper, blossoming white with flowers on top and with hovering bees, and disappeared in it.**

**Комментарий:**

Lotus faced Radha came to the creeper and disappeared in it. The creeper is described. It was white with flowers on top. The rest is clear. The phrases such as

“Eyes wandering about playfully” (text 9) indicate the sancari-bhava of avdhittha.

The meter is bhramara. It is described as follows.

*gau gau nau go bhramaravila site*

**11    11 sss sss 1 (gu, gu, gu, gu, na, na, gu) manifests as bhramara.**

### Text 11

*añjasā vyāharat kañjasārekṣaṇas*  
*tām asau sragviṇīṁ dāma-saurabhya-bhāk \|*  
*mādhurīm udgiran sādhu-rīty-ujjvalāṁ*  
*nūtanānandadāṁ pūtanā-mardanaḥ \|\|11\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Wearing a fragrant garland, lotus eyed Krsna, radiating beauty, spoke to Radha, bright with trembling limbs, wearing a garland and giving fresh bliss.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna, killer of Putana, spoke joyfully (anjasa) to Radha. He is described. He had lotus eyes. He radiated beauty (madhurim udgiran). Riti indicates that she trembled. The rest is clear.

### Text 12

*bhaṅgurān aṅkurān nirdayaṁ chindatī*  
*vīrudhaḥ komlodbhedinīr bhindatī \|*  
*āḥ kathaṁ luṇṭhasi tvaṁ mṛgāṅkānane*  
*puṣpa-rājīm asau hanta mat-kānane \|\|12\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O moon-faced Radha! Mercilessly cutting the crooked sprouts, breaking the creepers with tender buds, why do you plunder the flowers in my grove?**

**Комментарий:**

What did he say? O moon-faced Radha! Why are you stealing all the flowers in my grove? Hanta expresses grief. Ah indicates anger according to Amara-kosa. Radha is described. Mercilessly she cuts the crooked shoots. She breaks the tenderly sprouting creepers. Sragvinl is the meter.

### Text 13

*sadātra cinumaḥ prasūnam ajane*  
*vayaṁ hi niratāḥ surābhi-bhajane \|*  
*na ko’pi kurute niṣedha-racanaṁ*  
*kim adya tanuṣe pragalbha-vacanam \|\|13\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Engaged in worshipping the devatas, we always pick flowers in this solitary forest. No one has forbidden us. Why do you today use such rough words?**

**Комментарий:**

She speaks with boldness at first to Krsna who spoke with seeming anger.

Engaged in worshipping the devatas we always pick flowers in this solitary forest (ajane). No one has forbidden us. Today you express some bold words. Knowing dharma, you should not argue about worshipping devatas. Since it is a solitary place, there is no worry about other people coming.

### Text 14

*prasīda kusumaṁ vicitya sarasā*  
*prayāmi sarasīruhākṣa tarasā \|*  
*kriyādya mahatī mamāsti bhavane*  
*vilambam adhikaṁ tanuṣva na vane \|\|14\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Krsna! Be merciful! Picking the flowers, being gracious, I will quickly leave. I have plenty of work to do at home. Do not delay me further in the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

She then speaks politely.

O lotus-eyed one! Be merciful! Do not stop me from picking flowers. Since I am gracious (sarasa), I cannot speak roughly. Picking the flowers, I will quickly go, since I have important work to do in the house today. Do not delay me further in the forest by arguing. Another meaning is “Please accept me as 1 have great attraction to you (sarasa).” I am attracted to you with lotus eyes, and thus cannot stay in my house. Thus, quickly be merciful. I do not have any great work in the house. Thus, delay more in the forest.

The meter is jaloddhata. This was explained previously.

### Text 15

*niyuktaḥ kṣitīndreṇa tenāsmi kāmaṁ*  
*vanaṁ pālayāmi krameṇābhirāmam \|*  
*janaḥ śīrṇam apy uddhared yo dalārdhaṁ*  
*harāmy ambaraṁ tasya vittena sārdham \|\|15\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Engaged by Cupid, I nicely protect this attractive forest. I will take away the clothing and wealth of anyone who takes a withered leaf or half a petal from the forest.**

**Комментарий:**

Desiring to hear attractive words again, he speaks roughly in two verses (15-16). Engaged by the famous Cupid (ksitindrena), 1 protect this attractive garden, a place of pastimes. I will take the cloth and wealth of anyone who takes a withered petal or half a petal from the forest.

### Text 16

*parijñātam adya prasūnālim etāṁ*  
*lunīṣe tvam evaṁ pravālaiḥ sametām \|*  
*dhṛtāsau mayā kāñcana-śreṇi-gauri*  
*praviṣṭāsi gehaṁ kathaṁ puṣpa-cauri \|\|16\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I have understood today that you have taken flowers with branches. I have caught you. О flower thief! Somehow, you have entered the king’s house.**

**Комментарий:**

I have understood today that you have plucked flowers with shoots. I have caught you. О flower thief! By some madness (katham), constantly doing this, you have entered the king’s house. Powerful Cupid is dependent on me and according to his desire speaks. If I meet you what can he do? Thus, waiting for you, I stay in the forest. By good fortune, you have come. I am attracted to only you. О Radha, pale as gold!

The meter is bhujanga-prayata. It was described previously.

### Text 17

*sa patiḥ piśunaḥ kupito’piśunaḥ*  
*sadane mukharā jaratī mukharā \|*  
*caturā guravo bhavitā kuravo*  
*vyasanaṁ puruṣeśvara kiṁ kuruṣe \|\|17\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**My husband is a fault finder and getting angry causes me pain. Old Mukhara, constantly talking, resides in the house. The spying elders will criticize. О supreme person! Why do you make this fruitless attempt?**

**Комментарий:**

In order to experience greater bliss, she explains the suffering that will be caused by being late.

My husband always finds fault. Not only that, he becomes angry, he does not only find fault but inflicts pain. Other meanings are not appropriate. There is another cause of fear. Mukhara, the grandmother, the old women who speaks roughly, stays in the house. Elders, like the mother-in-law, very alert, stay in the house. They will criticize my lateness, though I belong to you. O lord of men! Why are you intent on a fruitless endeavor by which both of us are criticized? Vyasandm means a fruitless attempt according to Visva. You, the supreme person, should make me happy, not afflict me at this time.

### Text 18

*jalajekṣaṇa he kulajām abalāṁ*  
*na hi duryaśasā racayādhavalām \|*  
*tarasā viramat-kiraṇaṁ taraṇiṁ*  
*divi paśya tatas tyaja me saraṇim \|\|18\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O lotus-eyed Krsna! Do not spoil this child of good family with infamy. Look at the sun, withdrawing its rays quickly in the sky. Stop blocking my path.**

**Комментарий:**

O lotus-eyed one! Do not contaminate me, a child of good family, with infamy (dur-yasasa). Look at the sun withdrawing its rays in the sky. For this reason, stop blocking my path. Who will criticize us? Since the sun is setting, quickly fulfil my desires.

“Giving up their relationship as eternal husband and wife, since they are eternally in this position like heat in fire, as sakti and saktiman, why do they perform this pastime as paramours?” They do this out of their supreme power. They are not bound to rules. They are not fixed in married life out of fear, under the control of rules of dharma. Paramours are fixed in ignoring the rules of dharma. It is not for attracting others’ minds. It is by their desire as proven by statements like na paraye ’ham (SB 10.32.22).

Their absorption is caused only by beauty of the object. It is not for nourishing their longing, since that is eternally nourished. Therefore, the sakti and saktiman being married or unmarried arises from their supreme power. This is the conclusion of the wise.

The meter is totaka.

### Text 19

*jāne tava kaca-pakṣaṁ*  
*sambhṛta-vara-mallikā-pakṣam \|*  
*urasi ca kañcuka-rājaṁ*  
*dhruvam arbudha-mādhavī-bhājam \|\|19\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I know that in your tied hair there are many fine jasmine flowers and in the bodice on your chest there are certainly ten million madhavi flowers.**

**Комментарий:**

In two verses (19-20), Krsna explains that Radha should obey. O moon-faced Radha! You desire to cheat me by sweet words. I am not like that. Moreover, I am dependent on Cupid. If you desire to go quickly to your house, then give these items belonging to the king which I see. Kaca-paksam means the tied hair. Madhavi means the vasanti flower.

### Text 20

*ehi tava kṣaṇa-mātraṁ vicārayāmi kramād gātram \|*  
*tattve kila nirṇīte prayāhi bhavanaṁ taḍita-pīte \|\|20\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Come here a moment. I will inspect your limbs one after the other. O Radha, yellow as lightning! Having discerned the truth, go home.**

**Комментарий:**

He reveals his suggestion. In order, 1 will touch your hair, your chest, your skirt, etc. After having looked in your hair, which are actually the king’s possession, go home. О Radha, yellow as lightning. The meter is arya. This is the same as upagiti.

*āryāparārdha tulye dala dvaye prāhur upagītim*

**Aryaparardha of two lines is called upagiti.**

Aryaparardha has twenty-seven matras.

### Text 21

*na mudhā mādhava racaya vivādaṁ*  
*vidadhe tava muhur aham abhivādam \|*  
*gokula-vasatau svaram iva mūrtaṁ*  
*na kim u bhavantaṁ jāne dhūrtam \|\|21\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Madhava! Do not uselessly quarrel. I give you proof all the time. I know that you are the very form of Cupid, a cheater, living in Gokula.**

**Комментарий:**

Hearing Krsna’s sweet words, intoxicated Radha looked at him with a side glance and gave an answer to counter his speech.

О Madhava! Madhava means he who possesses spring (madhu). It means he who is dependent on the pleasure of spring. It also means he who destroys Radha’s knowledge of family dharma by his sweetness of form, etc. Abhivadam means proof. Therefore, give the instruction to go home. “I am the servant of Cupid. Unless I determine his valuables, how can I give the order?” You are not the servant of Cupid but the king of rasa full of knowledge and bliss. Cupid is somewhat comparable. You speak like this because of your cheating nature.

### Text 22

*vetti na gopī vṛndārāmaṁ*  
*vṛndāvanam api bhuvi kaḥ kāmam \|*  
*aham iha tad idaṁ kitava rasālaṁ*  
*katham avaceṣye na kusuma-jālam \|\|22\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Who in this world does not know that Vrndavana is the garden of the gopi Vrnda? О cheater! Why should I not pick the sweet flowers?**

**Комментарий:**

Vrndavana belongs to us gopis because my friend Vrnda is its protector. This is known to all people. Who is Cupid in this place? Who are you to forbid us picking the flowers? The meter is pajjhatikd. This was explained previously.

### Text 23

*nedam atra kalasa-stani śaṁsa*  
*krodhano nṛpatir eṣa nṛśaṁsaḥ \|*  
*tena hanta vidite vana-bhaṅge*  
*yauvataṁ patati bhīti-taraṅge \|\|23\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Radha with pot-like breasts! Do not speak like this. The king is cruel and angry. When he learns that you have pillaged his forest, he will throw your youth into the waves of fear.**

**Комментарий:**

When Radha spoke, Krsna, glancing at her breasts, spoke to her with a gentle attitude.

О Radha with pot-like breasts! Do not speak (samsa) these words. King Cupid is cruel and angry. Hearing your words, he will become angry. Therefore, do not speak. “What will happen if he becomes angry?” When he understands that young girls have broken his forest, he will make your youth fall into waves of fear. He will pierce your heart with many arrows. He will have me crush your breasts and bite your lips. The present tense is used to show that it is about to happen.

### Text 24

*tanvi geha-gamana-vyavasāyaṁ*  
*cet karoṣi śṛṇu ramyam upāyam \|*  
*atra matta-bahu-ṣaṭpada-vīre*  
*līlayā praviśa kuñja-kuṭīre \|\|24\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О slender Radha! If you want to go home, please listen to this easy method. Enter the bower cottage with ease, where intoxicated bees stand guard.**

**Комментарий:**

“How should I escape the cruel king of love? How will I return home?”

The meaning is clear. Enter casually into the bower cottage. If I am satisfied, you do not have to fear Cupid at all. You do not have to worry about neutral people entering. There are warriors to prevent them, the bees.

The meter is svagata.

*svāgatā ranabhagair guruṇā ca*

**Isl sss Iss 11 (ra, na, bha, gu, gu) is svagata.**

### Text 25

*gokule kula-vadhūbhir arcitā*  
*śīla-candana-rasena carcitā \|*  
*rādhikāham adhikāritām ataḥ*  
*kiṁ karoṣi may dhūrta kāmataḥ \|\|25\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**In Gokula, I, Radha, am worshipped by the cultured women and anointed with sandalwood of good character. О rascal! Out of your desire, you control me. What shall I do?**

**Комментарий:**

Though internally pleased, she showed boldness externally. Sila means good character. Claiming me, of this character, what should I do? My inner consent does not waiver, however.

### Text 26

*nākṣiṇī kṣipa kuraṅgi sarvataḥ*  
*sākṣiṇī bhava sakhībhir anvitā*  
*mādhavaḥ kila dunoti mām asau*  
*sādhavaḥ śṛṇuta bhoḥ śikhi-striyaḥ \|\|26\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Do not glance at me. О deer! Be my witnesses along with my friends. О chaste wives of the peacocks! Please listen. Madhava attacks me.**

**Комментарий:**

If you desire to do something improper with me, I will scold you. I will make the deer my witness. The meaning of the verse is clear. There is no one else here. You can freely enjoy with me.

Rathoddhata is the meter.

*rātparair naralagai rathoddhatā*

**Isl sss Isl si (ra, na, ra, la, gu) is rathoddhata.**

### Text 27

*bhrūlekhāṁ kim arālāṁ tvaṁ nirmāsi karālāṁ*  
*kiṁ vā paśyasi vāmaṁ saṁrambhād abhirāmam \|*  
*diṣṭyā kānana-lolā helotphulla-kapolā*  
*vṛttā tvaṁ hari-haste trātānyo bhuvi kas te \|\|27\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Why do you frown at me so fiercely? Why do you look at my beautiful form with crookedness, out of anger? Going happily to the forest, your cheeks showing signs of love, you have fallen into my attractive hands. Who on this earth can save you?**

**Комментарий:**

Crazed by the sweetness of her suggestion Krsna speaks.

Dear Radha! Satisfying me with the nectar of suggested meanings, why do you show crooked (aralam) eyebrows? This rhymes with karalam. It means possessing kolas or parts. Why do you look at me, so beautiful, with crookedness (vdmam) because of anger? Distya means with happiness according to Amara-kosa. You have fallen into my attractive hand (hari-haste) or into the hands of a lion. No one on earth can rescue you from a lion. Radha is described. She desires to go to the forest. Her cheeks are blossoming with symptoms of love (held).

*abhilakṣye vikāre tu hāvo helā smṛtā budhaiḥ*

**The wise defined held as hdva with visible symptoms of love. (Kdvya-kaustubha)**

Your love for me is known by the hairs standing on end on your cheeks. Thus, 1 know that your anger indicated by your frown is false. Therefore, fulfill my desire.

### Text 28

*āruhya druma-vāṭīṁ muñcemāṁ paripāṭīṁ*  
*gehāntas tava sarvaṁ jāne bhāmini garvam \|*  
*nediṣṭaḥ kila bhūpaḥ so’yaṁ bhairava-rūpas*  
*tasyāgre cala vāme colīm arpaya vāme \|\|28\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О beautiful Radha! Coming to the forest, give up these actions. I know your pride belongs to your house. The king, of terrifying form, is near. О splendid woman! Go to him. Or offer to me your bodice.**

**Комментарий:**

О beautiful Radha! Coming to the forest (druma-vatim), free yourself from this action, showing anger because of wanting to go home. Your pride gives results in the house with assistance of your friends like Lalita, but not in the forest, when you are alone. “How will I go home?” He explains two methods. This fearful form, Cupid, the king, is near. Go to him. О vama! He will punish you according to your fault. If you are afraid of that terrifying form, give me your bodice. I will be satisfied with that. When I am satisfied, the king will be pleased with you.

The meter is alola. It is described as follows:

*dviḥsapta-cchid alolā msau mbhau gau caraṇe cet*

**111 ssl 111 Iss 11 (ma, sa, ma, bha, gu, gu) with caesura after the seventh syllable and fourteenth syllable.**

### Text 30

*iti vacana-kadambais tatra narmāvalambaiḥ*  
*skhalad-amala-dukūlāṁ prollasad-bāhu-mūlām \|*  
*aviśada-pada-baddhaṁ  gadgadodgāra-naddhaṁ*  
*kim api kim api jalpaṁ kalpyantīm analpam \|\|29\|\|*

*smita-mudita-kapolāṁ nirmitāpāṅga-dolāṁ*  
*vara-yuvatiṣu rādhāṁ prema-pūrād agādhām \|*  
*sadanitalatikāntaryo nināyātikāntaḥ*  
*sa harir alam abhīṣṭa-prāpaṇaṁ me kṛṣīṣṭa \|\|30\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Having spoken these words full of jokes, leading into the creeper bower Radha, deepest with full prema among the gopis, whose pure cloth had slackened, whose lower shoulders were exposed, who spoke indescribable, unclear words profusely in a choked voice, who glanced with fickleness, with smiling cheeks, may Krsna, the son of Nanda, full of desire, fulfill my desire.**

**Комментарий:**

Having tasted many playful words, the two lovers attained their desire. This is described in two verses.

May Krsna, the son of Nanda, attracting Radha’s mind, fulfill my desire, (next verse)

Having spoken these words, full of desire (atikantah), he took Radha into the creeper pavilion. Radha is described. Her pure dress became loose from the playful conversation. Her lower shoulders then became exposed (prollasat). She spoke indescribable (kim apt) words, which were woven with unclear words, in a choked voice. Her cheeks were joyful with a smile. She had fickle glances. She was deep because of having full prema among all the gopis.

The meter is malini. It was explained previously.

Thus, Svayam utpreksita-lila has been explained.

## atha khanḍitā

**The abandoned woman**

*namaḥ śrī-vraja-nāgarāya \|*

**Перевод:**

**I offer respects to the hero of Vraja.**

### Text 2

*avajñāya bhartur mahā-ghora-daṇḍaṁ*  
*guror bhāṣitaṁ ca vyatikramya caṇḍam \|*  
*niṣedhoddhurāṁ kiṅkarīm ākṣipantī*  
*hare kṛṣṇa nātheti bālā japantī \|\|1\|\|*

*rasan-megha-jāle taḍidbhiḥ karāle*  
*galad-vāri-dhāre durantāndhakāre \|*  
*milad-bhūri-doṣe sakhi me pradoṣe*  
*prayāṇāya lajjām anādṛtya sajjā \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna! My friend, a shy young girl, decorated herself for going out in the night, which was filled with rumbling, rainladen clouds and lightning, full of darkness, ignoring terrible punishment from her husband, overcoming the words of elders and rejecting the forbiddance of servants, while uttering, “O Hari! O Krsna! O master!”**

**Комментарий:**

Lalita speaks to Krsna when Krsna comes to Radha’s place in the morning with marks of enjoyment from another woman on his body, after cheating on Radha. Two verses are joined together. O Krsna! My friend decorated herself in the evening for going out to meet you. She prepared herself by dressing up nicely. She ignored the terrible punishment of her husband and overcame the words of elders and sister-inlaw. She chastised servants who forbade her strongly from going into the great darkness. “O fools! What do you know?” The night is described. There were many clouds making terrifying sounds (rasat), filled with lightning. The night had many faults.

### Text 4

*adūrollasad-bhallukārabdha-yuddhāṁ*  
*valad-dandaśūkāvalī-bhoga-ruddhām \|*  
*samantād dhvanad-vāyasārāti-bhīmāṁ*  
*rasotphullam ullaṅghya kāntāra-sīmām \|\|3\|\|*

*praviśyānavadyaṁ latā-geha-madhyaṁ*  
*dhṛtautsukya-cakrā nisargād avakrā \|*  
*nakhāgra-pralūnaiḥ sugandhi-prasūnaiḥ*  
*payaḥ-phena-kalpaṁ vyadhatteha talpam \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Passing with joyful love by the forest edge, where, not far off bears were fervently fighting, slithering snakes wiggled everywhere with their bodies and hoods, and frightening owls hooted, entering a faultless creeper cottage, with great anuraga, with great sincerity, she prepared a bed, white as foam, made of fragrant flowers picked with her nail tips.**

**Комментарий:**

Two verses are joined together.

Passing the impenetrable edge of the forest with blossoming love (rasotphullam), entering the praiseworthy creeper house, my friend prepared a bed of fragrant flowers. The forest edge is described. Not far off bears were fighting enthusiastically. Crawling snakes covered the place with their bodies and hoods. It was frightening with hooting owls. What did she do? She was filled with anuraga (dhrta-autsukya-cakra). She was not duplicitous (avakrah). She did not know you were cheating her. The rest is clear.

### Text 5

*praṇītekṣaṇeyaṁ muhus te padavyāṁ*  
*dadhānā mukunda spṛhāṁ navya-navyām \|*  
*alabdhaṁ tatas tvām ametyātikhinnā*  
*babhūva prasūneṣu-bāṇair vibhinnā \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Mukunda! My friend, maintaining her ever-fresh desire, gazing constantly at your path, understanding that you would not come, and pierced by Cupid’s arrows, fell into lamentation.**

**Комментарий:**

О Mukunda! My friend (iyam), gazing on your path, maintained her ever-fresh desire. Understanding (avetya) you were unavailable because the time of your coming had passed, she was pierced with Cupid’s (prasunesu) arrows and began lamenting.

### Text 6

*sukaṇṭhī śaṭheyaṁ bhajantī prajalpaṁ*  
*muhur bhāvayantī nimeṣaṁ ca kalpam \|*  
*cakārādya kuñje batālabdha-kāme*  
*sakhī jāgaraṁ sambhramādekikā me \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**My friend constantly muttered, “This cheater!” thinking one moment was a kalpa. Out of illusion, my friend remained awake alone in the bower which was no longer attractive.**

**Комментарий:**

О cheater! My friend with a beautiful throat, uttered constantly, “Why has he not come?” Experiencing a second as a kalpa, she remained awake in the bower, alone, since she erred, thinking that you had affection, when you do not. The bower is described. It was no longer attractive (alabdha-kame). Cheating this girl with such attraction, you are a cheater (satha). This is described:

*śaṭha ekasyāṁ rakto bahiḥ parasyā dhṛtapraṇayaḥ*

**The cheater, attached to one woman externally, has affection for another. (Kavya-kaustubha)**

Though Radha was served by thousands of servants, she sometimes went alone, out of great longing.

### Text 7

*aho bhāgyam adya prapanno’si sadyas*  
*tvam asminn agāre yad ārān murāre \|*  
*sakhī-vṛnda-dṛṣṭir dhṛtānanda-vṛṣṭir*  
*babhūvātta-raṅgaṁ vilokya tvad-aṅgam \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Murari! How fortunate, that today you have immediately come to our place from far off. All our friends’ eyes shower tears of bliss on seeing the marks of love on your limbs.**

**Комментарий:**

Having described Radha’s suffering Lalita scolds Krsna.

О Murari! It is fortunate that today you have come to our house from far away.

Seeing your limbs which have had enjoyment, all the sakhis eyes are filled with tears of bliss. What other good fortune is there?

You bear the marks of love of our competitor, by their differing characteristics. Seeing your limbs ornamented with the rival’s nail marks and kunkuma from her breast, our friends weep tears of sorrow, because Radha was cheated. That is most unfortunate. How unfortunate she is. This speech is a sign of affection.

### Text 8

*dukūlasya lakṣmīṁ samantād viśālām*  
*asau vīkṣya pītasya te malli-mālā \|*  
*luṭhantī kucodbhāsi-kāśmīra-paṅke*  
*nijaṁ pītam aṅgaṁ cakārādya śaṅke \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I think that your jasmine garland, seeing the great beauty of your yellow cloth, has today colored your limbs yellow, by rolling in the kunkuma shining on the breast of our rival.**

**Комментарий:**

Though Krsna does not accept her accusations, she makes him accept the marks on his body in three verses (8-10). I think that your jasmine garland, seeing the great beauty of your yellow cloth, has colored your limbs yellow, rolling in the kunkuma shining on the breast of our rival.

### Text 9

*vikīrṇālakāntaḥ pariśrāntikāntas*  
*tava vyakta-tandraḥ sphuraty āsya-candraḥ \|*  
*kṛtānaṅga-yāgaṁ vibhaktāṅga-rāgaṁ*  
*nakhāṅkāli-pātraṁ tathedaṁ ca gātram \|\|9\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Your moon-like face, fatigued with withered beauty, has scattered locks. And your limbs colored by cosmetics and fingernail marks have performed Cupid’s sacrificial rites.**

**Комментарий:**

“The garland is naturally yellow.”

Your moon-like face has its locks scattered. Your limbs are decorated with cosmetics and patterns made by nails. It is certain that you have performed Cupid’s sacrificial rites.

### Text 10

*sphurad-bandhujīva-prasūnāpta-saṅgaṁ*  
*parispardhamāno vilāsena bhṛṅgam \|*  
*mudaṁ kasya bimbādharas tena raktaḥ*  
*karoty ujjvalāṁ kajjalenādya saktaḥ \|\|10\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Your bimba-red lips, stained by collyrium, competing with a bee on a shining bandhu-jiva flower, are not attractive to anyone.**

**Комментарий:**

“What you think as marks of love affairs, have occurred because of wrestling in the moonlight, on agreement with friends.”

Your red bimba lips, stained with collyrium, are not pleasing to anyone (kasya ujjvalam mudam). “All my friends did this to me.” The lips are described. They compete with a bee which has landed on a shining bandhu-jiva flower. It is not possible to conceal this mark. Your lips smeared with collyrium prove your association, just as the yellowed garland did. You can see your friends in the moonlight, as in a dream. Who would injure your face, since you are the prince?

### Text 11

*alaṁ deva-divyena jāne bhavantaṁ*  
*sadā rādhikāyām atipremavantam \|*  
*alindāt kuru tvaṁ mamādhi-prabhātaṁ*  
*drutaṁ gopakanyā-bhujaṅga prayātam \|\|11\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna fond of playing! May you be cursed. I know that you have great love for Radhika. O snake for the gopis! Go quickly from this porch and end my mental anguish.**

**Комментарий:**

Having established his faults though scolding him, she speaks with affectionate anger, rejecting his statements of innocence. О Krsna, inclined to play (deva)! О snake for the gopis (or lusty for the gopis) \\ О lover of Candravali! May you be cursed (divyena alam). Divyam means a curse according to Visvalocana. I know that you have love for Radha. This means you have no love for her—by stating the opposite. “Then what are you ordering me to do?” Go immediately from my porch. This will end the pain (prabhatam) in my heart. You pain our hearts by showing love marks of our rival. When you leave our sight, we can sleep happily.

### Text 12

*iti prema-garbhāṁ samākarṇya sarvāṁ*  
*tadā rādhikālī-giraṁ ratna-mālī \|*  
*haris toṣa-bhāraṁ sa vindann apāraṁ*  
*sadā me mahiṣṭaṁ vidhattām abhīṣṭam \|\|12\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna with a jeweled necklace, who, hearing all Lalita’s words filled with prema, became most pleased, grant my great wish.**

**Комментарий:**

May Krsna with a jeweled necklace grant my great desire. This is the statement of the poet. What does Krsna do? Hearing Lalita’s (radhikali) words filled with prema, he experienced great, incomparable satisfaction. Krsna is more pleased by the scolding of a respected gopi, than by hearing praises from the Vedas. He says in Adi-purana:

*na tathā rocate vedaḥ purāṇādyāstathetare \|*  
*yathā tāsāṁ tu gopīnāṁ bhartsanāgarbhitaṁ vacaḥ \|\|*

**The Vedas, Puranas and other scriptures do not please me as much as the gopis’ words indicating scolding.**

The meter is bhujanga-prayata. It was described previously.

## atha lalitokta-toṭakāṣṭakam

### Text 1

*nayanerita-mānasa-bhū-viśikhaḥ*  
*śirasi pracala-pracalāka-śikhaḥ \|*  
*muralī-dhvanibhiḥ surabhīs tvarayan*  
*paśupī-viraha-vyasanaṁ tirayan \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna is coming, throwing Cupid’s arrows with his glances, wearing a peacock feather on his head, herding the cows by the sound of his flute, protecting the gopis from pain of separation.**

**Комментарий:**

When Krsna, lord of their lives was rejected by Lalita, Lalita spoke to Radha, in a state of longing after a quarrel, showing her that Krsna was coming from the forest.

О friend! Krsna is coming to this place. But you are agitated (udvijase). (verse 5) The five verses are connected to this statement. Krsna is described.

He throws Cupid’s arrows from his glances. He has a trembling peacock feather (sikha) on his head. Sikha means peacock feather according to Medini. He prevents pain of separation for the gopis.

### Text 2

*parito jananī-paritoṣa-karaḥ*  
*sakhi lampaṭayann akhilaṁ bhuvanam \|*  
*taruṇī-hṛdayaṁ karuṇī vidadhat*  
*taralaṁ sarale kara-lambi-guṇaḥ \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О friend! Krsna is coming, completely satisfying his mother, making the whole world attracted to him, making the young girls’ hearts unsteady, being most compassionate, covered with dust from the cows.**

**Комментарий:**

О friend! He makes one attracted to him (lampatayari). He makes the hearts of the young girls unsteady (taralam). He is compassionate (karuni). He is covered with dust from herding the cows (kara-lambi).

### Text 3

*divasoparame paramollasitaḥ*  
*kalaśa-stani he vilasad-dhasitaḥ \|*  
*atasī-kusumaṁ vihasan-mahasā*  
*hariṇī-kulam ākulayan sahasā \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Radha with pot-like breasts! Krsna is coming, happy to distribute joy by showing his great beauty, smiling brightly, mocking the atasi flower by his effulgence, bewildering the deer by the strength of his flute sound.**

**Комментарий:**

He is joyful at producing joy in the gopis on seeing him attractive with great beauty when the day ends. He mocks the atasi flower by the effulgence (mahasa) of his limbs. Mahas means effulgence according to Amara-kosa. He confuses the deer by the strength of the sound of his flute (sahasa). Sahas means strength according to Haima.

### Text 4

*praṇayi-pravaṇaḥ subhaga-śravaṇa-*  
*pracalan-makaraḥ sa-sakhi-prakaraḥ \|*  
*madayann amarīr bhramayan bhramarīr-*  
*militaḥ katibhiḥ śikhināṁ tatibhiḥ \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna is coming, controlled by his devotees, with swaying earrings in his beautiful ears, accompanied by his friends, intoxicating the devata women, bewildering the bees, joined by flocks of peacocks.**

**Комментарий:**

He is obedient (pravanah) to affectionate people. He is controlled by them. He has makara earrings moving on his beautiful (subhaga) ears. Conquering Cupid, taking his flag, having the emblem of the makara, he has placed them on his earrings. Thus, he must be adored as a lover. He is with his friends. He intoxicates the young devata women by a portion of his pastimes. What to speak of intoxicating human women! He bewildered the bees by his bodily fragrance. Radha should not be inundated in it and become cheated. He is accompanied by group of peacocks. As a cloud give rain, he should give rasa, destroying the pain of your separation.

### Text 5

*ayam ujjvalayan vraja-bhū-saraṇīṁ*  
*ramayan kramaṇair mṛdubhir dharaṇīm \|*  
*ajire militaḥ kalita-pramade*  
*harir udvijase tad api pramade \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, brightening the path of Vraja by the marks on his feet, giving pleasure to the earth with his soft steps, comes to your delighted yard. O girl! But you are disturbed.**

**Комментарий:**

“Where is he at this moment?” He brightens the path of Vraja by the marks of flag and thunderbolt on his feet as he steps (kramanaih). He comes to your yard (ajire), which has become delightful (kalita-pramade). O young girl (pramade)!

### Text 6

*vada mā paruṣaṁ hṛdaye na ruṣaṁ*  
*racaya tvam ataś cala vibhramataḥ \|*  
*udite mihikā-kiraṇe na hi kā*  
*rabhasād ayi taṁ bhajate dayitam \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Do not speak harshly. Do not keep anger in your heart. Depart for pastimes. When the moon rises, what young girl would not worship that dear boy passionately?**

**Комментарий:**

This Krsna has come to your yard. For this reason, go away for pastimes. Do not speak harsh words such as “I will not see him.” Do not be angry in your heart. I scolded him this morning falsely, to bring him under your control. When the moon rises, what rasika girl would not passionately worship him? O friend! They all worship him.

### Text 7

*kalaya tvarayā vilasat-sicayaḥ*  
*prasaraty abhito yuvatī-nicayaḥ \|*  
*nidadhāti harir nayanaṁ saraṇau*  
*tava vikṣipa sa-praṇayaṁ caraṇau \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**All the young girls, dressed beautifully, gather around quickly. Look! Krsna gazes at your path. Go quickly with affectionate steps.**

**Комментарий:**

О friend! All the young girls quickly spread out everything to see him. They wear beautiful clothing (vilasat-sicayah). Krsna keeps his eyes on your path (saranau). Look! Place your feet with affection (sa-pranayam). Go to meet him.

### Text 8

*iti tām upadiśya tadā sva-sakhīṁ*  
*lalitā kila mānitayā vimukhīm \|*  
*anayat prasabhād iva yaṁ javataḥ*  
*kurutāt sa harir bhavikaṁ bhavataḥ \|\|8\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**May Krsna, brought forcibly and quickly by Lalita, who had instructed her friend Radha, who opposed because of anger, bestow auspiciousness to you.**

**Комментарий:**

May Krsna bestow auspiciousness (bhavikam) to you. He is described.

Lalita, instructing her friend Radha by the words above, forcibly (prasabhad) and quickly brought him (yam). She united her with him. Radha is described. She was opposed, because of anger. The meter is totaka. It is described as follows.

*iha toṭakam abdhisakārayutam*

**ssl ssl ssl ssl (sa, sa, sa, sa) is totaka.**

Thus, the astaka in totaka meter spoken by Lalita has been explained.

## citra-kavitvāni

**Picture poems**

## tatra yakṣarāṇi \| Two letter poem

### Text 1

*rasāsārasusārorurasurāriḥ sasāra saḥ \|*  
*saṁsārāsirasau rāse suriraṁsuḥ sasārasaḥ \|\|1\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He who is famous, who produces torrents of rasa, who has beautiful thighs, who is the enemy of the demons, who destroys ignorance, who desires beautiful women, who holds a lotus in his hand, went to the rasa dance.**

**Комментарий:**

May Sri Rupa, king of poets, who, very strong, makes difficult poems, give me a wealth of intelligence.

How does one make a poem using only one or two letters? That is astonishing (citra). Poetic works made with in this astonishing way are called citra-kavitva. Or cakra-bandha, etc., are pictures (citra). Thus, they are called citra-kavitva.

Bharata says:

*taccitraṁ yatra varṇānāṁ khaṅgādyākṛtihetutā \|*

**They called citra where the letters take the form of a sword, etc.**

Where the letters placed in particular places, manifest as a sword or wheel, it becomes a picture or is amazing. Citra means astonishing or a drawing according to Visva.

Krsna, son of Nanda (asurari) who is famous (sah) went (samsara) to the rasa dance (rase). He is called rasa asara: He from who torrents (asara) of rasa arise.

His two thighs (uru) are fine (susaroru).

He holds a play lotus (sa-sarasah).

He cuts the devotee’s ignorance (samsara asih).

He desires beautiful women (suriramsuh).

“Since there are visarga (h) and anusvara (m), how can this be a two letter poem?” That is true, but in citra-kavya, this is acceptable.

### Text 2

*carcorurocir uccorā ruciro’raṁ carācare \|*  
*caurācāro’cirāccīraṁ rucā cāruracūcurat \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He who acts as a thief, charming with his beauty, shining excellently with unguents, with a raised chest, exceedingly attractive to the world, stole the gopis’ clothing quickly.**

**Комментарий:**

The son of Nanda acts as a thief (caura acarah). But he is not a thief. Inclined to pastimes, he acts in this way to give pleasure to his devotees. He stole (aciicurat) the clothing (ciram) of the gopis quickly (acirat). He shines (rocih) excellently (uru) with unguents like sandalwood (carca). He has a raised (ucca) chest (urah). He is attractive (rucirah) to a high degree (агат) in the world (caracare). He is charming (caruh) because of his beauty (ruca).

### Text 3

*dhare dharādharadharaṁ dhārādhara-dhur-ārudham \|*  
*dhīra-dhīr ārarādhādhi-rodhaṁ rādhā dhuraṁdharam \|\|3\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Sober Radha worshipped the lifter of the mountain, the leader who destroys mental anguish, at Govardhana, which obstructed the heavy clouds.**

**Комментарий:**

Radha, daughter of Vrsabhanu, worshipped (araradha) the lifter of the mountain (dharadhara-dharam) at Govardhana (dhare). She did this by offering her wealth of youthfulness. Radha is described. She was steady minded (dhira-dhih). Govardhana is described. It obstructed (arudhi) the weight (dhura) of clouds (dharadhara) released by Indra. The lifter of the mountain destroyed all mental anguish (adhirodham). (Dhuramdharam means the leader.)

## ekākṣaram \| A poem with one letter

### Text 4

*ninunnānenonanaṁ nūnaṁ nānūnonnānanano’nunīḥ \|*  
*nānenānāṁ ninunnenaṁ nānaun nānānano nanu \|\|4\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Oh! Four-headed Brahma, leader of the various devatas, his faces completely moist with tears, pacified, praised with certainty his master who threw the life of cart demon far away.**

**Комментарий:**

Why praise Krsna, the cowherd, so much? Someone answers that person with this poem.

О protester (nanu)’. Four headed Brahma (nanananah) praised (na na anaut) his master the cowherd (inam) for certain (пйпат). He was the leader (ninut) of various masters like Indra (папа inanam). Nud means to inspire. He is further described. His faces (ananah) were moist (unna) with tears completely (na апйпа). Und means moist. He wept warm tears out of fear. He was pacified (anunlh). Krsna (inam) is described. He threw (ninunna) the life (anana) of the cart demon (anah) far away.

## cakrabandhaḥ \| The wheel poem

### Text 5

*gandhākṛṣṭa-gurūnmadālini vane hāra-prabhāti-plutaṁ*  
*sampuṣṇantam upaskṛtādhvani yamī-vīci-śriyo rañjakam \|*  
*sadyas tuṅgita-vibhramaṁ sunibhṛte śītānilaiḥ saukhyade*  
*devaṁ nāga-bhujaṁ sadā rasamayaṁ taṁ naumi kañcin mude \|\|5\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**For my bliss, I praise the Lord, endowed with snake-like arms, who is filled with rasa, who increases bewilderment, who is effulgent with necklaces, who nourishes the devotees, who colors the beauty of Yamuna’s waves, in the deserted forest filled with intoxicated bees attracted to the fragrance, having clean paths, giving bliss by its cool breezes.**

**Комментарий:**

I praise some deva for my own bliss (made). Where? In the forest (vane). The forest is described. There, the most intoxicated bees are attracted by the scent. Its paths are cleansed. It is without other people (su-nibhrte). It destroys suffering, giving happiness by the cool breeze. The deva is described. He is spread with the effulgence of necklaces. He nourishes the devotees (sampusnantam). He colors (ranjakam) the beauty of the Yamuna’s waves by the effulgence of his nails, lips, yellow cloth, necklaces, bracelets and crown. He immediately increases bewilderment in others. His arms are rounded like snakes.

## sarpa-bandhaḥ \| Snake poem

### Text 6

*rāse sāraṅga-saṅghā-cita-nava-nalina-prāya-vakṣaḥ-stha-dāmā*  
*barhālaṅkāra-hāra-sphurad-amala-mahā-rāga-citre jayāya \|*  
*gopālo dāsa-vīthī-lalita-hita-rava-sphāra-hāsaḥ sthirātmā*  
*navyo’jasraṁ kṣaṇopāśrita-vitata-balo vīkṣya raṅgaṁ babhāse \|\|6\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the arena for the rasa dance, variegated in pure, radiant, primary colors from peacock feathers, ornaments and garlands, ever-fresh Gopala, wearing a garland of very fresh lotuses covered with swarms of bees, broadly smiling at the attractive, favorable praises uttered by the devotees, remaining calm, gathering strength for the rasa festival, shone to manifest his own excellence.**

**Комментарий:**

The author describes Krsna, enjoyer of the rasa dance.

Gopala, son of Nanda, Bhagavan, seeing the arena for the rasa dance (rase), shone for his own excellence (jay ay a). He is described. He wore a garland of very fresh lotuses on chest, which was covered with swarms of bees (sarahga). He smiled broadly when there were favorable, attractive (lalita-hita) shouts of “O Lord! Manifest your excellence!” made by groups of devotees (dasa-vithi) such as Brahma and Siva.

He remained calm (sthiratma), though hearing himself praised. He inducted the necessary strength for the rasa dance (ksanopasrtia-vitata-balah). He was ever fresh (ajasram navy ah'). The rasa dance is described. It was variegated with pure, radiant, primary colors like blue, yellow and red from peacock feathers, ornaments and garlands.

## padma-bandhaḥ \| Lotus poem

### Text 7

*kala-vākya sadāloka kalodāra milāvaka \|*  
*kavalādyādbhutānūka kanūtābhīra-bālaka \|\|7\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O cowherd child! O sweet speaker! O proficient in all arts! O protector! O Krsna, astonishing with yogurt rice in your hand! O Krsna, followed by Siva and praised by Brahma! Become visible.**

**Комментарий:**

The author prays to directly meet the Lord.

O cowherd child, Nanda’s son (abhlra-balaka)! Become visible (mila). O sweet speaker (kala-vakya)! O seer of the devotees (sad-dloka)! O Krsna, excellent with skills (kalodara)! O protector (avaka)! O form astonishing with yogurt rice, stick, flute and horn. O Krsna, followed by Siva (anuka)! Sesadvibhasa: After all other Bahuvrihi compounds not covered by the foregoing rules, the affix kap (i.e. ka) may optionally be added. (Panini Sutras 5.4.154) O Krsna, praised by Brahma (ka) (ka-nuta)! Brahma said:

*naumīḍya te'bhravapuṣe taḍidambarāya guñjāvataṁsa-paripiccha-lasan-mukhāya \|*  
*vanya-sraje kavala-vetra-viṣāṇa-veṇu-lakṣma-śriye mṛdupade paśupāṅgajāya \|\|*

**My dear Lord, you are the only worshipable Lord, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and therefore I offer my humble obeisances and prayers just to please you. O son of the king of the cowherds, your transcendental body is dark blue like a new cloud, your garment is brilliant like lightning, and the beauty of your face is enhanced by your gunja earrings and the peacock feather on your head. Wearing garlands of various forest flowers and leaves, and equipped with a herding stick, a buffalo horn and a flute, you stand beautifully with a morsel of food in your hand. (SB 10.14.1)**

## prātilomyānulomya samam \| Read forwards and backwards with the same syllables

*tāyisāradharādhārātibhāyātamadārihā \|*  
*hāridāmatayā bhāti rādhārādhara-sāyitā \|\|8\|\|*

**That attractive form, effulgently holding up the huge, solid mountain, killer of proud enemies, attained by the rasa of Radha offering her youth, shines with an attractive garland.**

**Комментарий:**

That form (sa) (inferred) shines with an attractive garland (hari-damataya).

The subject, (sa), deity of the rasa dance with the gopis, (ballavl-rasa-devata) is taken from the next verse.

That form has excellent luster (atibha) in holding up the mountain (dharadhara) with huge (tayi) firmness (sara). He kills proud enemies who have come (ayata-mada ari-ha). That form is attained (ayitd) by the rasa of Radha offering (aradha) her youthfulness. Aya means attaining. This poem can be read forward (normal) and backwards with the same syllables.

## go-mūtrikā-bandhaḥ \| The cow’s urine

### Text 9

*sā malla-raṅge ramaya phulla-sārā mudedhitā \|*  
*śrama-nīra-dharā tuṣṭā ballavī-rāsa-devatā \|\|9\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

The deity of the rasa dance with the gopis, accompanied by Laksmi, blossoming with strength, increasing in bliss, covered in perspiration, was satisfied in the wrestling arena.

The devata of the rasa dance with the gopis was satisfied (tusta) with Canitra in the wrestling arena (malla-rahge). He was with Laksmi (ramaya) in the form of a golden line on his chest. His strength (sara) was blossoming. This means he was very strong. He increased (edhita) his bliss (mud). The rest is clear.

## muraja-bandhaḥ \| The drum

### Text 10

*śubhāsāra-sasāra-śrīḥ prabhāsāndrama-sārabhā \|*  
*bhārasā mahasāvitta tarasā rasa-saritam \|\|10\|\|*

**Комментарий:**

The deity of the rasa dance, with the luster of sapphire rays, who produces streams of auspiciousness, who destroys the burden of the world by his power, made everything harmonious with madhurya-rasa.

The subject, deity of the rasa dance, is from the previous verse.

The deity of the rasa dance quickly produced (avitta) the state of following rasa (rasa-sdritam). Vit means to attain. Rasa-saritam means the state of having the quality of following (saritam) madhurya-rasa. (He made everything congruent with madhurya-rasa.) The ending tam indicated a general state (samanye napumsakam). From him arises wealth (srih) with excellent (sasdra) streams of auspiciousness (subha dsdra). Sara can mean excellent according to Visvalocana.

He has luster (bha) like a concentrated (sandra) sapphire (masdra) with rays (prabhd). He destroys (sa) the burden of the world (bhdra) by his power (mahasd).

Sa comes from sa, meaning to destroy according to Dhatu-sangraha: so’nta-karmani.

## sarvatobhadraḥ \| Auspicious diagram

*rāsāvahā hāvasārā sā lalāsa salālasā \|*  
*balāramā māralāvahāsam ādadamāsahā \|\|11\|\|*

**The devata of the rasa dance, performing the rasa dance, thirsty for the dance, enjoying intensely, intolerably controlling everyone by his smile which conquered Cupid and by his intoxication with his youth, shone.**

**Комментарий:**

The devata of the rasa dance shone (lalasa). He performed (avaha) the rasa dance. He had strength (sard) of hava. He had thirst (sa-lalasa) for the rasa dance. He enjoyed strongly (balarama). He conquered (lavah) Cupid (тага). He had intolerable (asaha) control (dama) by his smile which conquered Cupid and by his intoxication (mada) with his youth. He was independent.

## bṛhat-padma-bandhaḥ \| The big Lotus

### Text 12

*tāra-prasphāra-tālaṁ sarabhasa-saralam bhāsurāsyaṁ subhālaṁ*  
*pāpaghnaṁ gopa-balatn karaṇa-hara-kalaṁ nīrabhṛd-vāra-nīlam \|*  
*cārugrīvaṁ rucālaṁ rata-mada-taralaṁ cetasā pīta-celaṁ*  
*śīta-prasphīta-śīlaṁ varaya vara-balaṁ vāsudevaṁ sabalam \|\|12\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Meditate on Vasudeva, the cowherd boy, who produces long talas with purity, who is sincere in his joyous love, who has a moon-like face, whose forehead is beautiful, who destroys ignorance in devotees, whose songs attract the ear, whose black complexion surpasses a mass of clouds, whose neck is graceful, who decorates the surroundings with his beauty, whose mind trembles from passion of love, who wears yellow cloth, whose abundant good qualities destroy samsara, who has excellent strength, who is accompanied by children.**

**Комментарий:**

Krsna in the rasa dance circle is described.

О friend! Accept Vasudeva, the cowherd child (gopa-balam), with your mind. Siva says:

*vasanādeva vādeṣu vāsudeveti śabditaḥ*

**The word vasudeva means “he dwells in words.” (Hari-vamsa)**

He is known through words. He is purna-brahman. He is described. He produces long talas (beats) such as rupaka, endowed with purity (tara). Tara means pure according to Visva. He is sincere (sarala) in prema (sa-rabhasa—full of joy). His face shines like the moon (bhasura). His forehead is attractive (su-bhalam). He destroys ignorance in his devotees (papa-ghnam). The sound of his sweet singing attracts the ear (karana-hara-kalam). He is blacker than a group (vara) of clouds. He ornaments (lam) the area around him with his beauty (rucu). His widespread good qualities destroy the heat of samsara (sita-prasphtta-silam). He is accompanied by children (sa-balam). The rest is clear. Making the wheel from the words is well known among poets.

Thus, citra-kavitvani has been explained.

## gītāvalī

*śrīrādhākṛṣṇau jayataḥ \|*

**Radha and Krsna manifest their excellence.**

## prathamaṁ nandotsavādi

### 1

*putram udāram asūta yaśodā \|*  
*samajani ballava-tatir atimodā \|\| dhruva. \|\|*  
*ko’py upanayati vividham upahāram \|*  
*nṛtyati ko’pi jano bahu-vāram \|\|*  
*ko’pi madhuram upagāyati gītam \|*  
*vikirati ko’pi sad adhi navanītam \|\|*  
*ko’pi tanoti manoratha-pūrtim \|*  
*paśyati ko’pi sanātana-mūrtim \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Yasoda gave birth to a generous son. All the cowherds became joyful. (Chorus) Someone offered various gifts. Someone danced for a long time. Someone sang sweet songs. Someone sprinkled butter everywhere. Someone was fulfilled in his desires. Someone gazed at the eternal form of Krsna.**

**Комментарий:**

This is a collection of songs. The first describes Nanda’s festival in bhairava raga.

*vittiviraktiśrīharikathānukīrtanakṛtātsāmyāt \|*  
*śukamūcuryaṁ santastaṁ stavamālārthadeśikaṁ vande \|\|*

**I offer respects to the guru for the meaning of Stavamala, whom the devotees call Suka, because of similar glorification of Krsna’s pastimes, which are detached from material acquisition.**

The son was excellent (udaram) with all thirty-two qualities mentioned in samudrika-sastra. Or he was a generous giver (udaram) giving even himself.

Upaharam means gifts. Someone sprinkled (vikirati) butter on the people.

Someone satisfied the minds of the singers by giving them plenty of wealth. Someone, such as Nanda, coming, sees the eternal form of Yasoda’s son, not desiring anything else. Or he sees the form worshipped (word to be supplied) by Sanatana.

This may refer to Krsna (who is eternal), Rupa’s elder brother or to the third son of Brahma. With the last two meanings, it becomes mudra alankara.

The meter is gatha. It is described as follows.

*viṣamākṣarapādaṁ vā pādairasamaṁ daśadharmavat \|*  
*yacchandotoktamatra gātheti tatsūribhiḥ proktam \|\|*

**The wise say that gatha meter, where meter is not stated, has irregular arrangement of syllables per line (for instance eight, ten, seven, nine) or irregular number of lines (like three, five or six lines) or ten, like the ten dharmas. (Vrtta-ratnakara)**

The first type is the above verse. The second type has ten lines. The ten dharmas are described in Mahabharata.

*daśadharmaṁ na jānanti dhṛtarāṣṭra nibodha tān \|*  
*mattaḥ pramatta unmattaḥ śāntaḥ kruddho bubhukṣitaḥ \|*  
*tvaramāṇaśca bhīruścālasaḥ kāmī ca te daśa \|\|*

**О Dhrtarastra! They do not know the ten dharmas. Understand these ten: bewilderment, agitation, insanity, peace, anger, hunger, haste, fright, laziness and lust.**

This poem has six lines. The meters which are not mentioned in Vrtta-ratnakara are gatha.

### 2

*vipra-vṛndam abhūd alaṅkṛti-godhanair api pūrṇam \|*  
*gāyanān api mad-vidhān vrajanātha toṣaya tūrṇam \|\|*  
*sūnur adbhuta-sundaro’jani nandarāja tavāyam \|*  
*dehi goṣṭha-janāya vāñchitam utsavocita-dāyam \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**All the brahmanas were fully satisfied by the gift of ornamented cows. О lord of Vraja! Quickly satisfy singers like me. О King Nanda! Your astonishingly beautiful son has been born. Give to the people of Gokula the desired mercy suitable to this festival.**

### 3

*tāvakātmaja-vīkṣaṇa-kṣaṇa-nandi mad-vidha-cittam \|*  
*yan na kair api labdham arthibhir etad icchati vittam \|\|*  
*śrī-sanātana-citta-mānasa-keli-nīla-marāle \|*  
*mādṛśāṁ ratir atra tiṣṭhatu sarvadā tava bāle \|*

**Перевод:**

**My heart, expanding with joy on seeing your son, desires a treasure which is not attainable by any wealth. May my rati for your son, a black swan playing in the Manasa Lake heart of Sanatana, always remain.**

**Комментарий:**

The raga is asavan.

Narada makes generous Nanda happy at the birth of Krsna as he attempts to give generously.

The brahmanas became fully satisfied with donations of decorated cows.

О lord of Vraja! Quickly satisfy singers like me.

Not only to us singers, but to the people of Gokula, give mercy, proper for a festival. The singular janaya is used to indicate the whole group.

Give to whoever desires. The time has come for great fortunate mercy.

О King Nanda! Such a beautiful son has been born. This is the chorus.

“What do you want? Please say.”

The heart of a person like me who glorifies your son’s qualities and form, which expands with the joy of seeing your son, desires a treasure which is not attained by any type of wealth received from you.

“Explain that.”

May rati for your son always exist for persons like me. The child is described. He is a black swan playing in the Manasa Lake of the heart of sage Sanatana and Rupa’s elder brother.

## vasanta-pañcamī

**Vasanta-pancami celebration**

### 1

*abhinava-kuṭmala-guccha-samujjvala-kuñcita-kuntala-bhāra \|*  
*praṇayi-janerita-vandana-saha-kṛta-cūrṇita-vara-ghana-sāra \|\|*  
*jaya jaya sundara nanda-kumāra \|*  
*saurabha-saṅkaṭa-vṛndāvana-taṭa-vihita-vasanta-vihāra \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Krsna, with curly hair beautiful with clusters of buds! О Krsna, covered with camphor mixed with red powder thrown by the gopis! О beautiful son of Nanda! May you manifest your excellence! О Krsna, playing in the spring at the edge of Vrndavana filled with fragrance!**

**Комментарий:**

The raga is vasanta.

О son of Nanda! May you manifest your excellence. You have curled locks of hair beautiful with clusters of fresh buds. You are covered with camphor mixed with red powder (vandana) thrown (irita) by the gopis.

You perform spring pastimes at the edge of Vrndavana spread (sankata) with fragrance. This is the chorus.

### 2

*adhara-virājita-mandatara-smita-locita-nija-parivāra \|*  
*caṭula-dṛg-añcala-racita-rasoccala-rādhā-madana-vikāra \|\|*  
*bhuvana-vimohana-mañjula-nartana-gati-valgita-maṇi-hāra \|*  
*nija-vallabha-jana-suhṛt-sanātana-citta-viharad-avatāra \|\|2\|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Krsna, increasing greed in the gopis by the soft smile on your lips! O Krsna, causing ecstatic love symptoms in Radha, agitated with anuraga by your sweet glance! O Krsna, whose trembling jeweled necklace, dancing with charm, enchants the world! O friend of your gopis! O avatara playing in the heart of Sanatana!**

**Комментарий:**

The first line is clear in meaning. You produce ecstatic symptoms of love in Radha, fickle with anuraga produced by your sweet glance. You have a jeweled necklace quivering (valigita) with attractive dance movements which enchant the world.

You are the friend of your gopis. Your avatara plays in the heart of Sanatana.

Or the avataras like Rama approach repeatedly with flower balls and colored powder in their hands for the pastimes.

## dolotsavaḥ

**Swing Festival**

### 1

*keli-rasa-mādhurī-tatibhir atimedurī-*  
*kṛta-nikhila-bandhu-paśu-pālam \|*  
*hṛdi vidhṛta-candanaṁ sphurad-aruṇa-vandanaṁ*  
*deha-ruci-nirjita-tamālam \|\|*  
*sundari mādhavam avakalayālam \|*  
*mitra-kara-lolayā ratna-maya-dolayā*  
*calita-vapur-ati-capala-mālam \|\| dhruva \|\|*

Look at your lover, Madhava, who produces affection in the cowherd boys by the sweet rasa of his pastimes, with sandalwood on his chest, mixed with shining red powder, whose bodily complexion conquers the tamala tree, whose garland sways on his body moved by the jeweled swing pushed by friends’ hands.**

**Комментарий:**

This section is in vasanta-raga. O beautiful gopi! Look at your lover, Madhava! He is described. He produces affection in the cowherd boys by the sweet rasa of his pastimes. The next phrase is clear. He has a trembling garland on his body moving because of the jewel studded swing moving by friends’ hands. This is the chorus.

### 2

*vraja-hariṇa-locanā-racita-gorocanā*  
*tilaka-ruci-ruciratara-bhālam \|*  
*smita-janita-lobhayā vadana-śaśi-śobhayā*  
*vibhramita-nava-yuvati-jālam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Look at Madhava, whose forehead is attractive with the beauty of gorocana tilaka made by the doe-eyed gopis, who enchants all the youthful gopis by his moon-like face smiling with greed.**

### 3

*narma-maya-paṇḍitaṁ puṣpa-kula-maṇḍitaṁ*  
*ramaṇam iha vakṣasi viśālam \|*  
*praṇata-bhaya-śātanaṁ priyam adhi sanātanaṁ*  
*goṣṭha-jana-mānasa-marālam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Look at Madhava, most skillful at joking, decorated with many flowers, a lover with broad chest, who destroys fear in his devotees, who is dear to learned Sanatana, who is a swan in the Manasa Lake minds of the people of Vraja.**

**Комментарий:**

His forehead is attractive with the beauty ofgorocana tilaka made by the doe-eyed gopis. He is dear to learned (adhi) Sanatana. The rest is clear.

### 4

*nipatati parito vandana-pālī \|*  
*taṁ dolayati mudā suhṛd-ālī \|\|*  
*vilasati dolopari vanamālī \|*  
*tarala-saroruha-śirasi yathālī \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Red powder falls all around. A friendly sakhi swings him joyfully. Wearing a forest garland, he shines on the swing, like a bee on a trembling lotus.**

**Комментарий:**

This section is in asavari-raga. A friendly sakhi like Lalita (suhrd-ali) or a group of friends, swings the wearer of the forest garland. Piles of red power fall around him. He shines on the swing shaped like a lotus, like a bee on top of a trembling lotus. This is the chorus.

### 5

*janayati gopī-jana-karatālī \|*  
*kāpi puro nṛtyati paśupālī \|\|*  
*ayam āraṇyaka-maṇḍana-śālī \|*  
*jayati sanātana-rasa-paripālī \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The gopis’ hand clapping produces joy. One gopi dances in front of the swing. Krsna, decorated with forest flowers, arranging eternal madhurya-rasa, controls them.**

**Комментарий:**

The hand clapping of the gopis like Tungavidya produces joy. Some gopi like Visakha dances in front of the swing, displaying various movements that stimulate love. His love stimulated by the dance movements, Krsna controls (jayati) their minds. He is described. He obtains decorations like crown and bracelets made of forest flowers. His body is decorated with flower ornaments. He arranges eternal madhurya-rasa for them. Or he maintains in himself attraction to Sanatana.

### 6

*na kuru kadarthanam atra saraṇyām \|*  
*mām avalokya satīm aśaraṇyām \|\|*  
*cañcala muñca paṭāñcala-bhāgam \|*  
*karavāṇy adhunā bhāskara-yāgam \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O moon-faced Krsna! Seeing me, chaste, devoid of shelter, without friends, on this path, do not harass me. O fickle Krsna! Let go of the edge of my cloth. I must now worship the sun.**

**Комментарий:**

This section is in dhana-sri-raga. Going to worship the sun, with the object of meeting Krsna, Radha speaks to Krsna, whom she meets on the path.

O moon-faced Krsna! Seeing me, chaste, devoid of shelter, without friends, on this path, do not cause trouble for me. My friends are following behind. She explains the trouble he causes. Let go of my cloth. “What is the fault in this?” Let me worship the sun. This is the chorus.

### 7

*na racaya gokula-vīra vilambam \|*  
*vidadhe vidhu-mukha vinati-kadambam \|\|*  
*rahasi bibhemi vilola-dṛg-antam \|*  
*vīkṣya sanātana deva bhavantam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O hero of Gokula! Do not waste my time. O moon-faced Krsna! I offer many respects to you. Seeing you with your roving eye in this solitary place, I fear. O Krsna, worshipped by Sanatana!**

**Комментарий:**

O hero of Gokula! Do not waste my time by blocking the path. I offer many respects to you. “Why do you lament?” O Krsna, worshipped by Sanatana (sanatana deva)! Seeing your roving eye in a solitary place, I am afraid. Do not contaminate me by touching me, as 1 am going to worship the sun after taking a daily bath.

These words are svayam dhti. Asaratiyam indicates that parents are absent. Another meaning of vilambam na racaya is “Do not delay.” The word rahasi means no one can see them. Deva indicates one who plays. О eternal one (sanatana)! О playful one (deva)!

### 8

*rādhe nigada nijaṁ gada-mūlam \|*  
*udayati tanum anu kim iti tāpa-kulam anukṛta-vikaṭa-kukūlam \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Radha! Tell me the cause of your sickness. Seeing your body, why does it produce such pain, like fierce fire from burning chaff?**

**Комментарий:**

This section is in sorathi-raga. A sakhi inquires from Radha longing for more happiness after going home, after experiencing happiness in associating with Krsna to some degree. Tell me the cause of your malady. “How do you know about my sickness?” By looking at your body (tanu anu) why does it produce such pain, which is like a fierce fire from chaff? Vikata means fierce and kukula means a fire from chaff, according to Visva. This is the chorus.

### 9

*pracura-purandara-gopa-vinindaka-kānti-paṭalam anukūlam \|*  
*kṣipasi vidūre mṛdulaṁ muhur api sambhṛtam urasi dukūlam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You throw far away your soft cloth, worn on your chest at all times, whose color derides the indragopa, and which enhances your beauty.**

**Комментарий:**

You throw away the cloth worn on your chest, which enhances your beauty (anukulam), whose hue derides the red indragopa insect.

### 10

*abhinandasi na hi candra-rajo-bhara-vāsitam api tāmbūlam \|*  
*idam api vikirasi vara-campaka-kṛtam anupama-dāma sa-cūlam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**You do not welcome the betel nut scented with camphor power. You throw away the incomparable garland made of campaka along with your head jewel.**

**Комментарий:**

The garland is scented with lots of camphor dust (candra-raj as) made of fine campaka flowers. You throw away the garland along with the jewel on your hair part (sa-culam). Culam is equivalent of cudam since I and d are interchangeable.

### 11

*bhajad-anavasthitim akhila-pade sakhi sapadi viḍambita-tūlam \|*  
*kalita-sanātana-kautukam api tava hṛdayaṁ sphurati sa-śūlam \|\|*

**Комментарий:**

O friend! Your heart, which is joyful with Krsna, which has become unsteady in all places, which is now light as cotton, is pierced by a lance.

Your heart is pierced by a lance (sa-sulam). Sula means a weapon according to Haima. Your heart produces joy with Krsna (sandtana). Or it knows the joy of worshipping Krsna. He is eternally with her. In all places like the palace, while sleeping, or sitting, it is unsteady (anavasthitim). It is lighter than cotton (vidambita-tulam). Previously it was very heavy or profound.

### 12

*kuṭilaṁ mām avalokya navāmbujam upari cucumba sa raṅgī \|*  
*tena haṭhād aham abhavaṁ vepathu-maṇḍala-sañcalad-aṅgī \|\|*  
*bhāmini pṛccha na vāraṁ vāram \|*  
*hanta vimuhyati vīkṣya mano mama ballava-rāja-kumāram \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Playful Krsna, gazing at me with a crooked glance, kissed a fresh lotus. Suddenly my limbs began to tremble. O Visakha! Do not ask repeatedly. On seeing the son of Nanda, my mind becomes bewildered.**

**Комментарий:**

This section is in saurastn-raga. In reply to the question of her sickness, Radha speaks. Krsna, making hints (rang!), looking at me crookedly, taking a fresh lotus in his hand, kissed it. By that, suddenly my limbs began to tremble. My body began to tremble, as I understood by the hint that he wanted to kiss my mouth. O beautiful Visakha (bhamini)! Do not ask again and again because seeing him, my mind becomes bewildered. I cannot explain it. This is the chorus.

### 13

*dāḍima-latikām anu nistala-phala-namitāṁ sa dadhe hastam \|*  
*tad anubhavān mama dharmojjvalam api dhairya-dhanaṁ gatam astam \|\|*  
*adaśad aśoka-latā-pallava-mayam atanu-sanātana-narmā \|*  
*tad aham avekṣya babhūva ciraṁ bata vismṛta-kāyika-karmā \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He puts his hand on a pomegranate creeper laden with round fruit. Realizing his hint, my wealth of steadiness in dharma was destroyed. Fond of great jokes, he bit an asoka leaf. Seeing that, I forgot bodily actions for a long time.**

**Комментарий:**

Again, in longing she speaks. He places his hand on a-pomegranate creeper, bent down with two round (nistala) fruit. This means the fruit were plump. Understanding that he wanted to touch my breasts by that hint, my wealth of chastity, shining with dharma was destroyed (gatam). He bit the leaf of an asoka creeper. He is always fond of joking profusely (atanu-sanatana-narma). Understanding from that hint of biting the leaf that he wanted to wound my lip, I lost memory of using my body for a long time. Babhuva is first person perfect tense to express her despair. Or he always jokes about Cupid (atanu-sanatana-narma).

The alankara is suksma. Suksma manifests if suggestive actions are understood.

### 14

*anadhigatākasmika-gada-kāraṇam arpita-mantrauṣadhi-nikurambam \|*  
*avirata-rudita-vilohita-locanam anuśocati tām akhila-kuṭumbam \|\|*  
*deva hare bhava kāruṇya-śālī \|*  
*sā tava niśita-kaṭākṣa-śarāhata-hṛdayā jīvati kṛśa-tanūrālī \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**O Lord! O Hari! The whole family, not understanding the cause of her disease, offering many mantras and medicines, their eyes red from constant weeping, lament for her. Be merciful! With thin body, she lives, her heart pierced by your sharp glances.**

**Комментарий:**

The raga is dhana sri. A messenger, understanding the cause of the pain in Radha’s heart, spoke to Krsna. O Lord! O Hari! The whole family laments for Radha. They do not understand the cause of this sudden illness. They applied many mantras and medicines. Their eyes are red with constant weeping. You should be merciful (karunya-sdll). My friend, with thin body, maintains her life, her heart pierced by sharp glances. She has not a drop of happiness without your mercy. This is the chorus.

### 15

*hṛdi valad-avirala-saṁjvara-paṭalī-sphuṭad-ujjvala-mauktika-samudāyā \|*  
*śītala-bhūtala-niścala-tanur iyam avasīdati samprati nirupāyā \|\|*  
*goṣṭha-janābhaya-satra-mahā-vrata-dīkṣita bhavato mādhava bālā \|*  
*katham arhati tāṁ hanta sanātana viṣama-daśāṁ guṇa-vṛnda-viśālā \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Her shining pearls bursting because of the constant pain in her heart, her body motionless on the cold ground, with no method of relief, she now suffers. O Madhava, who vows to make the people of Vraja fearless! O eternal Krsna! Does this young girl, famous for her many good qualities, deserve this dangerous state because of you?**

**Комментарий:**

“How is she now?” Samjvara means pain. She is in pain (avasidati), not seeing any method to destroy her sickness except you (nirupdyd). “I cannot see others’ wives.” You have made a great vow to make the people of Vraja fearless. O Krsna, appearing in the Madhu dynasty! Does this young girl deserve this disturbing state because of you? O eternal form! Or O Krsna who have Sanatana as your eternal servant! The word sandtana with this meaning is explained by the following sutra, arsa-adibhyo ’c: The affix ac (a) comes in the sense of tnatup (possessive) after the words arsa, etc. (Panini Sutras 5.2.127)

Radha is described. She is famous (visald) for her many qualities or is the huge abode (visdla) of many qualities. Why does he who take away suffering caused by pure love not remove what is caused by him?

### 16

*hanta na kim u mantharayasi santatam abhijalpam \|*  
*danta-rocir antarayati santam asamanalpam \|\|*  
*rādhe pathi muñca bhuri sambhramam abhisāre \|*  
*cāraya caraṇāmburuhe dhīraṁ sukumāre \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Why do you not stop chattering constantly? The splendor of your teeth destroys the deep darkness. O Radha! Give up hurrying on the path to the appointment. Place your lotus feet softly, delicate girl!**

**Комментарий:**

The raga is asavari.

“O messenger! Why do you give this opposite message? I am fully devoted to her. I live with her, brought by meditation.” The messenger, understanding Krsna’s love, speaks to her as she hurries on the path to meet him. She speaks to Radha as follows.

Hanta expresses lamentation. Why do you not stop babbling? “What is wrong with that?” The beauty of your teeth when you speak destroys the deep darkness (samtamasam). Samtatnasam means great darkness according to Halayudha. Stop hurrying so fast on the path for the appointment. Place your tender lotus feet softly. This is the chorus.

### 17

*santanu ghana-varṇam atula-kuntala-nicayāntam \|*  
*dhvāntaṁ tava jīvatu nakha-kāntibhir abhiśāntam \|\|*  
*sa-sanātana-mānasādya yāntī gata-śaṅkam \|*  
*aṅgīkuru mañju-kuñja-vasater alam aṅkam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Cover your fingernails with the tips of your long, dark locks of hair. The darkness destroyed by the luster of your fingernails will be restored. Thus, going without worry, mind concentrating on Krsna, may you enter within the attractive bower.**

**Комментарий:**

“I have covered the effulgence of my teeth. How can I cover my nails?” Spread the tips of your long (atula) locks of hair over your fingernails. They are dark like clouds. “Then what will happen?” May the darkness destroyed (abhisantam) by your fingernails’ luster be restored to its nature. “Then what will happen?” With mind on Krsna (sanatana) you can go without worry and enter (angikuru) the attractive bower. Or with your mind concentrated on your devotee Sanatana, you can go.

### 18

*sicayam udañcaya hṛdayād alpam \|*  
*vilikhāmy adbhuta-makarākalpam \|\|*  
*iha na hi saṅkuca paṅkaja-nayane \|*  
*veśaṁ tava karavai rati-śayane \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Raise the cloth on your chest a little. I will draw astonishing patterns there. О lotus-eyed Radha! Do not be reserved. I will make patterns on all your limbs on the bed of love.**

**Комментарий:**

This is sung in Gaudi raga. Krsna speaks to Radha, who is enjoying with him, controlling him. О Radha! Raise your cloth a little from your heart. Uncover your chest a little. “Why?” I will draw makara patterns. О lotus-eyed Radha! Do not be reserved on the love bed. I should make patterns on all your limbs. This is the chorus.

### 19

*rādhe dolaya na kila kapolam \|*  
*citraṁ racayāmy aham avilolam \|\|*  
*tava vapur adya sanātana-śobham \|*  
*janayati hṛdi mama kañcana lobham \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Do not move your cheek since I am drawing a pattern with steadiness. Your body, eternally beautiful produces indescribable greed in my heart.**

**Комментарий:**

Do not move your cheeks since I am drawing patterns there steadily. Being very pleased I am decorating you. Your body whose beauty is eternal produces indescribable greed in my heart. Or your body is beautiful for Sanatana. 1 make myself successful by the touch of your naturally beautiful body.

### 20

*tava cañcala-matir ayam aghahantā \|*  
*aham uttama-dhṛti-digdha-digantā \|\|*  
*dūti vidūraya komala-kathanam \|*  
*punar abhidhāsye na hi madhu-mathanam \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Your killer of Agha has a fickle mind. I am famous everywhere for my great determination. О messenger! Give up speaking gently. I will not speak again with the killer of Madhu.**

**Комментарий:**

The raga is asavari. Angry Radha speaks to a messenger who has come to decorate her. Your killer of Agha has a fickle mind. The directions are anointed with my great determination (dhrti). I am famous in all directions for my steadiness. О messenger! Give up speaking gently. I will not speak with the killer of the Madhu demon. This is the chorus.

### 21

*śaṭha-carito’yaṁ tava vanamālī \|*  
*mṛdu-hṛdayāhaṁ nija-kula-pālī \|\|*  
*tava harir eṣa niraṅkuśa-narmā \|*  
*aham anubaddha-sanātana-dharmā \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**Your wearer of the garland has a cunning nature. With soft heart, I protect my family’s dharma. Your Krsna is an uncontrolled joker. I am fixed in eternal dharma.**

**Комментарий:**

Your wearer of the garland has the nature of a fraud. I am the protector of my family’s honor and have a soft heart. I would think, “My heart melted by sudden affection for the most beautiful boy. May he not suffer because of me.” Not respecting family dharma, I have acted favorably to him. But now understanding his cunning nature, why should I act favorably towards him? Your Krsna is an uncontrollable joker.

I have firmly accepted eternal family dharma. Since your natures are opposite, friendship with him will not bring happiness. Or I am fixed in Krsna, who is eternal dharma. Or eternal bhakti is fixed in me.

### 22

*maṇḍita-hallīsaka-maṇḍalām*  
*naṭayan rādhāṁ cala-kuṇḍalām \|\|*  
*nikhila-kalā-sampadi paricayī \|*  
*priya-sakhi paśya naṭati murajayī \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He makes Radha, with swaying earrings, dance in the decorated circle. Expert in a wealth of all arts, Krsna dances. Dear friend, look!**

**Комментарий:**

The raga is bhairava.

A friend describes the rasa dance of Krsna with Radha who has been brought there with respect. Halllsaka is a dance where the girls are bound in a circle. Paricayl means expert. This is the chorus.

### 24

*muhur āndolita ratna-valayam \|*  
*salayaṁ calayan kara-kiśalayam \|\|*  
*gati-bhaṅgibhir avaśīkṛta-śaśī \|*  
*sthagita-sanātana-śaṅkara-vaśī \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**He delightfully moves his bud-like hands while his jeweled bracelets swing constantly. He is an uncontrolled moon with his gait and gestures. He stuns Sanatana and Siva, whose senses are controlled.**

**Комментарий:**

He moves his bud-like hands delightfully (salayam). Lay a means delight according to Visva. He stuns Sanatana and Siva who have controlled their senses.

### 25

*dāmodara-rati-vardhana-veśe \|*  
*hari-niṣkuṭa-vṛndā-vipineśe \|\|*  
*jaya jaya rādhe mādhava-dayite \|*  
*gokula-taruṇī-maṇḍala-mahite \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О Radha, dressed to increase Krsna’s love! О Radha, mistress of Vrndavana, Krsna’s garden! О Radha, beloved of Madhava! May you display all excellence! О Radha, worshiped by the girls of Gokula!**

**Комментарий:**

This is in bhairava-raga. The author prays for the mercy of most attractive mistress, Radha. О mistress of Vrndavana, which is Krsna’s garden. О Radha, worshipped by the groups of girls in Gokula. This is the chorus.

### 26

*vṛṣabhānu-dadhi-nava-śaśi-lekhe \|*  
*lalitā-sakhi guṇa-ramita-viśākhe \|\|*  
*karuṇāṁ kuru mayi karuṇā-bharite \|*  
*sanaka-sanātana-varṇita-carite \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О fresh moon rising in the ocean of Vrsabhanu! О friend of Lalita! О Radha, giving joy to Visakha by your qualities! О Radha, full of mercy! Be merciful to me. О Radha whose qualities are described by Sanaka and Sanatana!**

**Комментарий:**

О new moon rising in the ocean of Vrsabhanu! О friend of Lalita! You delight Visakha with qualities like friendship, mercy and favorability to Krsna. You are full of mercy. Be merciful to me. Her qualities are described by Sanaka and Sanatana.

### 27

*rāja-purād gokulam upayātam \|*  
*pramadonmādita-jananī-tātam \|\|*  
*svapne sakhi punar adya mukundam \|*  
*ālokayam avataṁsita-kundam \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**О friend! In a dream today I again saw Mukunda, wearing jasmine earrings, who had come from Mathura to Gokula, giving joy to his mother and father.**

**Комментарий:**

The raga is dhanasrt. Radha separated from Krsna, who is in Mathura, speaks about her dream to her sakhi.

О friend! In a dream today I saw Mukunda again. It is understood she saw him in dreams previously also. He is described. He came to Nandisvara or Gokula from Mathura. He gave bliss to his mother and father (jananl-tatam). He had jasmine ear ornaments.

### 28

*parama-mahotsava-ghūrṇita-ghoṣam \|*  
*nayaneṅgita-kṛta-mat-paritoṣam \|\|*  
*nava-guñjāvali-kṛta-para-bhāgam \|*  
*prabala-sanātana-suhṛd-anurāgam \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I saw Mukunda, causing the cowherds to swoon from great joy, satisfying me with his glance, dressed most attractively with gunja berries, greatly attracted to his friends eternally.**

**Комментарий:**

The first two lines are clear. He was most attractive with fresh gunja berries. “Why did he give up Mathura and come to Gokula?” He has eternal, great attraction to his friends. He is not attracted to the majesty of Mathura. He is greedy for prema only. Thus, he left Mathura and came here.

*bhagavān bhakta bhaktimān*

**The Lord has devotion to his devotee. (SB 10.86.59) Or he has great attraction to his devotee named Sanatana.**

### 29

*pulakam upaiti bhayān mama gātram \|*  
*hasasi tathāpi madād atimātram \|\|*  
*vāraya tūrṇam imaṁ sakhi kṛṣṇam \|*  
*anucita-karmaṇi nirmita-tṛṣṇam \|\| dhruva \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**The hairs on my limbs stand on end out of fear. You laugh profusely out of pride. О friend! Quickly prevent this Krsna from doing improper actions out of thirst.**

**Комментарий:**

This is in saurdstn rdga. Fixing Krsna, pained by anuraga, at the appointment place, Radha, brought there on the pretext of seeing the beauty of the forest, talks to a sakhi, understanding that he is agitated by her touch.

О friend! When I see Krsna, out of fear, all the hairs on my body stand on end. Still out of pride, you laugh profusely (atimatram), thinking, “Today I have conquered you.” Atimatra means greatly according to Amara-kosa. “What should I do?” Prevent him from doing improper acts like embracing me.

### 30

*jāne bhavatīm eva vipakṣām \|*  
*mām upanītā yad vana-kakṣām \|\|*  
*adya sanātanam atisukha-hetum \|*  
*na parihariṣye vidhi-kṛta-setum \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**I know you are my enemy because you have brought me into the forest. Today I will not give up the rules prescribed by the Vedas, eternal and the cause of great happiness.**

**Комментарий:**
